ἔκθρεψις.definition: bringing up, rearing, Ael.NA3.8, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11

ἔκθυμος.definition: spirited, ardent, Plu.Aem.12,cf. App.BC5.38 . Adv. ardently, Diog.Oen.15; Luc.JTr.16; vehemently, bravely, Plb.2.67.7, cf. 1.17.9 ; D.H.2.54, etc

ἑκκαιδεκατάλαντος.definition: worth sixteen talents, with a dowry of sixteen talents, cj. in Men.402.11

ἑκκαιεικοσάεδρον.definition: solid with twenty-six surfaces, Papp.in Archim.2p.536H

ἑκκαιπεντηκοντάγωνον.definition: figure of fifty-six sides, prob.in Plu.2.363a

ἔκκαιρος.definition: out of date, antiquated, AP11.417; unseasonable, POxy.729.18

ἐκκεντρεπίκυκλος.definition: requiring both eccentric and epicycle, Procl.Hyp.2.3

ἔκκεντρος.definition: Astron., not having the earth as; not occupying a cardinal point, opp. Vett.Val.97.11

ἐκκεντρότης.definition: eccentricity, Eudem. ap. Theo Sm.p.201 H., Gem.1.39, Ptol.Alm.3.3, Iamb.VP6.31 , etc

ἔκλαμψις.definition: shining forth, brightness, LXX2; metaph., sudden development, at puberty, Hp.Epid.6.114 ap. Gal. ad loc.)

ἔκλειψις.definition: of Sun or Moon, eclipse, Th.1.23, cf. Arist.Metaph.1044b10, etc.; Cleom.2.6; ib.5: metaph. , Plb.29.16.1, cf. Plu.Aem.17

ἔκλευκος.definition: quite white, Hp.Prog.2, Arist.HA617a12, PCair.Zen. 129.18, LXXLe.13.24: Comp., inclining to white, Arist.HA592b7

ἔκληψις.definition: taking out, collecting, Dsc.1.68.4; farming of taxes, BGU897.1, Just.Nov.123.6; of any trade enterprise, PTeb.38.11

ἐκλιμία.definition: exceeding hunger, faintness, LXXDe.28.20, Aq. Jb.41.14

ἐκλιπής.definition: failing, deficient; omitted, overlooked, Th.1.97, Arr.An.1.12.2

ἔκλυσις.definition: release, deliverance from a thing; weakening of an opponent's case, Hdn.Fig.p.91 S., cf. Alex.Fig.1.2

ἐκμαγεῖον.definition: napkin, Pl.Ti.72c, Meyer; that which wipes off, gets rid of, of the spleen, Aret.SD1.15; rough towel, Archig. ap. Gal.12.621, Paul.Aeg.1.57

ἔκμαγμα.definition: impression in wax, etc., Poll.9.131; = Hp.Steril.235

ἐκμανής.definition: quite mad, Nicias ap.Ath.10.437e; Ph.1.408. Adv. Ath.13.603a

ἐκμελής.definition: out of tune, dissonant, Ph.1.375, al., Ti.Locr.101b, Plu.Demetr.1; unbridled, Id.Lys.23; of persons, Just.Nov.136.6. Adv. Poll.4.57

ἕκμηνος.definition: of six months, half-yearly; six months old, of an animal, Arist.HA562b27; IG12.647.8

ἔκνευσις.definition: turning the head aside to avoid; deviations, Sch.Ar.Ra.113; cf. diverticulum, Gloss

ἔκνομος.definition: = foreg., Orph.A.60; unlawful, monstrous, D.S.14.112, cf. Ael.Fr.217, Ph.2.165, al.: Sup., ib.280

ἐκπαθής.definition: passionate, furious, Plb.16.23.5; out of harm, unhurt, Anon. ap. Suid

ἐκπεμπτέος.definition: that must be sent out, Plu.2.595c; one must reject, Porph.Abst.2.31

ἔκπεμψις.definition: sending out or forth; emission, expulsion, Gal.UP6.2

ἐκπέταλος.definition: outspread, flat, Mosch. ap. Ath.11.485e , cf. Sch.Ar.Ach.1109

ἐκπετήσιμος.definition: ready to fly out of the nest, just fledged, Ar.Av.1355, Ael.NA2.43, Procop.Vand.1.4: metaph., of a marriageable girl, Ar.Fr.582

ἕκπλεθρος.definition: six plethra long, Phryn.387; in = E.El.883, and Id.Med.1181 is the better reading, narrowing

ἐκπομπή.definition: sending out or forth, Th.3.51; divorce, Antipho Soph.49

ἔκπτυξις.definition: spreading, parting of the legs in riding, Aët.3.7

ἔκπτωμα.definition: dislocation, Hp.Art.28; collapse of a dam, PTeb.72.78

ἔκπτωσις.definition: breaking forth, escape; banishment, Plb.4.1.8, D.S.13.65,PMag.Osl.1.222

ἔκπυστος.definition: heard of, discovered, Th.3.30, cf. 4.70,8.42, J.AJ19.1.7, Plu.Cam.3, etc.; Hdn.2.7.7, cf. 3.12.6

ἔκρηγμα.definition: broken bed of a torrent, ravine, Plb.12.20.4; breaking forth of a stream, Thphr.CP1.5.2

ἐκροή.definition: I, Pherecyd.Syr.7, Pl.Grg.494b; = II, Hp.Epid.2.1.7 , Arist.Mete.356a10, Pl.Phd.112d, al.; the places of efflux, in the human body, Arist.PA688b28

ἔκροος.definition: contr. outflow, issue; by excretion, Hp.Epid.2.1.7

ἔκρυθμος.definition: out of tune, S.E.M.11.186; of the pulse, irregular, Gal.8.516

ἔκρυσις.definition: = II, Arist.Mete.351a5; efflux, flooding, differing from , Hp.Septim.9, Arist.GA758b6 , HA583a25

ἐκσκευάζω.definition: disfurnish of tools and implements, D.30.30:—Med., carry away with one, Str.15.3.9; plunder, J.BJ4.7.2:—Pass., f.l. for Plu.Cleom.37

ἔκσκευος.definition: without equipment, without mask; special masks, Poll.4.141; but Hsch

ἔκσπονδος.definition: out of the treaty, not a party; contrary to a treaty, violating it, D.H.2.72

ἔκστασις.definition: standing aside, Arist.Rh.1361a37; = Lat. cessio bonorum, CPR20ii9 ; Porph.Abst.1.53; a tax on cessions, BGU914.6 , PLond.2.305.2

ἐκστροφή.definition: dislocation, Alciphr.3.54; transmutation of base metal, Zos.Alch.p.195 B

ἐκταγή.definition: delegation of powers; assessment of taxes, PGiss.54.9 , etc

ἔκτακτος.definition: detailed for special duties, of soldiers; special, reserved, POxy.646 ; on a separate sheet, PStrassb.34.15

ἔκταμα.definition: extent, length, Sch.Ar.Nu.2; gloss on Sch.E.Ph.308

ἔκταξις.definition: array of battle; expedition, title of work by Arr

ἔκτασις.definition: stretching out, extension; extent, Max.Tyr.6.2; Iamb.VP29.162

ἔκτεισις.definition: Arc. later payment in full, IG5.6.37 , SIG279.17 , PCair.Zen.1.18,44 , PPetr.3p.160 , etc.; Pl.Lg.855a ; Din.2.17; And.1.73; D.40.56; = Id.27.67; PHib.1.94 , etc.; Iamb.Myst.4.5, PLond.1.113

ἑκτέος.definition: to be held, Ar.Ach.259; one must have, X.Mem.3.11.2; Aen.Tact.Praef.3; = Pl.Grg.490c

ἑκτεύς.definition: the sixth part of the Schwyzer 725 , cf.IG12.76.6, Ar.Ec.547, Men.91

ἕκτη.definition: a silver coin, the sixth of a stater; tax of one-sixth, PTeb.343.69 , cf. PHib.1.109 , PRev.Laws 36.9

ἔκτηξις.definition: melting away: hence, attenuation; cancelling of contract, BCH37.91

ἔκτολμος.definition: audacious, f.l. in Suid. s.v. Adv. Man.3.331

ἕκτος.definition: sixth, Il.2.407, etc.; , Plu.2.268a; v. sub voc

ἐκτράπελος.definition: turning from the common course; odious, prob. in Pi.P.1.92, 4.105

ἐκτροφή.definition: bringing up, rearing, nurture, E.Fr.317.5 , Sor.1.81, Arist.HA542a30 , GA754a8, al.; J.AJ5.1.21: metaph., breeding, Phld.Ir.p.27 W

ἐκτυμπάνωσις.definition: swelling out like a drum, Str.16.4.13

ἕκτωρ.definition: Hom. only as pr. n. Hector, the prop or stay of Troy, Il.6.403:—Adj. or also E.Rh.1 :—of Hector, Hom., B.12.154, etc.: also Anaxil.38; Lyc.1133

ἔκφασις.definition: Ion. ) declaration; emergence, reappearance, of an eclipsed body, Phld.Sign.10 ; rising of the sun, Agatharch.105; prob. f.l. for in Procl.in Prm.pp.480,520 S

ἔκφατος.definition: beyond power of speech, Max.451; Adv. with loud voice or ineffably, impiously, A.Ag.706

ἔκφρων.definition: gen. out of one's mind, beside

ἐκφυής.definition: abnormally developed; eminent, extraordinary. Adv. App.Ill.25

ἔκφυλος.definition: foreign, alien, Luc.Lex.24, Sol.11, Porph.Abst.1.4; alien to generation, Simp.in Ph.220.12: metaph., strange, unnatural, horrible, Str.4.4.5, Plu.Brut.36; Id.Caes.69. Adv. Philostr.VS1.16.4

ἔκφυμα.definition: eruption of pimples, v.l. in; outgrowth of vine tendrils, EM330.29

ἔκφυσις.definition: growing out or forth; bony projection, Hp.Art.45; origin, attachment of muscles, nerves, etc., Gal.8.61, al

ἐλάδιον.definition: Dim. of young olive-tree; a little oil, Telesp.41H., Sotad.Com.1.7, Arched.2.11, PSI4.418.11

ἐλαία.definition: Att. olive-tree, Hom., esp. in; variety of III, ib.4.7.2, Str.16.3.6

ἔλαιον.definition: olive-oil, in Hom. mostly; any oily substance, Hp.Mul.2.194; etc., Dsc.1.32,33, etc.; PAmh.2.93 , etc.; like our 'cod-liver' oil, Arist.HA520a18; butter, Hecat.154 J

ἔλαιος.definition: = wild olive, Pi.Fr.46; a bird, prob. a kind of warbler, Alex.Mynd. ap. Ath.2.65b, cj. in AP7.199 ; cf

ἑλάνη.definition: torch of reeds, Neanth.4J.; also, bundle of reeds, Nic.Fr.89

ἐλασίβροντος.definition: thunder-hurling, Pi.Fr.144 (dub; hurled like thunder, Ar.Eq.626

ἐλάσιππος.definition: horse-driving, horse-riding, knightly, Pi.P.5.85; Lyr.Adesp.97; of the sun, Orph.H.8.18

ἔλασις.definition: driving away, banishing; march, expedition, Hdt.4.1, etc.; Id.7.37; also, procession, X.Cyr.8.3.34; IG22.847.20

ἐλάτη.definition: silver fir, Abies cephalonica; oar, as made of pine-wood, Od.12.172, cf. Il.7.5; later, ship or boat, E.Ph.208 , Alc.444

ἐλάτινος.definition: also Anaxil.22.17: Ep; made of fir or pine-wood, Od.2.424; E.Hel.1461, cf. Anaxil.l.c

ἔλατρον.definition: = III, SIG57.36; a garment, Eucrat. ap. eund

ἐλάφειος.definition: of a stag or hart, hartshorn; for catching stags, Aen.Tact.11.6, 38.7

ἐλέα.definition: perh. reed-warbler, Salicaria arundinacea, Arist.HA616b12: Call.Fr.100c.14; cf

ἐλέατρος.definition: = seneschal or steward, PCair.Zen.59.5, 71.1 , dub. in Ath.4.171b: but, = acc. to Et.Gud., where it is distd. from

ἐλεγεῖον.definition: distich consisting of hexameter and; in pl., elegiac poem or inscription, merely in reference to the metre, not to the subject, Pl.R.368a, Arist.Rh.1375b32, Lycurg.142, D.59.98; even in two hexameters, Pherecr.153.7; …

ἐλεγξῖνος.definition: wrangler, pun on the name of the philosopher Alexinus, D.L.2.109

ἔλεγος.definition: song, melody, orig. accompanied by the; poem in elegiac distichs, Call.Fr.121; AP10.19

ἔλεγχος.definition: reproach, disgrace, dishonour, Il.11.314; Od.21.329, cf. Pi.N.3.15; of men, the abstr. being put for the concrete, base reproaches to your name, Il.5.787, al., Hes.Th.26; alone, Il.24.260

ἑλεδώνη.definition: a kind of octopus, Arist.HA525a17, Henioch.3, Artem.2.14

ἑλειός.definition: or a kind of dormouse, Myoxus glis; a kind of hawk, Hsch., prob. in Arist.HA620a21

ἑλείτης.definition: marsh-growing, Dion.Byz.23; title of Apollo in Cyprus, Schwyzer 682.15

ἑλέναυς.definition: ship-destroying, epith. of Helen, prob. for A.Ag.689

ἑλένη.definition: torch, Hsch.; cf; corposant, St. Elmo's fire, Lyd.Ost.5

ἑλένιον.definition: calamint, Calamintha incana; elecampane, Inula Helenium, ib.28

ἐλεός.definition: kitchen table, dresser, in pl., Il.9.215; a kind of owl, Arist.HA592b11

ἔλεος.definition: pity, mercy, compassion, Il.24.44, etc.: also; personified. worshipped at Athens, Sch.S.OC260; at Epidaurus, IG4.1282; Timocl.31

Ἐλευσίνιος.definition: of Eleusis, h.Cer.266, Hdt.9.57; their temple at Eleusis, And.1.110, IG 12.6.129

Ἐλευσίς.definition: Eleusis, an old city of Attica; Advs. at Eleusis, IG12.76.10, al., And.1.111, Lys.6.4, etc.; later IG22.1028.11, al.: to Eleusis, Lys.12.52, from Eleusis, And.1.111, Lys.6.45

ἔλευσις.definition: coming, arrival, Corn.ND28; the Advent of Christ, Act.Ap.7.52

ἐλέωτρις.definition: a fish of the Nile, Ath.7.312b

Ἐλιεύς.definition: title of Zeus at Thebes, Hsch

Ἑλικώνιος.definition: title of Poseidon, Il.20.404: acc. to Sch., from Helice in Achaia, where he was especially honoured, 8.203

ἕλινος.definition: vine-tendril, Philet. ap; fem., the vine, Nic.Al.181, Opp.C.4.262, D.P.1157. [Later prob. in Nonn.D.12.299.]

ἑλινοφόρος.definition: Ep. bearing vine- tendrils, Nonn.D.16.278; ib.17.333

ἕλιξ.definition: as Adj., twisted, curved: in Hom. and Hes., as in S.Aj.374 , Theoc.25.127, epith. of oxen, commonly understood of their twisted, crumpled horns, cf. I; also expld. of the movement of their bodies as they walk, rolling…

ἕλιξις.definition: rolled bandage, Hp.Off.10; convolution of the bowels, Aret.SA2.6

ἑλίχρυσος.definition: gold-flower, Helichrysum siculum, Alcm.16, Ibyc.6, Cratin.98; Theoc.2.78

ἕλκος.definition: festering wound, sore, ulcer, the festering bite of a serpent, Il.2.723; plague-ulcer, Th.2.49, X.Eq.5.1, etc

Ἑλλάς.definition: Hellas, said to have been originally; a city of Thessaly, founded by Hellen, Il.2.683

ἑλλέβορος.definition: Ion. hellebore, Hp.Acut.23; = of women, Ar.Fr.320.6, Nicostr.33, cf. Hsch

ἐλλεδανός.definition: band for binding corn-sheaves, in pl., Il.18.553, h.Cer.456, Hes.Sc.291: sg., in Suid

ἔλλειμμα.definition: defect, deficiency, Hp.Praec.9; remnant, v.l. in LXX2 Ki.21.2

ἔλλειψις.definition: falling short, defect, opp; the conic section ellipse, Apollon.Perg.Con.1.13

ἔλλεσχος.definition: talked of in the commonly talked of, Hdt.1.153

Ἕλλην.definition: Hellen, son of Deucalion, Hes.Fr.7.1; the Thessalian tribe of which Hellen was the reputed chief, Il.2.684

ἐλλιπής.definition: Act., leaving out, omitting; Pass., wanting, defective, Th.7.8; Pl.Lg.669a, R.504b, etc.: c. dat., Th.6.69; . . Euang.1.3; Plb.18.22.5

ἐλλόβιον.definition: that which is in the lobe of the ear, ear-ring, Nic.Dam.p.5 D., Luc.Gall.29, S.E.P.3.203, Them.Or.13.167d

ἐλλοβόκαρπος.definition: bearing fruit in a pod, Thphr.HP6.5.3

ἐλλοβοσπέρματος.definition: with its seed in a pod, opp. ib.7.3.2

Ἐλλοπία.definition: a district in Euboea, Hdt.8.23, etc.:—hence its inhabitants, Hsch

ἐλλοπίης.definition: name of a fish, cj. for in Numen. ap. Ath.7.326a

ἑλλός.definition: or , a young deer, fawn, Od.19.228, cf. Ant.Lib.28.3, Eust.1863.40

ἔλλοψ.definition: epith. of fish (exc; as Subst., fish, in general, Nic.Al.481, Lyc.600, Opp.H.2.658, 3.55,89; fem., Lyc.796

ἐλλύτης.definition: Dor. a kind of cake, Test.Epict.5.35, al., Hsch

Ἑλλωτία.definition: or epith. of Athena; wreath worn at the Seleuc. ap. Ath.15.678a, cf. Hsch

ἑλμινθοβότανον.definition: a herb used as a specific for worms, Alex.Trall.Verm.2p.595P

ἕλμινς.definition: intestinal-worm, either flat or round , Id.Morb.4.54, cf. Prog.11, Aph.3.26, Arist.HA551a8, Thphr.HP9.12.1

ἑλξίνη.definition: pellitory, Parietaria; bindweed, Convolvulus arvensis, Dsc.4.39

ἕλξις.definition: dragging, trailing; attraction, attractive power, Id.Ti.80c, Hp.Gland.7; Porph.Gaur.3.3

ἑλονόμος.definition: dwelling in marshes, f.l. for Hp.Vict.2.49

ἐλπωρή.definition: Ep. form of c. fut. inf. et aor., . . Od.23.287; 6.314: pl., A.R.3.1255

ἐλύδριον.definition: = used to make yellow dye, PHolm.11.16, PLeid.X.68, Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.48B., v.l. in Paul.Aeg.3.2

ἔλυμα.definition: the stock of the plough, Hes.Op.430,436: also expld. by Hsch

ἔλυμος.definition: case, quiver, Hsch; a kind of Phrygian pipe, made of box-wood, with a horn tip and bend in the left pipe, S.Fr.450,644, Call.Com.18; used by the Cyprians, Cratin.Jun.3

ἔλυτρον.definition: bow-case, S.Fr.1043 ; sheath of a spear, Ar.Ach.1120; mirror-case, IG2.706Ab13; ib.11 .219B76 ; case of a shield, D.S.20.11

ἕλωρ.definition: Ep. word , only; in pl. also, . . may pay penalty for the slaughter of P., Il.18.93

ἔμβαμμα.definition: sauce, soup, X.Cyr.1.3.4, Theopomp.Com.8, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.23.4, Aret.CD1.3, etc

ἐμβάς.definition: felt-shoe or slipper, used by; = Callix.2, Plu.Demetr.41, v.l. in Luc.Gall.26; Id.Pseudol.19, etc

Ἐμβάσιος.definition: favouring embarkation, epith. of Apollo, A.R.1.359,404

ἔμβασις.definition: embarkation, Plb.4.10.3; place of; step, interpol. in Luc.Salt.10

ἐμβασίχυτρος.definition: pot-visitor, name of a mouse in Batr.137

ἐμβελής.definition: within range of missiles, Plb.8.5.2, D.S.20.44

ἔμβολος.definition: or anything pointed so as to; tongue of land, Hdt.4.53; prob. the headland of in Caria, Pi.O.7.19

ἔμβρυον.definition: young one, put a; embryo, foetus, A.Eu.945 , Hp.Aph.5.52, Arist.GA746a1, al

ἐμίας.definition: one who is inclined to vomit, Eup.412

ἐμμανής.definition: frantic, raving, Hdt.3.25, S.Ichn.15, etc.; A.Pr.675; maddened by . ., Id.Eu.860; E.Ba.1094; Id.Cyc.3; Men.Sam.200; of elephants in the rutting season, Arist.HA571b34; LXXWi.14.23: Comp. Luc.Am.14: Sup. Pl.Lg.734a, cf…

ἐμμέθοδος.definition: according to rule or system, S.E.P.2.21; systematic arrangement, Ph.2.512. Adv. systematically, Cleom.2.1, HeroDef.138.5, A.D.Synt.155.21, S.E.M.1.188, etc.: Comp. Procl.Hyp.6.2

ἐμμέλεια.definition: harmony in music or the fit; a tragic dance, opp. Pl.Lg.816b; opp. and Ath.1.20e, 14.631d, Luc.Salt.26; the tune of this dance, Hdt.6.129

ἐμμελής.definition: in tune, harmonious, opp; of persons, harmonious, orderly, Pl.Criti.106b; ib.121b; also Plu.Pel.19

ἐμμέριμνος.definition: in anxiety, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.210, Sch.E.Or.93. Adv. Eust.ad D.P.Praef

ἔμμεσος.definition: inserted, ib.41.23; mediate, Eustr.in EN331.2. Adv. mediately, Them.in APo.31.6

ἔμμεστος.definition: filled full of a thing, S.Ichn.282, Pl.Ep.338d

ἐμμήνιος.definition: monthly: the menses of women, Hp.Nat.Mul.7; J.BJ4.8.4

ἔμμηνις.definition: Cret. wroth, SIG527.78 , cf. GDI5041.18, etc

ἔμμηνος.definition: lasting a month; done or paid every month, monthly, S.El.281, Pl.Lg.828c; Plu.Caes.8; Theoc.16.35

ἔμμηρος.definition: poet. for as a hostage, Demetr.Com.Vet.2

ἔμμισθος.definition: in receipt of pay, hired, Th.6.22; of work, paid, Pl.Lg.920e

ἔμμορφος.definition: endued with form, Thphr.Metaph.14; Plu.Num.8, cf. 2.362d; Plot.5.9.4

ἔμμοτος.definition: treated with tents , Hp.Aph.5.47; used with such tents, Dsc.1.68; Gal.11.125; Id.13.500; treatment by tents, Paul.Aeg.6.3

ἔμμουσος.definition: = Heph.Astr.2.32: Sup. Nicom.Ar.2.2; in literature, IG9.235 . Adv. Plu.2.1119d

ἔμπαιος.definition: knowing, practised in, c.gen., [penult. short] Od.20.379; 21.400; Lyc.1321

ἐμπέδιος.definition: deep-rooted, cj. in Numen. ap. Ath.9.371c

ἔμπεδος.definition: in the ground, firm-set; mostly of qualities, etc., steadfast, Il.5.254, Od.11.393; Il.6.352, 10.94, 11.813; 19.33; of a person, 20.183; prays that it may be sure and certain, Od.8.30, cf. Pi.N.7.57; A.R.4.372, etc.; …

ἔμπειρος.definition: experienced or practised in a; Adv. to know a person or thing by experience, by its issue, X.An.2.6.1, Antiph.3, etc.; D.59.18; Aen.Tact.2.6; Jul.Or.2.95a: Comp. Aeschin.1.82

ἐμπέπτας.definition: hollow wheaten cake, Seleuc. ap. Ath.14.645d; Rhodian, acc. to Hsch

ἐμπέραμος.definition: = skilled in the use of, Call.Jov.71; IG14.1957, cf.888 , Arch.Anz.1904.8 : abs., Androm. ap. Gal.14.37:—also Lyc.1196, Man.4.536, AP10.14 , Nonn.D.39.181. Adv. Call.Lav.Pall.25

ἐμπεταλίς.definition: dish consisting of cheese wrapped in a leaf , Hsch

ἔμπετρος.definition: growing on rocks: sea- heath, Franklinia pulverulenta, Dsc.4.179, Gal.11.875

ἐμπήκτης.definition: one who sticks up judicial notices, Arist.Ath.64.2, al

ἐμπίμελος.definition: of a fatty substance, Dsc.2.61, Xenocr.63

ἐμπίς.definition: mosquito, gnat, Ar.Nu.157; larva of the ib.487b5

ἐμπλατία.definition: Arc. a kind of cake, IG5.4

ἔμπλεος.definition: of persons, Id.R.411c; Plb.27.15.6, etc; in full measure, complete, Ph.1.185; f.l. for in Orph.Fr.261

ἔμπληκτος.definition: stunned, amazed; in Att., impulsive: hence, unstable, capricious, S.Aj.1358, Arist.EE1240b17; E.Tr.1205; Pl.Grg.482a; Id.Ly.214d; Plu.Dio18

ἐμπληξία.definition: amazement: hence, stupidity; capriciousness of policy, Aeschin.2.164

ἐμποίνιμος.definition: liable to punishment, that may be violated with impunity, Trag.Adesp.525, cf. Corn.ND24. Adv. Eust.1243.3

ἔμπονος.definition: patient of labour, Hp.Aër.12; toilsome, painful, Aret.SA1.9; vehement outcry, LXX3 Ma.1.28

ἐμπόρφυρος.definition: inclining to purple, Dsc.3.100, Orib.Syn.2.56.17, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.251

Ἔμπουσα.definition: Empusa, a hobgoblin, assuming various shapes, said to be sent by Hecate, Ar.Ra.293, Ec.1056, D.18.130; sts. identified with Hecate, Ar.Fr.500

ἐμπρεπής.definition: conspicuous among or above others; conspicuous for, A.Supp.115 ; cf.sq

ἐμπρόθεσμος.definition: within or before the stated time, opp. Ph.2.170; Sor.1.33; Plu.2.502a; Luc.VH2.27. Adv. Ph.2.532, Sch.Ar.Eq.392, POxy.61.12

ἐμπροίκιος.definition: given by way of dower, App.Mith.75, BC1.10; Anon.Hist. in Rev.Ét.Gr. 5.321:—also Gloss

ἐμπρόσωπος.definition: before the face of, in the presence of, c. dat., Phalar.Ep.147

ἐμπύλιος.definition: at the gate, epith. of Artemis Hecate, Orph.A.902: Boeot. , epith. of Poseidon at Thebes, IG 7.2465

ἐμπυριβήτης.definition: made for standing on the fire, Il.23.702

ἐμπυρισχησίφως.definition: deriving light from the empyrean, PMag. Par.1.601

ἔμπυρος.definition: in, on or by the fire; exposed to fire or sun, burnt, scathed, E.Ph.1186; roasted, AP6.89 ; fiery hot, torrid, Str.16.1.10; Thphr.CP1.13.5; ib.4; feverish, Hp.Morb.2.40 ; LXXAm.4.2; inflammatory, of a bite, Arist.Mir.…

ἐμύς.definition: or fresh-water tortoise, esp. Emys lutaria, Arist.HA558a8, al.; also ib.600b22

ἔμφασις.definition: appearing in a smooth; outward appearance, impression, presentation, Arist.Div.Somn.464b12; Stoic. 2.24 ; Plb.5.63.2; give the appearance of. ., suggest, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.257; . . make as if . ., Plb.5.110.6; c. fut. …

ἐμφλοιοσπέρματος.definition: with the seed covered by an integument, Thphr.HP7.3.2

ἔμφρων.definition: gen. in one's mind or senses; to one mad, brings thee to thy senses, A.Pr.848; Id.Ch.1026; I come to myself, S.Aj.306; Pl.Lg.719c; . . ib.791b

ἔμφυλος.definition: and the latter being preferred; one's native land, S.OC1385

ἔμφυσις.definition: insertion of a muscle, Gal.UP1.21, Orib.25.31.6

ἔμψυξις.definition: cooling, refreshing, Aret.SA1.9, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.9.1, Gal.6.626

ἐναγγειόσπερμος.definition: having the seed in a capsule, Thphr.HP1.11.3,CP4.7.5

ἐναγωγή.definition: prosecution, suit, claim, Sammelb.5357.13 , Cod.Just. 3.10.2, etc

ἑνάενος.definition: of a year old, Thphr.HP8.11.5, Stud.Pal.1.62.33, al

ἐναέριος.definition: in the air, Ti.Locr.101c, Gal.Thras.40; Luc.Musc.Enc.6; opp. Them.Or.13.168b. cf. Porph.Gaur.10.6

ἐναετία.definition: period of nine years, PSI4.281.40 ; cf

ἔναθλος.definition: laborious, Ph.1.646; contest, in pl., dub. in IG7.2532

ἔνακμος.definition: = in full bloom or strength, Poll.2.10

ἐναλίγκιος.definition: also A.R.3.857:—like, resembling, c. dat., Il.5.5, al., Parm.8.43, Theoc.22.94, etc.: c. acc. rei, Od.1.371; Pi.I.8.41: neut. as Adv., Man.6.443.--Poet. word

ἐνάλιος.definition: and E.Andr.855 , Plu.Luc.39: Ep. and Lyr. also : :—in, on, of the sea, Od.4.443, 5.67, etc.; Archil.74.8; while the rest of the tackle is at work fishing deep in the sea, Pi.P.2.79. cf. Theoc.21.39; A.Pers.453; of Pos…

ἔναλλος.definition: changed, contrary, Theoc.1.134, AP5.298 . Adv. Plu.2.1045e

ἔναλος.definition: = h.Ap.180, CritiasFr.2.7 D.; E.Hel.1130 , Tim.Pers.109; E.El.1348 ; Arion 1.9; in later Prose, opp. S.E.M.7.414

ἔναμμα.definition: thing bound or tied on; garment, covering, a deerskin cloak, D.S.1.11

ἐναντίος.definition: opposite, = (which is rare in; of Place, on the opposite side, opposite, c.dat., Od.10.89; . . Il.9.190, cf. Od.23.89: hence, fronting, face to face, 6.329; Sapph.2.2; . . before him, E.Hipp.947; things open to one's …

ἐναντιότης.definition: contrariety, opposition; in the Philos. of Arist., contrariety, Int.21a29, EN1108b27; v. I.4

ἐνάπλωσις.definition: resolution into the elements, Simp.in Epict.p.43 D

ἐναρμογή.definition: fitting of a surgical tube, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.4

ἐναροκτάντας.definition: Dor. for spoiler and slayer, of death, A.Fr.151

ἔναρος.definition: subject to a curse, Rev.Ét.Gr.24.415 , Hsch

ἔναρχος.definition: in office, in authority; under authority, Stob.2.7.3a

ἑνάς.definition: = unit, Pl.Phlb.15a: pl., of an order of existences, Dam.Pr.40,99, al.; Procl.Inst.62, cf. 6

ἔναστρος.definition: among the stars, Achae.16; starry, Corp.Herm.3.2

ἐναταῖος.definition: on the ninth day, Hp.Aph.4.36, Th.2.49, PSI4.286 ; of recurring fevers, Hp.Epid.1.24

ἔνατος.definition: ninth, Il.2.313, Hes.Op.772, IG12.304.15, PGrenf.2.24.1 , etc.; Ep. Il.2.295, 8.266; Aeol. BCH37.166 ; , sacra novendialia, Is.8.39, Aeschin.3.225

ἔναυλος.definition: bed of a stream, . . Il.16.71; torrent, mountain-stream, 21.283, cf. 312

ἔναυρος.definition: exposed to the air, Thphr.HP8.11.6; epith. of Apollo, Hsch

ἔναυσμα.definition: metaph., spark, glimmer, Plb.9.28.8, Plu.Flam.11 ; Ph.2.437: pl., slight indications of a testator's wishes, Just.Nov.107 Pr

ἐναυχένιος.definition: in or on the neck, AP7.493

ἐνδάπιος.definition: native of the country, Mosch.2.11, Coluth.238, AP9.153 ; Bull.Inst.Egypt. 1912.91; Nonn.D.4.423: also in late Prose, Agath.2.15; cf

ἔνδεια.definition: want, lack, Th.4.18; abs., deficiency, defect, opp. Id.Prt.357b, Arist.EN1109a4: pl., opp. Isoc.2.33, cf. 8.90

ἔνδειγμα.definition: evidence, . . Pl.Criti.110b, cf. Iamb.Myst.1.11; token, D.19.256, cf. Dam.Pr.46

ἔνδειξις.definition: as law-term, laying of information against one who discharged public functions for which he was legally disqualified, writ of indictment in such a case, And.1.10, D.20.156 , Arist.Ath.52.1 , cf. Decr.ib.29.4, IG22.112…

ἑνδεκαταῖος.definition: on the eleventh day, Hp.Aph.4.36, Th.2.97; for nearly eleven days, Theoc.10.12

ἔνδεμα.definition: thing bound on, Gloss.: pl., amulets, Dsc.Eup.2.136

ἐνδέξιος.definition: Hom. only neut. pl. towards; after Hom. without any sense of motion, on the right, v.l. in E.Hipp.1360 ; on thy right, Id.Cyc.6; on the right as one enters, PPetr.3p.203; Inscr.Prien.19.46 : c. gen., ib.53.74

ἔνδηλος.definition: visible, manifest, clear; manifest, discovered, known, mostly of persons, Ar.Eq.1277, Th.6.36; Id.4.41: with a part., . . Id.2.64, cf. Pl.Phd.88e, Tht.174d, D.21.198; of things, Arist.de An.422b34

ἐνδιαεριαυερινήχετος.definition: floating in midday airy breezes, dithyrambic parody in Ar.Pax831

ἔνδιον.definition: place of sojourn in the open air, of a grotto, Opp.H.4.371; seat of joyousness, epith. of a winecask, AP11.63 ; ib.9.668 ; . . IG5.730.14 . --Poet. word

ἔνδιος.definition: at midday, at noon (but; in the daytime, Arat.498; AP7.703

ἐνδίφριος.definition: sitting on the same seat, X.An.7.2.33, cf. 38

ἐνδομάχας.definition: fighting or bold at home, epith. of a dunghill-cock, Pi.O.12.14

ἐνδόρωμα.definition: perh. ornament in plaster of a sarcophagus, 1884/5 p.24 No.241; cf

ἐνδόσιμος.definition: serving as a prelude, Artem.2.66; yielding, ib.442c, cf. Max.Tyr.1.2, Hld.9.4; of arguments, easily refuted, Hyp.Fr.241; D.H.Rh.8.15

ἔνδοσις.definition: striking of the key-note; imparting, Thphr.CP1.15.3; Simp.in Ph.440.8; Dam.Pr.100

Ἐνδρομώ.definition: epith. of Demeter at Halicarnassus, Hsch

ἔνδροσος.definition: bedewed, dewy, A.Ag.12, cf. Str.6.1.9, Dion. Byz.29, Alciphr.Fr.6.6: Ph.2.292, cf. Dsc.5.53; Jul.Or.7.236a

ἔνδρυον.definition: oaken peg or pin by which the yoke; heart-wood of trees, Hsch

ἔνδυμα.definition: garment, IG12.593 A4 , Men.Pk.269, LXX4 Ki.10.22,al., BCH6.25 , PFay.12.20 , Str.3.3.7, Ev.Matt.7.15, Plu.Sol.8, Porph.Abst.1.31, etc.; covering, Gal.19.367, prob. in Hp.Cord.8

ἔνδυσις.definition: entry, coined by Pl.Cra.419c; putting on, 1 Ep.Pet.3.3; dressing, dress, LXXEs.5.1, Aristeas96, Agatharch.57

ἐνδώμησις.definition: enclosing with a wall, SIG996.30 , cf. BCH28.78 , J.AJ15.9.6 , Apoc.21.18

ἐνειμένος.definition: pf. part. Pass. of , clad, c. acc., Agath.2.8; Id.4.1

ἐνεκέχειρον.definition: = travelling allowance for Inscr.Magn.38 : pl., ib.40 , 41 :—also ib.35 , 42

ἔνεμα.definition: injection, clyster, Dsc.2.118 , Gal.13.295, Orib.Fr.60, etc

ἐνεότης.definition: dumbness, Arist.Pr.895a16; stupidity, dub. in Cratin.188

ἔνερσις.definition: fitting in, fastening, used by old men at Athens to fasten up their hair, Th.1.6

ἐνέρτερος.definition: Comp. of lower, of the nether; simply, lower, Nonn.D.44.164.—After Hom. usu. in form

ἐνεσία.definition: suggestion, used only in Ep. form dat. pl., with gen. pers., once in Hom., at her suggestion, Il.5.894; Hes.Th.494, h.Cer.30, Call.Dian.108; A.R.1.7, prob. in Q.S.3.475: gen. pl., A.R.3.1364

ἐνέστιος.definition: offered at the public hearth, Inscr.Magn.36.20 :—also ib.72.40 :—Subst. , ib.42.12 :—Arc. ib.38.41

ἔνζῳος.definition: full of beasts, dub. in Nic.Fr.31.2

ἐνήλατον.definition: anything driven in: as Subst; the four rails, which make the frame of a bedstead, S.Fr.315, cf. Ph.1.666 : later in sg., bedstead, Sor.2.61; PSI6.616.17

ἐνῆλιξ.definition: of age, in the prime of manhood, OGI338.21 , LXX4 Ma.18.9, POxy.646 , etc

ἐνηλύσιος.definition: struck by lightning: places set apart from worldly uses, because a thunderblot has fallen there, A.Fr.17, cf. EM341.5, Hsch

ἐνηρόσιον.definition: rent for corn-land; right of tillage, SIG1044.18

ἔνθεμα.definition: thing put in, graft, Thphr.CP1.6.8; deposit, of money in a bank, CIG3599.15

ἐνθέμιον.definition: cabin on the poop of a ship, Poll.1.90; socket of a lampstand, LXXEx.38.16

ἔνθεος.definition: in later Prose contr. Ph.2.542; of divine frenzy, inspired by the god, A.Ag.1209; Pl.Phdr.244b; Id.Ti.72b; Arist.Rh.1408b19; Plu.2.752c; frenzied rites, prob.in Herod.8.70. Adv. Men.Mon.229, App.Hisp.26, Jul.Or.7.215b…

ἔνθερμος.definition: hot, Hp.Epid.6.4.13; metaph., passionate, prob. in Com.Adesp.24.10D.; hot, fervid, Arist.Phgn.806b26, cf. Ph.1.605, al

ἔνθεσις.definition: putting in, insertion; that which is put in the mouth, mouthful, Ar.Eq.404 , Pherecr.108.6, Telecl.1.10, Hermipp.41, etc

ἔνθεσμος.definition: lawful, LXX3 Ma.2.21, cf. Plu.Nic.6; Peripl.M.Rubr.23; authorized, BGU1127.30 ; valid, POxy.271.21 . Adv. Gal.14.216

ἐνθήκη.definition: store, Ph.2.525 , Sm.Ge.41.36; capital; late word for Phryn.199,Arg.D.36

ἔνθηρος.definition: full of wild beasts, haunted; metaph., wild, rough, A.Ag.562; 'angry', of the ulcerated foot of Philoctetes, S.Ph.698 ; savagery, Ael.NA6.63

ἔνθινος.definition: Cret., = , GDI5039.11 , cf. 5041.7 ; cf; = prob. in GDI3087.33

ἔνθορος.definition: impregnated, of animals, v.l. in Nic.Th.99

ἑνιαῖος.definition: single, unitary, Aristid.Quint.1.3; Iamb.Myst.8.3; Procl.in Prm.p.564S., etc.: pl., individual elements, Iamb.in Nic.p.81P.; concerned with unity, Dam.Pr.25bis. Adv. Ptol.Tetr.1, Iamb.Comm. Math.10, Procl.in Prm.p.589…

ἐνιαυθμός.definition: abode, EM342.35, prob. in Call.Fr.127 . metri gr.]

ἑνίγυιος.definition: joined in one body, Ibyc.16.3; lame of one foot, Suid

ἔνικμος.definition: with wet in it, humid, Arist.HA570a17, Thphr.CP1.2.1; Ph.1.8; Gp.10.75.2, cf. Dsc.2.101; Porph.Antr.5; of young pigs, Ar.Byz. ap. Ath.9.375a; of perspiring patients, Orib.Fr.116

ἐνιπή.definition: poet. Noun, rebuke; later, of any violent attack, as of the sun's rays or thirst, Opp.C.1.133,299

ἐνναετήρ.definition: inmate, inhabitant, AP9.495 , v.l. in Mosch.2.123:—fem. APl.4.94

ἔνναιον.definition: f.l. for , Clinias ap.Sch.A.R.2.1085, cf. Suid., Zonar

ἐννεάς.definition: body of nine, Theoc.17.84; the number nine, Plu.2.726d,744a, Nicom.Ar.1.19, etc

ἐννεετηρίς.definition: nine-year period, Pl.Min.319e, IG2.985 A2, Delph. 3.48.8; written in Vett.Val.337.17; Plu.2.293b; Thphr.HP4.11.2: v

ἔννευμα.definition: signal, wave of the hand, LXXPr.6.13

ἔννοια.definition: act of thinking, reflection; notion, conception, Id.Ti.47a; . . Id.Phlb.59d; to form an idea, opp. Id.Phd.73c; Arist.EN1179b15; Id.Metaph.1073b12; opp. Id.MA701b17; Epicur.Ep.1p.23U. ; Epicur.Sent.24; Plb.1.57.4; ib.4…

ἐννόμιος.definition: of or for pasturage, IG2.1059.13 , cf. OGI55.14 ; dues paid for pasturage, IG2.584c7, 7.3171.49 , Inscr.Délos353A 34 , PSI4.368.4 , OGI1629.173 , etc

ἔννομος.definition: ordained by law, lawful, legal, Pi.O.7.84; of persons, keeping within the law, upright, just, A.Supp.404 , Pl.R.424e; also, subject to the law, 1 Ep.Cor.9.21

Ἐννοσίγαιος.definition: Ep. for Earth-shaker, as a name of Poseidon, Il.13.43,al., Mosch.2.149, Nonn.D.36.126, etc.: Luc.JTr.9

ἔνογκος.definition: swollen, Steph.in Hp.1.206D; possessing bulk, corporeal, Porph.Sent.27; Iamb.Comm. Math.8

ἐνόδιος.definition: Subst. nets for stopping the pathways, X.Cyn.6.9; blisters caused by walking, Thphr.Sud.15

ἔνοικος.definition: inhabitant, A.Supp.611, etc; Pass., dwelt in, E.Ion235

ἔνολμος.definition: sitting on the tripod, epith. of Apollo, S.Fr.1044

ἐνοπή.definition: crying, shouting, as of birds; of things, sound, Il.10.13; of thunder, Hes.Th.708; E.Ion882 ; crushing, Pi.Fr.168.—Ep. and Lyr. word, used by E. in lyr

ἐνόρειος.definition: in the mountains, prob. for Scymn.832

ἐνόριος.definition: within the boundaries, Poll.9.8; on the boundaries, Hld.10.1: Subst. territory of a city, POxy. 1101.5 , cf. Cod.Just.1.2.25.1, etc

ἔνος.definition: year, Lyd.Mens.4.1, Hsch; found only in oblique cases of fem., gen. Ep. dat. acc. in the sense of the day after tomorrow: Hes.Op.410 ; gen. Ar.Ec.796, Dor. Theoc.18.14; Ar.Ach.172; Antipho6.21; prob. l. in D.C.47.41; …

ἔνοσις.definition: shaking, quake, Hes.Th.681,849; personified in poet. form prob. in E.Ba.585

Ἐνοσίχθων.definition: Earth-shaker, epith. of Poseidon; later, as Adj., earth-stirring, Euph.152; Nonn.D.2.67

ἑνότης.definition: union, Epicur.Ep.1p.13U.; Ep.Eph.4.3,13; Plu.2.769f; in concrete sense, Epicur.Nat.Herc.1634.1; Demetr.Lac.1055.7 F., cf. Phld.Piet.80

ἐνουράνιος.definition: in heaven, heavenly, AP9.223 , Poll.1.23; Sammelb.5620.9

ἐνοχή.definition: liability, obligation, PIand.48.11 , etc.; conduct and responsibility of a transaction, POxy.133.7

ἔνοχος.definition: = held in, bound by; c. gen., connected with, Hp.Ep.23

ἔνρυθμος.definition: of rhythm, Pl.Lg.654a; possessing rhythm , D.H.Comp.11; Ephor.6 J.; opp. S.E.M.11.186. Adv. Ath.5.179f, 14.631b

ἔνσαρκος.definition: of flesh, flesh meat, Porph.Abst.1.1, cf. Gaur.3.2

ἔνσημος.definition: significant, important, Hp.Superf.17: f.l; coined, Tz.H.1.928

ἔνσιμος.definition: somewhat snub nosed, PPetr.3p.21 (iii B; concave, of surfaces, Ruf.Anat.40,52

ἐνσινής.definition: injured, Man.2.445; in ill- health, BGU560.22

ἐνσκέπαρνος.definition: oblique, of bandages, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.64.2

ἐνσόριον.definition: place for a sarcophagus, IGRom.4.1452 , AJA18.68 , etc

ἔνσοφος.definition: wise in a thing, Man.4.549: abs., IG14.1020

ἔνσπονδος.definition: included in a truce or treaty; of animals, gently disposed, Ael.NA1.3; ib.57

ἔνστημα.definition: objection, Epicur.Ep.2p.39U; check, obstacle, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.268, M.Ant.8.41, S.E.M.7.253,al

ἐνσύζυγος.definition: in choric lyrics, assigned to Sch.Ar.Ra.357

ἔνταξις.definition: putting in, insertion; placing of light-armed soldiers alternately with hoplites in the phalanx, Ael.Tact.31.3, Arr.Tact.26.6, Suid

ἔντασις.definition: tension, straining, Id.Aër.4; Id.Fract.30; fixed stare, prob. in Aret.CD1.3 ; distension, Gal.7.728

ἐντάφιος.definition: of, belonging to or used in burial; shroud, winding-sheet, AP11.125; . . Simon.4.4; Isoc.6.45; Plb.15.10.3; AP9.294

ἐντενής.definition: on the stretch, intent: only neut. as Adv., A.R.2.933

ἐντερόμφαλον.definition: umbilical hernia, Gal.14.786; patient suffering therefrom, Id.19.444

ἔντερον.definition: piece of the guts or intestines; earth-worms, Arist.IA705b28, 709a28, Arat.959, Numen. ap. Ath.7.305a; but worm-casts, Arist.HA570a16, Thphr.Sign.42, Nic.Th.388

ἐντερόνεια.definition: = Hsch., Suid.; timber for the ribs of a ship, belly- timber, Ar.Eq.1185 , v. Sch

ἐντευξίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq. 4, little petition, Arr.Epict.1.10.10

ἔντευξις.definition: lighting upon, meeting; converse, intercourse, Arist.Rh.1355a29: c. gen., Vit.Philonid.p.7C.; hold converse with . ., Isoc.1.20; Arist.Top.101a27, cf. Metaph.1009a17, etc.; Sor.2.8

ἔντιλτος πλακοῦς.definition: prob. a cake seasoned with , Clearch.65

ἐντοίχιος.definition: on the walls, D.H.16.3; prob. cj. in X.An.7.8.1; Ruf. ap. Orib.49.32.5

ἔντοκος.definition: with young, Lyc.185, PTeb.53.20 (ii B; bearing interest, PStrassb.92.8 , etc

ἐντόσθιος.definition: intestinal, Lyd.Ost.32: but; Subst. inwards, entrails, Arist.PA685a3, Ti.Locr.100b: —also LXXEx.12.9, al., Hsch., EM345.21

ἐντράπελος.definition: shameful, dub. l. in Pi.P.4.105, Thgn.400 cod.A

ἔντριτος.definition: of three strands, threefold; = Lat. sequester, Gloss

ἔντριψις.definition: rubbing in, of cosmetics; cosmetic, Ael.VH12.1

ἔντρομος.definition: trembling, Plu.Fab.3, AP5.203 ; LXXPs.17.8, Act.Ap.7.32, Sor.1.89, PMag.Par.1.3076

ἔντροφος.definition: living in or acquainted with; as Subst., nursling of . ., E.IA289 , cf. Arist.Fr.675, AP9.242 . —Poet. word

Ἐνυαλία.definition: name of a tribe at Mantinea , IG5.271

Ἐνυάλιος.definition: the Warlike, in Il. as epith. of the; battle, E.Ph.1572 ; the battle-cry, Hld.4.17; also Jul.Or.1.36b

ἔνυγρος.definition: in the water, aquatic, of animals; wet, damp, Arist.Mete.351a19; Id.HA569b21

ἔνυδρος.definition: with water in it, holding water; of water, watery, E.Ph.659 , Ion872

Ἐνύειον.definition: the temple of Bellona at Rome, D.C.42.26, 50.4

ἔνυλος.definition: involved or implicated in matter; wooded, f.l. for in Ar.Did.Epit.11

ἐνυμενόσπερμος.definition: with seeds enclosed in a membrane, i.e. husk, Thphr.HP8.3.4

ἐνύποπτος.definition: suspicious, Sor.1.79; Act., suspecting: Adv. Ps.-Callisth.1.9

Ἐνυώ.definition: Enyo, goddess of war, Il.5.333; = Lat. Bellona, Plu.Sull.9

ἔνωμος.definition: rather raw, Archestr.Fr.57.5 ; Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.51f; of bread, under- baked, Hp.VM14; not too much cooked, Id.Mul.2.211 ; of fruit, rather crude, unripe, Dsc.1.115, cf. Gp.8.20 , Ruf. ap. Orib.45.11.2; of swelling…

ἔνωρος.definition: early, in Adv. Comp. Epist. Hadrian. in Gloss. iii p.37, Gem.12.5, 13.9: irreg. Comp. earlier: Adv. Phylarch.44J

ἕνωσις.definition: combination into one, union; compression, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.20

ἐνώτιον.definition: ear-ring, A.Fr.102, Testamentum Platonis ap. D.L.3.42, Aen.Tact.31.7, IG11.161B26 , Hedyl. ap.Ath.8.345b, etc.; cf

ἐνωτοκοίτης.definition: with ears large enough to sleep in, Str.2.119, 15.1.57

ἐξάγιστος.definition: devoted to evil; in S.OC1526 what things are matters of religion: cf. Hsch

ἐξαγώνιος.definition: beside the mark, irrelevant; excluded from competition, Ph.2.60; = Hsch

ἑξάγωνος.definition: hexagonal, Arist.Cael.306b7; Astrol., in sextile aspect, Vett. Val.20.2

ἑξάδαρχος.definition: leader of a body of six, X.Cyr.3.3.11

ἔξαθλος.definition: past athletic exercise, Luc.Lex.11; disqualified, in an athletic competition, Sch.Od.21.76

ἔξαιτος.definition: picked, choice, excellent, Il.12.320; Od.2.307; 5.102: in later Poets like A.R.4.1004, AP6.332.5 , Man.2.226, 3.354, Mus.Belg.16.71

ἑξάκλινος.definition: with six couches, also EM346.14:—as Subst. couch to hold six, Mart.9.59.9

ἑξακονταμοιρία.definition: arc of sixty degrees, Heph.Astr.2.11 cod

ἔξαλλος.definition: special, distinguishing, Plb.6.7.7, cf. LXX2 Ki.6.14; OGI737.19 ; Ph.1.468; Plu.2.330a. Adv. strangely, of superstitious veneration, Plb.32.15.7

ἔξαλμα.definition: distance, interval, A.D.Adv.209.2 , cf. Sch.D.P.30 ; of the sun or moon, Paul.Al.S.1, cf. Barbill.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.104

ἔξαλος.definition: out of the sea, leaping out of the sea, Emp.117; Luc.Am.8; Opp.H.2.593; a blow on a ship's hull above water, Plb.16.3.8; Luc.JTr.47; rising high out of the water, of islands, Str.17.1.52

ἔξαλσις.definition: leaping with the legs held together; dislocation, displacement, Hp.Art.46

ἑξαμάρτυρος.definition: attested by six witnesses, UPZ124.11; BGU813.10 ; PHaw.303.20 , BGU260.7 : neut. as Subst., BGU1239.20

ἑξάμετρος.definition: of six metres, in hexameter measure, Hdt.1.47; Id.7.220, cf. Pl.Lg.810d; Arist.Rh.1404a34, Po.1449a27, Demetr.Eloc.1, etc

ἑξαμηνόβιος.definition: living six months, v.l. in Arist.HA558a17

ἑξάμηνος.definition: of, lasting six months; Subst. , half-year, X.HG[2.3.9]; a half-year's supply, ib.3.4.3; Arist.HA573a13; Thphr.HP8.2.7 also Hdt.4.25

ἑξάμιτος.definition: of six strands, prob. in AP7.702

ἑξαπέλεκυς.definition: with six axes, = Lat. sexfascalis, of the praetor, Plb.3.40.9; or simply a praetor, Id.2.24.6, 3.40.11; ib.106.6, D.S.31.42: pl., App.Syr.15

Ἑξάπολις.definition: league of six cities, of the Asiatic Dorians, Hdt.1.144, Sch.Ar.Pl.385

ἑξάπτυχος.definition: with six folds, Sch.Il.12.295, Hsch. s.v

ἑξάπωλος.definition: with six colts or horses, Hdn.5.6.7

ἔξαρμα.definition: rising, swelling; meridian height or elevation of the heavenly bodies, Str.2.1.18, cf. 1.1.21; Hipparch.1.3.6, Gem.6.24, Plu.Mar.11, Ptol.Alm.2.3,6, Tetr.76; opp. Theol.Ar.25; Plu.2.410f

ἐξαρμόνιος.definition: out of harmony, discordant, Pherecr.145.9, cf. ib.26

ἔξαρμος.definition: with dislocated limbs, v.l. in Lyd.Mag.3.57

ἔξαρσις.definition: setting out, ib.Nu.10.6; rising, height of water in a vessel, Cleom.1.1

ἑξᾶς.definition: a coin, Lat. sextans, as adopted by the Sicil. Greeks, Arist.Fr.510, cf. Hsch.; cf

ἑξάς.definition: the number six, Ph.1.3, Luc.Sat.4, Plu.Lyc.5, etc.: pl., Ph.2.239,418

ἑξάσημος.definition: of six times, Heph.14.1; Aristid. Quint.1.14

ἑξασκελής.definition: six-tailed, of a bandage, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.22 tit., Gal.18.774, Paul.Aeg.6.60

ἑξάστερον.definition: the six stars, i.e. the Pleiades, Sch.Hes.Op.383, Eust.870.26

ἔξαστις.definition: selvage of linen or cloth, Hp.Off.11; fringe, Michel 832.15

ἑξάτονος.definition: in or of six tones, Plu.2.1028e, Aristid.Quint.1.9, Alex.Eph. ap. Theo Sm.p.141 H

ἔξαυλος.definition: piped away, worn out, of a flute, Poll.4.73

ἑξάφορον.definition: at Rome, litter borne by six men; bearers of such a litter, Vitr.10.3.7

ἔξαψις.definition: fastening, Theo Sm.p.72 H; heating, Hp.Acut.46

ἑξάωρος.definition: of six equinoctial hours, Theol.Ar.52; period of six such hours, Balbill. in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.243

ἐξέλκωσις.definition: causing of sores in or on, D.S.3.29

ἐξεπερώτησις.definition: formal question put to a contracting party, PMasp.243.22

ἐξεσία.definition: sending forth, mission, embassy, Hom. only in phrase, Il.24.235, cf. Od.21.20: acc. pl. in Hsch

ἐξέφηβος.definition: one who is beyond the age of an a youth of seventeen, Censor in.Nat.14.8

ἐξεχής.definition: gradual: neut. as Adv., dub. l. in Aret.CD1.8

ἑξηκοντάς.definition: the number sixty, Vett.Val.300.17; sixtieth part, Str.2.5.7

ἐξήλυσις.definition: way out, outlet, Hdt.5.101; of a river, Id.3.117; Id.7.130

ἑξήμερος.definition: space of six days, Vett.Val.369.24, Procl.Hyp.3.56

ἑξήρετμος.definition: of six banks of oars, i.e. in command of a Epigr.Gr.337

ἕξις.definition: having, being in possession of, possession, opp. Pl.Tht.197b; Id.Cra.414b; Id.Lg.625c, cf. R.433e, Sph.247a, al., Arist.Metaph.1022b4; opp. ib.1055b13, S.E.P.3.49

ἐξίτηλος.definition: going out: hence, losing; metaph., food that has lost its properties during assimilation, Hp.Alim.4; so of seed sown in alien soil, Pl.R.497b; of a drug or wine that has lost its power, Phylarch.10J., Dsc.5.6; of a fa…

ἐξιτήριος.definition: of or for departure, IG3.1184.21 : day of leaving office, at Athens, Hsch

ἑξίτης.definition: the throw of six on the dice, = Epigr.Gr.1038.2 , Poll.9.100

ἐξίωσις.definition: reduction to metallic state, Syn. Alch.p.66 B., cf. Maria ap.Zos.Alch.p.148 B

ἔξοδος.definition: going out, opp. S.Aj.798, 806; procession, Hdt.3.14; esp. of women of rank with their suite, Pl.Lg.784d, cf. Thphr.Char.22.10; D.48.55, cf. Lex Solonis ap.Plu.Sol.21

ἐξολκή.definition: extraction, Sor.1.69, Antyll. ap.Orib.45.18.21, Paul. Aeg.3.72

ἐξόμφαλος.definition: with prominent navel, as in umbilical; as Subst., prominent navel, Dsc.4.69, Gal.19.444, Paul.Aeg.6.51

ἐξόστωσις.definition: diseased excrescence on the bone, node, esp. on the temples, Gal.7.728, 10.1013

ἐξούλης δίκη.definition: action of ejectment, brought; action of ejectment brought by one who claims property in consequence of a judgement of court and is excluded from it by the former defendant or his agent, against a defendant who has sei…

ἑξποδιαῖος.definition: six feet high or broad, CIG2860i9

ἐξωκέλης.definition: barebacked horse, Suid; piratical craft, Id

ἐξώκοιτος.definition: sleeping out, Hsch.:—as Subst., a fish which comes upon the beach to sleep, = Clearch.73, Thphr.Fr.171.1, Ael.NA9.36, Opp.H.1.158

ἐξώμαλλος.definition: with the nap outside, Sch.D.Chr.72.1 p.789 Emp

ἐξωμοσία.definition: denial on oath that one knows anything of; declining an office, D.19.129

ἐξώπιος.definition: out of sight of, hence, out of, freq. in E., Supp.1038; Med.624, Alc.546; used in parody by Ar.Th.881

ἔξωρος.definition: untimely, out of season, unfitting; too late, too old, superannuated, Aeschin.1.95, Plu.Sull.36, Luc.Herm.78, al. : c. gen., too old for . ., Luc.Merc.Cond.7. Adv. Philostr.VS1.21.8

ἑξώροφος.definition: with or of six stories, D.S.14.51

ἐπάγαθος.definition: = used in CIG4991, 5020 ; also of the Nile, Sammelb. 991.4

ἐπάγχιστος.definition: next of kin, IG9.334.17; neut. pl.as Adv., GDI4986

ἔπαθλον.definition: prize of a contest, mostly in pl., E.Ph.52, etc.; Plu.Flam.15; rewards, D.S.28.4, cf. OGI455.3 , Hdn.1.17.11; not even if the advantages were obvious, Archig. ap.Orib.8.23.2: also in sg., Inscr.Prien.113.31 ; D.S.4.64…

ἐπάϊστος.definition: heard of, detected, usu. c. part., Hdt.2.119; Id.8.128, cf. 6.74; Id.3.15, cf. 7.146; perceived, Ant.Lib.34.4. Adv. Onat. ap. Stob.1.1.39

ἐπαίτιος.definition: blamed for a thing, blameable; of persons, Il.1.335; for a thing, A.Eu.465, E.Hipp.1383 ; accused of a thing, Th.6.61; Plu.Comp.Dion.Brut.2

ἔπαιτον.definition: dub. sens. in PFay.81.13 , BGU792.12, etc

ἔπακμος.definition: in the bloom of age, D.H.4.28; pointed, Dsc.1.90; Plu.2.966c; sharp- edged, Sor.1.80; Gal. ap. Orib.inc.12.1

ἐπακταῖος.definition: = Opp.H.2.127,4.273; epith. of Poseidon at Samos, Hsch

ἐπάκτιος.definition: E.Fr.670.2, and S.Tr.1151,Fr.549, E.Andr.853 : :—on the strand or shore, ll.cc., S.Aj.413 ; epith. of Apollo, A.R.1.403 codd.; of Hermes at Sicyon, Hsch

ἐπαλής.definition: open to the sun, sunny, Hes.Op.493

ἐπαλλόκαυλος.definition: clinging to another plant, quasi- parasitic, prob. cj. in Thphr.HP3.18.9,11

ἔπαλπνος.definition: cheerful, happy, Pi.P.8.84 codd.; expld. by Sch

ἐπαλωστής.definition: one who threshes with oxen, X.Oec.18.5

ἐπάμερος.definition: Dor. and Aeol. for Pi.P.8.95, Theoc.30.31: neut. as Adv., = IG4.800

ἑπάμων.definition: = attendant, restored in Clitarch. Gloss. ap. Ath.6.267c, cf. Hsch

ἐπαρά.definition: Ion. solemn curse, imprecation, Il.9.456, cf. ThebaisFr.2.7; SIG38.30 ; ib.167.28 . in Hom.]

ἐπάρατος.definition: accursed, laid under a curse, Th.8.97; which it was accursed to inhabit, Id.2.17; Pl.Lg.877a; of persons, Arist.Fr.148, Ev.Jo.7.49, J.AJ6.6.3: Sup., Ph.1.516; used in imprecations on those who violated graves, CIG2824…

ἐπάργεμος.definition: having a film over the eye; metaph., dim, obscure, A.Pr.499, Ag.1113, Ch.665

ἔπαρμα.definition: something raised, a; metaph., elation, vanity, Sotad.9.4

ἐπασσύτερος.definition: Ep.Adj. one upon another, one; frequent, repeated, Nic.Th.246: with sg. word, perh. following breeze or ever- freshening, A.R.1.579; and so ever-growing penury, Id.2.472

ἐπασσυτεροτριβής.definition: following close one upon another, A.Ch.426

ἐπαυχένιος.definition: on or for the neck, Pi.P.2.93; AP6.34

Ἔπαφος.definition: a son of Zeus and Io, A.Pr.851 ; the Hellenic representative of the Egyptian god Apis, Hdt.2.153, 3.27,28

ἐπείκοστον.definition: a sum greater by 1/20 than another, PPetr.2p.156 :—also PRev.Laws56.15

ἐπέραστος.definition: lovely, lovable, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.18, D.S.4.7, Ph.1.671, Vett.Val.18.29, Luc.Tim.17, Im.10; Porph.Antr.12; Heph.Astr.1.1

ἔπεργος.definition: assistant, Sammelb.5680.3; work done in addition to payment of rent, IG12.62.15

ἐπέτειος.definition: Dor. gen. pl. A.Ag.1015; lasting for a year, Arist.Long.466a2; ib.464b25, cf. Thphr.HP1.1.2; having force for a year, D.23.92; Plb.6.46.4

ἑπέτης.definition: Dor. follower, attendant, Pi.P.5.4: fem. A.R.3.666

ἐπετήσιος.definition: = from year to year, yearly, Od.7.118, cf. PSI4.320.12 ; Th.2.80; Jul.Or.4.131d; lasting the whole year, Call.Ap.78; for a year, Epigr.Gr.815

ἐπετίνη.definition: name of a plant, dub. in Thphr.HP7.8.1

ἐπεχές.definition: Adv., = following, next, IG 4.841.30,32 : Delph. GDI2642.47

ἐπήκοος.definition: Dor. listening, giving ear; obedient, J.BJ3.8.5

ἐπῆλυξ.definition: overshadowing, take the rock as a screen, E.Cyc.680

ἐπήορος.definition: uplifted, A.R.2.1065, cf. Nonn.D.37.47: c. dat., lifted upon, A.R.3.856, cf. Nonn.D.10.205

ἐπήρατος.definition: lovely, delightsome, Il.9.228; Od.8.366; freq. of places, 4.606; Hes.Fr.76.4; also Id.Op.63; Id.Th.67; Sapph.Supp.20c.4; Alc. Supp.23.13; later of persons, A.Eu.958 ; A.R.3.1099

ἐπήρεια.definition: insulting treatment, abuse, D.18.12, cf. Is.4.5, etc.; D.21.25; order haughtily or by way of insult, Th.1.26; is done to insult him, Amips.9; BGU180.8 ; Philem.92.2; D.18.13; Arist.Pol.1287a38; ib.195.20 ; OGI262.24 :…

ἐπηρεφής.definition: overhanging, beetling; Pass., covered, sheltered, Hes.Th.598; of a dragon, A.R.4.144; Id.2.736; Simm.1.8; Nic.Fr.74.24, cf. Hld.8.14

ἐπήριστος.definition: or contended for, coined by Eust.725.16, 1962.7, to expl

ἐπητής.definition: courteous, gentle, opp. rude and barbarous, Od.13.332; 18.128: pl. as fem., A.R.2.987 ; cf

ἐπήτριμος.definition: prop. woven to, closely woven: hence, generally, close, thronged, torch upon torch, Il.18.211; . . ib.552; . . too many one after another, 19.226, cf. A.R.1.30, etc.: later in sg., Q.S.14.248; Opp.C.3.382: neut. pl. a…

ἐπιβάθρα.definition: ladder or steps to ascend by: scaling; metaph., means of approach, stepping-stone, Plb.3.24.14 ; Id.16.29.2; J.AJ11.8.2; towards . . , Plu.Demetr.8; Arr.Epict.1.7.22, cf. Plot.1.6.1; Gal.9.149

ἐπίβαθρον.definition: fare of an passenger's fare; of a sacrifice, regarded as a fare paid on embarking, A.R.1.421

ἐπιβάλλον.definition: a kind of ephemeron , Sch.[Arr.]Peripl.M. Eux.60 , Sch.Antig. Mir.85

ἐπίβδα.definition: the day after a festival, Sch.Pi.P.4.249; new-year's day, Aristid.Or.51 .26

Ἐπιβήμιος.definition: epith. of Zeus at Siphnos, Hsch

ἐπιβλαβής.definition: hurtful, Aret.CD1.2; Hierocl.in CA13p.448M.; Procl.Par.Ptol.166. Adv. Poll.5.135

ἐπιβόθριος.definition: in or at the trench, Aristid.Or.48.27

ἐπίβοιον.definition: = sacrifice of a sheep to Pandrosos after an ox offered to Athena, Philoch.32, Lycurg.Fr.35

ἐπιβουκόλος.definition: = Od.3.422, al., usu. in pleon. phrase, without 22.292

ἐπίγαιος.definition: upon the earth, the parts on or near the ground, Hdt.2.125; cf

ἐπιγάστριος.definition: over the belly: the covering of the abdominal cavity from thorax to pubes, Ruf.Onom.97, Sor.2.55, Gal.17.534, Aret.SA2.10, Plu.2.559f, PSI3.252.37 : esp. of the part above the navel, Poll.2.170, Ps.-Gal.14.705

ἐπίγειος.definition: on or of the earth, terrestrial; creeping, of plants, Thphr.HP3.18.6,6.2.2, al.; but land-plants, opp. water-plants, Arist.PA681a21; living on the ground, Id.HA633b1, PA657b24

ἐπιγειόφυλλος.definition: with radical leaves flat on the ground, rosulate, Thphr.HP7.8.3,9.10.1

ἐπιγναφεῖον.definition: and angle-stone of a so called from its resemblance to a carding comb, SIG245 G21,22

ἐπίγναφος.definition: cleaned, of clothes, Poll.7.77; cf. II

ἐπιγονατίς.definition: knee-pan, Ruf. ap. Orib.25.1.50; garment reaching to the knee, Paus.Gr.Fr.144

ἐπιγόνειον.definition: Egyptian harp, with forty strings arranged in pairs as in the named from the inventor Epigonus, Juba ap. Ath.4.183c, Poll.4.59

ἐπιγονή.definition: increase, growth, become; offspring, breed, D.S.4.15; of men, LXX2 Ch.31.16

ἐπίγονος.definition: born besides, of superfetation; as Subst., offspring, posterity, A.Th.903 ; breed, of bees, prob. in X.Oec.7.34

ἐπίγρυπος.definition: somewhat hooked, of the beak of the ibis, Hdt.2.76; of the muzzle of the Arist.HA499a7; of horses and men, somewhat hook- nosed, Pl.Phdr.253d, Euthphr.2b, PPetr.3p.7, al. , etc

ἐπιγύαλος.definition: hollow on the surface, dub.l.in S.OC1492

ἐπίγυιον.definition: or stern-cable, Ar.Fr.80, cf. 426: written in Aristid.Or.23.17, Zonar., in IG22.1611.255-8 , Plb.3.46.3, Harp.s.v. : scanned ⏑⏑⏑⏑ in Ar

ἐπιγώνιος.definition: at the angle, Nicom.Ar.1.19; corner-stones or -columns, Aq.Ps.143.12

ἐπίδαιτρον.definition: additional dish, dainty, Philem. ap. Ath.14.646c; = Hsch

ἐπιδεής.definition: poet. , in need of, Pl.Ti.33c, v.l. in X.Cyr.8.7.12, etc.: pl., v.l. in Hdt.4.130: Comp. inferior to . . , Pl.Plt.311b: Sup. most in need, Id.R.579e. Adv. inadequately, Id.Lg.899d

ἐπίδειγμα.definition: pattern, example, X.Smp.6.6; display, X.Cyr.8.2.15; show-pieces, gauds, Demetr.Eloc.108

ἐπιδείελος.definition: at even, about evening: neut. pl. as Adv., Hes.Op.810,821

ἐπίδειξις.definition: Ion. showing forth, making; exhibition, display, demonstration, Th.6.31; of a military demonstration, Id.3.16; showing off, Pl.Grg.447c: generally, . . exhibit how . . , Id.Phd.99d; come to display oneself to one, Ar.…

ἐπιδέμνιος.definition: on the bed or bed-clothes, E.Hec.927

ἐπιδευής.definition: poet. for in need or want of; lacking, failing, that thou may'st have no point of right wanting, Il.19.180: c. gen., failing in strength, Od.21.185; A.R.2.315: as Comp., inferior to Ulysses in strength, Od.21.253, cf.…

ἐπίδημος.definition: Dor. = Antiph.11; sojourning in a place, Call.Dian.226; of Artemis, Id.Aet.3.1.26; GDI5040 , cf. Milet.3.149

ἐπιδορατίς.definition: tip, point of a lance, spear-; spear-shaft, gloss on Sch.Pi.Dith.Oxy.3.13

ἐπιδοχή.definition: reception in addition, Th.6.17; undertaking, POxy.102.18, 103.16

ἐπίδροσος.definition: catching the dew, prob. cj. in Thphr.HP7.14.1

ἐπιδώτης.definition: the Bountiful, epith. of gods, esp. Zeus at Mantinea, Paus.8.9.2, cf. Plu.2.1102e:—hence temple at Epidaurus, IG4.1492.24

ἐπιείκεια.definition: equity, opp. strict law, Arist.Top.141a16, etc.; opp. Isoc.18.34; Plu.Cat.Mi.4

ἐπιείκελος.definition: = like, the masc. freq. in Hom. , but only in phrases Il.1.[265], 4.394, Od.24.36, etc.; so Hes.Th.968

ἐπιελίκτωρ.definition: one who rolls round, coined to explain the Homeric Sch.Il.19.398

ἐπίελπτος.definition: to be hoped or expected, Archil.74.5, Opp.H.4.311

ἐπιζάφελος.definition: vehement, violent, Il.9.525. Adv. vehemently, furiously, Il.9.516, Od.6.330; h.Merc.487: also neut. as Adv., A.R.4.1672

ἐπιζέφυρος.definition: towards the west, western, Euph.121: the Italian Locrians were called Hdt.6.23, etc., f.l. in Pi.O.10.13

ἐπίζηλος.definition: Dor. enviable, happy, B.5.52, cf. A.Ag.939, Ptol.Tetr.186: written in TAM2.245.12

ἐπιήρανος.definition: pleasing, acceptable; after Hom., helping, assisting, Orph.A.98

ἐπιθαλέωσις.definition: perh. celebration of the festival of the Corybantes SIG1014.95

ἐπιθέατρον.definition: building adjoining a theatre, IG11.287 A94,120

ἐπίθεσις.definition: setting on its base; laying or putting on, opp. Arist.Juv.470a11; Act.Ap.8.18, etc.; application, Plu.2.102a, cf. Luc.DDeor.13.1

ἐπιθήκη.definition: addition, increase, Hes.Op.380; cover put over a statue, CPR27.10

ἐπίθημα.definition: something put on; lid, cover, lids of chests, Il.24.228, cf. Hippon.56, Hp.Morb.2.26, Hdt.1.48, Arist.Ath.68.3, IG22.1408; Ar.Fr.295; Hegesipp.Com.1.13; slab, used as the top of a table, Ath.2.49a

ἐπιθυλλίς.definition: f.l. for in Ath.9.371f, cf. Eust.1155.20

ἐπίθυμα.definition: that which is burnt in magic, PMag.Par.1.1308, al.; sacrificial victim, Hsch. s.v

ἐπιθυμίς.definition: wreath of flowers for the neck

ἐπίθυμον.definition: a parasitic plant growing on thyme, Cuscuta Epithymum, Dsc.4.177, Gal.6.414, 11.875, Artem.1.77

ἐπιθώϊος.definition: under penalty of a fine fornon- attendance, Schwyzer687 B6

ἐπιίστωρ.definition: privy to a thing: c.gen; acquainted with, practised in, AP11.371 , App.Anth.7.2 ; IG3.946, cf. Doroth.in Cat.Cod.Astr.2.172

ἐπικαδεία.definition: fixing of buckets on a water- wheel, PLond. 3.1177.178, al

ἐπικάλυμμα.definition: in animals, covering of any orifice, of the gills of fish, Arist.HA505a1, PA696b3; of the opercula of crabs and other crustacea, Id.HA527b26, 541b26, cf. 530a21

ἐπίκαμψις.definition: enveloping movement in naval; curvature, Ael.Fr.76, cf. Paul.Aeg.6.30

ἐπικαταλλαγή.definition: money paid for exchange, discount, Thphr.Char.30.15, SIG252.7

εὔθερος.definition: pleasant in summer, sunny, Poll.5.108 codd

εὐθεσία.definition: good condition, habit of body, Hp. ap. Gal.19.101; a year of plenty, ibid

εὐίσχιος.definition: with beautiful hips, Inscr.Prien.317, cf. AP5.115 ; of a horse, with fine quarters, Hippiatr.115; Hsch. s.v

εὐκάματος.definition: of easy labour, easy; crowns won by noble toils, APl.4.335

εὐκάρδιος.definition: stout-hearted, S.Aj.364; good for the stomach, Diocl.Fr.120 , Ruf. ap. Orib.5.11.3 , Xenocr.8

εὔκαυστος.definition: easily burning, Thphr.Ign.72 , Sch.Ar.Pax1134 : Phot. s.v

εὐκίων.definition: gen. with beautiful pillars, E.Ion185 , cf. AP7.648.7

εὔκλαδος.definition: with fine boughs, Quint. Ps.47 .3; gloss on Sch.Nic.Th.648; on Suid

εὐκλεής.definition: acc.sg. contr. Pi.P.12.24; Orphic title of Hades, IG14.641

εὔκλωνος.definition: with fine twigs, Androm. ap. Gal.14.40

ἐϋκνήμις.definition: well-greaved, freq. in nom. and; with goodly spokes, Nonn.D.7.140

εὔκνημος.definition: with beautiful ankle, AP5.202; as Subst., a plant in Nic.Th.648, Al.372

εὔκολος.definition: of persons, easily satisfied, contented with one's food, AP9.72 ; Plu.Lyc.16; Id.Galb.3: but, in earlier authors

εὐκομιδής.definition: well cared for, Hdt.4.53 , cf. Hsch

εὐκόμιστος.definition: = foreg., Poll.9.161; easily extracted, Sor.2.62; easily carried off, App.Mith.90

εὐκράς.definition: = temperate, of even; mixed for drinking, Poll.6.23

εὐκρασία.definition: of persons, good temperament, Arist.PA673b25, cf. GA744a30, Zeno Stoic.1.37, Gal.6.31, etc

εὐκύμαντος.definition: easily made to undulate; metaph., strong-surging, Eust.1392.49

εὔκωπος.definition: well-equipt with oars, Opp.H.5.242; gloss on Hsch

εὐλᾶϊγξ.definition: gen. poet. for AP9.767 ; ib.7.605 , cf. Coluth.46, Nonn.D.5.134

ἐγκάλυψις.definition: concealment, Str.10.2.12 ; Plu.2.266e; to be wrapped in obscurity, M.Ant.5.10

ἐγκάμνω.definition: grow weary or slack in or at a thing, J.AJ2.15.5; become slack, Id.BJ3.10.2; Aret.SD1.15

ἐγκανάσσω.definition: pour in wine, E.Cyc.152, Ar.Eq.105; Alciphr.3.36

ἐγκαναχάομαι.definition: make a sound on a thing, blow on a conch, Theoc.9.27

ἐγκάρδιος.definition: in the heart, (or; in close proximity, of planets, Antioch.Astr.in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.105

ἐγκάρπιος.definition: of fruit, containing seed: hence, ripe; unreaped crops, SIG633.87

ἔγκαρπος.definition: containing fruit; festoons of fruit on friezes or the capitals of columns, Lat. encarpa, Vitr.4.1.7

ἐγκαρτερέω.definition: persevere or persist in a thing, v.l; c. acc., await stedfastly, E.HF1351, Andr.262

ἐγκαταβαίνω.definition: go down into, put oneself in, c. acc., Pi.N.1.38: c. dat., dub. l. in D.S.14.28; Gal.UP2.15: abs., Id.8.686

ἐγκαταβιόω.definition: pass one's life in, Plu.2.783d, Longin.44.11

ἐγκαταγηράσκω.definition: = grow old in, Arist.Ath.17.1; Plu.Phoc.30; become inveterate in, Din.2.3:—also Them.Or.19.232c

ἐγκατάγομαι.definition: put up at a place, Nic.Dam.p.138 D., Poll.1.73

ἐγκαταγράφω.definition: write down among, Ael.Fr.67; portray, Aen. Gaz.Ep.12

ἐγκαταδαρθάνω.definition: sleep in, Plu.2.647f; go to sleep over a thing, ib.688f

ἐγκαταδέω.definition: bind fast in, Pl.Phd.84a, Them.Or.23.297a , Opp.H.3.201

ἐγκαταδύνω.definition: aor. of the sun, set upon a place, Hp.Aër.6; sink beneath, AP7.532 ; Opp.H.1.153: abs., sink, be absorbed in, Archig. ap. Aët.3.167, Gal.7.217: metaph., to be immersed in, c. dat., Dam.Pr.10:—Med., Procop.Arc.1

ἐγκατάκειμαι.definition: lie in, c. dat., Thgn.1191; lie in bed, sleep, Ar.Pl.742

ἐγκατάκλειστος.definition: shut up in a place, E.Fr.1132.39

ἐγκατακλείω.definition: shut up in, enclose, Alex.40.3, cf. Arist.Pr.937a29; Thphr.CP5.13.2:—Pass., Hp.Acut.16, Arist.Mete.378a29

ἐγκατακλίνω.definition: put to bed in a place, Ar.Pl.621:—Pass., lie down in, Id.Av.122; Hyp.Eux.14

ἐγκατακρούω.definition: tread a measure among them, Ar.Ra.330

ἐγκατακρύπτω.definition: hide in, Lyc.1231, cf. Gal.2.305, al.; in religious mysteries, IG3.900

ἐγκαταλαμβάνω.definition: catch in a place, hem in, Th.4.116; follow in immediate succession, Aristid.Or.47.6, cf.26.84; attack immediately after, Id.47.60

ἐγκαταλέγω.definition: count or reckon among, Luc.Par.3; = Lat. adlegere inter patricios, D.C.43.47; enlist soldiers, AP11.265

ἐγκατάλειμμα.definition: remnant, residue, trace; residual trace, Epicur.Ep.1p.12U

ἐγκαταλείπω.definition: leave behind, Hes.Op.378; leave in the lurch, Pl.Smp.179a, Lycurg.2, D.57.58, Ev.Matt.27.46, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.22, etc.; abandon, Th.4.44; X.HG5.4.13

ἐγκατάληψις.definition: catching or being caught in a; concept , Gal.14.685, cf. 19.350

ἐγκαταλοχίζω.definition: divide into relays or courses, LXX2 Ch.31.18

ἐγκαταμείγνυμι ἐγκαταμειγνύω.definition: Luc.Lex.25), mix with, Timo33, Luc.Hist.Conscr.13, etc.; Ach.Tat.4.15; D.H.6.2; Hdn.7.12.7: metaph., Ph.2.570; Plu.2.414f; of a sculptor, APl.4.57 , cf. AP9.593:—Pass., to be mixed in or with, Hp.Aër.6; Isoc.15.10; D.…

ἐγκαταμένω.definition: remain in, Thphr.HP1.3.4, Hld.1.33, etc.; continue the use of, Antyll. ap. Aët.9.42

ἐγκατάμιξις.definition: intermingling, infusion, Alex.Aphr.in Sens.74.26, Olymp.in Mete.157.29

ἐγκαταναίω.definition: aor. 1 make to dwell in, A.R.3.116, Moero1

ἐγκαταντλέω.definition: wash over with a thing, Hippiatr.26

ἐγκαταπίνομαι.definition: pf. aor. to be swallowed up, of a ship, Ph.1.670: metaph. of persons, Id.2.300, al.; to be absorbed, immersed, Dam.Pr.67

ἐγκαταπίπτω.definition: poet. aor. fall or throw oneself upon, A.R.3.655; AP9.82

ἐγκαταπνίγω.definition: suffocate in, Gal.7.673:—Pass., aor. inf. Diocl.Fr.55

ἐγκαταριθμέω.definition: count, number, reckon in or among, Hermog.Prog.10, cf. Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.46.9:— Pass., to be counted in or among, Arist.SE167b24

ἐγκατασβέννυμι.definition: or quench in a thing, Plu.2.975c, cf.987d

ἐγκατασήπομαι.definition: grow rotten or corrupt in, Hp.Mul.1.63, E.ap.Stob.3.41.6

ἐγκατασκευάζω.definition: prepare in a place, D.S.16.54; but the Prep. freq. has little force, Id.2.24 , 14.91

ἐγκατάσκευος.definition: elaborate, ornate, of style, opp. D.H.Comp.18, al., cf. Phld.Rh.1.164S., Demetr.Eloc.15. Adv. S.E.M.2.56

ἐγκατασκήπτω.definition: fall upon, of lightning; trans., hurl down among or upon, of lightning, S.Tr.1087; A.Pers.514

ἐγκατασκιρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be engrained, Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81

ἐγκατασπείρω.definition: scatter, sow, implant in or among, Ph.2.673; Plu.2.1001b; Hdn.2.1.3:—Pass., Plu.Cic.14, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.69 B

ἐγκαταστοιχειόομαι.definition: to be implanted as a principle in, Plu.Lyc.13, 2.353e

ἐγκαταστρέφω.definition: return a ball in a game, Antiph.234.6

ἐγκατατάσσω.definition: Att. arrange or place in, Longin.10.7, Marcellin.Puls.474:—Pass., Onos.10.3; - rhythms introduced unobtrusively, D.H.Comp.25

ἐγκατατέμνω.definition: cut up the foetus in the womb; cut up among a number, Pl.R.565d

ἐγκατατίθημι.definition: lay or put in, Orph.H.25.9; Hom. only in Med., put the band upon or round thy waist, Il.14.219, cf. 223; stored up, devised mischief in his heart, Od.23.223; stored up the belt in his art, designed it by his art, Od.1…

ἐγκατατομή.definition: cutting up of the foetus in the womb, Hp.Foet.Exsect.tit

ἐγκαταχέω.definition: pour out besides, Epigr. ap. Plu.Marc.30

ἐγκατειλέομαι.definition: to be cooped up in, Arist.Mu.395b33, dub. in Ph.2.504

ἐγκατεφάλλομαι.definition: Ep. aor. 2 leap down into, Opp.H.4.661

ἐγκατέχω.definition: Pass., to be owned or possessed, PFlor.97.3

ἐγκατοικέω.definition: dwell in, Hdt.4.204; E.Fr.188; dwell among, 2 Ep.Pet.2.8

ἐγκατοικίζω.definition: Att. fut. Lyc.1261:—settle or place in or on, Luc.Asin.25: metaph., Dam.Pr.257; implant, Plu.2.779f

ἐγκατοικοδομέω.definition: to build in a place, Th.3.18; build in, immure, Aeschin.1.182:—metaph. in Pass., Arist.de An.420a9, cf. Porph.Abst.4.3

ἐγκατοπτρίζομαι.definition: Med., aor. IG4.951.64; contemplate as in a mirror, Ph.Byz.Mir.Praef.III

ἐγκατορύσσω.definition: Att. bury in:—Pass., D.H.Rh.6.5, cf. Jul.Or.6.189c

ἐγκάτοχος.definition: recluse, Ptol.Tetr.163; Adj., fixing, Olymp.Alch.p.74 B

ἐγκαυλέω.definition: to be in stalk, Arist.Pr.926a26, Thphr.HP1.2.2

ἔγκαυμα.definition: mark burnt in, sore from; encaustic picture, Pl.Ti.26c, JHS41.195 , Dicaearch.1.8, Plu.2.759c

ἔγκαυσις.definition: encaustic painting, IG2.808d.52; heat-stroke, Dsc.5.13 , Gal.12.504: pl., Plu.2.127b

ἐγκαυστής.definition: encaustic painter, Plu.2.348f; IG14.1494:—also ib.12.374, CIG4958c

ἔγκαυστος.definition: burnt in, painted in encaustic, Mart.4.47: encausto pingere, Plin.HN35.149; encausta pictura, ib.122

ἐγκαυχάομαι.definition: pride oneself on, LXXPs.73.4; Aesop.230, Eustr.in EN272.14

ἔγκειμαι.definition: fut. used as Pass. of; lie in, be wrapped in, Il.22.513; so, Hdt.2.73 ; simply, to be in, Hes.Th.145: in mal.part., Herod.5.3

ἐγκείρω.definition: in pf. part. Pass., with shorn head, E.El.108

ἐγκέλευσις.definition: = foreg., Str.13.1.35, Sammelb.4284.8 , Them.Or.19.232b: pl., A.D.Synt.258.20; by command, IG14.926 , Zucker Les temples immergés de la Nubie p.3

ἐγκελεύω.definition: urge on, cheer on, A.Pr.72; in Med. also, command, Arist.Fr.11; IPE12.79.23 , cf. Asp.in EN135.13: c. acc., enjoin, Ti.Locr.104a

ἐγκέλλω.definition: aor. 1 fit into, as a socket, Hp.Fract.30

ἐγκεντρίζω.definition: goad, spur on, LXXWi.16.11; of plants, graft, Thphr.HP2.2.5, Porph.Gaur.10.1 , etc.: metaph., Ep.Rom.11.17, Plot.2.9.7; of a Centaur, APl.4.116

ἐγκεντρίς.definition: goad, X.Cyn.6.1, Pl.Com.40; also, spur, Pherecr.48; pointed stile for writing, Poll.8.16, Aristaenet.1.20

ἐγκέντρισις.definition: inoculation or grafting of trees, Colum. 3.9.6, Jul.Ep.180

ἔγκεντρος.definition: furnished with a sting; of stars, occupying a cardinal point, Vett.Val.57.30, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.148

ἐγκεντρόω.definition: thrust in a sting: fix firmly in, Hsch. : —Pass., to be furnished with a sting, Sch.Ar.V.1069

ἐγκεράννυμι.definition: or mix, esp. wine; Pass., to be multiplied together, of numbers, Theol.Ar.45

ἐγκεραυλέω.definition: play on the Phrygian flute, Hsch.:—hence Id

ἐγκέφαλος.definition: within the head: as Subst; the heart or 'cabbage' of the date-palm, X.An.2.3.16, Thphr.HP2.6.2

ἐγκηδεύω.definition: bury in a place, LXX4 Ma.17.9 , J.AJ9.5.3, JHS 6.359

ἐγκηρόω.definition: wax over, rub with wax, Gp.10.21.5

ἐγκηρύσσω.definition: invite tenders for a contract, PPetr.3p.101

ἐγκιθαρίζω.definition: play the harp in the midst, h.Ap.201; at midday, h.Merc.17

ἐγκιλικίζω.definition: play the Cilician to one, i. e. cheat, Pherecr.166

ἐγκίρνημι.definition: poet. for mix by pouring in, Pi.N.9.50; Alc.34.4: metaph., Lysis ap.Iamb.VP17.77; Dam.Pr.412:—Pass., Com.Adesp.1203.3, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.81 P

ἐγκισσάω.definition: have yearnings like one pregnant, LXXGe.30.38

ἐγκισσεύομαι.definition: Pass., twine like ivy: metaph., form a plexus, Hp.Oss.14

ἐγκλάω.definition: Ep. aor. thwart, frustrate; Pass., to be bent, inclined, Apollod.Poliorc.187.16; of the eyes of swine, Plu.2.671a ; of a diadem, Heraclit.Ep.8.1

ἐγκλεισμός.definition: shutting up, Eust.1391.63; under lock and key, POxy.1734.6

ἐγκλείω.definition: shut or confine within, S.Aj.1274; Id.Tr.579: generally, shut up, confine, Id.Ant.180; ib.505; E.Hec.1284

ἔγκλημα.definition: accusation, charge; in Law, written complaint: generally, of complaints which were to lead to private suits, file a complaint against . . , D.34.16, al., cf. PTeb.616

ἐγκληματογραφέω.definition: draw up an indictment against, UPZ124

ἐγκλήμων.definition: gen. liable to a charge, AP5.187

ἐγκληρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be assigned or planted by lot, Ael.VH8.1

ἔγκληρος.definition: having a lot or share in . . , c. gen; having a share of an inheritance, heir or heiress, E.IT682; a marriage which brings wealth, Id.Hipp.1011; land possessed as an inheritance, Id.HF468

ἐγκλητέος.definition: to be blamed, Plu.2.1051c; one must blame, Plb.4.60.9; M.Ant.12.24

ἔγκλητος.definition: liable to a charge, PTeb.27.42 (ii B; written for Hsch

ἔγκλιμα.definition: slope, Plb.5.59.9; inclination, tilt, Hipparch.1.3.5, Gem.6.24; of an engine, Bito55.10

ἐγκλίνω.definition: fut. pf. Plu.Sull.1; cause to incline, Pl.R.436e; Arist.Oec.1348b3:—Med., lean to the right, Id.Phgn.813a17

ἔγκλισις.definition: inclination, of the; the inclination or slope, as of a wave, Arist.Col.792a22

ἐγκλύζω.definition: fut. rinse the inside of a thing; treat by clysters, Id.4.154:— Pass., to be administered as a clyster or injection, Id.1.73, Eup.1.197, etc

ἐγκνήθω.definition: grate in, in Med., Nic.Th.911 , Al.368

ἐγκοιλαίνω.definition: hollow, scoop out, f.l. in Hdt.2.73:—Pass., Thphr.HP5.2.4

ἐγκοίλιος.definition: in the belly:—as Subst; intestines, Id.1.91, SIG958.13 , LXXLe.1.9

ἐγκοιμάομαι.definition: Pass. with fut. Med., sleep in a place; sleep upon or after a meal, Hp.Acut.29

ἐγκοίμησις.definition: a sleeping in a temple , D.S.1.53

ἐγκοιμητήριος.definition: for sleeping on, Poll.6.11: grave, BSA18.145

ἐγκοίμητρον.definition: counterpane, PCair.Zen. 48.4 , Ammon.p.140 V.; expld. by dormitorium, Gloss

ἐγκοιμίζω.definition: lull to sleep in . . , AP7.260 : metaph., HeroAut.16.2:— Pass., IG4.951.90

ἐγκοισυρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be luxurious as Coesyra , Ar.Nu.48

ἐγκοιτάζομαι.definition: to be embedded, Apollod.Poliorc.161.4; to be soaked, PLeid.X.98

ἐγκοίτιος.definition: belonging to a bed, EM255.44: = Hsch. s.v

ἐγκόλαμμα.definition: anything engraven, LXXEx.36.13 ; engraved inscription, Inscr.Prien.42.9

ἐγκολάπτω.definition: cut or carve upon stone, Hdt.1.187, cf. IG12.313.166; ib. 12.694.9 ; Hdt.2.106, 136, al., cf. LXX3 Ki.6.33; Hdt.5.59; Suid. s.v. Plu.Per.21: metaph., Lib.Decl.43.49

ἐγκοληβάζω.definition: in Ar.Eq.263, gulp down, swallow up, v. Sch. ad loc., Hsch.; also expld. by Suid. s.v

ἐγκολλάω.definition: glue on or to, IG12.373.208, LXXZa.14.5 , HeroAut.24.2

ἐγκολπίζω.definition: form a bay, Str.5.4.5; go into or follow the bay, Id.9.5.22

ἐγκόλπιος.definition: in or on the bosom, Heraclit.All.39

ἐγκολπόω.definition: make full and round, like the folds of a robe, Orph.A.1183 :—Pass., to be curved into a bay or bays, Arist.Mu.393a23:—Med., put in the fold of one's robe: hence metaph., 'have in one's pocket', D.C.48.52:—Pass., to ha…

ἐγκομβόομαι.definition: Med., bind a thing on oneself; Pass., = , Epich.7

ἐγκόμβωμα.definition: a sort of frock or apron, worn esp. by slaves to keep the clean, Longus2.33, Poll.4.119, Thd. Is.3.20, cf. Varro ap. Non.p.870 L

ἐγκονέω.definition: to be quick and active, esp. in service; urge on, incite, AP6.268

ἐγκονίομαι.definition: Med., sprinkle sand over oneself after anointing, and before wrestling, X.Smp.3.8:—Pass., Luc.Am.45; to be in the dust, prob. l. in Hp.Vict.3.76

ἐγκοπεύς.definition: tool for cutting stone, chisel, Luc.Somn.3

ἐγκοπή.definition: incision, Gal.7.38; fracture of skull; steps cut in the wall of wells, etc., Ael.Dion.Fr.90

ἐγκόπτω.definition: knock in, Thphr.HP2.7.6; (i.e; engrave, SIG279.33 :—Med., IG12.536

ἐγκοσμέω.definition: Pass., to be adorned, v.l. in Aristid.Or.26.99; LXX4 Ma.6.2

ἐγκοτέω.definition: to be indignant at, A.Ch.41 , S.Fr.1042, LXXGe.27.41

ἔγκοτος.definition: bearing a grudge, spiteful, malignant; Subst. grudge, Hdt.3.59, 9.110; for a thing, Id.8.29; Id.6.73, cf. 133; also D.H.9.7

ἐγκράζω.definition: aor. pf. cry aloud at one, esp. in anger, v.l. in Ar.Pl.428; v.l. in Th.8.84; Arist.Phgn.813b5

ἐγκραιπαλάω.definition: to be drunk at or with, Hdn.2.10.6:—also dub. in Phld.Rh.1.173 S

ἐγκράτεια.definition: mastery over, self-; abs., self-control, X.Mem.1.5.1, Isoc.3.44, Arist.EN1145b8, al., LXXSi.18.30, Act.Ap.24.25, etc

ἐγκρατεύομαι.definition: exercise self-control, Arist.EE1223b12; to be a member of the Encratite sect, Anatolian Studies87

ἐγκρατέω.definition: to be master of, exercise control over, Metop. ap. Stob.3.1.115, cf. LXXEx.9.2

ἐγκρατής.definition: in possession of power; holding fast, a hand with the firmest hold, X.Eq.7.8

ἐγκρατίτης.definition: member of the Encratite sect, Cod.Theod.16.5.9

ἐγκραυγάζω.definition: shout at a person, Phld.Lib.p.5 O

ἐγκρεμάννυμαι.definition: Pass., to be hung up in, Gp.2.4.2, al

ἐγκρικόω.definition: enclose as in a ring, bind as in a hoop, Hp.Oss.18

ἐγκρίνω.definition: reckon in or among: reckon as; of persons, select, admit, 2 Ep.Cor.10.12:—Pass., Pl.Lg.755d; D.20.107; X.HG4.1.40; of IG7.29 ; of athletes, Artem.1.59; subject of statue by Alcamenes, Plin.HN34.72

ἔγκρισις.definition: approval, judgement; examination of athletes before admitting them to a contest, Luc.Pr.Im.11, Artem.1.59, Aristid.Or.29.18

ἐγκριτήριος.definition: of or for admission: rooms where the athletes were examined before they were admitted as candidates, IG4.203.12

ἔγκριτος.definition: admitted, accepted, Pl.Lg.966d, IG12.189.9 ; Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.106

ἐγκροστόω.definition: = Lat. incrustare, veneer with marble, Supp.Epigr.2.698

ἐγκροτέω.definition: strike on the ground; Pass., to be fastened by nails, Philostr.VA2.20

ἐγκρύβω.definition: late form of D.S.1.80 , Apollod.3.13.6, Gal.6.620, PHolm.5.7

ἐγκρύπτω.definition: hide or conceal in; Med., hide oneself, Nonn.D.32.285

ἐγκρυφιάζω.definition: intr., keep oneself hidden, act; hide, conceal, Procop.Arc.1: abs., Id.Vand.1.25

ἔγκρυψις.definition: banking up of a fire, Arist.Juv.470a12

ἐγκτάομαι.definition: acquire possessions in a foreign country, Hdt.5.23; citizens who possess property in a deme not their own, opp. D.50.8, cf. X.Vect.2.4, PGnom.243

ἔγκτημα.definition: land held in a country by a person not belonging to it, And.3.15, D.7.42, IG22.43.27, App.Mith.47

ἔγκτησις.definition: Dor. tenure of land in a; estate, property, LXXLe.25.13, etc.; register of properties, BGU76 , etc

ἐγκτητικόν.definition: a land-tax paid for the right of holding IG22.1214

ἔγκτητος.definition: possessed in a foreign country, LXXLe.14.34, al

ἐγκτίζω.definition: found, build among, Plu.2.328e:—Med., v.l. in Hdt.5.23

ἐγκυέομαι.definition: to be borne in the womb, TheonProg.2

ἐγκυκάω.definition: mix up in, Ar.Ach.939 :—Act., Dsc.Ther.2, Lyc.674

ἐγκυκλέομαι.definition: Pass., roll or rotate in the sockets, of; in com. sense, to be cooped up, Ar.V.699

ἐγκύκλιος.definition: also Orph.A.981; revolving in a cycle, recurrent: hence, at Athens, public services required regularly every year, opp. to those required at uncertain times, D.20.21; rights common to all citizens, Id.25.74

ἔγκυκλος.definition: circular, Epicur.Ep.2p.52U.; round; woman's upper garment, Ar.Th.261, Lys.113; IG2.754.48

ἐγκυκλόω.definition: move round in a circle, E.IT76; surround, Str.2.5.24:—more freq. in Med. with pf. part. Pass., encompass, encircle, E.Ba.292, cf. Ar.V.699; a voice has echoed around me, ib.395; surround, hem in, Plu.Marc.6, etc.; of …

ἐγκυλίνδω.definition: Hp.Mul.1.75, Arist.Pr.914a22; metaph. in Pass., to be involved in, X.Mem.1.2.22, cf. Vett. Val. l.c.; D.H.11.36; Porph.Chr.26; Cat.Cod.Astr.7.208:—in aor. Med., Luc.Hipp.6

ἐγκύμων.definition: gen. pregnant, X.Cyn.7.2, Arist.HA546b10, etc.; Id.Fr.76; big with arms, of the Trojan horse, E.Tr.11; Pl.Com.174.8; Dsc.3.7: metaph., of the mind, Pl.Smp.209b, Ph.1.651, etc.; AP9.210

ἐγκυοποιέω.definition: impregnate: metaph. of a chemical reaction, Zos.Alch.p.211 B

ἐγκύπτω.definition: stoop down and peep in, look closely into, Hdt.7.152; Pl.R.359d: abs., stooping to the ground, Ar.Nu.191, Th.4.4; retracted, Hp.Hebd.51

ἐγκύρησις.definition: meeting with or happening; in Medicine, definite phenomenon, BKT3p.30

ἐγκύρω.definition: impf. fut. aor. aor. 1 lessfreq. in early writers, Heraclit.72, freq. in Phld. as Sign.21, al., cf. Plb. and D.H. , Ael.Tact.1.2:—fall in with, light upon, meet with, c.dat., Il.13.145; Hes.Op.216; Archil.70; Pi.P.4.2…

ἐγκωμάζω.definition: take part in a revel, Gloss

ἐγχαλάω.definition: relax, in Pass., Plu.2.690a, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.8.4

ἔγχαλκος.definition: in or with brass: moneyed, rich; for sale, Ath.13.584e

ἐγχάραξις.definition: scarification, Apollon. ap; furrow, gloss on Sch.A.R.3.413

ἐγχειμάζω.definition: pass the winter in, Jul.Ep.185, Poll.1.62; Dicaearch.1.21

ἐγχείμορος.definition: dealing death with the spear, ib.630.24

ἐγχειρέω.definition: lay hands on, attack, ib.122: abs., X.HG4.5.16; Plb.2.22.11; put hand to a case requiring medical treatment, Hp.de Arte3; ib.13

ἐγχείρησις.definition: taking in hand, undertaking; Practical Anatomy, title of work by Gal

ἐγχειρία.definition: manipulation, v.l. for Hp.Art.35, cf. Phld.Hom.p.45 O.: pl., Hsch

ἐγχειρίδιος.definition: as Subst., hand-knife, dagger, Hdt.1.12,214, Th.3.70, etc.; Lys.4.6, etc

ἐγχεσίμαργος.definition: raging with the spear, EM313.7, Hsch

ἐγχεσίμωρος.definition: fighting with the spear, Il.2.692, al., Od.3.188, Cerc.6.9: Comp., with play on AP11.16

ἐγχέσπαλος.definition: wielding the spear, Il.2.131, B.5.69, etc

ἐγχέω.definition: Ep. subj. : fut. late; of dry things, pour in, shoot in, . . Od.2.354

ἐγχλαινόομαι.definition: Pass., to be clothed in, Lyc.974, cf. 1347

ἐγχλαμυδόομαι.definition: to be wrapped in a cloak, Hsch. s.v

ἐγχλίω.definition: to deal wantonly with, insult, A.Supp.914

ἐγχλοάω.definition: to be of a greenish hue, Nic.Th.154

ἐγχονδρίζω.definition: form into grains, Archig. ap. Gal.12.661

ἐγχορεύω.definition: dance in, Plu.2.332b: generally, disport oneself, take pleasure in, etc., Ph.1.252, al.; of birds, sport in the air, c. acc., Vett. Val.344.22

ἐγχράω.definition: and Ep. Nic.Th.277:—like; Pass., there were wars undertaken.., Hdt.7.145

ἔγχρισις.definition: anointing, rubbing in; slight wound, scratch, Ael.NA3.22

ἔγχριστος.definition: rubbed in as an ointment, Theoc.11.2; Arist.GA747a9

ἐγχρίω.definition: anoint, Duris10 J., cf; sting, prick, Pl.Phdr.251d:—Pass., poison injected by a sting, Ael.NA1.54

ἐγχρονία.definition: Ion. chronic character, dub. in Hp.Praec.14

ἐγχρονίζω.definition: to be long about a thing, delay, Th.3.27; become chronic, Hp.Prog.17; Ph.2.203; continue in, Procl.Par.Ptol.51:—Pass., Pl.Grg.480b, cf. Arist.HA586a18

ἐγχρονισμός.definition: prolonged use, Sor.1.46, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.23.10

ἐγχυλόομαι.definition: to be converted into chyle, Gal.8.369

ἐγχυματισμός.definition: injection, instillation, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.26.1, Sor.1.56, Hippiatr.68

ἐγχώννυμι.definition: or fill up by depositing earth; throw in earth, ib.2.75, cf. D.S.17.42

ἐγχωρέω.definition: give room to do a thing, allow; c. acc., admit of, Arr.Tact.11.4

ἐγχώριος.definition: Subst., dweller in the land, inhabitants, S.OC871, cf. E.Ion1167; Arist.PA673a18, Wilcken Chr.1.2 , etc

ἔγχωρος.definition: = foreg., S.Ph.692 , OC125 , Lyc.509, etc.; S.Ichn.322

ἐθελόδουλος.definition: serving voluntarily, Pl.R.562d, Ph.1.376, Aristaenet.2.2. Adv. Plu.Arat.25

εἰδωλεῖον.definition: or idol's temple, LXX1 Ma.1.47, 1 Ep.Cor.8.10

εἰδωλόθυτος.definition: sacrificed to idols: Subst. meats offered to idols, Act.Ap.15.29, 1 Ep.Cor.8.1, etc

εἰδωλόμορφος.definition: formed after an image, Gp.10.9.1; like a phantom, of comets, Sch. Ptol.Tetr.75

εἰδωλοποιία.definition: formation of images, as in a mirror; image formed in the mind, imagination, D.S.1.96: pl., Longin.15.1

εἰδωλοποιός.definition: image-maker, Pl.Sph.239d; Adj., producing phantasmal appearances, ib.10.2, cf. 2.10

εἴεω.definition: a battle-cry of young warriors, Hsch

εἰκαστής.definition: one who conjectures, diviner; one who portrays, represents, D.H.Isoc.11, cf. Lys.19

εἰκονίζω.definition: copy from a pattern, PPar.65.12; draw up an official description, PFay.36.23 , etc

εἰκόνισμα.definition: image, S.Fr.573, cf. AP13.6 , Porph.Sent.43, Plot.1.4.10; portrait, Herod.4.38

εἰκονογραφέω.definition: depict, Ph.2.588; describe; make an image, dub. in PPetr.2p.9

εἰκονογράφος.definition: portrait-painter, Arist.Po.1454b9, Them.Or.24.309b; prob. in IG7.3064

εἰκοσάεδρος.definition: of twenty surfaces: body with twenty surfaces, Plu.2.719e, Gal.5.668

εἰκοσαετία.definition: period of twenty years, Ph.2.224, J.AJ8.5.3, PTeb.287.7

εἰκοσάκωπος.definition: with twenty oars, Hsch. s.v. etc

εἰκοσάρουρος.definition: holder of twenty of land, PTeb.61. 65 , al

εἰκοσιδύω.definition: or two and twenty, PSI4.390 , Eust.726.13

εἰκοσιεπταετής.definition: twenty-seven years old, Annales du Service22.16

εἰκοσικαιτετραπλασίων.definition: gen. twenty-four times as great, Procl.Hyp.3.51

εἰκοσίκλινος.definition: with twenty places at table, Antig.Caryst. ap. Ath.12.548a, D.S.1.49

εἰκοσίπεδος.definition: twenty feet wide or long, in Dor. form Tab.Heracl.1.62, al

εἰκοστολόγος.definition: one who collects the twentieth, tax- or toll-collector, Ar.Ra.363
