εἰλαπιναστής.definition: feaster, guest, boon-companion; name of Zeus at Cyprus, Hegesand.30

εἷμαι.definition: pf. Pass. of; pf. Pass. of

εἰροπόκος.definition: wool-fleeced, woolly, Il.5.137; Od.9.443, Theoc.8.9, cf. Hes.Op.234

εἰρωνεύομαι.definition: feign ignorance, so as to perplex; employ understatement, Polystr.p.15 W

εἰσαγγελεύς.definition: one who announces, usher at the; metaph. of the senses, Them.in de An.87.8

εἰσαγγελία.definition: information, news, Plb.9.9.7; public announcement, IG12.325.16

εἰσαγγέλλω.definition: go in and announce a person, Hdt.3.118; submit a person's name, PCair.Preis.18.7 , etc

εἰσαγωγή.definition: bringing in, Str.5.3.8; introduction, as of heirs by adoption, Is.10.9 ; of children to a IG22.1237.108

εἰσαγωγός.definition: epith. of Hermes, watching over imports, Ath.Mitt.37.216; conduit, PTeb.86.4 , etc

εἰσαείρομαι.definition: Med., take to oneself, Thgn.976 codd

εἰσαθρέω.definition: look at, descry, Il.3.450, cf. Theoc.25.215; Epigr.Gr.906 ; Pl.Epigr.14: metaph., IG3.716.—Poet. Verb

εἰσαίρω.definition: bring or carry in, Ar.Ra.518, cf. Anaxandr.2

εἰσαΐσσω.definition: contr. Att. fut. aor. dart in or into, Ar.Nu.543, Aristid.Or.49.16, prob. in D.C.37.32; cf

εἰσαΐω.definition: poet., = catch the sound of, hear; perceive, feel the effect of, Hp.Morb.4.37; contr. fut. and aor. forms are prob. in ib.35,38, al

εἰσακοντίζω.definition: throw or hurl javelins at; abs., spout, of blood, E.Hel.1588

εἰσακούω.definition: hearken or give ear to one; in Poets, simply, hear, .. S.Tr.351; Id.El.884, cf. Aj.318, Axiop.1.12; E.El.416

εἰσαλείφω.definition: smear or rub in, Hp.Nat.Mul.9; anoint, Aristid.2.292 J

εἰσαναγκάζω.definition: force one thing into another, Hp.Art.47

εἰσανάγω.definition: lead up into, into slavery, Od.8.529; APl.4.201 ; Plb.1.82.2

εἰσανέχω.definition: intr., rise above, c. gen., ib.1360, cf. 4.291: c. acc., ib.1578

εἰσαποβαίνω.definition: pass out to.., c. acc., A.R.4.650, etc

εἰσαποκλείω.definition: shut up in, v.l. for Sever.in Rh.1p.546 W

εἰσαποστέλλω.definition: send in or to, PPetr.3p.113 , Ant.Lib.41.2

εἰσαράσσω.definition: Att. dash or force into, drive the enemy’s horse in upon his foot, Hdt.4.128, cf. D.C.51.26; Id.5.116

εἰσαρτίζω.definition: join or fit into, Hp.Morb.2.33 vulg

εἰσαφάσσω.definition: feel in, feel by putting in the finger, Hp.Nat. Mul.11; but ib.36,al

εἰσαφίημι.definition: admit, X.Cyr.4.5.14 codd., Str.15.1.42, J.BJ1.13.3: —Pass., Aen.Tact.32.9

εἰσβαίνω.definition: go on board a ship, mostly abs., embark; come in, be imported, Alex.117

εἴσβασις.definition: an entrance, devising ways of entrance, E.IT101; embarkation, Th.7.30, D.C.41.42; introductory process, first stage of a magical operation, PMag.Par.1.397

εἰσγίγνομαι.definition: arrive, PGiss.69.17; dub. in; incomings, revenue, PBaden 47

εἰσγράφω.definition: simply, write down, S.Tr.1167; send in a report, BCH46.400

εἰσδανείζω.definition: lend at interest as well, Pl.R.555c

εἰσδέχομαι.definition: Ion. take into, admit; of certain animals, take in their young after birth, Arist.HA566b17, GA754a29

εἰσδύνω.definition: c. acc., go into, enter, Il.23.622; Hdt.1.193; .. having put on.., Anaxil.33.3

εἴσειμι.definition: inf. serving as fut. to; of the Chorus or actors, come upon the stage, enter, Pl.Lg.664c; .. take the part of king, D.19.247, cf. Lib.Or.30.28

εἰσεμπορεύομαι.definition: Pass., enter a country as a trader, IG12.57.20: expld. by Hsch

εἰσευπορέω.definition: procure in plenty, Supp.Epigr.1.366.40 ; D.S.16.40; GDI3069 : abs., SIG364.74

εἰσέχω.definition: used intr. by Hdt., stretch into; in pictures, is the retiring part, the shade, opp. , Philostr.VA2.20

εἰσηγέομαι.definition: Dor. fut. lead in; introduce, propose, Th.3.20; Pl.Lg.684e; Diph.38, cf. D.18.148, etc.; Ph.1.140,al.; make a proposal on a subject, Isoc.4.170: c. inf., propose, to let her go, Pl.Smp.176e, cf. Cri.48a, cf. D.H.6.51,…

εἰσθέω.definition: run into or in, J.BJ6.4.6, Philostr.VA1.28, D.C.62.16, etc.; runs up to us, Ar.Av.1169

εἰσκομιδή.definition: importation of supplies, Th.7.4: pl., ib.24; bringing in, Orib.Eup.3.7.5

εἰσχειρίζω.definition: put into one's hands, entrust, S.OT384

ἑκατερέω.definition: in dancing, kick the rump with one heel after another, Hsch

ἑκατέρω.definition: Dor. Adv. on either side, Schwyzer251 A 10

ἑκατηβελέτης.definition: = sq., Il.1.75, Hes.Sc.100: Subst., h.Ap.157:—fem. Pythag. name for six, Theol.Ar.37

ἑκατόγγυιος.definition: with a hundred limbs or bodies, a band of 100 maidens, Pi.Fr.122.15

ἑκατόγχειρ.definition: = sq., Acus.8 J., Pi.Pae.8.31, Orph.Fr.57,al., Corn.ND17, etc

ἑκατόμβαιος.definition: epith. of Apollo and Zeus, to; name of a month, Hemerolog.Flor

ἑκατομβαιών.definition: the month Hecatombaeon, in which were offered at Athens and elsewhere, Antipho6.44, Plu.Thes.12, IG11.203 A31, al., etc.; ib.12.76.53

ἑκατόμβη.definition: prop. an offering of a; name of an eye-salve, Alex.Trall.2

ἑκατόμβιος.definition: epith. of Apollo, SIG1024.30; name of month at Halos, IG9.109b50

ἑκατόμβοιος.definition: worth a hundred oxen; festival at which hecatombs were offered, SIG 36.36 , 82.6 , BCH29.243 , IG 5.142 , Str.8.4.11 codd.: dat. Schwyzer 91.19

ἑκατόμπεδος.definition: a hundred feet long, a hundred feet all ways, Il.23.164; Th.3.68 , IG12.256, al., cf. Pi.I.6.22, Tab.Heracl.2.24, al.; Plu.Per.13; Id.Dio45; on the Acropolis of Athens, IG12.4.10, 18; at Dodona, Ptol.Geog.3.13.5

ἑκατόμπους.definition: hundred-footed: in S.OC718 , some take it literally to mean the 50 Nereids .6, A.Fr.174, E.IT427), others the 100 Nereids , others merely to express a notion of multitude

ἑκατονταεβδομηκονταπλασίων.definition: gen. 170 times as great, Olymp.in Mete.118.21:— also Ptol.Alm.5.16

ἑκατοντάκλινος.definition: with 100 couches, with room for 100 couches, of a room, Chares ap.Ath.12.538c, D.S.17.16, J.BJ5.4.4

ἑκατοντάλαντος.definition: worth 100 talents, an action for damages laid at that sum, Ar.Eq.442

ἑκατονταπλάσιος.definition: = sq., Simp.in Ph.1115.33. Adv. LXX1 Ch.21.3

ἑκατονταπλασίων.definition: gen. a hundred times as much or many, c. gen., X.Oec.2.3: without gen., a hundredfold, LXX2 Ki.24.8; Ev.Luc.8.8

ἑκατοντάρχης.definition: leader of a hundred, Hdt.7.81, A.Fr.182; = , Ascl.Tact.2.8, etc.; = Lat. centurio, D.H.2.13 , Act.Ap.10.1, J.AJ9.7.2, Plu.Pomp.78, etc

ἑκατονταρχία.definition: post of a centurion, Onos.34.2; centurion's command, century, J.BJ3.6.2, Ph.2.33

ἑκατοντάρχιον.definition: name of an eye-salve, Aët.7.11, al

ἑκατοντάς.definition: the number a hundred, Hdt.7.184: pl., Ph.2.423, Jul.Ep.180

ἑκατοντάχοος.definition: contr. of 100 measures : yielding fruit a hundredfold, Thphr.HP8.7.4; Str.15.3.11

ἑκατοντόργυιος.definition: 100 fathoms high, Pi.Fr.282: in Ar.Av.1131 shd. be read

ἑκατοστήριος.definition: subject to a tax of one per cent., GDI5661.13 ; —Subst. Ion. tax of one per cent., ib.48, PCair.Zen.12.76, al

ἑκατοστιαῖος.definition: = interest of 1/100 monthly, i.e. twelve per cent. per ann., IG22.1104.4, PGrenf.2.89

ἐκβαίνω.definition: go out of, depart from, Pl.Phd.77d; Plb.3.40.7; c. gen., E.IT907; Pl.R.380d; Arist.Po.1449a27; Pl.R.406b; Id.Ti.44e; withdraw from, Id.Lg.744a; BGU1120.52 , PTeb.309.14

ἐκβακχεύω.definition: excite to Bacchic frenzy, E.Tr.408, cf.Pl.Phdr.245a; Philostr.VS2.10.4; cause to rage with anger, Phld.Ir.p.63 W.:—Pass., to be filled with Bacchic frenzy, E.Ba.1295, cf. Pl.R.561a, Hdn.5.8.1, etc.; Aristaenet.1.16; M…

ἐκβάλλω.definition: throw ashore, .. Od.19.278; .. .. Hdt.6.44; Id.7.170 :—Med., put ashore, Hdt.6.101; jettison, Syngr. ap. D.35.11

ἐκβαρβαρόω.definition: make quite barbarous, Isoc.9.20; —Pass., become so, Pl.Ep.353a, Aristox.Fr.Hist.90, Plb.3.58.8

ἐκβασανίζω.definition: put to the question. in Pass., J.AJ15.8.4; test thoroughly, BGU1141.47 , Philostr.VA2.31

ἐκβασιλίζομαι.definition: to be raised to royal rank, POxy.471.54 ; — prob. to be read for Hsch

ἐκβατήριος.definition: of or for disembarkation; Subst. landing-place, PPetr.3p.89 , Lyc.516, PTeb.33.9

ἐκβάω.definition: Dor. for Foed. Dor. ap. Th.5.77

ἐκβεβαιόομαι.definition: confirm, establish, Plu.2.283a; Id.Pomp.19, cf. Ages.19

ἐκβιάζω.definition: to force out, dislodge, expel, prob.f.l. for; Med., constrain, Hdn.2.3.4; c. inf., Id.2.2.5; Eun.Hist.p.216 D.:—Pass., Lib.Decl.40.14

ἐκβίασμα.definition: prob. f.l. for II, Vett. Val.161.18

ἐκβιβάζω.definition: Att. fut. causal of make to; in athletic contests, eliminate, i.e. win heats, IGRom.3.626 , al.; SIG728 H

ἐκβιβασμός.definition: execution of a sentence or judgement, Aq. IKi.15.23, Cod.Just.12.60.7.1

ἐκβιβαστής.definition: one who executes a sentence, Aq.De.16.18, Lyd.Mag.3.11,12, Cod.Just.3.2.4.2

ἐκβιβρώσκω.definition: devour, S.Tr.1054; — Pass., Gp.2.35.7; metaph., Corn.ND18

ἐκβλαστάνω.definition: aor. I Hp.Alim.6, but inf; c. acc., grow out of, Hp.l.c

ἐκβλάστημα.definition: new shoot, sprout, v.l. in Dsc.5.92, cf. Ph.1.48, Gal.12.349

ἐκβλάστησις.definition: shooting, budding; esp. later budding, Thphr.HP3.5.3

ἐκβλέπω.definition: look, Philostr.Jun.Im.I, cf; get the power of sight, Ael.NA3.25

ἔκβλητος.definition: cast overboard, E.Hec.699; to be thrown out, Heraclit.96, cf. Ph.1.477

ἐκβλύζω.definition: gush out, Orph.L.490; LXXPr.3.10; trans., cause to gush out, Orph.Fr.255; Plu.TG13

ἐκβλώσκω.definition: come forth, only aor. imper. Il.11.604

ἐκβοάω.definition: call out, cry aloud, X.Cyn.6.10, Pl.R.492b, A.R.3.631 , Ph.1.129, al., Polyaen.8.52: c. acc., drive away , Anacreont.25.19; —Pass., POxy.1242.54 ; notorious, Sch.Lib.Or.11.207

ἐκβοηθέω.definition: march out to aid, Hdt.6.16; Id.9.26: abs., Polyaen.1.1.3, Plu.2.773f; make a sally, Th.1.105, Thphr.Char.25.3

ἐκβολβίζω.definition: peel, as one does an onion of its outer; metaph., uproot, destroy, Com.Adesp.992

ἐκβολή.definition: throwing out, casting; expulsion, banishment, A.Supp.421 ; Arist.Pol.1275b36; Pl.Lg.847b; dislodgement, ejection, Plb.4.8.4

ἐκβόλιμος.definition: thrown out, ejected; metaph., abortive, futile, Phld.Po.5.29, cf. Plu.2.44d; to be rejected, PGrenf.2.71 ii II

ἐκβόλιον.definition: drug or other means for expelling the

ἔκβολος.definition: thrown out or away, exposed; frustrated, LXXJu.11.11

ἐκβόμβησις.definition: shouting in token of approbation, Them.Or.23.282d

ἐκβόσκω.definition: aor. consume, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.29; — Med., feed on, Nic.Th.803; absorb, Gal.1.517; metaph. of grief, Aristaenet.2.5

ἐκβράζω.definition: throw off humours, Hp.Mul.2.113; —Pass., gush out, Id.Gland.4; —Med., Id.Int.1

ἔκβρασμα.definition: cutaneous eruption, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.30 , cf.Crito ap.Gal.12.448; scab, Sm. Le.13.6

ἐκβρασμός.definition: = foreg. II, Suid. and Phot. s.v; trembling, shaking, LXXNa.2.10; confusion, Hsch

ἐκβρέχω.definition: cause to rot, of water, in Pass., PPetr.3p.120

ἐκβροντάω.definition: to strike out by lightning; intr., thunder loud, Poll.1.118

ἐκβρυχάομαι.definition: bellow forth or aloud, E.Hel.1557; Id.IT1390

ἐκβυθίζομαι.definition: Pass., come forth from the deep, v.l. in Callistr.Stat.14

ἐκβυρσόω.definition: cause to project from the skin, Gal.18.721

ἐκβύρσωμα.definition: projecting of the bones out of the skin, ib.714

ἐκγαλακτόω.definition: turn into sap, Thphr.CP3.23.1; —Pass., to be turned into sap, of the seeds of plants, Id.HP8.6.1; also, become like milk, Sch.Hes.Th.353

ἐκγαμέομαι.definition: Pass., to be given in marriage, AB259, Suid

ἐκγαυρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be proud of, admire greatly, E.IA101

ἐκγελάω.definition: Ep. aor. h.Merc.389, Theoc.4.37; —laugh out, laugh loud, Od.16.354, 18.35, cf. X.Cyr.1.3.9, etc.; Pl.R.473c; Arist.Pr.965a24; metaph. of a liquid that rushes out with a gurgling sound, E.Tr.1176

ἐκγεννάω.definition: beget, v.l. in LXXPs.109.3; also, bring forth, Eup.99; Boeot. 3pl. fut. Corinn.Supp.2.62

ἐκγιγαρτίζω.definition: take out the stone from, Dsc.1.25, cf. Androm. ap. Gal.13.23, Archig.ib.12.585; Gp.8.27.1

ἐκγίγνομαι.definition: later and Ion. fut; c. dat., to be born to, .. Il.14.115, cf. Hdt.1.30,4.155; fut. perf., h.Ven.197

ἐκγλευκίζομαι.definition: cease fermenting, newly fermented wine, Hp.Epid.7.64

ἐκγλύφω.definition: scoop out, Meges; hatch, Ael.NA2.33; —Med., Plu.TG17; —also intr. in Act., Gp.14.7.28

ἐκγράφω.definition: write out, copy, IG9.687.12; strike out, expunge from a list, IG12.84.28, Decr. ap. And.1.77 ; D.H.19.18. .357.14 .)

ἐκγρυτεύω.definition: search out from old lumber, aor. Hsch

ἐκδακρύω.definition: burst into tears, weep aloud, S.Ph.278, E.Ph.1344; of trees, exude drops of gum, J.BJ1.6.6, Plu.2.384b

ἐκδανείζω.definition: lend out at interest, Arist.Oec.1350a14; fut. part. IG9.694 ; 3pl. ib.4.841.16 ; fut. also LXXDe.28.12; pf. AP11.173 :—Med., borrow, SIG1068.15 : —Pass., IG12.237.23

ἐκδανεισμός.definition: lending at interest, ib.12.515 , BGU362xiv21 ; OGI509.16

ἐκδανειστής.definition: one who lends at interest, Test. Epict.6.30, BMus.Inscr.481*.131

ἐκδαπανάω.definition: exhaust, Plb.21.10.9; Id.24.7.4, cf. PBaden19.19 ; Gal.10.192, 15.86; metaph., J.AJ15.5.1; Lib.Decl.37.30; —Pass., 2 Ep.Cor.12.15

ἐκδασύνομαι.definition: Pass., pf. inf. become hairy, Hsch

ἐκδειματόω.definition: strengthd. for Pl.R.381e, Porph.Chr.49, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.68 B.:—Pass., LXXWi.17.6, D.H.Dem.54

ἐκδερματίζω.definition: flay, skin, Hsch. s.v. Suid. s.v

ἐκδέρω.definition: Ion. fut. strip off the skin; cudgel soundly, 'hide', Ar.V.450, Pl.R.616a, Hyp.Fr.200, PSI4.403 ; — Pass., Macho ap.Ath.13.580b

ἐκδέχομαι.definition: mostly of persons; take or receive from another, Il.13.710; A.Ch.762; of a beacon-fire, .. Id.Ag.285; take it on oneself, D.19.37

ἐκδέω.definition: bind so as to hang from, fasten to or on, c. gen., Od.10.96; they bound the oaks to the mules, i.e. they yoked the mules to them, Il.23.121; Aen.Tact.11.6; abs., bind planks behind, Od.22.174; E.Andr.556; metaph., tra…

ἐκδηθύνω.definition: to be protracted, of disease, Aret.CD1.1

ἐκδηϊόω.definition: destroy, ravage, in aor. I, Hsch.; —Med., Procop.Arc.19

ἐκδημαγωγέω.definition: win by the arts of a demagogue, D.H.7.4

ἐκδημέω.definition: to be abroad, to be on one's travels; c. acc., travel through, IG14.905

ἐκδημία.definition: going or being abroad, E.Fr.768: pl; metaph., departure from life, AP3.5

ἐκδημοσιεύω.definition: in Pass., to be made known, D.C.61.12, 52.31

ἐκδιαιτάω.definition: decide a case as; more freq. Med. or Pass.,regulate one's habits, Hp.Insomn.89; change one's mode of life, Th.1.132, cf. D.H.5.74; Ath.13.556c: abs., having gone astray, Ph.2.48; undisciplined, Men.Prot.p.2 D.: later …

ἐκδιαίτησις.definition: change of habits, Ph.1.360, Plu.Alex.45: c.gen., Ph.2.76, Plu.2.493c

ἐκδιαφορέω.definition: draw out and dissipate, Phlp.in GC146.37, cf. Olymp.in Mete.278.18:—Pass., Pall.in Hp.2.121 D., Phlp.in Ph.625.25

ἐκδιδάσκω.definition: poet. aor. Pi.P.4.217:—teach; c. acc. pers. et inf., to teach one to be so and so, Id.El.395, cf. Ant.298; Ar.Ra.1026: with inf. omitted, ib.1019

ἐκδιδράσκω.definition: Ion. fut. aor. E.Heracl.14 , D.C.37.47; part. Hdt.4.148, Ar.Ec.55:—run away, escape, Hdt.3.4, cf. 9.88, etc.; Ar.V.126: abs., Id.Ec.55, Th.1.126

ἐκδιδύσκω.definition: = strip, despoil, LXX1 Ki.31.8; plunder, J.BJ2.14.2

ἐκδίδωμι.definition: give out of one's house; give one's daughter in marriage, Hdt.1.196, E.IA132 , cf. Thphr.Char.22.4; having provided for their marriage at their own expense, D.27.69; D.S.4.53; freq. also without any acc., give in marr…

ἐκδιηγέομαι.definition: tell in detail, Hp.Prog.1, Arist.Rh.Al.1434b4, Ph.2.118, LXXJb.12.8, etc

ἐκδικάζω.definition: pf. OGI7.3 :—Med., fut; avenge, .. E.Supp.1215, cf. 154

ἐκδικαιόομαι.definition: fut. = III, Keil- Premerstein Dritter Bericht 117 ; conduct legal proceedings, AJA16.14

ἐκδικέω.definition: avenge, punish, Ctes.Fr.37; 2; decide a case, Ph.2.432, POxy.1020.6

ἐκδίκησις.definition: avenging, to give satisfaction, Plb.3.8.10; obtain it from.., CIG2826 ; legal remedy, PLond.5.1674.102 ; avenge him, Act.Ap.7.24; Ev.Luc.18.7,8

ἐκδικία.definition: decision of a case, D.C.38.7; office of II.3, CIG2719 , 2771 , POxy.901.3 ; BMus.Inscr. 481*.219

ἔκδικος.definition: lawless, unjust, A.Pr.1093; maintaining the right, avenging, Batr.97; AP12.35 , cf. LXXWi.12.12

ἐκδιφρεύω.definition: throw from a chariot, in Pass., Luc.DDeor.25.3, Electr.2

ἐκδιψάω.definition: to be parched with drought, of plants, Thphr.CP5.9.3; of a person, to be very thirsty, Plu.Cleom.29

ἐκδιώκω.definition: chase away, banish, Th.1.24; Arist.HA618b12; Luc.Tim.10; attack, persecute, PMasp.2 iii4 , etc.:—Pass., Hyp.Fr.238

ἐκδονέω.definition: shake utterly, confound, in Pass., .. AP11.64

ἐκδόσιμος.definition: contracted for, let out, Poll.7.200; certificate of delivery of a document, service of summons, etc., POxy.34vii6 , etc

ἔκδοσις.definition: Arc. IG5.6.16; —giving up; giving in marriage, dowering, Id.Lg.924d, cf. Arist.Pol.13352 22; D.44.66

ἐκδότης.definition: one who farms out contracts or taxes; one who gives his daughter in marriage, POxy.497.15

ἔκδοτος.definition: given up, delivered, esp. betrayed; given in marriage, PMasp.5.10

ἐκδοχεύς.definition: forwarding agent, PEdgar5.11 , OGI140.8 , Ptol.Tetr.179, POxy.1669.2

ἐκδοχή.definition: Arc. IG 5.6.40; —receiving from; receiving, containing, J.BJ5.4.3, cf. Paul. Aeg.6.106

ἐκδρακοντόομαι.definition: Pass., become a very serpent, A.Ch.549

ἐκδρομάς.definition: one who has outrun the age of youth, Eub.11, cf. Eust.1915.20

ἐκδρομή.definition: running out, sally, charge, X.HG3.2.4; abstr. for concrete, party of skirmishers, Th.4.127

ἔκδρομος.definition: one that runs out : skirmishers, Th.4.125, X.HG4.5.16

ἐκδυάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be conjoined, Phld. Herc.1003

ἐκδυσωπέω.definition: put to shame, Hld.8.3; J.BJ1.2.2; Id.AJ15.4.1

ἐκδύω.definition: causal in pres. impf. fut. aor. 1 late pf. AP5.72 :— take off, strip off, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, they stripped me of my cloak, Od.14.341; .. A.Ag.1269; X.Cyr.1.3.17; c. acc. only, strip, D.24.204; Id.54.8

ἐκδωριεύομαι.definition: Pass., become a thorough Dorian, Hdt.8.73

ἔκζεμα.definition: a cutaneous eruption, eczema, Dsc.1.43 , Erot. s.v. , Gp.1.12.19

ἔκζεσις.definition: boiling out or over, breaking out; = foreg., Erot. s.v

ἔκζεσμα.definition: = Archig. ap. Gal.12.468 , Crito ap. eund.12.485

ἐκζέω.definition: boil out or over : break out, in disease; c. gen., bred worms, Hdt.4.205; c. dat., D.L.4.4; c. acc., LXXEx.16.20; of a country, ib.1 Ki.6.1

ἐκζητέω.definition: seek out, Aristid.1.488 J., PMag. Osl.1.354; demand an account of, LXX2 Ki.4.11, al., cf. Ev.Luc.11.50

ἐκζωόομαι.definition: Pass., become full of worms, Thphr.CP4.8.4

ἑκηβολία.definition: Ep. skill in archery, Il.5.54 : later in sg., Call.Ap.99,Str.8.3.33, AP6.26

ἐκθάλλω.definition: put forth blossoms, Sm.Ca.2.13, Al.Hb.3.17; metaph., become active, of heat in the ground, Adam. ap. Aët.3.163

ἐκθάλπω.definition: warm thoroughly, metaph. in Pass., Phryn.PSp.71 B., cj. in S.Fr.474

ἐκθαμβέω.definition: to be amazed, Orph.A.1218; trans., amaze, astonish, LXXSi.30.9; —Pass., Ev.Marc.9.15, Gal.16.493

ἐκθαρρέω.definition: strengthd. for have full confidence, Plu.Rom.26; to be encouraged, Id.Galb.7

ἐκθαυμάζω.definition: strengthd. for Aristeas312, D.H.Th.34, Longin.44.8; LXXSi.27.23; Ev.Marc.12.17

ἐκθεάομαι.definition: see out, see to the end, S.OT1253; Pass., to be made visible, prob. for in Ph.1.96

ἐκθεατρίζω.definition: bring out on the stage, metaph. in Pass., Ath.11.506f; in bad sense, make a public show of, Plb.11.8.7; expose to public shame, Id.3.91.10, etc

ἐκθειάζω.definition: make a god of, deify, Luc.Tox.2, S.E.M.9.35; of things, treat or regard as supernatural, Plu.Sert.11, Hdn.1.14.6

ἐκθειόω.definition: make a god of, worship as such, Pass., to be deified, D.H.2.75; Plu.2.856e

ἐκθεόω.definition: = , Ael.NA10.23, Porph.Marc.17; of temples or places, consecrate, App.BC3.3

ἐκθεραπεύω.definition: cure perfectly, Plb.3.88.1, Agath.1.15; —Med., get oneself quite cured, Hp.Vict.3.83

ἐκθερίζω.definition: reap or mow completely, of a crop; cut out, Anacreont.9.7

ἐκθερμαίνω.definition: strengthd. for warm thoroughly; cause to evaporate by heat, Arist.Pr.870a17 : metaph., Plu.2.48c

ἔκθερμος.definition: very hot, Vett.Val.162.23, Gal.4.490, Aspasia ap. Aët.16.22

ἔκθεσις.definition: exposure, of a child, Hdt.1.116; setting forth, exposition, Arist.APr.48a25, 49b6

ἔκθετος.definition: sent out of the house, sent away; projecting, salient, Sor.1.68; opp. Heliod.ap. Orib.49.4.23

ἐκθέω.definition: run out; make a sally, Ar.Lys.456; X.HG3.1.7; of javelins, fly out, Plu.Marc.16; rush, hurry out, Arist.EN1149a28

ἐκθηλάζω.definition: suck the breast, LXXIs.66.11; —Pass., Hp.Mul.1.73; to be sucked out, Arist.HA587b27

ἐκθήλυνσις.definition: becoming soft, relaxation, Hp.Aph.5.16, cf.Art.52; —also Nic.Fr.135

ἐκθηλύνω.definition: aor. D.H.7.9; —soften, weaken; Gramm., make a feminine of, EM473.35

ἐκθηράομαι.definition: hunt out, catch, X.Cyn.5.25, Plu.Pomp.26; .. Max.Tyr.31.3

ἐκθηριόω.definition: make savage, Ph.Fr.98 H.; Longus1.20:— Pass., become quite wild or savage, Ph.1.430, Iamb.Protr.5; also, assume animal shape, E.Ba.1331

ἐκθλίβω.definition: squeeze out, Arist.HA578b4, 626a20; Pass., to be crowded, cramped, of troops, X.An.3.4.19

ἔκθλιψις.definition: squeezing out, Hp.Aph.7.85; affliction, distress, LXXEz.12.18

ἐκθνῄσκω.definition: fut. aor. —die away; to be in a death-like swoon, Hp.Epid.5.42, cf. Philem.1.6 D.; opp. Pl.Lg.959a; opp. Arist.HA521a11, cf.Pr.962b4:—so in S.Tr.568 may retain its usual sense, fainting away, at the point of death

ἐκθόρνυμαι.definition: later .28) collat. form for M.Ant.8.51; start up from sleep, Aret.SA2.9

ἐκθροέω.definition: speak out loud, Poll.6.207; Pass., to be startled out of, Gal.16.221

ἐκθρομβόω.definition: clear from clots, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.2.10; Paul.Aeg.6.60

ἐκθρόμβωσις.definition: coagulation, Dsc.1.128.7; curdling of milk, Gal.14.142

ἐκθρῴσκω.definition: fut. aor. out of,c.gen., Il.16.427; 7.182, cf. 23.353; A.Pers.457; of the violent beating of the heart, 11.10.95; abs., leap forth, 21.539, cf. Corn.ND19; rarely c.acc., AP9.371; start up, Luc.DMar.2.3; come from the …

ἐκθυελλόω.definition: carry away as by a storm, Moschio Hyp.1

ἐκθυμαίνω.definition: strengthd. for aor. Ant.Lib.7.4; fut. Phld.Ir.p.16W

ἐκκράζω.definition: cry out, cj. in S.Fr.722; Plu.Mar.44; D.C.66.15

ἐκλάμπω.definition: shine or beam forth, Hdt.6.82, A.Pr.1083; to be distinguished, Plu.Cic.2; Lib.Or.62.37

ἐκλατομέω.definition: hew in stone, LXXNu.21.18; hew or hollow; quarry stones from, Jul.Gal.135c

ἐκλαχαίνω.definition: dig or hollow out, A.R.1.374, Tryph.208

ἐκλεαίνω.definition: smooth out or away, Pl.Smp.191a; smooth or polish off, Agatharch.82; smooth them down, Plu.2.83c

ἐκλέγω.definition: fut. Pass. IG12.76.16; pf. Pass; Lit. Crit., select, D.H.Comp.3; cf

ἐκλειόω.definition: rub down or to pieces, Alex.Trail.7.5, Steph.in Hp.1.156D

ἐκλεκτέος.definition: to be picked out, selected; one must select, ib.412d, Arist.APr.43b6, Sor.1.78

ἐκλεκτόω.definition: in Pass., to be separated, i.e.purified, LXXIs.52.11

ἐκλέπισις.definition: taking off the shell: hatching, Suid. s.v

ἐκλεπυρόω.definition: strip off the bark: metaph., strip, Sophr.22

ἐκλογεύς.definition: collector of first-fruits, taxes, etc., IG12.76.14; Lys.Fr.9, IG12.1001.14 , Ph.2.33, al

ἐκλογή.definition: choice, selection, Pl.R.414a; levying of troops, Plb.5.63.11

ἔκλογος.definition: balance of accounts, PLond.1.131.6 , etc; picked out, choice, Ph.2.479,539

ἐκλοφίζω.definition: quarry from a hill, Anon. ap. Suid.s.v

ἐκλοχεύω.definition: bring forth, Orph.A.129, AP9.602 :—so in Med., E.Hel.[258]: metaph., Orph.A.43:—Pass., to be born, E.Ion1458

ἐκλοχίζω.definition: pick out of a cohort or troop, LXXCa.5.10

ἐκλυτήριος.definition: bringing release, S.OT392: expiatory offering, E.Ph.969

ἔκλυτος.definition: easy to let go, light, buoyant, of; let loose, unbridled, Ti.Locr.102e; lascivious, Lyd.Mag.3.65; unlimited, extreme, Timocl.13.3; Olymp.in Mete.198.12
