ἐκμασάομαι.definition: chew completely, in aor. Pass. Ph.1.334

ἐκμάσσω.definition: wipe dry, Hp.Acut.65 , cf. Herod.6.9; of bees, Arist.HA624b1

ἐκμαστεύω.definition: track out, A.Eu.247, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.9

ἐκμεθύσκω.definition: make quite drunk: metaph., .. over-charge them with moisture, Thphr.CP5.15.3; AP5.3

ἐκμειλίσσω.definition: soften, Gal.11.317; mostly Med., appease, Corn.ND21, App.BC1.97, Plu.2.380c, D.C.79.19, Conon18

ἐκμείρομαι.definition: obtain for one's lot, aor. 2 Nic.Th.791; Od.5.335

ἐκμελαίνομαι.definition: to be darkened, grow dark, Heraclit.All.39; ib.45

ἐκμελετάω.definition: train or teach carefully; learn perfectly, con over, practise, Antipho3.2.7, Pl.Hp.Ma.286d; Men.715

ἐκμεταλλεύω.definition: empty of ore or metal, Str.14.5.28

ἐκμετρέω.definition: measure out, measure, E.IA816; Id.Fr.382; to end life, to die, Tz.H.3.800: abs., measure a distance, LXXDe.21.2:—freq. in Med., measure for oneself, measure out, .. measuring, calculating its position by the stars , S…

ἐκμέτρησις.definition: measurement, Plb.5.98.10, BGU432 ii 10 , measurer, surveyor, PAmh.2.79.16 , etc

ἔκμετρος.definition: out of measure, measureless, S.Fr.353, cf. Man.4.464,626; of a verse, exceeding the due length, Luc.Pr.Im.18

ἐκμηρύομαι.definition: wind off like a ball of thread; intr., of the army, defile, X.An.6.5.22; Plb.3.53.5

ἐκμιαίνω.definition: pollute thoroughly, defile, Opp.H.4.663; —Pass., ejaculate semen, Hp.Superf.31, Ar.Ra.753, LXXLe.18.20

ἐκμιμέομαι.definition: imitate faithfully, represent exactly, E.HF1298, Ar.Av.1285, X.Mem.3.10.1, Duris89 J

ἐκμισθόω.definition: let out for hire, X.Vect.3.14; Lys.7.4; SIG1044.30 , etc.: c. inf., Aeschin.1.13; —Med., contract for, Them.Or.4.53a

ἐκμορφόω.definition: represent, express in form, Plu.2.537d; bring into shape, Ael.NA2.19

ἐκμουσόω.definition: strengthd. for teach fully, E.Ba.825; — Pass., Ael.VH14.34

ἐκμοχθέω.definition: work out with toil; struggle through, Id.IT1455, cf. A.Pr.825, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11

ἐκμοχλεύω.definition: lift out with a lever, Hp.Art.72 ; to force them open with crow- bars, Ar.Lys.429; generally, force, compel, Plu.2.662c; dislodge, Gal.7.195, cf. Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.22; Olymp.in Grg.p.143J

ἐκμυελίζω.definition: suck the marrow out of, deprive of strength, LXXNu.24.8

ἐκμυζάω.definition: suck out, Il.4.218, cf. Luc.Tim.8, Ael.NA3.39, Gal.UP6.15, Q.S.4.398; exhaust air from a vessel, HeroSpir. I Praef.: metaph., extort, Lyd.Mag.3.67; —also in form Dsc.Eup.1.62, Phlp.in Mete.115.18; —Pass., Antyll. ap. …

ἐκμυθόω.definition: make into a or fable, Philostr.Im.1.3

ἐκμυκτηρίζω.definition: hold in derision, mock at, LXXPs.2.4, Ev.Luc.16.14

ἐκμύσσομαι.definition: Med., blow the nose, read by Gal. for in Hp.Nat. Hom.7

ἐκναρκάω.definition: become quite torpid or sluggish, Plu.Cor.31

ἐκνέμω.definition: pasture, Ph.2.233; —more freq. in Med; go forth to feed: metaph. in Med., S.Aj.369

ἐκνευρίζω.definition: cut the sinews, Plu.2.451d; broken down, enfeebled, D.3.31; Plu.2.755c, cf. Ph.1.258, al.; exhausted soil, Id.2.434

ἐκνεύω.definition: aor. turn the head out of its natural; c. acc., shun, avoid, Phld.Sign.27, Ph.1.146, Orph.A.458; Hegesias ap.D.H.Comp.18; D.S.17.100

ἐκνεφίας.definition: a hurricane, caused by; rain with sunshine, Hp. ap. Gal.19.96; seen through clouds, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.9.1, cf. Philostr.Gym.58

ἐκνέω.definition: fut. aor. I pf. Men.Epit.355:—swim out, swim to land, E.Hipp.823; escape by swimming, Th.2.90; generally, escape, get safely through, Pi.O.13.114, E.Hipp.470, Men.l.c., E.IT1186

ἐκνηπιόω.definition: rear from childhood, Philostr.VS2.1.11; —Pass., to be reared, Id.VA5.14

ἐκνήφω.definition: fut. LXXGe.9.24; —sleep off a drunken fit; trans., carry off, LXXSi.34.2

ἐκνήχομαι.definition: aor. I Plb.38.16.12; pf. inf. Ath.7.315d; — = swim out or away, Plb.l.c.; .. Arist.Mu.398b32, Luc.DMar.8.2; Apollod.1.9.25; abs., Luc.Merc.Cond.2

ἐκνίζω.definition: wash out, purge away, E.IT1224; of; washed away, POxy.1469.6

ἐκνικάω.definition: achieve by force; c. acc., Ael.VH10.1; — Pass., Hld.5.23, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.9

ἐκνιτρόω.definition: cleanse with .. Alex.2.4, cf.IG7.3073.86 , Archig. ap. Gal.12.406

ἐκνοσηλεύω.definition: cure completely, Ph.1.631, Gal.10.522:—Pass., convalescents, Gal.6.726, Orib.3.15.7

ἐκξέω.definition: wipe off, erase, App. Anth.7.56,71, Tz.ad Lyc.874

ἑκουσιάζομαι.definition: offer or be offered freely, LXXJd.5.2; ib.1 Ma.2.42

ἑκουσιασμός.definition: free-will offering, ib.2 Es.7.16, Aq.Jd.5.2, etc

ἑκούσιος.definition: S.Tr.727,1123, etc.; also; rarely of persons, willing, acting of free will, S.Tr.1123; Th.1.138

ἐκπαγλέομαι.definition: to be struck with amazement, to wonder; wonder at, admire exceedingly, c. acc., A.Ch.217, E.Or.890, Tr.929; rarein Prose, D.H.1.40

ἔκπαγλος.definition: Ep. and Ion. word, terrible, violent; of persons, of Achilles, Il.21.589; also of Achilles, 1.146, 18.170; of other heroes, 20.389, 21.452

ἐκπαιδεύω.definition: bring up from childhood, ib.276; train; teach one a thing, J.Ap.2.29, D.C.45.2; but

ἐκπαίζω.definition: laugh to scorn, mock at, LXX1 Es.1.49, Phld.Rh.2.216S

ἐκπαιφάσσω.definition: rush madly to the fray, Il.5.803

ἐκπαίω.definition: throw or cast out of a thing; intr., dash out, escape, Anaxil.22.17 :—Med., Plu.Brut.51

ἐκπαλαίω.definition: transgress the laws of wrestling, Philostr.Im.1.6

ἐκπαλέω.definition: of a joint, start out of the socket, Hp.Fract.42, Art.55

ἐκπάλλω.definition: shake out:—Pass., spring or spurt out, .. Il.20.483; also Hsch

ἐκπαππόομαι.definition: Pass., of seeds, become plumous, Thphr.HP3.16.6, 6.4.8, Dsc.3.118

ἐκπαταγέω.definition: deafen, Them.Or.21.253c; but aor. I Hsch

ἐκπατάσσω.definition: strike, afflict, E.HF890 : metaph., AP9.309 :—Pass., stricken in mind, Od.18.327; Hsch

ἐκπατέω.definition: withdraw from society, D.L.1.112; pf. part. having finished his walk, Id.4.19

ἐκπάτιος.definition: out of the common path : excessive, A.Ag.49 ; expld. by Sch. as lonely. Adv. v.l. for in Hp.Mul.2.171

ἐκπαύω.definition: strengthd. for set quite at rest, put an end to, E.Ion144 :—Med., take one's rest, Th.5.75

ἐκπείθω.definition: persuade completely, over-persuade, S.OT1024, Tr.1141, E.HF469, PHal.7.6 , etc

ἐκπειράζω.definition: tempt, c. acc., LXXDe.6.16, al., 1 Ep.Cor.10.9

ἐκπειράομαι.definition: aor. make trial of; inquire, ask of another, Ar.Eq.1234.—Late in Act., Hld.7.19

ἐκπελεκάω.definition: hew, cut away with an axe, IG2.1054b9, Thphr.HP9.2.7, IG11.144A64

ἐκπέμπω.definition: bring out by calling, call or fetch out, Id.Ant.19:—so in Med., Id.OT951:—Pass., go forth, depart, Id.OC1664

ἐκπεπαίνω.definition: make quite ripe or mellow, Thphr.HP5.1.1, CP1.16.2:—Pass., Medic., to be concocted, Hp.Epid.4.56

ἐκπεραίνω.definition: finish off, A.Fr.78; E.HF428 :—Pass., of oracles, to be fulfilled, Id.Ion785, Cyc.696; of works, to be accomplished, X.An.5.1.13

ἐκπεράω.definition: abs., of an arrow, pass through, pierce, .. Il.13.652, cf. 16.346, etc.; of persons, go forth, X.Cyn.6.18; to Athens, Eub.10.5

ἐκπέρθω.definition: fut. destroy utterly, sack, of cities; take as booty from, Il.1.125

ἐκπεριάγω.definition: lead out round, Plb.3.83.3; tie behind the back, Lys. ap. Iamb.VP17.78:—Pass., to be passed round, Porph.Hist.Phil.Fr.4

ἐκπερίειμι.definition: go out and round, go all round, X.Cyn.6.10, dub. in Hld.7.19; Luc.Rh.Pr.5; Jul.Or.7.225c

ἐκπεριέρχομαι.definition: = foreg., Plb.10.31.3, Onos.22.4; surround, envelop, Hdn.3.3.8

ἐκπεριοδεύω.definition: go all round, ib.3.6.8; metaph., survey completely, Phld.Mort.37, S.E.M.7.188

ἐκπεριπλέω.definition: fut. to sail out round, so as to attack in flank, Plb.1.23.9; J.BJ3.10.9; circum-navigate, Arr.An.4.7.5: abs., ib.6.28.6; Plu.Aem.15:—Ion. Arr.Ind.20.1

ἐκπεριπορεύομαι.definition: make a detour, 'fetch a compass', of; march round, Ael.Tact.34.4

ἐκπερισπασμός.definition: an evolution consisting of a right- about-face followed by a wheel to r. or l., Plb.10.23.3, Ascl.Tact.10.8, etc

ἐκπερισπάω.definition: execute this manoeuvre, ib.12.7, Arr.Tact.32.1:—Pass., Ascl.Tact.10.11

ἐκπεριτρέχω.definition: run all about, Aristaenet.1.27; metaph., Procl.in Prm.p.781 S

ἐκπέσσω.definition: Att. cook thoroughly: hence; of animals, digest or concoct food thoroughly, Hp.VM22

ἐκπετάννυμι.definition: fut. spread out, of a sail; metaph., wholly given up to the revel, E.Cyc.497 : pf. part. Pass. wide open, Hp.VM22; of gaping wounds, Id.Off.11; Ael.NA2.12

ἐκπέτασμα.definition: that which is spread out or; planisphere, Ptol.Geog.7.7 tit

ἐκπέτομαι.definition: fut. Ar.V.208; aor. part. Id.Av.788; also E.El.944, Pl.Ti.81e, 20.249 : also in act. form Hes.Op.98, Batr.211, Ant.Lib.1.5, Palaeph.12; for aor. v. —fly out or away, ll. cc.: Luc.Rh.Pr.6

ἐκπήγνυμι.definition: make stiff or torpid, l.c.; esp. of frost, congeal, freeze, Thphr.CP5.14.2; —Pass., become stiff, congeal, Str.7.5.11; to be frozen, frost-bitten, Thphr.HP5.14.3

ἐκπηδάω.definition: fut. Luc.Zeux.8, App.Hisp.20; make a sally, X.An.7.4.16, App.l.c.; Hell.Oxy.16.2; escape, Men.Per.Fr.3, cf. Wilcken Chr.1 ii 13 , Plb.1.43.1; metaph., Pl.R.495d

ἐκπήδημα.definition: leap out, a height too great for over-leap, A.Ag.1376

ἐκπηνίζομαι.definition: fut. spin a long thread, Arist.Pr.947b2; metaph., of an advocate, will wind these things out of him, Ar.Ra.578

ἐκπιέζω.definition: oppress, LXX1 Ki.12.3; a form ib.Ez.22.29; —Pass., Plb.3.74.2

ἐκπίεσμα.definition: that which is squeezed out; false form for , Gal.19.432, 14.782

ἐκπικραίνομαι.definition: to be embittered, Nic.Dam.p.34 D; = sq. II, Hp.Mul.2.133

ἐκπικρόομαι.definition: become very bitter, Arist.Pr.880a29; have a bitter taste in the mouth, Hp.Aph.4.17

ἐκπίμπλημι.definition: fill up, E.Cyc.388; fulfil, fulfilled his destiny, Hdt.3.142; Id.1.43; to satisfy the requirements of the law, Id.1.199,4.117; paid the full penalty of the sin of Gyges, Id.1.91

ἐκπίνω.definition: fut. Amips.22.2; drain a cup dry, S.Fr.483; Pherecr.143.9; Antiph.3, etc.; also S.Ant.532

ἐκπιπράσκω.definition: sell off, pf. Pass. D.9.39, cf. Poll.7.9

ἐκπίπτω.definition: of seafaring men, to be cast ashore, Od.7.283; Hdt.3.138; Id.8.13; E.Hel.1211; ib.539; Pl.Lg.866d; of things, suffer shipwreck, X.An.7.5.13; of fish, to be cast up, Arist.HA601b32

ἐκπλανάω.definition: delude, cause to go astray, Hsch.s.v

ἐκπλάσσω.definition: model exactly, Chaerem.1.6; make into a plaster, Hippiatr.10

ἐκπλατύνω.definition: flatten out, Sor.1.102; broad at the top, Sch.Il.23.243

ἐκπλεθρίζω.definition: run round and round, in a course which narrows every time, Gal.6.133

ἐκπλέω.definition: fut. pf. IG2.793a7; Ion; metaph., go out of one's mind, lose one's senses, Id.3.155, Ael.Fr.240

ἔκπληκτος.definition: terrifying, Luc.Herm.18; amazed, terror-stricken, Orph.H.39.10, Man.4.81, Poll.5.72

ἐκπλημμυρέω.definition: gush out and overflow, Philostr.Jun.Im.4:—also ib.8

ἐκπληρόω.definition: make up to a certain number, Hdt.7.186; .. Id.8.82; making up the number of ten chariots, S.El.708; X.Cyr.5.3.24

ἐκπλήρωμα.definition: filling up, Hp.Art.9; pad or cushion to fill up, Id.Mochl.5

ἐκπλήρωσις.definition: filling up, Apollon.Cit.I; fulfilment of a cosmic cycle, Cat.Cod. Astr.1.163

ἐκπλήσσω.definition: Att. strike out of, drive away; drive out of one's senses by a sudden shock, amaze, astound, Od.18.231 ; Aeschin.1.134; .. Antipho2.1.7; Trag.Adesp.465; frightens me in speaking, E.Or.549:— in this sense most freq. in…

ἐκπλινθεύω.definition: take out bricks or tiles, Is.Fr.19S; turn into bricks, Jul.Gal.135b

ἐκπλίσσομαι.definition: gape, of a wound, Hp.Fract.25; of the womb, Id.Prorrh.2.24

ἐκπλύνω.definition: fut. IG7.3073.87 :—wash; wash out, i.e. wash thoroughly, Ar.Pl.1062; Id.Fr.686; SIG1025.35 ; IGl.c.:—Med., Hdt.4.73

ἔκπλυτος.definition: to be washed out, of colours; a kind of Gal.14.74

ἐκπνευματόω.definition: turn into vapour, Arist.Pr.866a3, Thphr; deflate, metaph., Plu.2.39d

ἐκπνέω.definition: breathe one's last, expire, A.Ag.1493 , E.Hel.142; Id.Or.1163; alone, S.Aj.1026; E.HF886 : abs., Id.Hyps.Fr.60i38, Parth.4.6: metaph., lose power, Gp.15.1.28; lose lustre, of pearls, PHolm.10.18

ἐκπνοή.definition: breathing out, exhalation, opp; death, J.AJ19.8.3

ἔκπνοος.definition: contr. breathless; breathing out, exhaling, Hp.Epid.6.6.1; smelling of.., Posidipp. ap.Ath.13.596c

ἐκποιέω.definition: put out a child, i.e. give him to be adopted by another, opp. D.C.60.33:—Pass., to be adopted, Is.7.25, cf. D.C.38.12

ἐκποίησις.definition: putting forth: emissio seminis; giving out a child in adoption, Poll.6.178, D.C.37.51

ἐκποκίζω.definition: Att. fut. pull out wool or hair, Ar.Th.567

ἐκπολεμέω.definition: go to war with, LXXDe.20.10, al

ἐκπολεμόω.definition: make hostile, involve in war, Hdt.4.120, Hell.Oxy. 2.2, 13.1, D.1.7,3.7, Plb.15.6.6; Th.6.77:— Pass., fut. Med. , become an enemy to, be set at feud with, Hdt.3.66, 5.73: abs., Th.8.57

ἐκπολίζω.definition: make into a city, in Pass., Aristid.Or.26.6

ἐκπολιορκέω.definition: force a besieged town to surrender, force to capitulate, Th.1.94,134, X.HG2.4.3, etc.: metaph. of argument, ChioEp.10:—Pass., to be forced to surrender, Th.1.117; ib.131, cf. Inscr.Prien.37.112; Arist.Ath.19.3: metaph…

ἐκπολιτεύω.definition: change the constitution of a state, cause it to degenerate, LXX4 Ma.4.19

ἐκπονέω.definition: work out, finish off, Sapph.98, Pi.P.4.236; practise, X.Cyr.5.1.30; Plb.4.20.12:—Med., Pl.Lg.834e:—Pass., of persons, to be in good training or practice, X.Cyr.3.3.57; Id.HG6.4.28

ἐκπορεύω.definition: make to go out, fetch out, E.Ph.1068, HF723:—Med., with fut. Med. and aor. Pass., go out or forth, march out, X.l.c., etc.; Aen.Tact.24.4; to march out to a place.., Plb.11.9.4: c. acc. loci, ib.8; but Id.6.58.4; LXXP…

ἐκπορθμεύω.definition: carry away by sea:—E. has pf. Pass. in pass. sense, Hel.1179; but in med. sense, ib.1517

ἐκπορίζω.definition: invent, contrive, E.Ba.1042; discharge a cargo, OGI 521.27,30

ἐκπορνεύω.definition: commit fornication, LXXGe.38.24; metaph., of idolatry, LXXEx.34.15

ἐκπόρπισις.definition: lit., unfastening, hence of a compound fracture, Sor.Fract.24

ἐκποτάομαι.definition: Ion. = fly out or forth, of snowflakes, Il.19.357; of a ghost, Sapph.68.4: metaph., Theoc.11.72, 2.19

ἐκπράσσω.definition: Att. bring about, achieve; exact, levy, Id.HF43; SIG 554.19 ; ib.672.39 : c. dupl. acc., Th.8.108: abs., Pl.Lg.774e, cf. IG12.79:—Pass., to be made to pay, Paus.7.12.1

ἐκπρεπής.definition: distinguished out of all, pre-eminent; of things, = extraordinary, Th.3.55. Adv. without reasonable grounds, Id.1.38: Sup. X.Smp.8.31

ἐκπρέπω.definition: to be excellent in a thing, E.Heracl.597

ἔκπρισμα.definition: that which is sawn out, Arist.GC316a34; section sawn out of cylinder, HeroDef.97

ἐκπρίω.definition: fut. Men.Epit.41:—saw off, Th.7.25, Men.l.c.; excise, Hp.VC21; of bonds, Herod.5.25

ἐκπροθεσμέω.definition: to be later than the appointed day, Ulp. ad D.21.80

ἐκπρόθεσμος.definition: beyond the appointed day, for the debt, Luc.Herm.80; after seven days have expired, Id.Sat.2; past the time of, i.e. too old for, the games, Id.Anach.39; honours deferred till too late, Id.Nav.40; Ph.2.169

ἐκπροθρῴσκω.definition: spring out or forth, aor. part. Orph.A.346, Man.6.33; Max.226

ἐκπροκαλέομαι.definition: call forth to oneself; invoke, Orph.H.7.1

ἐκπροφεύγω.definition: flee away from, Hld.8.11; escape, Orph.L.397; AP6.218

ἐκπτερόομαι.definition: to be furnished with wings, Hp.Vict.1.25

ἐκπτοέω.definition: = Tz.H.5.484:—Pass., to be struck; to be scared, Plb.5.36.3,14.5.7

ἐκπτύσσω.definition: unfold, spread out, pf. part. Pass. prob. for Erot. s.v

ἐκπτύω.definition: fut. AP5.196 :—spit out; spit in token of disgust, Ar.V.792

ἐκπτώσσω.definition: to be in fear of, Man.5.237

ἐκπυέω.definition: suppurate, Hp.Epid.1.20, Prog.15,Epid.2.1.7:—Med., Id.Aph.7.38, Fract.27:—Pass., Id.Aph.6.20

ἐκπύημα.definition: sore that has suppurated, Id.VM22,Prog.15, Coac.278

ἐκπυΐσκομαι.definition: Pass., = Id.Prog.15, v.l. ib.22:— later in Act., Gal.11.728

ἐκπυρηνίζω.definition: squeeze out the stone: generally, squeeze out, Arist.Ph.214a33, Steph.in Hp.1.82 D.:—Pass., Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.119, de An.132.29

ἐκπυρήνισις.definition: squeezing out, Olymp.in Mete.38.25, Mich.in PN117.15

ἔκπυρος.definition: burning hot, Str.15.1.26, v.l. in Hdt.4.73; Sor.2.54: metaph., Poll.1.192: neut. pl. as Adv., AP5.81

ἐκπυρόω.definition: burn to ashes, consume utterly, E.IA1070; set on fire, Arist.Mete.341a18

ἐκπυρσεύω.definition: kindle, inflame: metaph., in Pass; give signals by a beacon-light, J.BJ4.10.5

ἐκπύρωσις.definition: conflagration, Str.12.8.18; Philos., conversion into fire, Zeno Stoic.1.32, Chrysipp. ib.2.131, etc.; Epicur.Ep.2p.45U

ἔκπωμα.definition: drinking-cup, beaker, Hdt.9.41,80, S.Ph.35, Th.6.32, IG2.649.13, etc.:—Dim. Diph.19, Str.16.2.25

ἐκπωματοποιός.definition: cup-maker, name of a play by Alexis, Ath.15.691d

ἐκραβδίζω.definition: flog out, drive out with a rod, Ar.Lys.576

ἐκραίνω.definition: scatter out of, make to fall in drops from, S.Tr.781; E.Cyc.402: metaph., dub. in Plb.8.6.3

ἐκρέω.definition: pf. : aor. Pass. in; of feathers, fall off, Ar.Av.104; of hair,Arist.HA518a32

ἐκρήγνυμι.definition: fut. S.Aj.775:—break off, snap; c. acc. cogn., let break forth, break out with, Plu.Fab.12; Luc.Cal.23:—Pass., break out, of an ulcer, Hdt.3.133; burst, of an abscess, Hp.Aph.4.82; .. A.Pr.369; of a quarrel, broke out…

ἔκρηξις.definition: breaking out, discharge; bursting asunder, Arist.Mu.395a15

ἐκρήσσω.definition: = TheanoEp.6.4 ; cause an abscess to burst, Paul.Aeg.7.1

ἔκριζος.definition: neut. as Adv., by the roots, Et.Gud

ἐκριζόω.definition: root out, LXXJe.1.10, al., Aesop.179, Ev.Matt.13.29:—Pass., LXXWi.4.4, Babr.36.8, etc.; IG12.405.24 ; in a form of execration, ib.3.1424

ἐκριπίζω.definition: fan the flame, light up, Arist.Mete.346a9; blow away, Aristid.Or.26.99

ἐκριπτέω.definition: = sq., f.l. for Plu.2.654e:—Pass., Agatharch.48, Lib.Decl.31.33

ἐκρίπτω.definition: Pass., to be spread abroad, LXXJd.15.9

ἐκροιβδέω.definition: empty by gulping down, in Pass., Mnesim.4.17

ἐκρομβέω.definition: displace air, of a falling weight, Ph.Bel.69.19

ἐκροφέω.definition: drink out, gulp down, cj. in Ar.Eq.701, cf. Pl.Com.149, Arist.HA612a30; swill, Jul.Caes.318c: metaph., Ar.V.1118

ἐκρύομαι.definition: deliver, E.Ba.258,Fr.190, A.R.4.83 : c. gen., Lyc.190

ἐκρύπτω.definition: wash or rinse out, Poll.1.44,7.39:—Med., Ph.1.613

ἐκσαλάσσω.definition: shake violently, AP5.234 , v.l. in Theoc.2.85

ἐκσαλεύω.definition: = foreg., Sammelb.4324.16, Hsch.s.v. shake out, Suid

ἐκσαόω.definition: Ep. for Il.4.12; Od.4.501; v.l. in Archil.6; A.R.1.10

ἐκσαρκίζομαι.definition: Pass., have the flesh stripped off, LXXEz.24.4

ἐκσαρκόω.definition: make grow to flesh:—Pass., grow to flesh; intr., = Pass., Dsc.Eup.1.75:—hence fleshy excrescence, Id.5.74

ἐκσάρκωσις.definition: formation of such an excrescence, Gal.13.317

ἐκσβέννυμι.definition: in pf. part. intr. run dry at the source, Hsch.s.v

ἐκσείω.definition: shake out or off; drive out or forth, Plu.Ant.14; reject it, D.S.18.66

ἐκσεύομαι.definition: Pass., pf. plpf. with sense of impf. , but usu. aor. : aor. I out or burst forth from, Il.7.1; Od.9.373; sleep fled away from his eyelids, 12.366: abs., rush out, Il.8.58; .. Od.9.438; the point burst out, Il.5.293 ; …

ἐκσηκόω.definition: weigh in the balance, assay, in Pass., Gloss

ἐκσήπομαι.definition: to be or become quite rotten, Hp.Aff.5, Thphr.CP5.16.2

ἐκσιγάομαι.definition: to be put to silence, AP7.182

ἐκσιφωνίζω.definition: emply by a siphon : metaph., drain, in Pass., LXXJb.5.5

ἐκσιωπάω.definition: put to silence, in Pass., Plb.28.4.13; intr., to be quite silent, Arr.An.6.4.5

ἐκσκάπτω.definition: dig out, PTeb.50.23 ; POxy.1758.10 :—Pass., to be hollowed out, Gal.18.618

ἐκσπένδω.definition: pour out as a libation, E.Ion1193, Eub.71

ἐκσπερματίζω.definition: semen emitto, of a woman, conceive, LXXNu.5.28

ἐκσπερματόω.definition: convert into semen, Steph.in; Pass., run to seed, Thphr.HP7.1.7

ἐκσπογγίζω.definition: wipe off with a sponge, Eub.83, Aen.Tact.31.13

ἐκσπονδυλίζω.definition: or break the vertebrae, LXX4 Ma.11.18: condemned by EM324.44

ἐκστέφω.definition: take off the crown : empty a full cup, opp; deck with garlands, E.Alc.171; esp. of suppliants, Id.HF526; but with garlands on the suppliant olive-branches, S.OT3, cf. 19

ἐκστραγγίζω.definition: squeeze or strain out, v.l. in LXXEz.23.34, Dsc.4.150

ἐκστρατεία.definition: going out on service, Luc.Gall.25, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. D.C.41.39

ἐκστράτευμα.definition: expeditionary force, Memn.15: metaph. of Nature, Steph.in Hp.2.418 D

ἐκστρατεύσιμος.definition: fit to take the field, Sch.Th.6.30

ἐκστρατεύω.definition: march out, Th.5.54; in Med., abs., take the field, Hdt.1.190; Id.4.159: pf. Pass., to be in the field, Th.2.12; And.1.45

ἐκστρατοπεδεύομαι.definition: encamp outside, Th.4.129, X.Cyr.6.3.1:— later in Act., J.BJ3.7.5

ἐκστρέφω.definition: turn inside out, Ar.Pl.721: metaph., change or alter entirely, Id.Nu.88; ib.554:—Pass., with feet turned outwards, Arist.Phgn.813a14; to be distorted, Gal.7.27

ἐκστροφόω.definition: force a door from its hinges, Hsch.s.v

ἐκσυριγγόομαι.definition: Pass., of an abscess, discharge itself by a fistulous opening, Hp.Coac.389

ἐκσυρίζω.definition: Att. fut. LXXSi.22.1; hiss loudly, D.C.l.c

ἐκσύρω.definition: sweep away, in aor. Pass. AP9.56

ἐκσφενδονάω.definition: throw as from a sling, Hld.9.5, Mich.in PN93.32

ἐκσφραγίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be shut out from; to be sealed, of a contract, BCH35.43

ἐκσφράγισμα.definition: official copy, CIG3276 , cf. IGRom.4.513 , POxy.1882 : generally, Mich.in PN20.10

ἐκσχίζω.definition: cleave asunder:—Pass., to be divided, Arist.Mu.400b4, Mir.846a14

ἐκσῴζω.definition: Ep. :—preserve from danger, keep safe, Hdt.9.107, S.Aj.1128, etc.; E.El.28; to bring him safe.., Id.HF1222; Pl.Grg.486b:—Med., save oneself, Hdt.2.107; also, save for oneself, .. A.Pers.360; S.Ant.713:—Pass., .. when …

ἐκτάδιος.definition: also Opp.C.3.276:— outstretched, .. double, with ample folds, Il.10.134; Orph.A.359; D.P.643

ἐκταλαντόομαι.definition: to be stripped of money, Sopat.19

ἐκταμιεύομαι.definition: dispense, Agatharch.102; receive from store, PRein.15.16, al

ἐκτανύω.definition: = Theoc.25.270:—Hom. has; extend, Epigr.Gr.1078.4 .— For S.OC1562, v. word, used by Hp.Fract.43. usu., but Anacreont.35.5 .]

ἐκταράσσω.definition: Att. throw into confusion; in Pass. also, to have a bowel-complaint, Hp.Aph.4.60, Epid.1.15

ἐκτάσσω.definition: Att. draw out in battle-order, of; keep muster-roll of, LXX4 Ki.25.19

ἐκταφρεύω.definition: to dig trenches, in Pass., J.BJ5.2.2, App.BC3.65, Hsch

ἐκτείνω.definition: fut. A.Pr.325, etc.:—stretch out; stretch, spread out a net, A.Ch.991; extend the line of an army, E.Heracl.801, Arr.Tact.5.6; E.Supp.654; X.HG6.5.19:—Pass., to be unfolded, smoothed, S.Fr.902

ἐκτειχίζω.definition: Att. fut. fortify completely, Th.7.26, X.HG3.2.10, etc.:—Pass., Ar.Av.1165

ἐκτεκμαίρομαι.definition: aor. I part. Pass. to be made out by guessing, Orac. ap. Eus.PE5.23

ἐκτελειόω.definition: or bring to perfection, Thphr.CP4.1.5, etc.; Plu.Publ.23

ἐκτελευτάω.definition: bring to an end, accomplish, Pi.P.12.29; intr. in Act., turn out, A.Supp.411

ἐκτελέω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.9.493, Od.4.7: Ep; of Time, Hes.Op.565, Hdt.6.69, Pi.P.4.104:—Pass., Od.11.294

ἐκτελής.definition: brought to an end, perfect, A.Pers.218; of corn, ripe, Hes.Op.466; also of persons, E.Ion780, cf. A.Ag.105 . Adv. in full, completely, BGU1116.9

ἐκτέμνω.definition: Ep. and Ion. , fut; cut trees out of a wood, cut down, Il.12.149, S.Tr.1196; also of planks, etc., hew out, hew into shape, Il.3.62, cf. 4.486; to cut the stumps out of the ground, Lys.7.19

ἐκτένεια.definition: zeal, assiduousness, Molpis3, PPetr.3p.18; abundance, Hdn.7.2.4, cf.8.2.6

ἐκτενής.definition: strained: hence of persons, warmly; extended, Dam.Pr.64; capable of extension, Herm.in Phdr.p.121A

ἐκτεφρόω.definition: burn to ashes, calcine, in Pass., Str.5.4.9, Dsc.1.68.4, 5.81, Plu.2.696b: metaph., of bile, Alex.Trall.Febr.7

ἐκτεχνολογέω.definition: set forth in technical language, reduce to system, Phld.Rh.1.203S

ἐκτήκω.definition: fut. E.Or.134:—melt out; metaph., let melt, pine or waste away, E.Or.134, cf. 529; Id.Hel.1419; Pl.R.411b; Critias6.12 D.; Plu.Lyc.5; Id.Brut.23; Ael.NA10.41

ἐκτίθημι.definition: set up, offer for a prize, S.Fr.378; Plb.15.9.4; fix or grant allowances, rates of pay, etc., PSI5.498 , PEdgar2.4 , etc

ἐκτίκτω.definition: aor. 2 Arist.HA621b20: pf. Pl.Tht.210b:—bring forth, Arist.HA571b11, al.; of fish, spawn, ib.547a2, 621b20: metaph., Pl.l.c

ἐκτίλλω.definition: fut. Hsch. s.v. aor. inf; pluck, strip bare, Hippon.84; D.53.16

ἐκτιναγμός.definition: shaking out, violent shaking, LXXNa.2.10, Ph.1.415; perh. winnowing or threshing, PFay.114.22

ἐκτινάσσω.definition: shake out, in cleaning; shake off, Ev.Matt.10.14, etc.:—Med., Act.Ap.13.51

ἐκτίννυμι.definition: = sq., v.l. in D.S.16.29, J.BJ3.8.5, Hermog.Inv.2.3, etc.: Cyr

ἐκτίνω.definition: Med., exact full payment for a thing, avenge, E.HF547; take vengeance on, Id.Med.267

ἐκτιτράω.definition: fut. bore through:—Pass., Orib.46.20.10: pf. Pass. HeroBel.96.2, part. Poll.2.70

ἐκτιτρώσκω.definition: bring forth untimely, D.S.3.64, 4.2; abs., miscarry, Hdt.3.32, Hp.Aph.3.12, Arist.HA585a22:—so in Med., Hp.Aër.10

ἐκτλάω.definition: bear, sustain to the end, aor.inf. Ph.2.464

ἔκτμημα.definition: section, segment, of the zones, Arist.Mete.362b5

ἐκτοιχωρυχέω.definition: break into a house and rob it: generally, pillage, plunder, Plb.4.18.8; Id.18.55.2

ἐκτοκίζω.definition: lend at interest, BGU1246.24; make to bring forth, Sm.Is.66.9

ἑκτολογέομαι.definition: to be subject to a tax of one- sixth of the produce, Arch.Pap.5.392

ἐκτολυπεύω.definition: wind off a ball of wool: metaph., bring to an end, Hes.Sc.44; . . A.Ag.1032

ἐκτομάς.definition: wicket-gate, Aen.Tact.24.5; a kind of spear , Id

ἐκτομή.definition: cutting out, excision, Plu.Alc.16; castration, Hdt.3.48,49, Pl.Smp.195c , etc

ἐκτομίας.definition: one that is castrated, eunuch, Hdt.3.92; Id.6.9; Arist.Pr.897b27; Antiph.133.5

ἔκτομον.definition: black hellebore, Hp.Mul.1.78; stone forming interior angle, Rev.Phil.29.240 , 49.6

ἐκτοξεύω.definition: shoot out, shoot away; metaph., reject, banish, Ph.1.528:—Pass., ib.252

ἐκτοπίζω.definition: remove from a place, PTeb.38.18 (ii B.C; metaph., pervert into a fable, Str.4.1.7

ἐκτόπισις.definition: removal from a place, deportation, Gloss

ἐκτοπισμός.definition: being away, distance, Str.4.5.5, prob. in Cic.Att.12.12.1

ἔκτοπος.definition: away from a place, c. gen; foreign, strange, by no strange hand, S.Tr.1132

ἐκτραγῳδέω.definition: deck out in tragic phrase, exaggerate; declaim tragically, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.18; simply, declaim, Ath.9.403d

ἐκτραχηλίζω.definition: Att. fut. prop. of a horse, throw; metaph., ruin, pervert, D.9.51, Luc.Rh.Pr.10, Alciphr.3.40, Porph.Abst.1.42; Mich.in EN523.20:—Pass., Ph.Fr.102 H

ἐκτραχύνω.definition: metaph., exasperate, Plu.Alc.14; App.BC2.12:—Pass., Plu.Arat.49: abs., App.BC1.10

ἐκτρέπω.definition: Ion. turn out of the course; turn a person off the road, order him out of the way, S.OT806:—Pass. and Med., get out of one's way, D.19.225, cf. Ar.Pl.837, Luc.Tim.5; avoid, Plb.35.4.14; Jul.Or.7.223d: c. inf., AP10.56…

ἐκτρέφω.definition: bring up from childhood, rear up, Hdt.1.122; Med., of pregnant animals, nourish, Pl.Ti.91d:—Act., bring to birth, Arist.GA773a34

ἐκτρέχω.definition: fut. Diph.19.3: pf; run off or away, Ar.Av.991

ἔκτρημα.definition: hole made in trepanning, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.16

ἔκτρησις.definition: hole, Hp.Steril.222 , Aret.SD2.13 , Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.26

ἐκτριαινόω.definition: shake with the trident, Ps.-Theopomp.Hist. ap. Luc.Pseudol.29

ἐκτρίβω.definition: fut. Pass. S.OT428:—rub; rub out, i.e. to destroy root and branch, Hdt.6.37; E.Hipp.684; Hdt.4.120; Herod.6.27, dub. in E.Cyc.475; bring life to a wretched end, = Lat. conterere vitam, S.OT248, cf. 428:—Pass., with th…

ἔκτριμμα.definition: sore caused by rubbing; rubber, towel, Philox.2.41

ἐκτροπή.definition: turning off or aside, diversion of water from its channel, Th.5.65; on account of [the river] being turned off over the country, Plb.9.43.5. II. turning aside, escape, from labours, A.Pr.913; a digression, Pl.Plt.267a…

ἐκτρόπιον.definition: everted eyelid, a disease in which the lid is turned outward, opp. Cels.7.7, Antyll. ap. Aët.7.74, Dem.Ophth.ib.73

ἔκτροπος.definition: turning out of the way. Adv. Erot. s.v

ἐκτροχάζω.definition: rush out, Apollod.2.7.3; treat summarily, Dsc.Ther.2

ἐκτρυγάω.definition: gather in the vintage, PGurob 8.10 , LXXLe.25.5

ἐκτρυγίζω.definition: clear from lees, Gp.5.2.12 ; of molten silver, prob. in PLeid.X.20

ἐκτρυπάω.definition: bore or hollow out, Gp.10.23.5, cf; intr., slip out through a hole, Ar.Ec.337

ἐκτρυχόω.definition: wear out, grind down, exhaust, Th.3.93, 7.48:—Pass., Luc.Merc.Cond.39; worn-out rags, Id.Tox.30

ἐκτρύω.definition: aor. wear out, App.BC2.66; cf. · Hsch

ἐκτρώγω.definition: eat up, devour, Ar.V.155, LXXMi.7.4:—Pass., of a letter in a Ms., Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.26F

ἔκτρωμα.definition: = Hsch.; untimely birth, Arist.GA773b18 , LXXJb.3.16, al., 1 Ep.Cor.15.8, Ph.1.59; as a term of contempt, Tz.H.5.515

ἔκτρωσις.definition: miscarriage, Arist.Pr.860a18 ; v.l. in Hp.Mul.2.122, cf.Sor.2.49

ἐκτρωσμός.definition: = foreg., Arist.HA583b12, Aret.SD2.11, Sammelb.3451.5; attempted abortion, Hp.Mul.1.78, Ptol.Tetr.116

ἐκτυλόω.definition: excise a callosity, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.23.32, Crito ap. Gal.13.794

ἔκτυπος.definition: worked in relief, Ion Trag.42; distinct, Stoic.2.21: Comp., Hsch. Adv. with a distinct impression or character, opp. S.E.M.7.171

ἐκτυπόω.definition: model or work in relief; metaph. in Med., etc., form an image of a thing in . ., Pl.Tht.206d, cf. Lg.775d

ἐκτύπωμα.definition: figure in relief, Id.Ti.50d; reflection, of light, Olymp.in Mete.33.1

ἐκτύπωσις.definition: modelling in relief, Aesar. ap; figure, J.AJ12.2.9

ἐκτυφλόω.definition: make quite blind, Batr.238, Hdt.4.2,9.93, X.Eq.10.2, Ar.Pl.301, etc.; Antiph.195.4: abs., Ar.Fr.569.2:—Pass., A.Ch.536: metaph., Philostr.VA4.36; of buds destroyed by hail, Id.Her.2.11

ἐκτυφόω.definition: delude, deceive, Ph.1.1; puff up, Id.2.569, cf. 215:—Pass., Plb.16.21.12

ἐκτύφω.definition: burn in a slow fire; cf. · Hsch.:—metaph. in Med., light a slow fire of love, Alciphr.3.50:—Pass., aor. 2 my face swelled up with weeping, Men.Epit.Fr.9

ἑκυρά.definition: Ep. for mother-in-law, Il.22.451, 24.770; also in Plu.2.143a, CIG 3846q

ἑκυρεύω.definition: Boeot. to be a father-in-law, Corinn.Supp.2.85

ἑκυρός.definition: Ep. for father-in-law, Il.3.172, 24.770, also CIG9136 , Jul.Or.3.127c. only in AP14.9.]

ἐκφαιδρύνω.definition: strengthd. for make quite bright, clear away, E.Ba.768

ἐκφαίνω.definition: fut. Ion. in Luc.Syr.D.32: aor; of persons, bring to light, reveal, . . 19.104; produce him, Hdt.3.36; . . S.Ant.307, cf. OT329: c. part., Hdt.3.71; . . E.Hipp.428:—Pass., showed himself, came forth to view, Il.19.46,…

ἔκφανσις.definition: exhibition, manifestation, Plot.3.5.9, Jul.Or.7.220b, Olymp.in Mete.106.9, Dam.Pr.432, Procl.Inst.125

ἐκφατνίζω.definition: throw out of the manger: generally, throw; Med., eat out of the manger, Nic.Dam.p.3 D

ἐκφάτνισμα.definition: that which is cleaned out of the; a board of the manger taken out in cleaning it, Poll.10.166

ἐκφαυλίζω.definition: depreciate, disparage, pour contempt on, J.AJ2.14.1, al., Arr.An.1.13.6, Luc.Merc.Cond.11, Hld.10.12; J.AJ5.8.6; reject with scorn, Ael.VH9.41, NA4.37 : c. inf., disdain to do, ib.11.31

ἐκφερομυθέω.definition: reveal, of secrets, Aen.Tact.22.5 , SIG360.25 , Corn.ND30

ἐκφέρω.definition: fut. Hdt.3.71: Ion. aor; carry out a corpse for burial, Il.24.786, cf. Hdt.7.117, Antipho6.21 , etc.; also, cause death, Plot.1.4.8

ἐκφεύγω.definition: of persons accused, to be acquitted, Ar.V.157; c. gen., escape out of, Od.23.236; Epigr.Gr.1041.9; of things, Il.5.18: with Prep., APl.4.182

ἔκφημι.definition: speak out or forth, utter loudly:—Ep. only in Med., Od.10.246, cf. 13.308; A.R.1.439: later aor. 1 EM687.30

ἐκφθείρω.definition: destroy utterly, Scymn.344, Str.17.1.44, etc.:—Pass., to be undone, ruined, E.Hec.669: Com., 'go to the devil', Ar.Pax72; Luc.DMeretr.15.2

ἐκφθίνω.definition: in Hom. only in 3 plpf. Pass., the wine had all been consumed out of the ships, Od.9.163; 12.329; they have utterly perished, A.Pers.679 , 927

ἐκφιλέω.definition: kiss heartily, AP12.250; love dearly, prob. in Epigr.Gr.522.6

ἐκφλαυρίζω.definition: make light of, f.l. in Plu.2.680c, cf. Pomp.57, prob. in Sch.Ar.Pl.885

ἐκφλεγματόομαι.definition: Pass., to turn into phlegm, Hp.Acut.61

ἐκφλέγω.definition: to set on fire: metaph., Ar.Pax608; warm up, Aret.SA2.1

ἐκφλογόω.definition: scorch, Phlp.in Mete.44.33:—Pass., blaze up, Arist.Mir.833a9, Dsc.1.68.2

ἐκφλόγωσις.definition: upper part of a torch, D.S.17.115

ἐκφλύζω.definition: or spirt out: c. acc. cogn., give vent to a groan, A.R.1.275

ἐκφοβέω.definition: alarm, A.Pers.606, cf. Pl.Grg.483c, etc.; so as to cause alarm, Th.2.87; E.Or.312; fright one with a thing, Th.6.11:—Pass., fear greatly, c. acc., S.El.276; . . ib.1426; Id.OT989

ἐκφοινίσσω.definition: make all red or bloody, E.Ph.42:—Pass., to

ἐκφοιτάω.definition: Ion. go out constantly, be in the; of things, to be spread abroad, Plu.Lyc.3

ἐκφορά.definition: carrying out, esp. of a corpse to; blabbing, betrayal of secrets, D.L.1.98

ἐκφορέω.definition: = carry out, as a corpse for burial; generally, carry out, Hdt.1.197, 9.116, Is.6.42 :—Med., take out with one, E.Cyc.234, etc.:— Pass., move forth, . . Il.19.360

ἐκφόριον.definition: that which the earth produces, Hdt.4.198; payment assessed on produce, = Arist.Oec.1345b33; esp. rent paid in kind, PAmh.2.87 , cf. PTeb.377.23 , OGI669.30, etc

ἐκφορόομαι.definition: Pass., to be worn into holes, Thphr.Lap.14, cf. 15

ἔκφορος.definition: exportable, f.l. for Ar.Pl.1138; to be made known or divulged, E.Hipp.295; Pl.La.201a; cf. I.2

ἐκφορτίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be sold for exportation: metaph., to be kidnapped, betrayed, v.l. for S.Ant.1036

ἐκφράζω.definition: tell over, recount, A.Pr.950, dub. l. in; describe, Hermog.Prog.10, Id.2.4, Men.Rh.p.373 S.:—Pass., TheonProg.2

ἐκφράσσω.definition: Att. aor. 1 Pass. D.S.18.35:—remove obstacles, open, Gal.11.730, D.S.l.c

ἐκφρέω.definition: poet. impf. Ar.V.125: fut. ib.156: aor. , also Hsch.: imper. prob. for Ar.V.162:—let out, bring out, . . restored in E.Ph.264 from the Sch. and Phot. , cf. Ar. ll.cc.; Luc.Lex.9:—Med., Hsch.:—Pass., go out, Ael.Fr.89

ἐκφροντίζω.definition: think out, discover, E.IT1323, Ar.Nu.695, Th.3.45, etc

ἐκφρύγομαι.definition: to be dried up, parched, c. acc; to be consumed, Ael.NA14.18

ἐκφυγγάνω.definition: = A.Pr.525, Diph.7, Plb.18.15.11; recover from disease, Hp.Morb.2.26

ἐκφυλάσσω.definition: guard or watch carefully, S.OC285, E.Or.1259; Id.Ion741

ἐκφυλλοφορέω.definition: expel or condemn by leaves, used of the Athen. which used olive-leaves as voting- papers, Aeschin.1.111, cf. AB248

ἐκφυσάω.definition: blow out, pours; blow away, LXXHg.1.9:—Pass., Plb.1.48.8; to be dissipated, Aret.SD2.1

ἐκφύσημα.definition: pustule, Poll.4.190; volcanic eruption, Sch.A.R.3.41; D.S.3.53 : pl., = Hsch

ἐκφύω.definition: generate: mostly of the male, beget; rarely of the female, bear, S.OC984

ἐκφωνέω.definition: cry out, Ph.2.49, Plu.Caes.66; utter, Id.2.1010a , Demetr.Eloc.15; pronounce, D.H.Comp.14

ἐκχαλάω.definition: let go from, AP11.354.18; relax, Chor. in Rev.Phil.1.68

ἐκχαρυβδίζω.definition: swallow like Charybdis, Pherecr.95 ; cf. : Hsch

ἐκχάσκω.definition: in pf. gape, gaze, LXX1 Es.4.19

ἐκχαυνόω.definition: puff up, make vain and arrogant, Alc.51; E.Supp.412, cf. Phld.Lib.p.32 O.; to make them gape and stare, Hp.Art.42

ἐκχέζω.definition: = Lat. ecacare, Anon. ap. Demetr.Eloc.126, v.l. in Arist.HA551a7

ἐκχέω.definition: pour away: hence, spill, a vessel, Ar.Fr.306; Men.l.c.:—Pass., to be drained, PRyl.154.18

ἐκχιλόω.definition: cover all over with grass : land that bears nothing but grass, Paus. Gr.Fr.323

ἐκχλοιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be or grow sallow, Hp.Coac.480

ἐκχοΐζω.definition: dig out, Ostr.Strassb.677 , Suid; Pass., to be decanted into jars, of wine, PSI5.517

ἐκχοιριλόω.definition: only pf. part. Pass. expld. by Hsch

ἐκχολόω.definition: turn into bile, Herod.Med. in; Pass., to be charged with bile, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.15

ἐκχόλωσις.definition: turning into bile, Alex.Trall.1.15, Steph.in Hp.1.130D

ἐκχορδόομαι.definition: Pass., to be deprived of strings, Sopat.16

ἐκχορεύω.definition: break out of the chorus: generally, break; Med., drive out of the chorus, E.Hel.381

ἐκχράω.definition: declare as an oracle, tell out; suffice, Hdt.8.70: impers., c. inf., how will it suffice him, how will he be content to . . ? Id.3.137

ἐκχρηματίζομαι.definition: squeeze money from, levy contributions on, Th.8.87, D.C.53.10

ἐκχυλίζω.definition: squeeze out, express juice or liquor, Hp.Mul.1.44; suck out, Arist.HA596b12

ἐκχυλόω.definition: in Pass., to be squeezed out, Gal.12.14

ἐκχυμόω.definition: extract juice from, Hp.Morb.2.47; in Pass., of the small veins, shed the blood and leave it extravasated under the skin, Id.Fract.11

ἔκχυσις.definition: outflow, Arist.Mete.354a26; pouring; effusion of pus, Erasistr. ap. Gal.8.318

ἔκχυτος.definition: poured forth, unconfined; immoderate, Suid. s.v

ἐκχυτρίζω.definition: pour out of a pot, Hsch

ἐκχωνεύω.definition: melt down, coin anew, D.C.68.15 codd

ἐκχώννυμι.definition: raise a mound, Aq.Ez.17.17:—usu. in Pass; of a bay, to be filled up by the deposit of a river, v.l. ib.11

ἐκχωρέω.definition: depart, SIG679.53; leave a country; slip out of, Hdt.3.129

ἐκχώρησις.definition: going out, Placit.4.22.1; retirement, withdrawal from, c.gen., Epicur.Sent.14; BGU1115.48

ἐκχωρίζω.definition: cut off, separate, PRyl.378.11 (ii A.D; Pass., to be voided, of excrements, Arist.HA551a7

ἐκψύχω.definition: fut. lose consciousness, swoon; to be short of breath, gasp, Arist.Pr.886b14

ἐκψωμίζω.definition: of corn, to be infested with grubs, Hsch. s.v

ἐλαίαγνος.definition: or , goat's willow, Salix Caprea, Thphr.HP4.10.1,2

ἐλαΐζω.definition: cultivate olives, Ar.Fr.119; to be olive-green, Hsch

ἐλάϊνος.definition: of olive-branches, D.Chr.31.110; of the olive-tree, Str.16.4.13

ἐλαιοβραχής.definition: Antyll. ap. Orib.7.21.8, Sor.1.82:—and Gal.13.581, = sq

ἐλαιόγαρον.definition: fish preserved in oil, Steph.in Hp.2.309D

ἐλαιοδόκος.definition: or holding oil, Hdn.Epim.78, Suid. s.v

ἐλαιοθέσιον.definition: oiling-room in the palaestra; = foreg., SIG900.18

ἐλαιοθετέω.definition: provide oil at the baths, ib.12 , Ephes.3 No.15

ἐλαιοκόμος.definition: rearing olives, AB248, perh. to be; olive-clad, Nonn.D.13.184

ἐλαιοκονία.definition: plaster made from lime and oil, Eust.382.37, Steph.in Hp.2.384D

ἐλαιόμελι.definition: sweet gum from the olive-tree, Dsc.1.31,etc

ἐλαιοπινής.definition: stained with or soaked in oil, Hp.Salubr.3

ἐλαιόπρῳρος.definition: like an olive at top, Arist.Ph.199b12

ἐλαιοσπάραγος.definition: olive-shoots used as a vegetable, POxy. 1849,1861

ἐλαιοστάφυλος.definition: vine grafted on an olive, Gp.9.14 tit

ἐλαιούργιον.definition: oil-press, Arist.Pol.1259a13, PRev.Laws 44.4, al., D.L.1.26, etc

ἐλαιοφανής.definition: resembling oil in appearance, of urine, Gal.19.588

ἐλαιοφόρος.definition: olive-bearing, E.HF1178 ; land fit for olives, Thphr.CP2.4.4: oil-shop, Gloss

ἐλαιοχρίστης.definition: municipal official responsible for supply of oil, POxy.300 , BGU 576.14

ἐλαιοχριστία.definition: supply of oil for anointing, D.L.5.71 :—also IG12.236.17 , Ath.Mitt.33.382 ,JHS9.231 :— Boeot. BCH26.156 ; tax levied for this purpose, Ostr.Strassb.178

ἐλαιόχροος.definition: of the colour of oil, of urine, Gal.19.588

ἐλαιοχύτης.definition: attendant who served out oil in the gymnasium, CPHerm.57.9, 59.7

ἐλαιόω.definition: oil:—only Pass., to be oiled, Arist.HA605b20; bring to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.163B

ἐλαιών.definition: olive-yard, PCair.Zen.57.2 (iii; the Mount of Olives, Olivet, Act.Ap.1.12, al., J.AJ7.9.2

ἐλαιωνέω.definition: purchase oil for the state, Inscr.Cos 113

ἐλαιώνης.definition: purchaser of oil for the state, IGRom.3.739xix 17 , IG22.1100

ἐλαιωνία.definition: purchase of oil for the state, Dig. 27.1.6.8, Cod.Just.10.55.1

ἐλαίωσις.definition: treatment with oil or reduction to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.215 B

ἐλασία.definition: = riding, X.Eq.Mag.4.4; striking from a die, Gloss

ἔλασμα.definition: metal beaten out, metal-plate; general name for probes and other surgical instruments, Gal.2.574; ibid.: esp. flat end of a probe, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.11.3

ἐλασμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Dsc.Eup.2.168, Heliod. ap.Orib.49.4.59, Gal.19.148

ἐλασσονέω.definition: to be deficient, wanting, PMagd.26.2 , BGU 1195.19

ἐλασσόω.definition: Att. aor. Lys.13.9; in early writers, lower, degrade, Lys.13.9, Isoc.8.17; LXXPs.8.6; cut down, shorten, D.H.Comp.6: c. gen., detract from, Th.3.42:—Med., reduce the power of, Plb.22.15.1

ἐλάσσωμα.definition: = D.L.9.68; reduction in amount or number, BGU20.8 , etc

ἐλάσσων.definition: c. gen. pers., worse than, inferior to, Ar.V.599, etc.: but c. gen. rei, giving way to, subservient to, X.Lac.5.8; Plu.Cor.34: abs., worse, inferior, Gp.2.48.1

ἐλαστρέω.definition: Ep. and Ion. for . . they drove the teams, Il.18.543; Thgn.600; to drive about, of the Furies, E.IT971; in later Prose, D.H.1.23; row, Ion. part. Arr.Ind.32.9:—Pass., of ships, to be rowed, Hdt.2.158, 7.24; cf. · Hsch…

ἐλατήρ.definition: driver, esp. of horses; rower, Luc.Am.6, Nonn.D.39.306

ἐλατήριος.definition: driving, driving away, c. gen; purgatives, Hp.Acut.2, cf. Epid.5.7, Erot

ἐλάτης.definition: epith. of Poseidon at Athens, Hsch

ἐλαττονέω.definition: receive less, LXXEx.16.18; but, give less; waste, be consumed, ib.3 Ki.17.16; to be missing, defective, PMagd.26.12

ἐλαττονότης.definition: being less, opp. Iamb.in Nic.p.33 P

ἐλάττωμα.definition: inferiority, disadvantage; loss, defeat, IPE 12.32B15 , Plb.1.32.2, Onos.32.8 , etc

ἐλάττωσις.definition: making smaller or less, lessening; depreciation, disparagement, Arist.Rh.Al.1436b34 , VV1251a5

ἐλαύνω.definition: Il.12.62, etc.: Ion. impf; with acc. omitted, intr., go in a chariot, drive, he whipped them on, Il.5.366, al., cf. S.El.734,739; he drove on over the waves, Il.13.27; travel the night through, Od.15.50; drive into th…

ἐλαφηβολία.definition: Ep. shooting of deer, Call.Dian.262: in pl., S.Aj.178

ἐλαφηβόλος.definition: shooting deer, Il.18.319; of Artemis, h.Hom.27.2, Anacr.1.1: Dor. S.Tr.213

ἐλαφίνης.definition: young deer, fawn, Aq. 1 Ki.24.3, Hsch

ἐλαφίς.definition: a bird, perh. heron or egret, Dionys.Av.2.11

ἐλαφόστικτος.definition: tattooed with figure of a deer, Lys.13.19

ἐλαφρίζω.definition: make light: hence, lift up, carry; make light of, scorn, Archil.87, cf. Hsch

ἐλαφρύνω.definition: make light, lighten, Jul.Or.1.18c; relieve, Eus.Mynd.1; Ruf. ap. Orib.8.47.1:—Pass., Hippiatr.126

ἐλάχιστος.definition: of Time, shortest, Th.3.39; with shortest deliberation, Id.1.138

ἐλάω.definition: Ion. poet. pres. for v. init

ἔλδομαι.definition: and poet. Verb, only pres. and impf., wish, long, c. inf., Il.13.638, Od.4.162, Pi.O.1.4: c. gen., long for, Od.5.210; eager to reach it, Il.23.122: c.acc., desire, Od.1.409, cf. Il.5.481: abs., Od.24.400:—Pass. only …

ἐλεαίρω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.24.23: aor. 1 A.R.4.1308, Sammelb.2134:—lengthd. form of take pity on, Il.6.407, Od.10.399, etc.—Ep. word, used by Ar.Eq.793 , Luc.Trag.305

ἐλεγαίνω.definition: to be wrathful, wanton, violent, EM152.50, 327.6

ἐλεγκτήρ.definition: one who convicts or detects, Antipho2.4.3

ἐλεγχής.definition: worthy of reproof; of men, cowardly; reproachful, Nonn.D.40.35

ἐλέγχω.definition: test, bring to the proof, B.Fr.10.2; A.Ag.1351 ; Pl.Sph.242b : with subject. clause, . ., A.Ch.851, Ar.Eq.1232

ἐλεεινολογέομαι.definition: speak piteously, Hermog.Stat.3, Id.2.7, Herm.in Phdr.p.196A

ἐλεεινολογία.definition: Att. piteous appeal, Pl.Phdr.272a, cf. Hermog.Id.1.1; Agatharch.21

ἐλεέω.definition: impf. Apollod.Com.4.1: aor. Ep; abs.,feel pity, Ar.Ach.706

ἐλεημοσύνη.definition: pity, mercy, Call.Del.152; charity, alms, LXXTo.4.7, Ev.Matt.6.2, D.L.5.17

ἐλεήμων.definition: gen. pitiful, merciful, Od.5.191, D.21.101, LXXPs.111.4, Ev.Matt.5.7; of God, LXXEx.34.6, al.: c.gen., Ar.Pax425:—Comp.and Sup., Arist.HA608b8, Lys.24.7. Adv. condemned by Poll.8.11

ἐλεητύς.definition: Ep. and Ion. = pity, mercy, Od.17.451

ἑλειοβάτης.definition: walking the marsh, marsh- dwelling, A.Pers.39

ἑλειονόμος.definition: dwelling in the marsh or meadow, A.R.2.821; Orph.A.1054; situate there, ib.157

ἑλειοσέλινον.definition: or marsh-celery, Apium graveolens, Thphr.HP7.6.3, Dsc.3.64

ἐλελίζω.definition: Ep. redupl. of , rare in; Med. and Pass., move in coils or spires, of a serpent, Il.2.316; 11.39, cf. A.R.4.143; Ar.Fr.500

ἐλελίχθων.definition: gen. earth-shaking, Pi.P.2.4; i.e. Poseidon, ib.6.50:—in S.Ant.153 Dionysus is called because the ground shook beneath the feet of his dancing bands

ἐλευθερία.definition: Ion. freedom, liberty; manumission, = Lat. vicesima manumissionum, BGU326ii 11

ἐλευθεριάζω.definition: speak or act like a freeman, Pl.Lg.701e, Arist.Pol.1314a8, Ph.1.380; Plu.2.6e; Luc.Cat.1; Epimenid. ap. D.L.1.113; to be free, Crat.Ep.8; esp. from public burdens, PFlor.382.7 : c.gen., Chaerem. ap. Porph.Abst.4.8

ἐλευθέριος.definition: also X.Smp.8.16:—speaking or; esp.freely giving, bountiful, X.Smp.4.15 , cf. Arist.EN1120a8, etc

ἐλευθεριότης.definition: the character of an esp. freeness in giving, liberality, Pl.R.402c, Arist.EN1119b22, etc.; Pl.Tht.144d: generally, generosity, Plu.Pomp.73

ἐλευθεροπρασίου δίκη.definition: prosecution for selling a freeman as a slave, Poll.3.78

ἐλευθεροπρέπεια.definition: disposition of a freeman, condemned by ib.119

ἐλευθεροπρεπής.definition: worthy of a freeman, Pl.Alc.1.135c. Adv. ibid

ἐλευθεροστομέω.definition: to be free of speech, A.Pr.182 , E.Andr.153; in later Prose, Ph.1.474, al

ἐλευθερόω.definition: set free, Hdt.5.62; c.gen., set free, release from, E.Hipp.1449; Pl.R.566e; Hld.5.23; also i.e. ceasing to flee, E.HF1010:—Pass., Pl.Phd.114b; Id.R.569a

ἐλεύθω.definition: causal of stem bring, Dor. fut. Hsch., Dor. 3pl. aor. Ibyc.Oxy.1790.18; cf

ἐλεφαίρομαι.definition: old Ep. Verb, perh. connected with; of the Nemean lion, he used to destroy them, Hes.Th.330

ἐλεφαντάρχης.definition: commander of a squadron of sixteen elephants, Ascl.Tact.9, Phylarch.31 J., Plu.Demetr.25, LXX2 Ma.14.12

ἐλεφαντίασις.definition: the disease elephantiasis, Cels.3.25, Dsc.2.70.3, Plu.2.731a

ἐλεφαντιάω.definition: suffer from elephantiasis, Phld.Rh.2.120S., Dsc.1.77, Ptol.Tetr.151, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.27.2

ἐλεφάντινος.definition: of ivory, Alc.33.1, Ar.Eq.1169; white as ivory, Anacreont.15.12; Crates29

ἐλεφαντιστής.definition: elephant-driver, Arist.HA497b28; shield of elephant-hide, App.Pun.46

ἐλεφαντομάχος.definition: fighting against elephants, Str.16.4.15, cf. D.S.3.26

ἐλεφαντουργική.definition: the art of ivory- working, Sch.Paul. Al.P.1

ἕλιγμα.definition: bracelets, in pl., Hsch., prob. in Sapph.Supp.20a.8; curl, lock of hair, AP6.211

ἑλιγμός.definition: Ep. winding, convolution, of the Labyrinth, Hdt.2.148; X.Cyr.1.3.4; of the gut, Arist.HA532b7; of the Fallopian tubes, ib.510b19; of the brain, Erasistr. ap. Gal.5.603; of a snake, Sch.Nic.Th.159; of dancers' feet, Or…

ἑλικάμπυξ.definition: wreathed with a circlet, Pi.Fr.75.20; Id.Pae.3.15

ἑλικάστερος.definition: with circling orbit, epith. of the moon, Man.4.224

ἑλικαυγής.definition: with circling rays, of the sun, Orph.Fr.236.1; of the moon, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.173

ἑλίκη.definition: the constellation of the Great Bear, from its revolving round the pole, Arat.37, A.R.3.1195

ἑλικοβλέφαρος.definition: with ever-moving eyes, quick- glancing, epith. of Aphrodite, h.Hom.6.19, Hes.Th.16, Pi.Fr.123.5; of Alcmene, Id.P.4.172

ἑλικογραφέω.definition: describe a curve, of the Nile, Anon.Geog.Comp.31

ἑλικοδρόμος.definition: running in curves, twisting, Orph.H.9.10; circular, E.Ba.1067

ἑλικοειδής.definition: poet. of winding or spiral form, D.S.5.30; Plu.Num.13; of planetary orbits, Cleom.1.4; Aret.SD2.3; S.E.P.1.126; D.L.7.144. Adv. Cleom.1.4, Dsc.2.165, Olymp.in Mete.13.9

ἑλικοπέταλος.definition: with twining leaves, prob in Sacerd.p.540.1 K

ἑλικόρροος.definition: with winding stream, Orac. ap. Paus.4.20.1

ἑλικτήρ.definition: anything twisted: ear-ring, Ar.Fr.320.14, Lys.12.19, IG2.747.5

ἑλίκων.definition: thread spun from the distaff to the; a nine-stringed instrument, Aristid.Quint.3.3, Ptol.Harm.2.2

ἑλίκωψ.definition: fem. with rolling eyes, quick-glancing, as a mark of youth and spirits , Il.1.389, al.; ib.98; Hes.Th.298, cf. Sapph.Supp.20a.5; Pi.Pae.2.99,P.6.1

ἐλινύω.definition: c. gen. rei, rest from, Hp.Acut.47 ; D.H.1.33; c. part., rest or cease from doing, . . Hdt.8.71, cf. A.Pr.529 , Call.Cer.48,Fr.248. of the impf. short in A.R.1.862, long ib.589, indeterminate in Trag.]

ἑλίσσω.definition: or (the latter more freq. in codd. of; generally, roll, roll life's stream along, Pi.I.8.15; of the chariot of Day, A.Pr.1092 ; . . E.Ph.3; roll the eddying dust, A.Pr.1085 ; of the Euripus, E.IT7, cf.1103 ; Id.HF868 …

ἑλκεσίπεπλος.definition: trailing the robe, with long train, Il.6.442, al., Mus.286, Nonn.D.1.103

ἑλκεσίχειρος.definition: drawing the hand after it, AP6.103

ἑλκετρίβων.definition: cloak-trailer, nickname of a Laconian, Pl.Com.124

ἑλκεχίτων.definition: trailing the tunic, with a long tunic, epith. of the Ionians, Il.13.685, h.Ap.147

ἑλκέω.definition: = drag about, tear asunder, in impf. . . Il.17.395: also in fut. and aor. ib.558; 22.336; he did violence to Leto, Od.11.580; Arat.638:—Pass., Il.22.62

ἑλκηθμός.definition: being carried off, violence suffered, Il.6.465

ἕλκημα.definition: that which is torn in pieces, prey, E.HF568

ἑλκητήρ.definition: one that drags, of a harrow, AP6.297

ἑλκοποιέω.definition: make wounds or sores: metaph., rip up old; make an incision in a tree, Gp.5.38

ἑλκόω.definition: wound, lacerate, E.Hec.405; ulcerate, Hp.VM19, al.:—Pass., of persons, to suffer from wounds or sores, Com.Adesp.106.8, Ev.Luc.16.20; of sores, suppurate, X.Eq.1.5

ἑλκύδριον.definition: Dim. of slight sore, Hp.Art.63; = Dionys.Trag.12

ἑλκύσιμος.definition: that may be drawn, Phot. s.v

ἕλκυσις.definition: attraction, Aret.SD1.10; drawing, in cupping, Hp.Loc.Hom.22

ἕλκυσμα.definition: that which is drawn, i.e. spun; = dross of silver, because drawn off with a hook, Dsc.5.86, Gal.12.236, Orib.Fr.90

ἑλκυσμός.definition: attraction; esp. of idle fancy; dragging, in pl., Anon.Fig.p.156 S

ἑλκυστέος.definition: to be dragged, X.Ages.9.4; one must draw, Gal. ap. Aët.8.50

ἑλκυστήρ.definition: instrument for drawing: surgeon's; as Adj., toil of dragging, Opp.H.5.20

ἑλκυστήριος.definition: fit for drawing, draught animals, Men.Prot.p.17 D

ἕλκυστρον.definition: handle or lever for raising a swing-; halter, Hsch. s.v

ἕλκω.definition: Il.24.52, etc., impf; draw after one, . . Il.8.486; trail fetters after one, Hdt.3.129; let one's cloak trail behind, Ephipp.19 ; Archipp.45

ἕλκωμα.definition: sore, ulcer, Hp.Epid.3.7; part wounded, Thphr.HP9.2.1

ἕλκωσις.definition: ulceration, Hp.Aph.3.21, Th.2.49, Ph.2.100; of plants, Thphr.CP1.14.2,al

Ἑλλαδάρχης.definition: president of the; official of the Delphic Amphictyony, IG4.590

ἐλλαμβάνω.definition: receive, Supp.Epigr.2.264.6 (Delph., ii; Med., aor. 2 IG12.1061.10 :—seize hold of, Dsc.4.183, cf. Ph.1.21, al., J.AJ6.7.5, etc

ἐλλαμπρύνομαι.definition: Pass., gain distinction, Th.6.12; pride oneself, Luc.Dom.1; D.C.73.10; App.BC3.66; J.AJ18.3.4

ἐλλάμπω.definition: shine, . . Archil.61: c; trans., illuminate, Plot.2.9.2, cf. Procl.in Ti.2.285 D., al.; Plot.6.4.16:—metaph. in Med., distinguish oneself, gain glory in or with, Hdt.1.80; Id.8.74

ἔλλαμψις.definition: shining, flashing, Placit.3.3.12; radiation of heat, Steph.in Hp.1.134D,al

Ἑλλανοδικέω.definition: to be a judge at the games, Paus.6.1.5,24.3

Ἑλλανοδικεών.definition: the place where the held their meetings, Id.6.24.1

ἑλλεβοριάω.definition: need hellebore, i.e. to be mad, Call.Com.28

ἑλλεβορίζω.definition: Ion. fut. Hp.Ep.20:—dose with hellebore, Id.Mochl.30, Plu.Alex.41, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.1 , etc.; and so, to bring one to his senses, D.18.121: title of play by Diph.,AB100

ἐλλείπω.definition: leave in, . . left in a; leave out, leave undone, freq. with neg. Pron. neut., S.Aj.1379; . . Ar.Lys.673; Pl.Plt.269c, cf. Ti.17b, X.Mem.4.3.17; Id.Cyr.1.2.14; Pl.Plt.267c, cf.R.362d; Id.Cra.431c, 431d, etc.:—Pass., I…

ἐλλείχω.definition: lick in, take one's fill of, Com.Adesp.125 Meineke

ἐλλήγω.definition: come to an end in, PLond.1.98r31

Ἑλληνάρχης.definition: chief of the Greek community, title at Tanais, IPE2.423, al

Ἑλληνίζω.definition: impf. without augm., Charito4.5; would not be Greek, Arist.SE182a34

Ἑλληνίς.definition: Grecian woman, E.El.1076, Men.79; pagan woman, Jul.Ep.112

Ἑλληνισμός.definition: imitation of the Greeks, Hellenism; use of a pure Greek style and idiom, as an Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.214, cf. Phld.Po.2.18, A.D.Pron.71.25, S.E.M.1.98; , Lex.Vind.311; title of works by Seleucus, Ath.9.367a; by Ptolemy of …

Ἑλληνιστής.definition: one who uses the Greek language: a; gentile, heathen, Jul.Ep.84a

Ἑλληνοκοπέω.definition: flatter the Greeks, Plb.25.3.1; affect Greek fashions, Id.20.10.7

Ἑλλησποντίας.definition: Ion. , wind blowing from the Hellespont, i.e. from the NE., Hdt.7.188;= Arist.Mete.364b19, cf.Pr.946b33, Thphr.Vent.62

Ἑλλησποντιάς.definition: fem. Adj. of the Hellespont, Archestr.Fr.35.14B

Ἑλλησπόντιος.definition: of the Hellespont, Hdt.7.95; Subst. name of a plaster, Heras ap.Gal.13.914

Ἑλλήσποντος.definition: Hellespont or sea of Helle , now the Dardanelles, Il.2.845, Hdt.4.38, etc.:—sts. taken to include the Propontis, Id.1.57, etc.:—the adjacent country, Th.2.9, etc.: in this sense without Art. in Att. Inscrr., IG12.106.…

ἐλλιμένιος.definition: Subst. harbour-dues, customs, Eup.48, SIG524.6 , Milet.3 No.37d68, Arist.Oec.1350a16, Plb.30.31.12: pl., GDI5018

ἐλλιμενιστής.definition: farmer of harbour-dues or customs, Aen.Tact.29.5, D.34.34

ἐλλογάω.definition: v.l. for sq. in Ep.Rom.5.13, Ep.Philem.18

ἐλλογέω.definition: = reckon, put to an; metaph., impute, BGU140.32 :—Pass., Ep.Rom.5.13

ἐλλόγιμος.definition: held in account or regard , in; eloquent, Men.Rh.p.354 S. , Poll.2.125. Adv. Gloss

ἔλλογος.definition: endowed with reason, opp. Arist.EN1172b10, Plot.3.8.1

ἐλλοχάω.definition: lie in ambush , Pl.Tht.165d:—Med; lie in wait for, Pl.Smp.213b, Ael.NA6.4

ἐλλόχησις.definition: lying in ambush, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ἐλλοχίζω.definition: lie in ambush, E.Ba.722; place in ambush, Polyaen.3.1.2, cf. Plu.Phil.14

ἐλλυχνιάζω.definition: furnish a lamp with a wick, PMag.Par.1.1099, PMag.Lond.121.376:—Pass., Dsc.1.72.4

ἐλλύχνιον.definition: lamp-wick , Hdt.2.62; surgical dressing, Sor.2.11, Gal.10.954

ἑλμίνθιον.definition: Dim. of little worm, Hp.Epid.4.16, Arist.HA570a14

ἐλπιδοδώτης.definition: giver of hope, AP9.525.6, cj. in Timo65

ἐλπιδοκοπέω.definition: lead by false hopes, S.E.M.6.26, cf. Eust.1063.60

ἐλπίζω.definition: Att. fut. LXXPs.43.7, Ep.Rom.15.12; of evils, look for, fear, in same constr., S.Tr.111 ; Id.Aj.799, cf. Lys.12.70; . . Ar.Av.956; Hdt.8.12; E.Ion348: with folld. by aor. subj., Hdt.1.77; Id.8.53

ἐλπίς.definition: hope, expectation; reason to expect or believe, Pl.Phd.67b, Lg.898d

ἐλύω.definition: roll round : only aor. 1 Pass; in later Ep., = wrap up, cover, shrouded in them, A.R.1.254; Opp.C.3.418, cf. H.2.89; A.R.3.1313

ἐμβαδᾶς.definition: cobbler, name given to Anytus, Theopomp.Com.57, cf. Archipp.30

ἐμβαδίζω.definition: walk on, Ael.NA10.24; simply, walk, march, Ph.1.232, D.C.79.14

ἐμβαδόν.definition: Adv. by land, = Il.15.505; wading, Paus.10.20.8; a surface, area (opp

ἐμβαθύνω.definition: make deep, hollow out, Alciphr.3.13; intr., go deep into, Ph.1.18,341; sink deep in, LXXJe.30.8

ἐμβαίνω.definition: fut. pf. Ep. part; go on, go quickly, says Antilochus to his horses, Il.23.403; advance! E.El.113

ἐμβάλλω.definition: fut. pf. aor. 2; of things, Thgn.551, X.Eq.6.7 , 9.9, cf. Il.19.394; E.IT1424; D.57.13, cf. X.Cyr.2.2.21; Id.An.7.1.12; Id.Cyr.8.1.38; throw food to . . , Thphr.Char.4.8; simply, lay or put in, put it into his hands, …

ἐμβάπτω.definition: dip in, Hippon.36; Ev.Matt.26.23; Cratin.143; Ar.Nu.150:—Med., Id.Fr.151, Arched.2.10, Luc.Asin.6

ἔμβαρος.definition: of weighty sense, Men.Phasm.Fr.3; pregnant, Gloss

ἐμβαρύθω.definition: to be heavy upon, Nic.Th.324; of smell, to be offensive, Id.Th.512

ἐμβασανίζω.definition: test, examine, dub. l. in HeroBel.73.10

ἐμβασικοίτας.definition: name of a cup, Ath.11.469a, Petron.24

ἐμβασίκοιτος.definition: epith. of shepherds, sleeping on the ground , Man.4.247

ἐμβασιλεύω.definition: to be king in or among, c. dat., Od.15.413; Pi.N.7.38; A.R.1.173; Hes.Th.71, etc.; Iamb.Protr.20; Il.2.572: c. gen., Theoc.17.85

ἐμβαστάζω.definition: bear in or on, carry, Luc.Ocyp.14

ἐμβατεύω.definition: step in or on, frequent, haunt: c. acc., of; enter on, come into possession of, E.Heracl.876, cf. LXXJo.19.49: more freq. enter on possession of the vessel, D.33.6; Id.44.19; Is.9.3: abs., enter on an inheritance, PEl…

ἐμβατέω.definition: = foreg., Nic.Th.147:—Med., Lyc.642; prob. f.l. for lead to pasture, AP7.657

ἐμβατήριος.definition: of or for marching; Subst., , marching tune, Plb.4.20.12, Polyaen.1.10; of the anapaests of Tyrtaeus, D.Chr.2.59

ἐμβάτης.definition: a kind of half-boot of felt; = Luc.JTr.41, Lib.Or.64.98, etc

ἐμβάφιον.definition: flat vessel for sauces, saucer, Hippon.112; . . Hdt.2.62: as a measure, = Hp.Loc.Hom.13

ἐμβιβάζω.definition: Att. fut. causal of set in; put on board ship, cause to embark, Th.1.53; X.An.5.3.1; Plu.Ant.7, cf. Charito8.3: abs., put on board, X.An.5.7.8, etc.:—Med., Id.HG5.1.19

ἔμβιος.definition: the moisture necessary to life, Thphr.CP1.1.3; Philostr.Im.1.24

ἐμβιοτεύω.definition: of epilepsy, flourish in certain conditions, Aret.CD1.4

ἐμβιόω.definition: fut. Philostr.Her.2.3:—live in; of plants, become established, Thphr.HP3.6.4; simply, take root, ib.6.7.3; Philostr. l.c

ἐμβίωσις.definition: maintenance of life, LXXSi.38.14; way of living, ib.3 Ma.3.23

ἐμβιωτήριον.definition: place to live in, dwelling, D.S.5.19

ἐμβλαστάνω.definition: grow on a plant, as mistletoe, Thphr.CP5.15.4

ἐμβλέπω.definition: pf. PLond.1.42.21 :—look; consider, Ev.Matt.6.26; look into a matter, PTeb.28.15

ἔμβλημα.definition: chased or embossed ornament used in decoration of plate, D.C.57.15, cf. Cic.Verr.4.17.37, etc

ἐμβοάω.definition: call upon, shout to, X.Cyn.6.17; D.H.11.38, etc.: abs., shout aloud, Th.2.92, 4.34; Diog.Oen.25

ἐμβόησις.definition: shouting, Aret.CA1.2, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.27, Antyll. ap. eund.6.6.5

ἐμβοθρόομαι.definition: to be embedded in a cavity, Hp.Cord.5

ἔμβοθρος.definition: like a pit or hole, sunken, Thphr.HP9.3.1

ἐμβολάδιον.definition: Dim. of sq., grafted tree, prob. in JHS18.308

ἐμβολάς.definition: fem. Adj.grafted, v.l. in Arist.Fr.274: Subst., Plu.2.640b

ἐμβολεύς.definition: anything put in: piston; model for metal fittings or stone- work, Ph.Bel.70.13, HeroBel.96.5

ἐμβολή.definition: putting in, Thphr.Od.26 : esp. putting; insertion of a letter, Pl.Cra.437a

ἐμβόλιον.definition: missile discharged, javelin, D.S.1.35; interlude, episode, Cic.QF3.1.7

ἐμβόσκομαι.definition: feed on or in, Ph.2.289: metaph., ib.351

ἐμβραδύνω.definition: remain long in or on; dwell on, Luc.Dom.3,23, S.E.M.9.1, Herm.in Phdr.p.158A

ἐμβράσσω.definition: cast up, of the sea, in Pass., Aq., Sm., Thd.Is.57.20

ἔμβρεγμα.definition: lotion, Dsc.2.124, Aret.CA1.1, Archig. ap. Gal.8.150

ἐμβρέμομαι.definition: Med., roar or bluster in, Il.15.627

ἐμβρέχω.definition: treat with embrocations, Philum. ap; wet, J.BJ3.7.13:—Med., soak, Nic.Al.237:—Pass., to be dipped, plunged, Sotionp.183 W.; to be soaked, Dsc.Eup.1.1: aor. 2 part. Pass. Paul.Aeg.3.43

ἐμβρίθεια.definition: weight, dignity, Suid., Zonar; clumsiness of parts, opp. Epicur.Nat.14.4

ἐμβριθής.definition: weighty, of ropes, Hdt.7.36; metaph., weighty, grave, dignified, Pl.Ep.328b; Plu.Per.4; Id.Brut.1; dignity, D.H.Amm.2.2; Hp.Ep.11; Jul.Or.2.88a; the more sedate, opp. Pl.Tht.144b

ἐμβρίθω.definition: press heavily, AP7.532; to be heavy, Nic.Th.867

ἐμβριμάομαι.definition: of persons, to be deeply moved, Ev.Jo.11.33,38; admonish urgently, rebuke, E.Fr.1099: c. dat. pers., LXXDa.11.30, Ev.Matt.9.30, Marc.1.43

ἐμβρίμησις.definition: = foreg., Aq., Sm.Ps.37.4, Thd.Is.30.27, Eustr.in EN119.21, Steph.in Hp.1.76D

ἐμβρονταῖος.definition: struck by lightning: place struck by lightning, Lat. bidental, D.S.8.9

ἐμβροντάω.definition: dumbfounder, Eup.17; Pass., to be struck by lightning, distd. fr. X.HG4.7.7

ἐμβροντησία.definition: sheer stupidity, Id.Sam.196; madness, Plu.2.1119b, Philostr.VS2.27.5

ἐμβρόντητος.definition: thunderstruck, stupefied, stupid; later of ideas, crack-brained, mad, Porph.Chr.35; Orph.Fr.47

ἐμβροχή.definition: infusion, Dsc.1.43; embrocation; noose, halter, Luc.Lex.11

ἐμβρυοθλάστης.definition: instrument to extract a foetus, Gal.19.104

ἐμβρυοτομέω.definition: cut up the foetus in the womb, c. acc., Olymp.in Grg.p.257 J., Aspasia ap.Aët.16.22:—Pass., of the foetus, to be cut up in the womb, Vett.Val.53.27, Procl.Par.Ptol.214

ἐμβρυοτομία.definition: cutting up of the foetus, Gal.19.107, Philum. ap. Aët.16.23, Olymp.in Grg.p.258 J., PTeb.676, Ptol.Tetr.149, etc

ἐμβρυοτόμος.definition: instrument for cutting up the foetus, Sor.2.63

ἐμβρυουλκία.definition: extraction of the foetus, Id.1.68 , Archig. ap. Aët.16.91, Gal.19.107

ἔμβρωμα.definition: that which is eaten away; meal, snack, Ath.1.11c, cf. Sor.1.40

ἐμβρωματίζω.definition: = EM819.6, Suid.:—aor. Pass. in med. sense, take a meal or snack, Apollon.Lex. s.v

ἐμβυθίζω.definition: cause to sink to the bottom, Plu.2.981a

ἐμβύω.definition: stuff in, stop with a thing, Ar.V.128; Herod.2.82

ἐμετήριος.definition: = I: an emetic, ibid.: pl. Aret.CD1.3

ἐμετοποιΐα.definition: causing to vomit, Dionys.Aeg. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.130B

ἔμετος.definition: vomiting, Hp.Aph.1.2 ; Hdt.2.77; Arist.HA612a6; disposition to vomit, sickness, ib.584a7

ἐμέω.definition: metaph., throw up a flood of words, Eun.VSp.488 B

ἐμμαίνομαι.definition: to be mad at, Act.Ap.26.11, J.AJ17.6.5

ἐμμάσσομαι.definition: press upon, inflict, Nic.Th.767; Opp.H.2.502; Call.Dian.124; APl.4.273 :—late in Act., smear, PMag.Lond.121.230

ἐμματέω.definition: put the finger down the throat to cause; implant a sting, of a bee, Nic.Th.809

ἐμμάχομαι.definition: fight a battle in, cf. D.C.50.12

ἐμμεθύσκομαι.definition: Pass., to be drunk in, J.BJ4.4.3

ἐμμείγνυμι.definition: mingle, Plu.2.61b; of persons, encounter, Pi.P.4.251

ἐμμειδιάω.definition: smile in, Philostr.Ep.51; to be glad at, of hounds, X.Cyn.4.3

ἐμμελετάω.definition: exercise or train in a thing, Plu.Cim.18, etc.; to practise upon, Pl.Phdr.228e; give a lecture, Plu.2.932d

ἐμμελέτημα.definition: that on which an art is practised, LXXWi.13.10; instrument for practice, AP6.83

ἐμμενής.definition: abiding in: steadfastness, Timo58.1 .—Hom. has only neut. as Adv., always in phrase, unceasing ever, Il.10.361, Od.9.386, etc. : also Adv. Hes.Th.712

ἐμμένω.definition: fut. S.OC648, etc.: pf; abide by, stand by, cleave to, be true to, c. dat., Hdt.9.106; A.Ch.977, etc.; S.OT351; Id.Aj.350; Th.5.18, cf. Isoc.7.81; X.Mem.4.4.16; Pl.Ap.39b; Id.Tht.145c, etc.; remain constant to them, A…

ἐμμεστόομαι.definition: Pass., to be filled quite full, S.Ant.420 , El.713 , unless in both passages be adverbial, v. B.3

ἐμμετεωρίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be carried aloft, Philostr.VA1.5

ἐμμετρέω.definition: measure by or according to; simply, measure out, provide, PMasp.138iv1

ἔμμετρος.definition: in measure, proportioned, opp; fitting, suitable, Id.Lg.823d; . . ib.955e. Adv. Id.Cra.395c, M.Ant.1.16: Sup. Pl.R.474d; also Lg.674c, prob. in Aristaenet.1.18

ἐμμολύνω.definition: pollute in or with, in Pass., LXXPr.24.9

ἔμμονος.definition: abiding, lasting; of disease, chronic, LXXLe.13.51; ib.Si.30.17

ἐμμυέω.definition: initiate in: what, were you initiated at the great mysteries in that shabby coat? Ar.Pl.845 cod. R

ἐμπάζομαι.definition: used only in pres. , busy oneself about, take heed of, care for, c. gen., Od.1.271, al.; Il.16.50, cf. Od.2.201; 19.134; Timo50: once c. acc. pers., Od.16.422; also Coluth.38:—Ep. word, used in late Prose, Ael.Fr.325

ἐμπαθής.definition: in a state of emotion, Arist.Insomn.460b7; opp. subject to passivity, Plot.4.7.13,5.9.4; opp. Procl.Inst.80

ἐμπαιδεύω.definition: lecture amongst, Philostr.VS1.21.3:—Pass., to be brought up in, E.Fr.413

ἐμπαιδοτριβέομαι.definition: to be brought up or educated in, D.C.77.21; J.BJ2.8.12

ἐμπαιδοτροφέομαι.definition: Med., bring up one's children on another person's property, D.44.23

ἐμπαίζω.definition: fut. LXXHb.1.10: pf; euphem. in mal. part., LXXJd.19.25

ἐμπαίω.definition: strike in, stamp, emboss; intr., bursts in upon my soul, S.El.902

ἐμπακτόω.definition: close by stuffing in or caulking, Hdt.2.96

ἐμπαλάσσομαι.definition: Pass., to be entangled in, Hdt.7.85; of fish, Ael.NA15.1: abs., entangled one with another, Th.7.84.—Act. Hsch

ἐμπάλλομαι.definition: poet. shake or quiver in, A.R.3.756

ἐμπανηγυρίζω.definition: hold festal assemblies in, Plu.Comp.Per.Fab.1; make a display in, Id.2.532b

ἐμπαραβάλλομαι.definition: throw oneself into, into punishment, Phalar.Ep.132; to venture to believe in one's heart, ib.130

ἐμπαράθετος.definition: laid in or on, Suid., cf. eund.s.v

ἐμπαραλιμπάνω.definition: pass over, c. acc., Them.in Ph.11.29

ἐμπαρασκευάζω.definition: to prepare, Clin. ap. Stob.3.1.76, cf.Aen.Tact.9.3

ἐμπαράσκευος.definition: prepared, Sm.Ps.26.3; a kind of wind-screen for engines, Ath.Mech.33.1. Adv. Suid. s.v

ἐμπαρέχω.definition: hand over to another, put into his power; supply, furnish, Id.1.12, 2.383, al.; Plu.Galb.29

ἐμπαρίσταμαι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 Act., stand by, Hld.7.19

ἐμπαροινέω.definition: aor. J.Ap.1.8:—behave like one drunken, Luc.Tim.14; act offensively, to another, Ph.2.403, Luc.DDeor.5.4; J.AJ6.12.7; indulge recklessly in slanders, ib.20.8.3

ἐμπαρρησιάζομαι.definition: speak freely against; drawing courage from their purpose to speak openly of the plot, J.AJ15.8.4

ἐμπάσσω.definition: Att. fut. in or on, Thphr.Lap.67; some powder, Pl.Ly.210a; Gal.11.134: in Hom. only metaph., weave rich patterns in a web of cloth, Il.3.126, cf. 22.441

ἐμπατέω.definition: walk in or into, c. acc., A.Ag.1434; c. acc., trample on, J.BJ6.9.4: metaph., Agath.4.15:—Med. or Pass., tread the wine-press, Poll.7.151

ἐμπεδορκέω.definition: abide by one's oath, Hdt.4.201, X.Lac.15.7; IG22.111.79:—with a play on Ar.Fr.772

ἐμπεδοσθενής.definition: with force unshaken, a settled, unruffled life, Pi.N.7.98

ἐμπεδόω.definition: impf. X.Cyr.8.8.2: aor. D.C.60.28: :—confirm, ratify, S.Ichn.50; E.IT790, cf. Ar.Lys.211,233, Polem.Hist.83; X.HG3.4.6; . . Pl.Phdr.241b; X.Cyr.5.1.22; Plb.29.24.4; D.H.4.79; Gal.5.315; uphold, Plu.Sol.25:—Med., Ph.1.…

ἐμπειράζω.definition: to make an attempt on, c. gen. rei, v.l. for Plb.15.35.5

ἐμπειρέω.definition: to be experienced in, have knowledge of, c. gen. rei, Plb.3.78.6, etc.; LXXTo.5.6

ἐμπειρία.definition: c. gen. rei, experience in, acquaintance with, Antipho5.1; Th.3.95; Pl.R.582b; also X.HG7.1.4; Th.2.3; Plb.10.24.4, etc

ἐμπειροπόλεμος.definition: experienced in war, D.H.6.14, Ph.1.426: Sup., App.BC3.97. Adv. ib.2.36

ἐμπειροπράγμων.definition: gen. versed in affairs, Suid. s.v

ἐμπείρω.definition: fix on or in, Ath.11.488d; impale, J.AJ16.10.3; studded, Alciphr.3.55

ἐμπελαγίζω.definition: to be in or on the sea, IPE12.35 , Ach. Tat.5.9

ἐμπελάζω.definition: bring near, having; intr. in Act., approach, c. dat., h.Merc.523; Democr.166; . .; S.Tr.748; Arist.Mu.395a19: abs., ib.b28, Porph.Abst.2.22; Orph.Fr.32a

ἐμπερίβολος.definition: ornate, expanded, Aristid.Rh.2 p.533 S.; Hermog.Id.1.11; Men.Rh.p.400S

ἐμπεριγράφω.definition: comprehend in a thing, v.l. for S.E.P.1.206 ; describe around, Poll.9.108

ἐμπεριέρχομαι.definition: pass round, prob. in Gal.2.826: metaph., Ph.2.61

ἐμπεριέχω.definition: encompass, surround, enclose; Astrol., blockade, Vett.Val.268.20

ἐμπεριλαμβάνω.definition: encompass, enclose, Hp.Ep.23, Thphr.CP5.3.4; Plu.Ant.63; Sammelb.5233.7 ; J.BJ3.7.7; comprehend, Arist.PA644a12; Inscr.Prien.105.27 :—Pass., Arist.Mete.388b21; is involved in the charge, Id.Rh.1416a20; Epicur.Ep.1p.22…

ἐμπερινοέω.definition: include in the thought of, Epicur.Nat.11.9

ἐμπερίοδος.definition: in periods, periodic, of style, D.H.Comp.9. Adv. Corn.ND27

ἐμπεριπατέω.definition: walk about in, Luc.Ind.6; walk about upon, LXXJb.1.7, al.; trample on, PHolm.18.30: metaph., insult, Plu.2.57a

ἐμπεριρρήγνυμι.definition: break all round, v.l. in Arist.HA557b26

ἐμπερισπούδαστος.definition: zealously frequented, of temples, interpol. in J.Ap.2.35

ἐμπερίσχεσις.definition: Astrol., hemming in of a planet by two others, Vett.Val.5.15, Porph.in Ptol.188, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.114.23, Heph.Astr.1.15

ἐμπερονάω.definition: fasten with a clasp, buckle on, in Med; Pass., of nails, to be fixed in, Ath.11.488b

ἐμπετάννυμι.definition: in Pass., to be hung about with cloths, Socr.Rhod.1

ἐμπέτομαι.definition: fly into, aor. inf. Arcesil. ap. D.L.4.32

ἐμπήγνυμι.definition: fix or plant in, c. dat; congeal, freeze, Thphr.CP5.12.2 :—Pass., to be congealed, ib.1.22.7 ; freeze to death, Arist.HA603a27

ἐμπηδάω.definition: jump upon, Hdt.3.32; leap or spring into, Hermipp.54, cf. Plb.12.8.4

ἐμπιέζω.definition: press, squeeze, in Pass., Hp.Gland.13, Plu.2.1005a

ἐμπίεσμα.definition: depressed cranial fracture, Id.Fract.6, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.14.1, Paul.Aeg.6.90

ἐμπικραίνομαι.definition: Med. or Pass., to be bitter against, Hdt.5.62, D.C.47.8: abs., Eus.Mynd.54; of disease, become virulent, J.AJ17.6.5

ἐμπιλέομαι.definition: Pass., to be compressed, Pl.Ti.74e, D.S.2.52

ἐμπίμπλημι.definition: Ion.2sg.pres. Hp.Morb.2.14, part; fill a hungry man with food, Od.17.503

ἐμπίμπρημι.definition: 3pl. impf. Th.6.94; also inf. Plu.Cor.26; part. Plb.1.53.4: impf. X.HG6.5.22: fut. Il.15.702, Ar.Th.749, 3pl. Tab.Heracl.1.145: aor. 1 Hom., etc.: aor. 1 Med. PTeb.61.289 , Q.S.5.485:—Pass., part. Hdt.1.19: fut. , Pau…

ἐμπίνω.definition: abs., drink one's fill, f.l. in Thgn.1129, cf. Ar.Pax1143,1156; drunken, Id.Ec.142

ἐμπιπίσκω.definition: aor. Pi.Fr.111.1:—Pass., aor. 1 causal of give to drink, Pi.l.c., Nic.Al.519:—Med., fill oneself, Id.Th.573, Al.320:—Pass., of liquor, to be drunk, Id.Th.624

ἐμπίπτω.definition: fut. aor. Ep. (v; Geom., meet, of a line meeting another, Euc.1 Post.5, etc.; to be placed, Archim.Sph.Cyl.1.9; ibid

ἐμπιστεύω.definition: entrust, D.S.1.67, Plu.Phoc.32; trust in, give credence to, LXXDe.1.32, al., Nic.Dam.Fr.130.19 J.; LXX2 Ch.20.20; ib.3 Ma.2.7

ἐμπίτνω.definition: poet. for fall upon, B.9.24; A.Ag.1468 , Supp.120 , cf. S.Aj.58

ἐμπιτυάζομαι.definition: to be curdled, of milk, Paul.Aeg.5.57

ἐμπλάζω.definition: drive about in:—hence in Pass., wander; metaph., Phld.Rh.1.376S

ἐμπλανάομαι.definition: wander in, Hld.2.29: abs., Plu.2.495e: metaph., erratic, ib.336f

ἐμπλάσσω.definition: Att. plaster up; stuff in, Arist.Pr.919b9

ἔμπλαστρος.definition: salve or plaster, Dsc.1.32; said to be later form of Gal.13.372; also Hierocl.Facet.221, PSI3.297

ἐμπλατύνω.definition: widen or extend, LXXEx.23.18: metaph., ib.Pr.18.16:—Pass., to expatiate, Str.8.7.3

ἐμπλέκτης.definition: one who plaits hair, Gloss.:—fem. ib., EM528.5

ἔμπλεκτος.definition: inwoven: ashlar filled up with rubble, Vitr.2.8.7

ἐμπλέκω.definition: Ep. pf. Hp.Oss.17; metaph., weave by subtle art, A.Pr.610; E.IA936

ἐμπλεονάζω.definition: to be profuse in, Heraclit.Ep.7.6; Sor.1.77

ἐμπλευρόομαι.definition: dash against one's ribs, charge him, S.Fr.53

ἐναναστρέφομαι.definition: Pass., to be conversant with, Aristox. ap. Stob.3.1.49, Hsch. s.v

ἐναντίωσις.definition: disagreement, discrepancy, Isoc.12.203 , Pl.R.607c, etc.: pl., contrarieties, Arist.Metaph.986b1, al

ἐναντλέω.definition: draw in: metaph. in Pass., Ph.1.574

ἐναξονίζω.definition: fit with an axle, in Pass., Placit.3.13.3

ἐναπασχολέω.definition: to be wholly occupied in, Steph.in Hp.1.134D

ἐναπειλέω.definition: threaten, prob. f. l. for D.H.5.54

ἐναπενιαυτίζω.definition: dwell for a year in a strange place, Parmenisc. ap. Sch.E.Med.273

ἐναπεργάζομαι.definition: produce in, Pl.Plt.273c, Sph.236a, v.l. in Isoc.7.38, etc

ἐναπερεύγω.definition: vomit forth upon, metaph. of lust, Ph.2.393, cf. 202

ἐναπηχέω.definition: in Pass., to be a faint echo or resonance, Plot.4.4.22

ἐναποβρέχω.definition: steep, soak in, Hp.Haem.4, Gp.12.19.2:—Pass., Heraclid.Tar. ap. Gal.14.187, Dsc.5.35

ἐναπόγραφος.definition: registered, esp. of cultivators or serfs, POxy.135.15, 137.12 , PAmh.2.149.6 , Just.Nov.54Pr., al

ἐναποδείκνυμαι.definition: Med., exhibit, to show; approved themselves, gained distinction among others, Hdt.9.58

ἐναποδέω.definition: bind up in a thing, Hp.Mochl.2:—; fasten to a bag, Hp.Liqu.6

ἐναποδύομαι.definition: Pass. with pf. Act., strip in a place, Him.Or.17.2, Men.Prot.p.1 D., Agath.Praef.p.132D

ἐναποζέννυμι.definition: boil in a thing, Gal.13.118: aor. 1 part. Dsc.4.176

ἐναποθησαυρίζω.definition: store up in a place, Iamb.VP29.162:—Pass., Ph.1.278

ἐναποθλίβω.definition: squeeze in, ib.541 , Archig. ap.Gal.12.858:—Pass., Harp.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.148

ἐναπόκειμαι.definition: Pass., to be stored up in, Plu.Aem.14, CPHerm.6.14 : metaph., Ph.1.293, Porph.Plot.1, cf. Plot.3.6.2

ἐναποκινδυνεύω.definition: run a hazard in or with, D.C.49.2, cf. J.AJ2.9.4

ἐναποκλείω.definition: enclose in, Olymp.in Mete.315.20, Alex.Trall.2:—Pass., Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.53, Artem.2.2, Philum. ap. Aeët.5.78

ἐναποκλύζω.definition: in Pass., to be stirred about in, Dsc.3.34

ἐναπολαμβάνω.definition: cut off and enclose, intercept; Astrol., annul by adverse influence, Vett.Val.112.14

ἐναπολείπω.definition: leave behind in or on, Xenocr.58; Plu.2.91b:—Pass., Arist.Mete.352b35, Ph.1.8

ἐναπολούομαι.definition: wash oneself or bathe in, Ath.2.43a

ἐναπομένω.definition: remain in, Lyd.Mag.3.61; Herm.in Phdr.p.100 A., cf. Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.67 B.: abs., Hld.1.15

ἐναποπνέω.definition: expire in, D.S.13.89, cf. M.Ant.5.4; expire in the act of . ., Plu.Cor.33; Luc.Harm.2

ἐναποπνίγω.definition: suffocate, drown in, aor. 2 Pass. Terpsicl. ap. Ath.7.325d, cf. Jul.Ep.82; Luc.Peregr.24

ἐναπορέω.definition: dub. l. for to be in doubt, Plb.29.27.6; . . Id.12.25c.1

ἐναποσβέννυμι.definition: aor. quench in a thing, Hp.Mul.1.78; Arist.Pr.937b13; Gal.14.377; Gp.7.12.8:—Pass., Arist.Mete.369b16, Cass.Pr.31, Hld.1.15

ἐναποσημαίνω.definition: indicate or point out in, Plu.Cim.2:—Med., impress or stamp on a thing, Philostr.Im.2.17, cf. Ph.1.291

ἐναποσκήπτω.definition: cause to descend; intr., supervene, attack, Cass.Pr.30, cf. Phlp.inde An.339.5

ἐναποστηρίζομαι.definition: Med., fix oneself in or on, Hp.Acut.9, cf. Placit.2.20.10

ἐναποσφάττομαι.definition: Pass., to be slain among, J.BJ4.6.3

ἐναποσφραγίζω.definition: impress in or on, LXX4 Ma.15.4: abs., D.L.7.46:— Med., Epicur.Ep.1p.11U.:—Pass., Zeno Stoic.1.18

ἐναποτελέω.definition: in Pass., to be produced, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.134

ἐναποτέμνω.definition: in Pass., to be cut off in, Str.2.5.27

ἐναποτίθεμαι.definition: lay aside or store up in, Id.Nat.Fac.3.12; D.C.73.10; Ph.2.42; deposit, Gal.Nat. Fac.3.7; Jul.Or.1.15d; include, Procop.Gaz.p.169B.; but vent one's anger upon . ., D.S.26.16; produce in, Alex.Trall.10:—Pass., Phld.Her…

ἐναποτίνω.definition: pay or spend in litigation in a place, Ar.Av.38

ἐναποτυπόομαι.definition: Pass., receive impressions; express, Hierocl.in CA26p.480M

ἐναποφέρω.definition: in Med., receive by heredity, Lib.Decl.43.56

ἐναποψύχω.definition: ease oneself in, euphem. for; cool off, PHolm.6.12

ἐναργυρόω.definition: in Pass., to be silver-plated, Timae. Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.97

ἐναρδεύω.definition: irrigate, and one who irrigates, Gloss

ἔναρθρος.definition: jointed: of speech, articulate; strong in limb, Aret.SD2.5

ἐναρκέω.definition: suffice, be able, c.inf., Sch.Pi.N.6.97: Hsch

ἐνασκέω.definition: train or practise in a thing; Pass., to be wrought in it, J.AJ3.7.5

ἐνδαίνυμαι.definition: Med., feast on, f.l. in Ath.7.277a

ἐνδαίω.definition: light or kindle in: metaph., Pi.P.4.184:— Med., burn or glow in, Od.6.131; A.R.3.286

ἐνδακρύω.definition: weep in or with, suffuse them with tears, A.Ag.541

ἑνδεκαγράμματος.definition: of eleven letters, prob. in Ath.10.455b

ἐνδεξιόομαι.definition: go round from left to right, E.IA1473

ἐνδέρω.definition: wrap in skin, of sacrificial offerings, in Pass., SIG1025.48 , 1026.8 , cf. Hsch. s.v

ἔνδεσις.definition: binding on, of the point of; swaddling, Sor.1.84

ἐνδεσμεύω.definition: bind to or in, D.S.20.71:—Pass., Dsc.Eup.1.146; D.S.3.40

ἐνδεσμέω.definition: = foreg., Aq.Ex.23.22, al., v.l. in; tie up in, Gp.8.1.3

ἐνδεύω.definition: Aeol.for , to be wanting, IG12.6; soak or dye in, Nic.Al.414

ἐνδιάζω.definition: pass the noon, take a siesta; weave in, in Pass., Hsch

ἐνδιάκειμαι.definition: Pass., to be set in; Adv. = Hermog.Id.2.7

ἐνδιαλαμβάνω.definition: in pf. part. Pass. divided at intervals, Dsc.2.94

ἐνδιασκευάζω.definition: work up, in literary composition, Sch.Ar.Ra.1488 , Sch.Il.3.393

ἐνδιασπείρω.definition: sprinkle, Gp.6.8.1:—Pass., to be; impregnated with, Epicur.Fr.250

ἐνδιατίθεμαι.definition: Med., dispose: hence, set forth in
