ἐνδομυχέω.definition: lurk in the recesses of a house, Sch.Ar.V.964; lie hidden, Gp.2.3.9; to be latent, of Steph.in Hp.1.164D

ἐνδόμυχος.definition: in the inmost part of a dwelling; insidious, Gal.9.837

ἐνδοξάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be glorified, LXXEx.14.4, al., 2 Ep.Thess.1.10, PMag.Leid.W.4.17

ἔνδοξος.definition: held in esteem or honour, of high; of things, notable, Aeschin.3.231, cf. Diod.Com.2.21; generally approved, = Epicur.Fr.513; glorious, Plu.Per.28; Id.2.99f. Adv. freq. in Inscrr., SIG442.7 , etc., cf. Vit.Philonid.p.…

ἐνδοξότης.definition: distinction, glory, Hsch. s.v; as a honorific address, Just.Nov.41 Pr., Sammelb.4736.1, etc

ἐνδοτέρω.definition: Adv.Comp.of more within, quite within; of Time, within a certain limit, sooner, Hp.Fract.33

ἐνδουπέω.definition: fall in with a heavy sound, Od.12.443; 15.479

ἐνδρομέω.definition: run into, Max.282; run through, AP7.395

ἐνδρομή.definition: air played during the pentathlon, Plu.2.1140d

ἐνδρομίς.definition: a sort of high shoe, worn by; Adj., used in the foot-race, GDI2517.11

ἐνδυναμόω.definition: strengthen, confirm, LXXJd.6.34, 1; endow with vitality, in Pass., metaph. of scientific theorems, Plot.4.9.5

ἐνδυναστεύω.definition: to have power or exercise dominion in or; procure by one's authority or influence, X.HG7.1.42

ἐνδυστυχέω.definition: to be unlucky in or with . ., in name thou art fit to be luckless, E.Ba.508, cf. Ph.727; Plu.Comp.Per.Fab.3

ἐνδύω.definition: c. acc. rei vel loci, go into; enter, press into, c. acc., Il.19.367; thou wilt enter the contest , 23.622; Pl.R.620c; Id.Lg.642b; Id.Tht.169c; also . . Ar.V.1020, Arist.HA609b21; enter upon it, undertake it, X.Cyr.8.…

ἐνδωσείω.definition: to be inclined to yield, D.C.46.37 , Agath.1.9

ἐνέδρα.definition: sitting in: hence, lying in wait, ambush, Th.5.56 , etc.; Id.3.90; X.Eq.Mag.4.10; D.S.19.108; Plu.Rom.23; X.Cyr.8.5.14; ib.5.4.4; Th.4.67. b. men laid in ambush, X.HG4.8.37. 2. metaph., trickery, treachery, Pl.Lg.908d…

ἐνεδράζω.definition: to be firmly established, pf. part. Gal.UP3.8

ἐνεδρεύω.definition: impf. X.Cyr.1.6.39: fut; abs., lay or set an ambush, Th.4.67, cf. X.An.1.6.2, 4.1.22,etc

ἐνέδριον.definition: row of reserved seats in a theatre, IGRom.4.1414

ἔνεδρον.definition: = I, LXXJo.8.2, 12, al; hindrance, obstruction, POxy.892.11

ἔνεδρος.definition: inmate, inhabitant, S.Ph.153; anal, Meges ap.Orib.44.24.1,11

ἐνέζομαι.definition: sit in or upon, Arist.Pr.881b36; have one's seat or abode in, c. acc. loci, A.Pers.140

ἐνεθίζω.definition: accustom to a thing, Socr.Ep.27.2:—Pass., Ptol.Tetr.5, cf. D.L.3.23; Hdn.6.6.2

ἐνειδοφορέω.definition: of a sculptor, work into shape, AP12.57

ἐνεικονίζω.definition: impart form to, Placit.1.10.1:— Med., have portrayed in a thing, Plu.2.40d; represent as by an image, Simp.in Ph.1355.11; Hierocl.in CA23p.468M., cf. Procl.Inst.152:—Pass., find a place in a metaphor or piece of symbo…

ἐνειλέω.definition: wrap in, Dsc.5.72:—Med; metaph., engage, PTeb.24.62 :—Pass., to be engaged, entangled in or with, Plu.Art.11; Id.Brut.45; Id.Caes.66; prob. for J.BJ6.2.8; Artem.l.c.; come to blows with, PRyl.144.18

ἐνείλησις.definition: wrapping, bandaging, Herod.Med. ap; confinement of intestinal gases, Ruf. ap.eund.8.24.9

ἔνειμι.definition: c. dat. pl., to be among, Thgn.1135, Hdt.3.81, al.; 1 Ep.Cor.6.5

ἐνείργω.definition: aor. shut up in, Sch.Pi.P.10.72; Phalar.Ep.136.1:—Pass., Tz.H.6.250

ἐνείρω.definition: aor. 1 , entwine, enwreath; thread, pass through, Aen.Tact.31.18; also Ael.NA1.15; LXXJb.10.11; Dsc.2.166

ἐνειρωνεύομαι.definition: employ irony in a matter, Procl.in Prm.p.728 S

ἐνεκπλύνω.definition: wash off in a thing, Polyzel.4

ἐνελαύνω.definition: drive in or into, c. dat., Il.20.259, cf. Pi.N.10.70: metaph., Id.P.8.9:—Med., drive in or on, D.C.49.30

ἐνέλκω.definition: in Pass., to be charged, imposed upon an estate, PFlor.370.14 , cf. PLond.5.1695.12 , etc.; of land, to be assigned for forced cultivation, PFlor.50.75

ἐνενηκονταετής.definition: ninety years old, ib.2 Ma.6.24, Ph.1.606 :—contr. Luc.DMort.27.7, App.Pun.106, D.C.69.17

ἐνενηκονταμοιρία.definition: arc of ninety degrees, Pancharius ap. Heph.Astr.2.11

ἐνενηκονταπλάσιος.definition: ninety times as large, c. gen., Gem.6.38

ἐνεξουσιάζω.definition: show independence in; exert authority, be supreme in, Procl.Theol. Plat.6.15, cf. ib.2, Id.inCra.p.98P.; Iamb.Myst.2.3: abs., ib.3.18

ἐνεορτάζω.definition: keep holiday in, Str.12.3.36, cf. Plu.Comp.Per.Fab.1, OGI383.98

ἐνεπιδείκνυμαι.definition: Med., display in; abs., show off, make a display, Ph.2.28, Lib.Decl.16.28

ἐνεπιδημέω.definition: sojourn in, Ael.VH12.52, Ath.6.233a; opp. Id.8.361f, D.C.51.17

ἐνεπιορκέω.definition: forswear oneself by; Pass., have false witness given against one, Themist.Ep.8

ἐνεπίσκημμα.definition: claiming of property alleged to belong to the state , Harp

ἐνεπισκήπτομαι.definition: Med., claim property alleged to belong; generally, take proceedings to enforce a claim, PGurob 2.28

ἐνέπω.definition: lengthd. both forms in Hom. and Pi; c. acc. et inf., bid one do so and so, Pi.P.9.96, S.OT350, OC932

ἐνεργάζομαι.definition: make or produce in; work for hire in, of harlots, Hdt.1.93; trade with the property, D.44.23; Plb.10.8.7

ἐνεργέω.definition: to be in action or activity, operate; to be efficacious, of drugs, Diocl.Fr.147, Dsc.1.98, al.; ib.106; Plot.6.1.22; to be effective, of troops, Ael.Tact.14.6:—Pass., to be the object of action, Arist.de An.427a7, Ph.…

ἐνέργημα.definition: action, activity, operation; realized object, Plot.6.8.16, cf.6.9.2

ἐνεργής.definition: later form of active, effective, D.S.17.44, etc.; of medicines, strong, POxy.1088.56 , Dsc.5.88, etc.: Comp. more effective, Arist.Top.105a19: Sup. D.S.1.88, cf. Dsc.1.19, A.D.Synt.291.9

ἐνεργητέος.definition: to be done, dub. l. in Zeno Stoic.1.49

ἐνεργμός.definition: a way of playing on the lyre; peg on the for tuning the strings, Euphron. ap.EM340.3

ἐνεργοβατέω.definition: step vehemently, pass wonderfully from one thing to another, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.3

ἐνερείδω.definition: intr., lie in or on, adherent to . ., Dsc.3.23:—Med., A.R.1.428

ἐνερεύγομαι.definition: belch on, Nic.Th.185: also aor.2 Act., . . . . Ar.V.913

ἐνερευθής.definition: somewhat red, Str.3.1.5; Dsc.1.100: Comp., Sor.1.13; of the countenance, flushed, Phld.Ir.p.5 W., Cic. Att.12.4.1; blushing, Plb.31.23.8; Luc.Im.7, cf. Antyll. ap. Orib.7.16.3

ἐνετήρ.definition: clyster-syringe, Cass.Fel.48; siege-engine of war for hurling projectiles, Ph.Bel.91.45, 100.18

ἐνευδαιμονέω.definition: to be happy in, Th.2.44, D.S.34.3; Lib.Or.14.43

ἐνευδιάω.definition: float in the clear sky, A.R.2.935

ἐνευδοκιμέω.definition: gain glory in, D.18.198, cf. D.S.34.2.18, J.Ap.1.5, Plu.2.71a; Cod.Just.1.2.25.1. 2. enjoy repute with another, Ael.VH8.12

ἐνεύδω.definition: sleep in or on, . . Od.20.95, cf. 3.350, al., Theoc.5.10; D.L.6.22

ἐνευεργετέω.definition: in Pass., well-treated, dub. in PLond. 2.177.26

ἐνευκαιρέω.definition: pass one's time in, Ph.2.522, cf. 1.387

ἐνευλογέομαι.definition: Pass., to be blessed in, Act.Ap.3.25, LXXGe.12.3, Ep.Gal.3.8:—Med., take a blessing to oneself, LXX1 Ki.2.29

ἐνεύναιος.definition: on which one sleeps, . . a skin to sleep on, Od.14.51; for want of bed-furniture, 16.35; bed-clothes, Hierocl.p.25A

ἐνεύχομαι.definition: adjure, implore, Test.Epict.1.13, Herod.6.46; IG5.1208.50 : c. dat., of god invoked, PMag.Par.1.2258; also I adjure you by A. not to . ., PBaden 51

ἐνεχυράζω.definition: fut. D.47.79 (but; c. acc. rei, take in pledge, D.24.197; Aeschin.3.21, cf. LXXDe.24.6, al., D.H.6.29, PPetr.3pp.56,69: abs., Plb.6.37.8 :—Pass., I have my goods seized for debt, Ar.Nu.241:—Med., have security given o…

ἐνεχυρασία.definition: taking property in pledge, security taken, pledge, Pl.Lg.949d, IG 2.1055.7 , PSI4.288 , etc.; D.47.76, 80

ἐνεχύρασμα.definition: pledge, thing pawned, LXXEx.22.26, al., PHamb.10.42

ἐνεχυριάζω.definition: later forms for Just.Nov.134.7, 52.1, Gloss.:—also ib

ἐνέχυρον.definition: pledge, security, and to offer a pledge, Hdt.2.136; And.1.39; ibid., X.An.7.6.23; Antipho6.11; Hermipp.29; PHib.1.46 , etc.; make a thing a pledge, put it in pawn, Ar.Pl.451, cf. Ec.755; Pl.Lg.820e; give on security, …

ἐνέχω.definition: hold or keep fast within; Pass., with fut. and aor. Med. , to be held, caught, entangled in, c. dat., X.An.7.4.17; Pl.La.183e

ἐνέψημα.definition: a thing boiled or infused, Aret.CA1.1

ἐνέψω.definition: boil in or among, Aret.CA1.1: pf. Pass., ib.6: aor. 1 Pass., . . Nic.Al.71

ἐνζάω.definition: live in, f.l. in Ph.1.65: metaph., prob. in IGRom.4.146

ἐνζεύγνυμι.definition: yoke, A.R.1.686; bind; metaph., involve in, A.Pr.108; . . . . ib.578

ἐνζωγραφέω.definition: paint in or on, Pl.Phlb.40a , Tz.H.12.560

ἐνηβάω.definition: spend one's youth in, Longus3.13; of plants, flourish in, Cratin.325, cf. Nic.Fr.85.2

ἔνηβος.definition: in the prime of youth, from fifteen upwards, Sch.Theoc.8.3

ἐνήδομαι.definition: Pass., rejoice in, Mich.in EN532.4, Sch.Il.8.51, Hsch.: abs., Gal.16.566

ἐνήδονος.definition: full of joy, delightful, Sch.E.Hec.828; 'glad eye', Heph.Astr.1

ἐνηής.definition: Ep. Adj. kind, gentle, . . Il.17.204; 23.252; of Athena, Od.8.200; Il.23.648; Hes.Th.651: later in nom. IG14.1648.8; etym. of Corn.ND21: pl., Opp.C.2.89; Id.H.2.644; of stars, propitious, Max.262, al

ἐνηλιόομαι.definition: to be exposed to the sun, Aët.8.16; sunlit objects, Gal.17.396

ἐνηλόω.definition: nail to, in Pass., Cels. ap. OrigenesCels.6.34,36

ἐνῆμαι.definition: used as pf. of to be seated in, Od.4.272, cf. Theoc.22.44; . . E.Fr.795

ἐνημερεύω.definition: spend the day in, D.S.17.70; Id.32.16, cj. in Thphr.Char.8.14

ἐνησυχάζω.definition: = . ., to be quiet in, ChioEp.16.7, Ph.2.140

ἐνηχέω.definition: to be resonant, Aret.SA1.6: c. dat., ring in; teach by voice, word of mouth, Eustr.in EN112.19

ἐνήχημα.definition: a sound in one's ears, Iamb.VP15.65 codd

ἐνήχησις.definition: musical accompaniment of a song, Et.Gud.576.34

ἔνηχος.definition: sounding within, of wind-instruments, opp; c. gen., acquainted, conversant with, LXXSi.prol.9

ἐνθακέω.definition: sit in or on, S.El.267, cf. OC1293

ἐνθάκησις.definition: sitting in, a twofold seat in the sun, i.e. both at morn and evening, S.Ph.18

ἐνθαλασσεύω.definition: Att. live at sea, Ael.NA9.63; to be at sea, Longus2.12; Ph.1.287

ἐνθάλασσος.definition: Att. in the sea, D.S.3.44; by the sea, Ath.Mech.32.3

ἐνθάπτω.definition: bury in a place, CIG2839.10 ,al.:—Pass., aor. 2 Aeschin.1.99, D.S.1.66, IG12.114 , CIG 2824 ; part. ib.2839.11 : fut. 2 ib.2826 , Ph.2.108, Plu.Dio43

ἐνθεάζω.definition: to be inspired, Hdt.1.63, Luc.DDeor.18.1:—Med., Id.Alex.13, Plu.2.623c, etc

ἐνθερίζω.definition: spend summer in a place, Poll.1.62; Dicaearch.1.21

ἐνθερμαίνω.definition: heat, in Pass., is heated by passion, S.Tr.368

ἔνθετος.definition: capable of being put in; grafted, Hp.Nat.Puer.26

ἐνθετταλίζομαι.definition: become a Thessalian, i.e. wear the large Thessalian cloak , Eup.201

ἐνθεωρέω.definition: observe in, in Pass., Nicom.Ar.1.16, cf. Eust.1722.62; Eustr.inEN281.25

ἔνθλασις.definition: dint or injury caused by pressure, Ael.NA16.22, Gal.7.39

ἐνθλάω.definition: Ion. indent by pressure, Hp.Int.44, Aristid.Or.47.13; impress , Ael.NA6.15

ἐνθλίβω.definition: press in, Nic.Al.454, Aret.SA1.9, Gal.UP5.15, S.E.P.3.68:—Pass., Arist.HA599b20, Pr.927a25; Peripl.M.Rubr.62

ἔνθλιψις.definition: pressing in, Archig. ap. Gal.8.110, Aret.SA1.6, etc.; pressure, Apollon.Cit.2

ἐνθνήσκω.definition: of the hand, grow rigid or torpid in, Id.Hec.246.—Dub. in Prose, Lys.16.15 , Plu.2.357d

ἐνθουσιάζω.definition: in Trag. always (also in; c. acc., inspire, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44 codd

ἐνθουσιασμός.definition: inspiration, enthusiasm, frenzy, Democr.18, Pl.Ti.71e, Ph.1.535 , S.E.M.9.20 ; Phld.Ir.p.67 W.; produced by certain kinds of music, Arist.Pol.1340a11, 1342a7

ἐνθουσιαστής.definition: person inspired, possessed, Ptol.Tetr.180, Eust.47 fin

ἐνθριόω.definition: wrap in a fig-leaf: muffle up, in pf; metaph., deceive, cozen, Men.Sam.241; cf. Hsch

ἐνθρομβόομαι.definition: become clotted, of blood, Aspasia ap.Aët.16.72; become full of clotted blood, Gal.8.409

ἐνθρονίζω.definition: place on a throne, metaph., LXX4 Ma.2.22:—in lit. sense only Pass., ib.Es.1.2; D.S.33.13

ἐνθρονισμός.definition: enthroning, title of by Pindar, Suid

ἔνθρυπτος.definition: crumbled and put into liquid; title of Apollo at Athens, Hsch

ἐνθρύπτω.definition: poet. crumble into liquid, make sop, Hp.Salubr.7, cf. LXX, Thd.Bel.33; Nic.Th.81; ib.655: —Med., Id.Al.266:—Pass., Lynceus ap.Ath.3.109e

ἐνθρῴσκω.definition: aor. 2 Ep. in, on, or among, c. dat., Il.21.233; 15.623; 5.161, cf. 20.381; Pi.P.3.37; E.El.327; kicked him on the hip, Od.17.233; D.C.74.14: metaph., Orac.Chald. ap. Dam.Pr.182

ἐνθυμέομαι.definition: fut. Lys.12.45, later; c. gen., think much or deeply of, Semon.2; Hermipp.41; Antipho5.6; Th.1.42, cf. Pl.Mx.249c, X.Mem.1.1.17; . . Lys.16.20; also Pl.R.595a

ἐνθύμημα.definition: thought, piece of reasoning; meaning, sense, opp. Olymp.in Mete.4.23

ἐνθύμησις.definition: consideration, esteem, E.Fr.246; consideration, reflection, Th.1.132, Ev.Matt.9.4 , Sm.Jb.21.27, Vett. Val.301.8, etc

ἐνθυμίζομαι.definition: later form of D.C.Fr.57.80b; = App.Mith.120.—Act. only in Hsch

ἐνθύμιος.definition: taken to heart, weighing upon; meaning, Ph.2.484; ideas, Iamb.VP5.20; reflect, c. acc. et inf., Alciphr.3.10; I take the hint, Ach. Tat.2.7

ἐνθωρακίζω.definition: arm: pf. part. Pass. mailed, X.An.7.4.16

ἐνιαυσιαῖος.definition: = sq. III, Arist.Cat.5b5; = sq. I, J.AJ3.10.1; Gp.3.2.1

ἐνιαύσιος.definition: annual, Hom.Epigr.15.11; Hdt.4.180, etc.; IG12.593 B5 : neut. pl. as Adv., Hes.Op.449. Regul.Adv. Sch.Arat.462, PLond.1.113.11

ἐνιαυτίζομαι.definition: spend a year, Pl.Com.113: late in Act., Sch.E.Or.1645, Suid

ἐνιαυτοκράτωρ.definition: zodiacal sign presiding over the year according to the Chaldean dodekaeteris, SerapioinCat.Cod. Astr.8.231

ἐνιαυτός.definition: prop. anniversary; = a year, Il.2.295; 8.404; 2.134; Pl.Ti.47a; LXXLe.25.29; during a year, Od.1.288; Indut. ap. Th.4.118; IG12.1.12 ; Lys.32.8; . . at what time in the year, Ar.Fr.569.7; twice a year, Pl.Criti.118e; …

ἐνιαυτοφορέω.definition: bear fruit a year before it ripens, Thphr.HP3.4.1

ἐνιαύω.definition: sleep among, Od.15.557, cf. 9.187; sleep in, Bion1.72

ἐνιδρόω.definition: sweat in, labour hard in, X.Smp.2.18

ἐνιδρύω.definition: set in a place, Plu.2.745c; establish in; Act. intr., settle in, Plot.1.3.4; Hierocl.in CA27p.483M

ἐνιζάνω.definition: sit or settle in or on, Il.20.11; offood, Alciphr.1.22, cf. Lib.Or.60.11: metaph. of and its object, Plot.4.6.3

ἐνίζω.definition: to set in, Ep. aor. 1 Med. he placed; intr., = pf. sit in or on, c.acc., E.Hel.1108 , prob. in A.Ch.801 : c. dat., . . Pl.Smp.196b; Gal.2.691; Id.11.354:—Med., Aret.CA2.8

ἑνίζω.definition: to be a partisan of the One, i.e. teach a; treat as a unity, Plot.6.9.6:—Pass., ibid

ἐνίημι.definition: fut. Th.4.115: aor. Ep; implant, inspire, c. acc. rei et dat. pers., Il.20.80; 17.570; 16.449; E.Ba.851; involve them in expense, PAmh.2.133.9 :—Pass., introduced from without, Plot.6.3.23

ἐνικλάω.definition: poet. for , break off: metaph., is wont to frustrate what I devise, Il.8.408, cf. 422; Call.Jov.90; Id.Aet.3.1.22; A.R.3.307

ἐνιππομαχέω.definition: fight a cavalry action in, D.H.2.13

ἐνίπτω.definition: fut. Il.7.447: aor. 2.245; after Hom., = tell, announce, Pi.P.4.201, cf. Nonn.D.27.59. cf

ἐνίσσω.definition: Ep. collat. form of attack, reproach, Il.15.198; 22.497; 24.238: also generally, maltreat, Od.24.161:—Pass., ib.163

ἐνίστημι.definition: causal in pres., fut.and aor. 1 Act., and; in Law, institute an heir, PMasp.151.75

ἐνισχύω.definition: strengthen, confirm; intr., prevail in or among, Arist.EN1180b4: abs., Id.PA653a31 al.; Thphr.Sens.63, cf. 67; D.S.20.58; . . the opinion prevailed that . ., Id.5.57

ἐνίσχω.definition: = to keep in one's voice, Plu.Cic.35:—Pass., to be held fast, Hdt.4.43; A.R.1.11; v.l. for in X.An.7.4.17; of phlegm, etc., to be impacted, Gal.15.221

ἐνιψηφίζομαι.definition: put to the vote, Maiuri NuovaSilloge 443

ἐνλαξεύω.definition: carve in or on, pf. Pass. AP3.9Arg

ἐνναέτης.definition: nine years old, Theoc.26.29: Ep. neut. as Adv., for nine years, Hes.Th.801:—fem. poet. AP7.643

ἐνναετία.definition: period of nine years, Sch.Il.1.1; cf

ἐνναίω.definition: dwell in, E.Hel.488; . . S.Ph.472, cf. Lyr.Alex.Adesp.35.22; S.OC788: c. acc. loci, inhabit, Mosch.4.36, A.R.1.1076: in later Prose, Aristid.Or.46.27: 3pl. fut. Med. A.R.4.1751: 3pl. aor. 1 Med. ib.1213, Call.Del.15: …

ἐνναυπηγέομαι.definition: Pass., have ships built in it, of a place, v.l. in Th.1.13

ἐννεάβοιος.definition: worth nine beeves, Il.6.236, Eleg.Alex.Adesp.1.3:—but also glossed by Hsch

ἐννεαγράμματον.definition: word of nine letters , Olymp.Alch.p.71 B

ἐννεάγωνος.definition: of a class of figurate numbers, enneagonal, Theo Sm.p.40H

ἐννεαδάκτυλος.definition: with nine fingers, Ptol.Heph. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.147B

ἐννεαέτης.definition: nine years old, IG9.639 , Annales du Service19.223

ἐννεάζω.definition: spend one's youth in, to be of great stature in one's youth, Hp.Aph.2.54; Ph.1.622; of one crowned in his mother's womb, Agath.4.25; having bloomed in spring, Philostr.Ep.51

ἐννεακαιδεκαετηρίς.definition: cycle of nineteen years, D.S.12.36, Placit.2.32.2, Ptol.Tetr.205

ἐννεακαιδεκαπλασίων.definition: gen. nineteen times as large as, Placit.2.25.1, cf. Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.20

ἐννεάκλινος.definition: with nine dining-couches, Phryn.Com.66, D.S.31.9, Them.Or.18.223a

ἐννεάκρουνος.definition: with nine spouts, name of a well at Athens, in earlier times called Hdt.6.137, Th.2.15, Polyzel.2: metaph. of an orator, copious, Lib.Ep.1493.4

ἐννεάμηνος.definition: of or in nine months, Hdt.6.69, cf. Hp.Septim.8; Gal.Nat.Fac.3.3; BGU977.13

ἐννεάμυκλος.definition: having nine stripes or folds, hence, nine years old, Call.Fr.180, cf. Hsch

ἐντρέπω.definition: turn about, Hdt.7.211; mostly metaph., make one turn, put him to shame, 1 Ep.Cor.4.14, Ael.VH3.17, S.E.P.3.135, D.L.2.29

ἐντρέφω.definition: poet. = bring up or train in, E.Ion1428; AP9.231 :—Med., Hes.Op.781, cf. Hp.Aër.12 :—Pass., to be raised or bred in, E.Ph.368, cf. Call.Iamb.1.184; Pl.Lg.798a; Plu.2.32e, 38b; Arr.Epict.4.4.48; 1 Ep.Ti.4.6

ἐντρέχεια.definition: skill, aptitude, Corn.ND18, M.Ant.1.8; concrete, an industry, Str.17.1.15

ἐντρέχω.definition: aor. run in, be active in: hence; to be current among, Arat.100

ἐντριβής.definition: metaph. from the touchstone, proved by; beaten track, App.Hann.4

ἐντρίβω.definition: rub in, esp. unguents or cosmetics; metaph., give him a drubbing, Plu.Alc.8, Luc.Prom.10:—Med., cause them to be given him, D.H.7.45; Luc.DDeor.20.2

ἐντριτωνίζω.definition: Com. word in Ar.Eq.1189, to third with water, i.e. to mix three parts of water with two of wine, with a pun on

ἔντριχος.definition: hairy, AP14.62, Sm.Ps.67.22; with; Subst., wig. Poll.2.30

ἐντρίχωμα.definition: edges of the eyelids, eyelashes; hair-sieve, also Plu.2.912e

ἐντροπαλίζομαι.definition: Pass., Frequentat. of only pres. part., often turning round, Il.6.496; esp. of men retreating with their face to the enemy, 11.547, cf. 17.109, 21.492, Q.S.12.583

ἐντροπή.definition: turning towards: only metaph. (cf; humiliation, LXXPs.34.26, al

ἐντροπία.definition: Ion. = Hp.Decent.2; subtle twists, tricks, dodges, h.Merc.245

ἐντροπόω.definition: fasten the oars with thongs, Hsch.:—Med., Agath.5.22; cf

ἐντροχάζω.definition: = intervene, occur; exercise a horse in a ring, Hippiatr.33

ἐντρυλλίζω.definition: or whisper in one's ear, Ar.Th.341; term used in quail-baiting, Poll.9.109

ἐντρυφάω.definition: revel in, delight in, c. dat; treat haughtily or contemptuously, E.Cyc.588, Plu.Them.18, Alciphr.1.35; exult over, Jul.ad Ath.279c; LXXHb.1.10: abs., Plu.Alc.23:—Pass., to be made a mock of, Id.Lys.6, Caes.64

ἐντρύφημα.definition: thing to take pleasure in, a delight, LXXEc.2.8 , Ph.1.690

ἐντρύχομαι.definition: Pass. or Med., waste away, D.C.38.46 codd

ἐντυγχάνω.definition: c. dat. rei, = S.Aj.433; cj. Valck. in E.Fr.287; of the crocodile, Hdt.2.70; . . he who fell in their way, Th.4.40; of obstacles, X.An.2.3.10; ib.4.2.10

ἐντυλίσσω.definition: wrap up, Ar.Pl.692, Nu.987 , Diocl.Com.13, Gal.10.541; Ev.Matt.27.59

ἐντυλόομαι.definition: Pass., grow hard, of callous lumps, dub. l. for Dsc.2.43

ἐντύνω.definition: fut. Lyc.734: aor. 1; c. acc., make one ready, urge him on, Thgn.196, cf. Pi.O.3.28: also c. inf., urge to do a thing, Id.P.9.66, N.9.36

ἔντυπος.definition: coined, Poll.3.86; receiving impressions, impressible, Plot.4.6.3

ἐντυπόω.definition: carve or mould in or upon; metaph., Longin.10.6

ἐντύπωμα.definition: that which is graved, of a pier, Agatharch.92

ἐντύπωσις.definition: impression, dint, pit, Thphr.Sens.51, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.2.1: metaph., Gal.10.74

ἐντυραννέομαι.definition: Pass., live under a tyranny, Cic.Att.2.14.1

ἐντυρόω.definition: in Pass., to be turned into cheese, prob. in Nic.Al.364

ἐντύφω.definition: fut. smoke as one does wasps; frost-bitten, EM458.42

ἐντύχημα.definition: = sq., in pl. prob. for Plu.Phoc.5, cf. Him.Ecl.32.4

ἐντυχία.definition: = conversation, intercourse; meeting, Plb.6.11a.4; interview, Aristeas1

ἐνυβρίζω.definition: insult or mock one in a thing; c. dat. pers., insult, Plb.10.26.3, cf. POxy.237 vi 17 ; D.S.34.2

ἐνυγροθηρευτής.definition: one who seeks his prey in the water, fisherman, Pl.Lg.824b

ἐνύδριος.definition: = Orac. ap. Lyd.Mens.3.5; Iamb.Myst.1.9. Adv. ibid

ἐνυπάρχω.definition: exist or be present in; to be immanent or inherent, = Arist.Ph.193a10, cf. 194b24; ib.233b35; the inherence whereof is the cause of existences, Id.Metaph.998a31, cf. 1014a26, Plot.5.3.11, Jul.Or.4.140c, etc

ἐνυπνιάζω.definition: dream, Arist.Insomn.459a21, Somn.Vig.453b19, HA537b13, al.:—in Med. and Pass. c. acc., Hp.VM10, cf. Arist.HA587b10, Ph.1.672, Plu.Cat.Ma.23: so in fut. LXXJl.3.1, Lyd.Ost.33: aor. Med. LXXJd.7.13, ib.Ge.37.5,6,10

ἐνυπνιάστρια.definition: she who dreams, title of book, prob. in IG2.992ii6

ἐνυπνιόμαντις.definition: one who divines by dreams, Hsch. s.v

ἐνύπνιον.definition: thing seen in sleep, in appos; after Hom., = dream, the vision of a dream, Hdt.8.54; A.Pers.518, cf. 226, Pl.R.572b; Pi.O.13.79; Ar.V.25, Pl.Plt.290b; Id.R.443b; Theoc.21.29, Sammelb.685 :—Artem. distinguishes a mere …

ἐνύπνιος.definition: in sleep, in dreams appearing, A.Th.710; AP12.124

ἐνυπόκειμαι.definition: subsist in, Aristombr. ap. Stob.1.52.21, cf. Hierocl.in CA11p.438M

ἐνυποτάσσω.definition: fut. Pass. to be made subject, LXXTo.14.9 cod. Alex

ἐνυπτιάζω.definition: throw back upon, Philostr.Im.2.16; glorying in his pomposity, Id.VS1.10

ἐνυφαίνω.definition: weave in as a pattern; weave in a place, Leg.Gort.2.51

ἐνύφασμα.definition: pattern woven in, D.S.17.70, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.14.7

ἐνωθέω.definition: aor. 1 A.R.4.1243:—thrust in or upon, l.c.; Plu.Luc.28

ἐνωμοτάρχης.definition: leader of an , Th.5.66 codd., X.Lac.11.4, Ascl.Tact.2.2:—also X.An.3.4.21 , Arr.Tact.6.2

ἐνωμοτία.definition: prop. band of sworn soldiers; later, = cj. in Ascl.Tact.2.2; also, a quarter of a Arr.Tact.6.2

ἐνώμοτος.definition: confirmed by oaths, PLond.1.113.1 . Adv. POxy.904.3; Subst., conspirator, Plu.Sert.26

ἐνωπή.definition: face, countenance, used by Hom. only in dat. as Adv., before the face, openly, Il.5.374, [21.510]; later Nic.Th.227

ἐνώπιος.definition: facing, to the front; neut. as Adv., face to face, Theoc.22.152; in person, IG12.1061.10 , PTeb.14.13 : as Prep. c. gen., Aeschin.3.43 codd., PCair.Zen.73.14 , PGrenf.1.38.11 , Ep.Rom.12.17, Ep.Gal.1.20, Hermog.Inv.1.…

ἐνωραΐζομαι.definition: beautify oneself for the benefit of; give oneself airs in, Agath.2.26

ἐνωτίζομαι.definition: give ear, hearken to, LXXGe.4.23; Act.Ap.2.14: c.dat., LXXEx.15.26

ἐξαγγελία.definition: secret information sent out to the; expression, of style, Longin.Rh.p.186H

ἐξαγγέλλω.definition: tell out, proclaim, make known, freq. with; express, Hermog.Id.2.5:—Pass., to be expressed, Arist.Po.1460b11; Ti.Locr.102e

ἐξάγγελος.definition: messenger who brings out news from; on the Greek stage, messenger who told what was doing in the house or behind the scenes ; first used by Aeschylus, Philostr.VS1.9

ἐξαγγίζω.definition: pour out of a vessel, Hp.VM22; cf

ἐξαγιάζω.definition: assay, Gloss.:—Pass., of measures, to be fixed, HeroStereom.2.54.3

ἐξαγίζω.definition: drive out as accursed, . . A.Ag.641: or perh. fr. taken as victims from many homes

ἐξαγκυλόω.definition: fasten by an Poll.5.56 :—Med., take a spear by the Sch.Nic.Th.170

ἐξαγκωνίζω.definition: nudge with the elbow, Ar.Ec.259; bind one's hands behind his back, D.S.34.2, Ph.2.564; D.S.13.27: metaph., Ph.2.128

ἐξάγνυμι.definition: break and tear away, rend, . . Il.5.161; 17.63: aor. 2 part. Pass. A.R.4.1686

ἐξαγοράζω.definition: buy from, Plb.3.42.2; buy up, Plu.Crass.2; buy off, Dicaearch.1.22; redeem, D.S.36.2; Ep.Gal.3.13:—Med., Ep.Col.4.5, cf. Ep.Eph.5.16

ἐξαγορεία.definition: or excantation of disease, cure by confession, Ptol.Tetr.170

ἐξαγορευτής.definition: one who confesses his sins, ib.158

ἐξαγορεύω.definition: fut. Epic.Alex.Adesp.2.55: aor. supplied by fut. and pf. by out, make known, declare, Od.11.234; betray a secret or mystery, Hdt.2.170; Id.9.89; Luc.Pisc.33; confess, LXXLe.5.5, Plu.2.168d: abs., Rhetor.inCat.Cod. Ast…

ἐξαγριαίνω.definition: make savage, Pl.Ly.206b; Ph.1.670; intr. in Act., = Pass., App.Ill.23

ἐξαγριόω.definition: make wild or waste, opp; = foreg., make savage, Hdt.6.123, E.Ph.876:—Pass., to be brutalized, Pl.Lg.870a, cf. Ph.1.584, al

ἐξάγω.definition: pf. D.42.19, PHib.1.34.10 (iii B; of persons, mostly c. gen. loci, Od.22.458, 23.372, Il.5.353; ib.35: with . ., Od.8.106, 20.21; Hdt.4.148, al.; having brought her out from Argos, Il.13.379; bring out of prison, rele…

ἐξαγωγή.definition: leading out of troops, X.Eq.Mag.4.9; drawing out of a ship from shallows, Hdt.4.179

ἐξαγώγιμος.definition: unsettled, migratory, of people, v.l. for E.Fr.360.10; for drawing off water, D.H.4.44

ἐξαγώγιον.definition: duty on exports, Inscr.Prien.3.28 , Decr. ap.J.AJ14.10.6, Just.Edict.13.15

ἐξαγωγός.definition: waste-pipe for letting off water; overflow drain, PPetr.2p.14 , etc

ἐξαγωνίζομαι.definition: fight, struggle hard, E.HF155; D.S.13.73 codd

ἑξαγωνίζω.definition: to be in sextile aspect, Ptol.Tetr.115

ἑξαδακτυλία.definition: possession of six fingers, Phlp.in GA194.4

ἑξαδακτυλιαῖος.definition: six inches long, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.4.41

ἑξαδάκτυλος.definition: = foreg., six inches long; having six fingers, Gal.19.454, Eustr.in EN376.1, Tz.H.7.902

ἐξαδιαφορέω.definition: to be utterly indifferent to, Ph.1.214, 2.279

ἐξαδυνατέω.definition: to be quite unable or incapable, c.inf., Arist.Pol.1282b4, Plu.Alc.23; Arist.GA785a10: abs., Id.HA575a21, Plb.1.58.5; Plu.Mar.33; generation becomes impossible, Thphr.CP1.16.3

ἐξᾴδω.definition: sing out, sing one's last song, of the swan; sing the of a chorus, Plot.6.9.8

ἑξάεδρος.definition: with six surfaces, Theol.Ar.25; Subst. hexahedron, Gal.5.669

ἑξάειδος.definition: composed of six ingredients, Phlp.in GC192.29, 269.34; cf

ἐξαερόω.definition: Ion. make into air, volatilize, Arist.Pr.938b34, Luc.Peregr.30:—Pass., evaporate, Hp.Nat.Puer.25, Arist.Pr.933a36; to be dissipated in perspiration, Aret.SD2.1

ἑξαετής.definition: or six years old; of six years, Plu.Pyrrh.26. Adv. for six years, Od.3.115; cf

ἑξαετία.definition: term of six years, Ph.2.371, J.AJ16.1.1, POxy.101.17 , etc

ἑξαήμερος.definition: of or in six days, the six days of creation, Ph.1.69: also Id.2.197

ἐξαθέλγω.definition: draw or drain off, in Pass., Hp.Oss.19, Hsch

ἐξαθρέω.definition: look at carefully, dub. in Thesp. ap. Chrysipp.Stoic.2.55

ἐξαθροίζομαι.definition: Med., seek out and collect, E.Ph.1169

ἐξαιγειρόομαι.definition: Pass., of the white poplar , degenerate into a black poplar , Thphr.CP2.16.2

ἐξαιθραπεύω.definition: to be a satrap, SIG167.2 ; cf

ἐξαιθριάζω.definition: expose to sun and air, Hp.Int.35, Dsc.5.16, Apollon. ap.Gal.12.478:—Pass., Com.Adesp. in PLond.ined.2294

ἐξαιμάσσω.definition: Att. make quite bloody; metaph., open one's griefs afresh, D.H.6.81

ἐξαιματόω.definition: change into blood, Gal.8.359:—Pass., Arist.Somn.Vig.456b4, Ph.2.244

ἐξαιμάτωσις.definition: conversion into blood, of food, ibid., Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.63, Gal.11.139

ἔξαιμος.definition: bloodless, drained of blood, Hp.VC16, Epid.5.6, D.S.3.35, etc

ἐξαίνυμαι.definition: take out or away, took out , Od.15.206: in Il. always in phrase animam eripuit, 5.155, al.; Nic.Al.272

ἐξαιρέσιμος.definition: that can be taken out, days taken out of the calendar, Arist.Oec.1351b15, cf. Cic.Verr.2.2.52.129

ἐξαίρεσις.definition: taking out the entrails of victims; removal, purgation, Porph.Abst.2.43

ἐξαιρετέος.definition: to be taken out or removed; one must take out, remove, Pl.Lg.942c, cf. Tht.157b

ἐξαιρέω.definition: fut. later D.H.7.56, etc.: aor. 2; Med., take out for oneself, from his quiver, Il.8.323; their large sails, X.HG1.1.13; discharge their cargoes, Hdt.4.196; X.An.5.1.16; Th.8.90: abs., Syngr. ap. D.35.13, etc.:—Pass.,…

ἐξαίρημα.definition: sum deducted, SIG1106.78 (Cos; reserved portion of an estate, AJA16.13

ἐξαίρω.definition: Ep. Hom. , also in Ion; seemingly intr., rise from the ground, of a bird, D.S.2.50; start, Plb.2.23.4, cf. LXXNu.2.9

ἐξαίσιος.definition: also X.HG4.3.8:—beyond what is; outstepping right, lawless, having done some lawless act, Od.4.690; . . fearing some lawless man, 17.577; . . Il.15.598; B.14.58

ἐξαΐσσω.definition: contr. Att. rush forth, start out, Il.12.145; Ar.Pl.733; Id.Ra.567; start, Arist.Pr.957a32; Phld.Mus.p.12 K., cf. Max. Tyr.37.5; the violence of these passions, Plu.2.83e:—Pass., Il.3.368

ἐξαισχύνομαι.definition: to be ashamed, c. inf., Procl.in Prm.p.648S

ἐξαιτέω.definition: demand or ask for from another, c. dupl; Med., ask for oneself, demand, Act., Hdt.1.159,9.87, S.El.656, etc.; Lys.20.31; Ev.Luc.22.31; for whose aid I prayed, PMag.Par.1.434, cf. 1290

ἐξαίτησις.definition: demanding one for punishment or; demand for satisfaction, D.S.8 Fr.25

ἐξαιτραπεύω.definition: = to be a satrap, prob. in SIG134.3

ἐξαιφνίδιος.definition: also Pl.Cra.414a, Gal.6.185:—sudden, Pl. l.c.; Gal. l.c.; Hierocl.p.60A

ἐξαιωρέομαι.definition: Pass., to be suspended from a thing, Hp.Art.70

ἐξακανθίζω.definition: pick out thorns: metaph., 'pick holes in', Cic.Att. 6.6.1

ἐξακανθόομαι.definition: Pass., become prickly, prob. in Thphr.HP6.4.2

ἐξακέομαι.definition: heal completely, Hp.Vict.3.67: hence, make; c. acc., appease, Il.4.36, cf. Od.3.145; quench, D.C.60.9; make up for, X.Cyr.8.2.22; Iamb.Myst.1.11

ἐξακεστήριος.definition: remedying evil, Lex Solonis; expiatory, Id.5.54

ἐξακμάζω.definition: to be gone by, of an opportunity, Sch.S.Aj.594

ἐξακολουθέω.definition: follow, of persons; of things, follow, result from, c. dat., Epicur.Fr.181; attend, c. dat., Plb.4.5.6, 5.78.4; D.H.Comp.24; esp. of penalties, UPZ112v10 , PTeb.5.132 ; also of obligations, fall on one, CPR5.15, etc

ἐξακοντίζω.definition: dart or hurl forth, launch; intr., dart away, Arist.HA590b29

ἐξακοντισμός.definition: = foreg., Gal.4.523, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.10.2; shooting of a shooting star, Arist.Mu.395b5

ἑξακοσίαρχος.definition: captain of six hundred men, Polyaen.Prooem.2

ἐξάκουστος.definition: heard, audible, Ph.Bel.93.51; famous, Sch.D.P.13, Hsch

ἐξακούω.definition: hear or catch a sound, esp. from a distance; understand in a certain sense, Id.7.89

ἐξακριβόω.definition: make exact, precise, or accurate; intr., speak accurately, Arist.EN1096b30; Plb.2.56.4, cf. Porph.Abst.1.39

ἐξακρίβωσις.definition: strict observance; exact statement, Eustr.in EN108.6

ἐξάκτωρ.definition: = Lat.exactor, BGU21 ii 17, Tz.H.5.607:—hence his office, PLond.2.378.8, PGen.56.32

ἐξαλαόω.definition: blind utterly, Od.11.103; make blind and useless, Opp.C.3.228

ἐξαλαπάζω.definition: sack, storm, Il.4.40, 1.129, etc.; also, empty a city of its inhabitants, clear it out, so as to plant new settlers in it, Od.4.176: generally, destroy utterly, Il.13.813, 20.30: metaph., Theoc.2.85.—Ep. word, used by…

ἐξαλγέω.definition: c. acc., suffer pain in, Ps.-Callisth.3.27

ἐξάλειπτρον.definition: unguent-box, Ar.Ach.1063, Antiph.208, LXXJb.41.22, IG2.751Biid4,11.161B125, , etc

ἐξαλείφω.definition: pf. Pass. : subj.aor.2; wipe out, obliterate, E.Hel.262: metaph., wipe out of one's mind, Pl.Tht.187b; D.37.34; Men.Pk.310 ; cancel, And.1.76; Lys.1.48; Arist.Ath.40.3; IG12.91.10; esp. at Athens, strike his name off …

ἐξαλέομαι.definition: beware of, avoid, escape, Il.18.586; mostly in Ep. aor. 1 inf., Hes.Op.105, cf. 758,802, Orac. ap.Ar.Eq.1080: abs., A.R.2.319, cf. 3.466: pres. Q.S.2.385.—Ep. word, cf. sq

ἐξαλεύομαι.definition: = foreg., . . . . S.Aj.656 codd., but is prob. l

ἐξαλίνδω.definition: only aor. part. pf. out or thoroughly, take him away when you have given him a good roll on the Ar.Nu.32 ; to which Strepsiades retorts, you have rolled me out of house and home, Ar.Nu.33

ἐξαλλαγή.definition: complete change, alteration; variations in the forms of nouns, Arist.Po.1458b2: generally, variation, Procl.Inst.162, 175

ἐξάλλαγμα.definition: recreation, amusement, in pl., Anaxandr.20, Parth.24.1

ἐξαλλάσσω.definition: Att. change utterly or quite; intr., of evolution, . . Hp.Vict.1.6; degenerate, Thphr.HP8.8.3:—Pass., ib.4.4.14

ἐξαλλοιόω.definition: change, alter, LXX3 Ma.3.21:—Pass., change utterly, Thphr.CP2.15.2, cf. Ph.1.674

ἐξαλλοίωσις.definition: metabolism, of food, prob. for Gal.15.250

ἐξάλλομαι.definition: fut. LXXMi.2.12: aor; start from its socket, be dislocated, of a limb, Hp.Art.46; of a broken bone, Plu.2.341b; of wheels, start from the axle, X.Cyr.7.1.32

ἐξαλλοτριόω.definition: export, Str.5.1.9; divert, alienate, BSA17.229 , cf. PGiss.2.24

ἐξάλμυρος.definition: having lost its saltness, of earth, Thunell Sitologen papyri 1viii 11

ἐξαλύσκω.definition: aor. flee from, c. acc., E.El.219, Hipp.673 : abs., escape, A.Eu.111, E.Hec.1194: c. gen., Opp.H.3.104; cf

ἐξαμαρτάνω.definition: Pass., to be mismanaged, to be a failure, Pl.Prt.357d; X.Eq.4.2; Arist.Pol.1289b9

ἐξαμαυρόω.definition: obscure utterly, E.Fr.781.64 :—Pass., of a plant, lose its natural character, Thphr.CP2.16.4: metaph., Ph.2.438; Plu.2.469a; Longin.17.2, dub.l. in Hp.Alim.6

ἐξαμάω.definition: mow or reap out, finish mowing or reaping, A.Pers.822, cf.Ag.1655 , E.Ba.1315; . . sowing and reaping, S.Tr.33; Plu.Demetr.4:—Pass., having all the race cut off root and branch, S.Aj.1178, cf. Paus.8.7.7.—Poet. and la…

ἐξαμβλόω.definition: make abortive: metaph., you have made a notion miscarry, Ar.Nu.137; to which Strepsiades retorts, your abortive thought, ib.139, cf. Pl.Tht.150e; Ph.1.219:—Pass., Thphr.CP4.5.3; Plu.2.2e

ἐξαμείβω.definition: exchange, alter; intr. in Act., Id.Or.816

ἐξαμέλγω.definition: milk out, suck out, A.Ch.898:—Pass; press out, E.Cyc.209

ἐξαμελέω.definition: to be utterly careless of, Hdt.1.97: abs., show no care, be negligent, Arist.Pol.1269b22:—Pass.impers., no care is taken . ., Id.EN1180a27; Plu.Cam.18; being uncared for, Arist.EN1180a30; Thphr.HP3.2.2

ἑξαμερής.definition: in six parts, of the hexameter, Orph.Fr.356

ἐξαμηχανέω.definition: get out of a difficulty, E.Heracl.495

ἐξαμιλλάομαι.definition: aor. 1 part. and; drive out of, E.Or.431; drive out of his wits, ib.38

ἐξαμυγδαλίζω.definition: make like an almond, Aq.Ex.25.32:—also ib.35

ἐξαμύνομαι.definition: Med., ward off from oneself, drive away, A.Pr.483; E.Supp.208; Id.Or.269:—Act. is dub. l. in Them.Or.23.284b

ἐξαμυστίζω.definition: drink off at a draught, Pl.Com.189

ἐξαμφοτερίζω.definition: make ambiguous, has led the argument into a contradiction , Pl.Euthd.300d; Hsch., cf. EM347.7

ἐξαναβαίνω.definition: get to the top of, Artem.2.28; Epigr.Gr.782

ἐξαναβρύω.definition: causal of foreg., cause happiness to spring forth from the earth, A.Eu.925

ἐξαναγεννάομαι.definition: Pass., to be born again, Jul.Ep.61c

ἐξαναγκάζω.definition: fut. S.Ichn.212:—force or compel; force out, Hp.Haem.2

ἐξανδρόομαι.definition: come to man's years; the host having grown to men from teeth, E.Supp.703

ἐξάνειμι.definition: go forth from, A.R.2.459; come back from, h.Pan.15

ἐξανεμόω.definition: blow out with wind, inflate:—Pass., to be; Pass., of corn, to be parched by wind, 'wind- bitten', Thphr.HP8.10.3

ἐξάνθησις.definition: = foreg., Hp.Aph.3.20, Ph.2.101; fading, Thphr.CP6.15.2 codd

ἐξανθίζω.definition: deck as with flowers, paint in various; Med., gather flowers, Plu.2.661f

ἐξανθρωπίζω.definition: humanize, bring down to men; less humanized , Hp.Oct.12

ἐξάνθρωπος.definition: unsociable, of epileptics, Aret.SD1.4; it is an inhuman calamity, Id.SA1.6

ἐξανίημι.definition: poet. impf. A.R.4.622: fut; c. gen., send forth from, Pi.P.4.99; E.Ba.762; Id.HF625

ἐξανιστάνω.definition: = sq., drive out of one's senses, Dsc.4.73

ἐξαντλέω.definition: drain or draw off, Pl.Lg.736b, PTeb.123.6 (i; metaph., endure to the end, see out, E.Cyc.10; ib.110; Id.Fr.454; Men.74; E.Supp.838

ἐξαπατύλλω.definition: Com. Dim. of cheat a little, humbug, Ar.Ach.657,Eq.1144

ἑξαπλάσιος.definition: Ion. six times as large as, Hdt.4.81: abs., Plu.2.1020a, 1028f: neut. six times as much wax, Orib.Fr.99

ἐξαπλόω.definition: unfold, roll out; unfold, explain, Ph.1.302:—Pass., Demetr.Eloc.254, S.E.M.7.233

ἐξάπλωσις.definition: opening out, of roots, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.12; explanation, Erot.Prooem

ἐξαποβαίνω.definition: step out of, Od.12.306; A.R.3.199, etc

ἐξαπόλλυμι.definition: Pass., with pf. 2 aor. 2 utterly out of, c. gen., Il.6.60; 18.290; Od.20.357; A.Ag.528: abs., perish utterly, Hdt.4.173, S.Fr.236

ἐξαπολογία.definition: title of three speeches of Antipho, second defence, rejoinder

ἐξαποστολή.definition: sending away, IG2.985A1; discharge of an engine or projectile, Ph.Bel.53.46, HeroBel.79.4, 110.10

ἐξαποχέω.definition: in Pass., pour forth from, Tz.H.3.327

ἑξάπρυμνος.definition: with six stems, i.e. ships, Lyc.1347

ἐξάπτω.definition: fasten from or to; metaph., let prayers fall from one's mouth, E.Or.383; consider actions as dependent upon chance, Plu.Sull.6; continue the narrative, D.L.8.50; dependent on it, Ti.Locr.102e

ἐξαράομαι.definition: utter curses, S.Ant.427; dedicate with solemn prayers, Aeschin.3.116

ἐξαράσσω.definition: c. acc. pers., assail him furiously with abuse, Ar.Nu.1373

ἐξαργέω.definition: to be quite torpid, Arist.EN1099a2; Pass., to be quite neglected, S.Ph.556; Plu.2.2e

ἐξαρθρόω.definition: dislocate, LXX4 Ma.10.5; = foreg. II, Arist.Phgn.810b35

ἐξαριθμέω.definition: enumerate, count, Hdt.7.59,60; count out, pay in ready money, D.27.58

ἐξαρίθμησις.definition: numbering, enumeration; reckoning up, recounting, Plb.16.26.5

ἐξαρτάω.definition: hang upon, Plb.18.18.4; stretch out, Ael.NA4.21

ἐξάρτημα.definition: that which is suspended from; that which is attached or dependent, Dam.Pr.130

ἐξάρτυσις.definition: equipment, esp. of musical arrangement, Callicrat. ap. Stob.4.28.16, Eurypham.ib.39.27; of the soul, Iamb.VP15.64 , 25.114

ἐξαρτύω.definition: get ready, E.El.422; Med., train musically, Plu.2.973d

ἑξάστυλος.definition: with six columns in front, of temples, Vitr.3.3.7

ἐξατιμόομαι.definition: Pass., to be utterly dishonoured, LXXEz.16.61

ἐξατμίζω.definition: turn into vapour, draw up as vapour; intr. in Act., = Pass., Arist.Mete.383a16, al., GA782a29

ἐξατονέω.definition: to be tired out, Arist.HA630b8; to be weakened, Ph.2.672

ἐξαττικίζω.definition: express in Attic form, Atticize, Phryn.PSp.19B

ἐξαυαίνω.definition: dry up, . . Hdt.4.173:—Pass., . . ib.151, cf. Hp.Carn.11, Ar.Fr.612, Arist.GA750a22, Hsch. s.v

ἔξαυγος.definition: not i.e. more than fifteen degrees from the sun, Olymp.in Mete.56.2, Porph. ap. Heph.Astr.2.18, Steph.in Hp.2.363D

ἐξαυλέω.definition: pipe away, wear out, of the mouthpieces of clarionets, Poll.4.67

ἐξαυλίζομαι.definition: leave one's quarters, go out of camp into villages, X.An.7.8.21; v.l. in Luc.VH1.37

ἐξαύξω.definition: increase, Thphr.CP1.22.1:—Pass., grow too fast, Id.HP6.6.6

ἐξαυστήρ.definition: flesh-hook for taking meat out of a pot, A.Fr.2, Poll.6.88, EM346.56, Hsch.; IG2.818.27; ib.689

ἐξαυτομολέω.definition: desert from a place, Ar.Nu.1104; Pass., to be betrayed by deserters, Aen.Tact.24.16

ἐξαυχέω.definition: boast loudly, profess, c. part., A.Ag.872 codd.: c. inf. fut., S.Ant.390; c. inf. pres., E.Supp.504: c. acc. rei, S.Ph.869

ἐξαυχμέω.definition: or suffer from drought; in Pass., to be dried up, D.L.7.141

ἐξαύω.definition: take out, esp. dressed meat , . . Pl.Com.38, cf. Hsch; heat, aor. 1 Med., Eratosth.24

ἐξαφαιρέω.definition: take away:—Med., Od.22.444, cf. S.El.1157; Trag.Adesp.296; f.l. in D.8.42

ἐξαφανίζω.definition: destroy utterly, Eub.107.11; J.AJ3.15.1; disappear utterly, Pl.Plt.270e, Sor.1.34

ἐξαφεδρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be excreted, dub. in Herm. ap. Stob.1.42.7 codd.; v

ἐξαφρίζω.definition: remove the froth by boiling, despumated, Dsc.2.82.3:—Med., metaph. from a horse, exhaust by foaming, A.Ag.1067

ἐξαφρόομαι.definition: Pass., turn into foam, cj. in Herm. ap. Stob.1.42.7

ἐξαφύω.definition: draw forth, . . Od.14.95: poet. aor., Opp.H.1.573: Ep. fut. 3pl., Hsch

ἑξάχαλκος.definition: coin of the value of six IG5.1433.29

ἑξάχρονος.definition: of six times, Heph.3.2, cf. Procl.in Prm.p.990S

ἐξεγγύησις.definition: giving of bail or surety, esp. to take one out of prison, D.24.77

ἐξεγείρω.definition: awaken, S.OT65, Tr.978:—Pass., to be awaked; raise from the dead, 1 Ep.Cor.6.14:—Pass., A.Ch.495

ἐξέγερσις.definition: awakening, Plb.9.15.4; waking up, D.H.3.70, Plu.2.909d

ἐξέδρα.definition: hall or arcade furnished with recesses and; bench, seat, in front of a house, D.L.4.19; any public bench, Str.13.4.5, D.Chr.28.2; belvedere, Nic.Dam.Fr.1J

ἐξέδριον.definition: Dim. of foreg., IG12.907.27 , GDI5075.58 , RousselCultes Égyptiens224 , Cic.Fam.7.23.3

ἔξεδρος.definition: away from home, opp; c. gen., out of, away from, E.IT80: metaph., insensate words, Id.Hipp.935

ἐξεθίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be habituated, accustomed, c. inf., Ph.2.363, 391

ἐξεθισμός.definition: change of habit, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.1.7

ἐξεικάζω.definition: make like, adapt, X.Hier.1.38:—Pass., was like it, Id.Cyr.1.6.39: mostly in pf. part., not mere semblances, but the things themselves, A.Ag.1244; . . Id.Th.445; portrayed, E.Ph.162; he is not represented by a portrait…

ἐξεικονίζω.definition: explain by a simile, Plu.2.445c; Pass., to be fully shapen or formed, LXXEx.21.22sq., Hsch

ἐξειλέω.definition: slip out from its cover; intr., escape, aor. PAmh.2.142.9 , cf. EM348.12

ἐξείλησις.definition: release, escape from, in wrestling, Pl.Lg.796a

ἐξείλλω.definition: = disentangle, of hounds at; keep forcibly from, debar from, D.37.35, cf. Sol.Oxy.221 xiv 13; Tab.Heracl.1.152

ἐξειλύω.definition: unfold:—Pass., of serpents gliding along the ground, Theoc.24.17

ἔξειμι.definition: come forth to apply the test, S.Ph.98; but, submit to the test, Id.Fr.105; . . E.Fr.334

ἐξείρω.definition: put forth, Hdt.3.87; pull out, Id.Eq.378 , Hermipp.Hist.43

ἐξειρωνεύομαι.definition: turn into jest, ridicule, J.AJ15.3.6; ib.15.7.4

ἐξελαιόω.definition: make into oil, Thphr.CP6.8.1:—Pass., become oily, ib.6.7.4

ἐξελασία.definition: driving out cattle, Plb.12.4.10; intr., expedition, Ps.-Hdt.Vit.Hom.9

ἐξέλασις.definition: driving out, expulsion; intr., marching out, expedition, Id.7.183, cf. X.Cyr.8.3.1, etc.; charge of cavalry, Plu.Art.16

ἐξελατέος.definition: to be driven out, Jul.Ep.89b; one must expel, Epicur.Ep.1p.24U.; Them.Or.21.259a

ἐξελίκτρα.definition: roller, cylinder, of a windlass, HeroAut.5.3

ἐξελίσσω.definition: Att. unroll, unfold; of any rapid motion, evolve the mazy dance, E.Tr.3; Aristid.1.97 J.; hunt one round and round, E.HF977; wheel in circles round him, Hld.5.14; Plu.2.368a; of the hare, double, Arr.Cyn.17.3:— Pass.,…

ἐξελκόω.definition: cause sores in, Arist.Pr.883b31; D.S.14.88:—Pass., break out into sores, Hp.VM18; J.AJ2.14.4

ἐξελκυσμός.definition: pulling out, removal, Ruf. ap; extension, Heliod. ap.Orib.49.10.6
