ἐξεμέω.definition: pf. Aristid.Or.50.5 (v.l; abs., vomit, be sick, Ar.Ra.11

ἐξεναρίζω.definition: strip or spoil a foe slain in fight; kill, slay, Od.11.273; Il.6.30, cf. Hes.Th.289, B.5.146, Lyc.50, etc.—In Hom. more freq. than the simple Verb

ἐξενέπω.definition: speak out, proclaim, Pi.N.4.33; abs., speak, A.R.1.764

ἐξενιαυτίζω.definition: spend a year in exile, Sch.E.Or.1645

ἐξενίαυτος.definition: in arrears, carried over from one; Adv. yearly, PAmh.2.85.14

ἐξεντερίζομαι.definition: Pass., have the entrails taken out, Dsc.2.62; of plants, have the pith taken out, Id.4.162:—also Gloss

ἐξεπᾴδω.definition: charm away, Pl.Phd.77e, Plu.2.384a:—Pass., to be charmed out of their nature, S.OC1194

ἐξεπαίρω.definition: stir up, excite one to do, c. inf., Ar.Lys.623; E.Fr.963

ἐξεπεύχομαι.definition: boast loudly that . ., c. inf., S.Ph.668

ἐξεπίσταμαι.definition: know thoroughly, Hdt.2.43, 5.93: c; know by heart, Pl.Phdr.228b

ἐξεπισφραγίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be stamped deep on a thing, Chaerem.14.10

ἐξεπομβρέω.definition: rain on, S.Fr.524.4: c. acc., Tz.H.3.59

ἐξεράω.definition: aor. :—Pass., aor.1 part; disgorge, Crates Com.14.8; = Pherecr.131.1

ἐξεργάζομαι.definition: accomplish, achieve, S.Ant.384, cf. Men.Epit.474; work utter confusion, X.Eq.9.4; E.Heracl.960; bring it about, Aeschin.3.239; Plb.5.26.6: c. dupl. acc., work him mischief, Hdt.6.3, cf. Pl.Ep.352d, etc.:—Pass., A.Pers…

ἐξεργασία.definition: working out, completion, Plb.10.45.6; labour at a thing, high state of cultivation, App.BC1.11: abs., Thphr.CP3.1.6: treatment, discussion of a subject by an author, D.H.Isoc.4, Gal.5.664, etc.; Plu.2.1004e, cf. Phld.…

ἐξέργω.definition: Att. fut. Ar.Ach.825:—shut out; constrain, compel, Pl.Lg.935c:—Pass., to be constrained by necessity to undertake a thing, Hdt.7.96: c. inf., ib.139; Id.9.111; Th.3.70

ἐξερεείνω.definition: c. acc. rei, inquire into, Od.10.14; c. acc. pers., inquire after, . . 23.86; inquire of, A.R.4.1250: abs., make inquiry, Il.9.672, etc.:—Med., 10.81

ἐξερεθίζω.definition: strengthd. for Pi.P.8.13, Ph.2.359, Plu.Aem.30, etc.; of a plaster, stimulate, CrateuasFr.8

ἐξερείδω.definition: prop firmly, Plb.8.4.6; support, Luc.Trag.55; Dsc.1.69.4:—Pass., to be underpinned, Plb.16.11.5, Sor.1.47

ἐξερείπω.definition: strike off, Pi.P.4.264; more freq. intr. in aor. 2 inf. to earth, Il.14.414; the mane streaming downwards from the yoke-cushion, 17.440; letting their necks fall on the ground, Hes.Sc.174; fall down, Id.Th.704.—Mostly…

ἐξερεύγομαι.definition: vomit forth, LXXWi.19.10; of a tumour, break out, Hp.Prorrh.1.168

ἐξερευνάω.definition: 2, al.), search out, examine, S.OT258, El.1100; Aen.Tact.28.4; Epicur.Ep.3p.64U.; Plb.14.1.13, cf. LXX l.c., al.; E.Hel.429:—Med., D.C.52.6; Plb.9.5.8, cf. 18.21.1

ἐξερεύνησις.definition: inquiry, investigation, LXXPs.63.7 , cj. in Lyd.Ost.16

ἐξερέω.definition: Att. contr. fut. of :—I will speak out, tell out, utter aloud, Hom. always abs. in sg., Il.8.286, 12.215, Od.9.365, al.; in tmesi, Il.1.204, 233, al.: c. acc. in Trag., S.OT800, cf. 219, etc.: c. dupl. acc., Id.El.984…

ἐξερημόω.definition: make quite desolate, leave it destitute of heirs, D.43.76, cf. LXXLe.26.31, al.; S.El.1010 ; Pl.Ep.332e; leaving their own places destitute , X.Vect.4.47; making it destitute of teeth, E.HF253:— Pass., to be left dest…

ἐξεριθεύομαι.definition: bind to oneself by party ties, Plb.10.22.9

ἐξέρομαι.definition: Ion. fut. aor. 2; c. acc. rei, inquire into a thing, Od.13.127; so also . . will inquire concerning him, what he is now about, S.Ph.439

ἐξέρπω.definition: aor. Arist.HA599a26; abs., creep out or forth, of a lame man, S.Ph.294; Ar.Eq.607; of insects, Arist.HA550a5, 599a26

ἐξέρρω.definition: in imper., away out of the land! E.Hipp.973: impf. Hsch

ἐξέρυθρος.definition: very red, Id.Coac.154; Thphr.HP4.6.10; red in the face, Arist.Pr.869a8, cf. 903a3

ἐξερύω.definition: Ion. aor.1 Ep. and also :—draw out of, . . Il.5.112; . . Od.22.386, cf. Hdt.1.141; Il.16.505; snatch out of, 23.870; but . . by the foot, 10.490; draw out, 13.194; tear out, Od.18.87; Hdt.2.38

ἐξέρχομαι.definition: fut. supplies the fut., also impf. aor. 2 the only tense used in Hom.:-go or come out of, c. gen.loci, Il.22.237,413,417; 10.140; etc., A.Ch.663, S.El.778, etc.; . . Hdt.8.75, 9.12, S.OC37, etc.; . . E.Ph.476; of an a…

ἐξερωέω.definition: swerve from the course, of shy horses, Il.23.468; Theoc.25.189

ἐξερωτάω.definition: search out, inquire, Pi.P.9.44; c. acc. pers., question, E.Fr.579, BGU1141.34

ἐξεσθίω.definition: fut. pf. aor. away, eat up, Ar.Eq.1032, cf. Epimenid.10; Id.V.925; Id.Eq.698; Arist.HA554b4, cf. Dsc.Eup.1.150

ἐξετάζω.definition: fut. rarely Isoc.9.34, cf; of troops, inspect, review, Th.7.33,35, etc.; Hell.Oxy.10.1:—Pass., E.Supp.391, cf. Th.6.97

ἐξέτασις.definition: close examination, scrutiny, test; a military inspection or review, hold a review of . ., Th.4.74, 6.45,96; X.An.1.2.14; ib.5.3.3

ἐξεταστής.definition: examiner, inquirer into; auditor of public accounts, Arist.Pol.1322b11, SIG284.10 , 976.77 , 1015.32

ἐξευγενίζω.definition: = Hsch.; produce noble offspring, Vett.Val.119.26; make noble, Sophon.in de An.145.14:—but apptly., = degeneration, Gloss

ἐξευθετίζω.definition: set in order, prob. in S.Ichn.270

ἐξευκρινέω.definition: handle with discrimination, Hp.Fract.15; treat them systematically, Plb.35.2.6

ἐξευλαβέομαι.definition: guard carefully against, Pl.La.199d, al.; E.Andr.644; . . A.Fr.205

ἐξευμαρίζω.definition: make light or easy, E.HF18; Med., prepare, E.HF81:—Pass., Hsch

ἐξευμενίζω.definition: propitiate, J.AJ8.13.8:—Med., ib.12.2.14, LXX4 Ma.4.11, Plu.Fab.4, Ph.2.2, al., Herm.in Phdr.p.89A.:—Pass., Ph.2.520,533, cf. Porph.Abst.2.37

ἐξευνουχίζω.definition: strengthd. for metaph., Plu.2.692c:—Pass., Ph.1.224; ib.389

ἐξευπορέω.definition: supply abundantly; abs., find a way out, ib.861b.—The form in X.An.5.6.19, is prob. f.l. for

ἐξεύρεσις.definition: searching out, search, Hdt.1.67; finding out, invention, ib.94

ἐξεύρημα.definition: thing found out, invention, Hdt.1.53,94,171, A.Th.649, Metrod.Fr.7 ; Ar.Ec.578 ; . . Eup.351.6; Metrod.Fr.6; stratagem, Phryn. Com.22

ἐξευρίσκω.definition: fut. aor. 2 Med; seek out, search after, Id.7.119,5.33

ἐξευτελίζω.definition: strengthd. for Acus.28 J; reduce one's standard of living, J.AJ18.1.3

ἐξευφραίνομαι.definition: to be delighted, Corp.Herm.1.30; show rejoicing, LXXEz.23.41

ἐξεύχομαι.definition: boast aloud, proclaim, boast; pray earnestly for, Id.Ch.215: c. acc. et inf., E.Med.930

ἐξεφίημι.definition: = Med. enjoin, command, c. inf., S.Aj.795, cf. E.IT1468

ἐξέχω.definition: stand out or project from, Ar.V.1377; abs., stand out, be prominent, Hp.VC1; Corn.ND27; convexities, opp. Pl.R.602c; in painting, Philostr.VA2.20:—Pass., projecting panels, LXX3 Ki.7.16

ἐξέψω.definition: boil thoroughly, Hdt.4.61:—Pass., to be boiled out, v.l. in Arist.Mete.384a2

ἐξηγέομαι.definition: to be leader of, c. gen. pers; c. acc. pers., lead, govern, in Th., 1.76; ib.71

ἐξήγησις.definition: statement, narrative; explanation, interpretation, Pl.Lg.631a; D.S.2.29; title of a work by Zeno Eleaticus; so in Gramm., Sch.Il.8.296

ἐξηγητεύω.definition: hold the office of PLond.2.153.14 , Sammelb.176 , PFay.85.1

ἐξηγητής.definition: one who leads on, adviser; expounder, interpreter, esp. of oracles, dreams, or omens, Hdt.1.78; at Athens, of sacred rites or customs, modes of burial, expiation, etc., spiritual director, Pl.Euthphr.4d,9a, Lg.759c, 7…

ἐξηθέω.definition: filter out, purify, in Pass., Arist.Pr.967a15, Thphr.CP6.13.1

ἑξηκοντάβιβλος.definition: consisting of sixty books, Suid. s.v

ἑξηκονταετία.definition: the age of sixty, Ph.2.276, Plu.Cic.25

ἑξηκοντάλιθος.definition: precious stone of many colours, Plin.HN37.167

ἐξήκω.definition: to have reached a certain point; of prophecies, dreams, etc., to have come to an accomplishment, turn out true, Hdt.1.120, 6.80; S.OT1182; of magical operations, succeed, PMag.Par.1.1273

ἐξηλιάζω.definition: hang in the sun, as a form of torture, LXX2 Ki.21.6,13:— Pass., to be burnt by the sun, Hsch

ἐξηλιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be sunny, light, Plu.2.929d

ἐξηλόω.definition: remove nails from, unfasten, PTeb.332.15 , cf. PFlor.69.21 :—Pass., unfastened, POxy.1272.8

ἐξημερόω.definition: tame or reclaim entirely, Hdt.1.126; free the land from wild beasts, etc., E.HF20,852; reclaim wild plants, Plu.Fab.20, cf. Thphr.HP2.2.12 , al.: metaph., soften, humanize, Plb.4.21.4; Ph.2.402; LXX4 Ma.1.29; Plu.Num.…

ἐξηπειρόω.definition: join to the mainland, of rivers which form deposits at their mouths, Str.1.3.7, 10.2.19:—Pass., Id.11.4.2

ἐξητριάζω.definition: filter: pf. Pass. Hp. ap. Gal.19.98

ἐξηττάομαι.definition: strengthd. for Plu.Alex.14; Arr.An.7.12.5; ib.4.9.1; Ph.1.179

ἐξηχέω.definition: sound forth, LXXJl.3.14, Nech. ap; utter senseless sounds, of idiots, Polem.Phgn.51

ἐξήχησις.definition: unpleasant sound, Ael.Dion.Fr.298; mode of utterance, PMag. Par.1.923

ἔξηχος.definition: rudely sounding: hence, absurd, stupid, Porph.Chr.35, EM696.39

ἐξιάομαι.definition: fut. Ion. thoroughly, Hdt.3.132,134, E.Rh.872, Ph.1.541; Pl.Lg.933c; Id.Phlb.54e; make full amends for, Id.Lg.879a; E.El.1024

ἐξιδιάζομαι.definition: Med., appropriate to oneself, Diph.42; win over, Plb.8.25.7, al

ἐξιδρόω.definition: perspire, Hp.Vict.4.89, D.S.4.78, Dsc.Eup.1.97: c. acc. cogn., Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.119

ἐξιδρύω.definition: fut. make to sit down, S.OC11:—Med., I have settled, E.Fr.884

ἐξίημι.definition: send out, let one go out; intr., of rivers, discharge themselves, Hdt.1.6 , al., Th.4.103

ἐξιθύνω.definition: make straight, Il.15.410; direct aright, A.R.1.562

ἐξικετεύω.definition: enireat successfully, persuade by entreaty, S.OT760, Parth.17.5, J.AJ3.11.3, Polyaen.6.16.5

ἐξικμάζω.definition: send forth moisture, cause to exude; intr. in Act., = Pass., Id.Mete.384b9, Pr.930b34

ἐξικμαστέος.definition: that must have moisture removed, c. acc., Philostr.Gym.52

ἐξικνέομαι.definition: poet. aor. Il.9.479, augm; come to as a suppliant, c. acc. pers., Od.13.206, 20.223, Pi.P.11.35; Ant.Lib.38.2

ἐξιλάσκομαι.definition: fut. propitiate, Orac; atone for, IG22.1365,1366:—Pass., that which is atoned for by . ., Pl.Lg.862c

ἐξίλασμα.definition: ransom, propitiatory offering, LXX1 Ki.12.3, Ps.48.8

ἐξιλεόω.definition: appease, Hld.4.15, 1.8 :—Med., Str.4.4.6 , Onos.5 tit., Hermog.Stat.3, Zen.4.93, Jul.Or.2.68b. — Cf. 3

ἐξινιάζω.definition: take out the fibres from, Peripl.M.Rubr.65:—Pass., Ath.9.406a

ἐξινόω.definition: strip of fibre and sinew, destroy, Lyc.841 ; but , = . ., Hsch.; = dub. in Com.Adesp.1004

ἐξιόω.definition: clean from rust, Arr.Epict.4.11.13; make poisonous, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.104

ἐξιπόω.definition: press or squeeze out, Hp.Art.50; dry thoroughly, Aristid.Or.36.69:—Pass., prob.l. in Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.44 B

ἐξιππάζομαι.definition: ride out or away, LXXHb.1.8, J.AJ9.3.2

ἐξίπταμαι.definition: later form of Arist.Fr.346, LXXPr.7.10, Plu.2.90c, Jul.Or.2.101a

ἐξισάζω.definition: Act. intr., to be equal, Id.17.3.1, Hermog.Stat.1, Olymp.in Mete.158.15

ἐξισασμός.definition: equalization, Simp.in Epict.p.8 D., in Cael.162.28

ἐξισόω.definition: make equal or even, bring to a level with; Pass., is levelled, equalized, i.e. resolved in harmony, S.El.1072 ; lit., levelled, J.BJ5.3.5

ἐξιστάνω.definition: later form of LXX3 Ma.1.25, Dsc.4.73:—also Act.Ap.8.9

ἐξίστημι.definition: metaph., drive one out of his senses, E.Ba.850; E.Fr.265; X.Mem.1.3.12; D.21.72; simply drive one out of his senses, confound, amaze, Hp.Coac.429; Muson.Fr.8p.35H.; diverts the attention, Arist.Rh.1408b23; excite, ib.…

ἐξιστορέω.definition: search out, inquire into, A.Th.506; roam about, X. Eph.1.12

ἐξισχύω.definition: have strength enough, be able; c. gen., fate prevailing over the children, Ael.VH6.13, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.71D

ἐξίσχω.definition: intr., stand out, project, Paus.5.12.1; prominent eyes, Hp.Prog.2, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.27; of bones, Aret.SA2.8

ἐξισωτής.definition: officer who apportioned and equalized the taxes among the payers, Lat. peraequator, Cod.Just.10.16.13Intr. , cf. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.19; Suid

ἐξίχνευσις.definition: tracking out, Gp.2.6.22; reduction of copper ore, Syn.Alch.p.66B

ἐξιχνεύω.definition: track out, E.Ba.352, 817; S.Ichn.160; Plu.Pomp.27; Polyaen.4.2.16: metaph., A.Ag.368 ; Arg.Men.Oxy.1235.49; 'feel for', try to talk Greek, Tim.Pers.161

ἐξιχνοσκοπέω.definition: seek by tracking, S.Tr.271:—so in Med., Id.Aj.997

ἐξιχωρίζω.definition: cleanse from humours, Suid. , prob. in Aët.6.50

ἐξογκέω.definition: form a prominence, Hp.Art.11; swell, Aret.CA1.7 bis

ἔξογκος.definition: prominent, Plu.Fr.inc.149, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.187 D

ἐξογκόω.definition: heap up, , Hp.Art.14: metaph., honour her by raising a tomb, E.Or.402, cf. to be swelled out, of Alcmeon with his garments stuffed with gold-dust, Hdt.6.125, cf. Arr.Tact.35.4; to be a luxurious liver, E.Supp.864: met…

ἐξόγκωμα.definition: anything raised or swollen, cairns, E.HF1332; swelling, Hp.Epid.2.2.24

ἐξόγκωσις.definition: raising, elevation, Eust. ad; swelling, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.1.6, Aret.CA1.7; corpulence, Ruf.Fr.62: metaph., Phld.Rh.1.219 S

ἐξοδεία.definition: prob. for expedition, Plb.4.54.3; procession from the shrines, OGI90.42

ἐξοδεύω.definition: march out, Plb.5.94.7, LXX1 Es.4.23; depart this life, LXXJd.5.27

ἐξοδία.definition: Ion. marching out, expedition; journey, PSI4.406.27

ἐξοδιάζω.definition: scatter, Nic.Dam.118; pay in full, defray, discharge, IG5.1167 ; ib.1390.52 ; Test.Epict.7.8, cf. IG12.168.7 :—Pass., LXX4 Ki.12.12: metaph. in Act., Gal.Anim.Pass.1.2

ἐξοδιάριος.definition: at Rome, actor in the Atellana , Lyd.Mag.1.40

ἐξόδιος.definition: of or belonging to an exit; as Subst., , finale of a tragedy, Philist.42, Plu.Alex.75: metaph., catastrophe, tragical conclusion, Id.Crass.33; also Jul.Or.1.26b

ἐξόζω.definition: intr., smell, smell; c. gen., smell of a thing, Thphr.Od.20

ἐξοιδέω.definition: swell or be swollen up, . . E.Cyc.227; Luc.DMort.14.5, cf. Aristid.Or.24.44: metaph., swell beyond its proper size, of a body in the state, Plb.6.18.7

ἐξοικειόω.definition: appropriate, assimilate; Pass., adapt oneself to one, Plu.2.649e

ἐξοικέω.definition: emigrate, remove, Lys.31.9; Pass., to be completely inhabited, Th.2.17

ἐξοικίζω.definition: remove one from his home, eject, banish; dispeople, empty, E.Hec.887; lay waste, D.H.5.77:— Med., Plu.Comp.Ages.Pomp.3

ἐξοικισμός.definition: expulsion of inhabitants, Sm.Ez.3.11, dub. l. in Ph.2.526

ἐξοικιστής.definition: one who expels, Charond. ap. Stob.4.2.24

ἐξοικοδομέω.definition: build, Hdt.2.176, 5.62; make a building; build up a road along it, Plb.3.55.6

ἐξοικονομέω.definition: eliminate, Sor.1.107, Philum. ap; alienate, dispose of, BGU184.21 , PFay.31.14

ἐξοινέω.definition: to be tipsy, Hegesand.21, Poll.6.21; get sober, Paul.Aeg.1.33

ἐξοινόομαι.definition: Pass., to be drunk, drunken, E.Ba.814, Ath.2.38e

ἔξοινος.definition: drunken, Alex.63, Plb.Fr.40, Macho ap.Ath.8.349a, Alciphr.1.39; Ph.1.382. Adv. censured by Poll.6.21

ἐξοιστέος.definition: one must bring out, E.Ph.712, Pl.Prm.128e, Aen.Tact.2.7

ἐξοιστράω.definition: or make wild, madden; intr., rave, Ph.1.380; go mad, Sch.Od.22.299: aor. v.l. in Palaeph.42.1

ἐξοιστρηλατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be driven to madness, Ps.-Plu.Fluv.18.1

ἐξοίχομαι.definition: to have gone out, to be quite gone, Il.6.379,384, S.OC867; Pl.Com.69.11: metaph., Antipho Soph.49; Pl.R.503c

ἐξοκέλλω.definition: intr., of a ship, run aground; metaph., drift into, Isoc.7.18; Id.Ep.2.13; Plb.18.55.7; Ph.1.686; Paus.8.24.9; Plu.2.5b; Phylarch.45 J.; ibid., Plb.7.1.1, Ath.12.523c ; Phld.Ir.p.35 W.: abs., to be ruined, Plb.4.48.11

ἐξολέθρευσις.definition: destruction, ib.Jd.1.17, al., interpol. in J.AJ11.6.6

ἐξολεθρεύω.definition: destroy utterly, LXXGe.17.14, al., Act.Ap.3.23, v.l. in J.AJ8.11.1. .)

ἐξολισθάνω.definition: later Epicur.Ep.2p.45U., Sm.Ps.35.3: aor. 2 off, slip away, Il.20.470; glance off, as a spear-point from a hard substance, E.Ph.1383; away from them, Arist.HA590b17; of leaves, drop off, Ael.NA12.18; slip out, escape,…

ἐξόλλυμι.definition: and fut. aor. 1 pf; Med., with pf. 2 perish utterly, Emp.11.3, S.Tr.84, Ar.Pax366, Pl.l.c., etc.; . . Ar.Pax483: opt. in imprecations, Id.Fr.105; Alex.120

ἐξομαλίζω.definition: make quite smooth; render homogeneous, Hp.Medic.10

ἐξομηρεύω.definition: bind by taking hostages, bind slaves to one's service by the pledges of wives and children, Arist.Oec.1344b17, cf. Phld.Oec.p.33J.:—Med., Onos.1.12; also, produce by hostages, Str.6.4.2; bind to oneself, D.S.27.7; win…

ἐξομιλέω.definition: have intercourse, live with; c. acc., win over, conciliate, Plb.7.4.6, Plu.2.824d, etc

ἐξόμιλος.definition: out of one's society, alien, S.Tr.964

ἐξομματόω.definition: open the eyes of; metaph., make clear or plain, A.Pr.499

ἐξομμάτωσις.definition: clearing or cleansing of the eyes, interpol. in Poll.2.48

ἐξόμνυμι.definition: mostly, swear in the negative, S.Ant.535; D.29.20:— mostly in Med., aor. deny or disown upon oath, swear formally that one does not know a thing, abjure, Id.57.36; Is.9.19: abs., ib.18, Pl.Lg.949a, etc.; D.57.59, cf. …

ἐξομοιόω.definition: make quite like, assimilate, Hdt.3.24; Pl.Grg.512e; produce fruit exactly like, Thphr.HP2.2.4; adapt, Anon.Oxy.1012i 28; compare, liken, Str.2.5.22, Ph.2.11, al.:—Pass., become or be like, E.Andr.354, cf. S.Aj.549, X.…

ἐξομοίωσις.definition: assimilation, Thphr.CP4.3.1; becoming like, Ph.1.35, Plu.Per.2, Dam.Pr.341, Procl.in Ti.3.200D

ἐξομολογέομαι.definition: confess, LXXDa.9.20; make grateful acknowledgements, give thanks, sing praises, LXX2 Ki.22.50, al., Ph.1.59, al., Ev.Matt.11.25: c. acc., LXXGe.29.35

ἐξομολόγησις.definition: admission, confession, Plu.2.987d; i.e. of the possession of a loaf, J.BJ5.10.3; confession of gratitude, Ph.1.60, al

ἐξομόργνυμι.definition: fut. wipe off from; metaph., wipe off one's folly on another, i.e. give him part of it, Id.Ba.344, parodied by Ar.Ach.843

ἐξονειδίζω.definition: c. acc. rei, cast in one's teeth, S.El.288, E.IA305; J.AJ5.1.18; having foul reproaches cast upon one, S.Ph.382

ἐξονομάζω.definition: utter aloud, announce, h.Merc.59; call by name, Plu.Cic.40:—Pass., to be referred to by name, PTeb.28.17 , etc

ἐξονομαίνω.definition: name, speak of by name, Il.3.166; . . name, tell it, Od.6.66, cf. h.Ven.252; SIG527.122

ἐξονυχίζω.definition: try a thing's smoothness by drawing the; deprive of the base of the petal, Orib.5.33.1; of lilies, in Pass., Aët.1.115

ἐξοπίσω.definition: of Place , backwards, back again, Il.11.461, 13.436; Hes.Op.88

ἐξοπλίζω.definition: arm completely, Hdt.7.100, X.Cyr.4.5.22; generally, fully prepared, ready, Ar.Pax566; . . Antiph.226.2, cf. 217.19

ἐξοπλισία.definition: muster of troops under arms, review; field-day, manoeuvres, Ael.Tact.24.1 ; Man.Hist.42

ἐξόπλισις.definition: getting under arms, X.Cyr.8.5.9, cf. Arist.Pr.922b14

ἐξοπτάω.definition: bake thoroughly; metaph., of love, S.Fr.474.3

ἐξοράω.definition: see from afar:—Pass; have the appearance, Hp.Morb.2.68

ἐξοργιάζω.definition: excite to mystic frenzy; intr., become frenzied, ib.p.26 K

ἐξοργίζω.definition: enrage, X.Eq.9.2; Aeschin.1.192; X.Mem.3.3.7:—Pass., to be enraged, furious, Batr.[184a], Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39x33 , Plb.6.57.8, al., Phld. Mus.p.78 K., Aristaenet.2.20

ἐξορθιάζω.definition: lift up the voice, cry aloud, A.Ch.271; intr., stand erect, Plu.2.371f

ἐξορθόω.definition: set upright, Pl.Lg.862c; metaph., set right, correct, S.Ant.83; Pl.Ti.90d; E.Supp.1083, cf. 1086

ἐξορθρίζω.definition: in pf. part. Pass., womb of the morning, Aq.Ps.109.3

ἐξορίζω.definition: expose a child, E.Ion504; banish, get rid of, Pl.Smp.197d; Arist.Pol.1336b5; Id.EN1180a10: c. gen., Jul.Or.6.186b

ἐξόριος.definition: out of the bounds of one's; Subst., , exile, Marcellin.Vit. Thuc.47, Eust.1161.35

ἐξορισμός.definition: sending beyond the frontier, D.H.5.12; Plu.2.549a; prob. cj. in Porph.Abst.1.10

ἐξόριστος.definition: expelled, banished; put beyond the borders, of the dead body of a criminal, . . Din.1.77

ἐξορκίζω.definition: conjure, LXXGe.24.3, cf. PMag.Lond.121.269; ib.892; Ev.Matt.26.63; also PMag.Par.1.356

ἐξορκόω.definition: earlier form of administer an oath to one, c. acc. pers., or abs., Foed. ap. Th.5.47, cf. D.21.65, IG22.1174.15: c. fut. inf., ib.2.841b35: folld. by Hdt.3.133,4.154: later, c. pres. inf., J.AJ9.7.4: c. acc. pers. et …

ἐξόρκωσις.definition: binding by oath, Id.4.154; exorcism, J.AJ8.2.5

ἐξορμάω.definition: send forth, send to war, A.Pers.46, E.IT1437; intr., like Pass., set out, start, esp. in haste, Od.12.221; X.An.5.7.17: c. gen., set out from, E.Tr.1131, etc.: metaph., break out, S.Tr.1089

ἐξορμενίζω.definition: shoot forth, sprout, S.Ichn.275; run to seed, Poll.6.54

ἐξορμέω.definition: to be out of harbour, run to sea, Lycurg.17, And.1.11, Is.6.27: metaph., Aeschin.3.209; to be out of one's senses, Paus.3.4.1

ἐξόρμησις.definition: urging on, Arr.An.3.9.7; rushing forth, Sch.Th.3.89; vehement attack, D.C.75.6; setting out, start, Arr.An.1.11.5

ἐξορμίζω.definition: bring out of harbour; let down, E.Hel.1247: pf. Pass. in med. sense, thou hast come forth, Id.Ph.846

ἐξορμιστόν.definition: a fish similar to the Cassiod.Var.12.4,14

ἔξορμος.definition: sailing from a harbour, c. gen; issuing forth, dub. l. in Arist.PA694a23

ἐξόρνυμι.definition: in Med., rush out, aor. , A.R.1.306

ἐξορύσσω.definition: Att. dig out the earth from a; dig out of the ground, dig up, Hdt.1.64, cf. BGU1024iv4 ; Ar.Ach.763; Lys.7.26:—Pass., PHal.1.109 ; X.Oec.19.4

ἐξορχέομαι.definition: dance away, hop off, D.22.68; c. acc. cogn., dance out a figure, go through it, Philostr.Im.2.12; Suid. s.v

ἐξοσιόω.definition: dedicate, devote, Plu.Cam.20, prob. in; Med., avert by expiation, D.S.15.9 , Plu.2.586f

ἐξοστεΐζω.definition: take out the bones, prob. l. in Horap.2.38, cf. Suid. s.v. take out of the bone, Dsc.2.77: metaph., of fruits, remove the seeds or kernels, . . Id.5.75; Ruf. ap. Orib.8.47.7

ἐξοστρακίζω.definition: banish by ostracism, Hdt.8.79, And.4.32, Lys.14.39, Pl.Grg.516d; Luc.Sacr.4:—Pass., Themist.Ep.2; also Ar.Fr.593; Demad.53; Anon.Alch. in Gött.Nachr.1919.14

ἐξοστρακισμός.definition: banishment by ostracism; formation of any external shell, interpol. in Corn.ND17

ἐξοτρύνω.definition: stir up, urge on, excite, A.Th.692 , cf. E.Supp.24; Th.1.84, etc.:—Pass., Ph.2.564

ἐξουδενωτής.definition: one who sets at naught, Phld.Vit.p.42J

ἐξουρέω.definition: pass with the urine, Arist.HA577a22; abs., make water, Ael.NA11.18; finish making water, Hierocl.Facet.118

ἐξούρησις.definition: passing with the urine, Aët. ap. Phot.p.179B

ἐξουσία.definition: power, authority to do a thing; abuse of authority, licence, arrogance, Th.1.38, cf. 3.45, D.19.200; ib.272; OGI669.51

ἐξουσιάζω.definition: fut. Phld. :—exercise; exercise authority over, CIG4584 ; Ev.Luc.22.25, cf. 1 Ep.Cor.7.4; PMasp.15.170 :—Med., LXXNe.5.15; ib.Ec.8.9:— Pass., to be held under authority, 1 Ep.Cor.6.12

ἐξουσιαστής.definition: mighty one, person in authority, LXXIs.9.6, Cat.Cod.Astr.5.86, PGen.53.2

ἐξοφέλλω.definition: increase exceedingly, offered higher and higher dowry, Od.15.18

ἐξοφθαλμιάζω.definition: have no eye for, disregard, PGoodsp.Cair.15.22

ἐξόφθαλμος.definition: with prominent eyes, opp; manifest, Plb.1.10.3. Adv. Diog.Oen.36

ἐξοφρυόω.definition: in pf. part. Pass. supercilious, Hsch., EM350.22

ἐξοχετεία.definition: drawing into channels or sluices, Str.4.6.7

ἐξοχετεύω.definition: draw off, Hp.Aër.18; Gal.UP10.11: metaph., Emp.35.2; Procl.H.1.4

ἐξοχή.definition: prominence, elevated; metaph., pre-eminence, in nullo est, Cic.Att.4.15.7; Longin.10.3; Hierocl.p.55 A.; par excellence, Str.1.2.10, Ph.1.65, A.D.Synt.26.15, OGI764.52 , etc.; leading men, Act.Ap.25.23

ἔξοχος.definition: standing out, jutting, Pi.N.4.52; more freq. metaph., eminent, excellent, Il.2.188; Pi.N.6.47: Comp. ib.3.71: Sup. ib.2.18, A.Ag.1622, E.Supp.889; Phld.Lib.p.20O.; = Lat. eminentissimus, OGI640.16 , POxy.1469.1 , cf. …

ἐξυβρίζω.definition: break out into insolence, wax wanton; c. acc. pers., treat with insolence or violence, Id.12.2; also Conon24.2:—Pass., Hyp.Phil.9; despised things, Longin.43.5

ἐξυγραίνω.definition: saturate, Arist.Pr.877a33, al.:—Pass., to; make watery, of the blood, Id.HA521a12 , cf. Plu.2.97b : metaph., ib.136b:—Pass., to be so, of plants, Thphr.CP6.6.4

ἐξυδαρόω.definition: make watery, Aët.4.10 : metaph., Simp.in Epict.p.94 D.:—Pass., become water, Arist. ap. Ath.10.434f, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.81

ἐξυδατόω.definition: make into water or make watery, Hp.Fist.7; Thphr.Od.66; Sor.1.93:—Pass., Corn.ND17, Archig. ap. Orib.44.26.6, etc.; become dropsical, Hp.Epid.4.49

ἐξυδάτωσις.definition: changing into water, Herod.Med.in Rh.Mus.49.556 , Zos.Alch.p.202B

ἐξυθλέω.definition: in Pass., to be foolishly spoken, Phld.Rh.1.249 S

ἐξυλακτέω.definition: bark out: burst out in rage, Plu.Arat.50; Aeschin.Socr.38: c. acc. cogn., yell it out, Lyc.764

ἐξυμενίζω.definition: strip off the skin or membrane, Dsc.2.76.1; Archig. ap. Aët.16.48

ἐξυμνέω.definition: strengthd. for Plb.6.47.7, Phld.Rh.1.219, 2.148 S., D.S.9 Fr. 26, Procl.in Alc.p.84 C.:—Pass., Lyc.1195

ἐξυπανίστημι.definition: only in intr. aor. 2, a weal started up from under the skin of the back, Il.2.267, cf. Pythag. ap. Porph.VP40

ἐξυπηρετέω.definition: assist to the utmost, S.Tr.1156; Lys.12.23, cf. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.123; J.AJ13.3.1: abs., Phld.Sto.339.9:—later in Med., IG12.406 :—Pass., every emergency will be provided for, Ael.Tact.35.1

ἐξυπνίζω.definition: awaken from sleep, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.334, cf. Ev.Jo.11.11:—Pass., wake up, LXXJd.16.14, Plu.Ant.30, M.Ant.6.31

ἔξυπνος.definition: awakened out of sleep, LXX1 Es.3.3, Act.Ap.16.27, J.AJ11.3.2, Zos.Alch.p.118 B. Adv. PGiss.1.19.4

ἐξυπνόω.definition: wake out of sleep, Sm., Al.Ps.138.18: also intr. metaph., LXX4 Ma.5.10

ἐξυπτιάζω.definition: turn a person quite on the back; intr., lie back, of the horns of wild cattle, Id.HA499a7

ἐξυφαίνω.definition: weave, Hdt.2.122,9.109, cf; finish weaving, Artem.4.40; Gp.15.5.2

ἔξω.definition: with Verbs of motion, out or out of, Od.14.526; Hdt.1.10; Pl.Phdr.247b; D.18.323; Luc.Alex.38, etc

ἐξωθέω.definition: aor. 1 , thrust out, force; put forth painful words, break forth into cruel words, S.Ph.1142

ἐξώθησις.definition: expulsion, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.90; Gramm., expulsion of a letter, Eust.378.3, 1542.32

ἐξωκεανίζω.definition: Geog., represent as placed out in the ocean, Str.1.2.17, 7.3.6:—Pass., Eust.1050.64

ἐξωκεανισμός.definition: a placing out in the ocean, Str.1.2.10

ἐξώλεια.definition: utter destruction, IG12.10.15, cf. Antipho5.11, Lys.12.10, Jusj. ap. D.24.151; D.21.119, 57.22; ib.53

ἐξωμίας.definition: one with arms bare to the shoulder, Luc.Vit.Auct.7

ἐξωμίς.definition: = tunic with one sleeve, leaving one shoulder bare, worn by slaves and the poor, Id.V.444 , Lys.662, X.Mem.2.7.5, etc.; by Laconizers, Ael.VH9.34; by Cynics, S.E.P.1.153; by the rich when not on ceremony, Suid. s.v.; …

ἐξωνέομαι.definition: buy off, redeem, c. gen. vel dat. pretii; generally, buy , the purchaser, Aeschin.3.66; bribe, Paus.4.17.3

ἐξωριάζω.definition: leave out of thought, neglect, f.l. for A.Pr.17

ἔξωσις.definition: putting out, displacement, Hp.Art.46; thrust, Marcellin.Puls.99

ἐξώστης.definition: one who drives out, E.Rh.322; violent winds which drive ships ashore , Hdt.2.113, Hp.VM9, Aeschin.Ep.1.3

ἐξώστρα.definition: stage-machine identified with the; bridge thrust out from the besiegers' tower against the walls of the besieged place, Lat. exostra, Veget.de Re Milit.4.21

ἐξωτάτω.definition: Adv., Sup. of outermost, Pl.Phd.112e, Arist.Cael.279a20, Ph.2.331, etc.:—later, Adj. LXX3 Ki.6.30; Ph.1.95

ἐξωτέρω.definition: Adv., Comp. of more outside, A.Ch.1023, cf. Arist.Metaph.1055a25, LXXJb.18.17, etc.:—hence later, Adj. outer, LXXEx.26.4, etc., Ev.Matt.8.12; POxy.896.14

ἐξώφορος.definition: brought out, published; tending outwards, Marcellin.Puls.65

ἑορτάζω.definition: in Ion.Prose impf. (with; celebrate as a festival, celebrate it by a festival, Plu.2.349f, cf. Ant.56; at Rome, celebrate by a triumph, D.C.51.21

ἑορτάσιμος.definition: of a festival, J.AJ11.6.13, cf. Plu.2.270a, OGI524.8 ; though I was in no holiday mood, Luc.Sat.11

ἐπαβελτερόω.definition: make a yet greater ass of, Men.Per.Fr.1

ἐπαγαίομαι.definition: Pass., exult in, A.R.3.1262; feel a malignant joy in, ib.470: Ep. aor. Epic. ap. Parth.21; Hsch

ἐπαγάλλομαι.definition: Pass., glory in, exult in, c. dat., Il.16.91, cf. Q.S.7.327, Tryph.671; Crates Theb.4; Them.Or.11.151c; Artem.3.31; X.Oec.4.17

ἐπαγανακτέω.definition: to be indignant, abs., J.BJ2.13.3, Plu.Alc.14, Ages.19

ἐπαγγελία.definition: command, summons, Plb.9.38.2; announcement, notice, IG22.1235.7 ; SIG561.9 , prob. in LXX1 Ma.10.15; v.l. in 1 Ep.Jo.1.5

ἐπαγγέλλω.definition: aor. Pass. IG12.188.25; give orders, command, abs., Id.1.70: c.acc. et inf., give orders that . ., ib.77, cf. Th.6.56: c. dat. et inf., order one to do, D.42.7, etc.: c. acc. rei, send them orders to furnish their con…

ἐπάγγελμα.definition: promise, profession, D.19.178; subject of a treatise, that which it purports to contain, D.H.Dem.33; Ael.Tact.Praef.7

ἐπαγγελτήρ.definition: envoy who announces a festival, etc., SIG558.5

ἐπαγείρω.definition: gather together, collect, of things, Il.1.126:—Pass., of men, assemble, Od.11.632, cf. Pi.P.9.54

ἐπάγερσις.definition: mustering of forces against an enemy, Hdt.7.19

ἐπαγινέω.definition: Ion. for bring to, Hdt.2.2, Q.S.6.235

ἐπαγκυλίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be fitted with an Sch.E.Or.1476

ἐπαγλαΐζω.definition: Med., pride oneself on a thing, glory or exult in it, Il.18.133

ἐπαγοράζω.definition: purchase a title to the next vacancy of a priesthood, SIG1014.17

ἔπαγρος.definition: in quest of prey, Arist.HA616b34; Call.Hec.1.4.10

ἐπαγροσύνη.definition: good luck in hunting, fishing, etc., Theoc.Beren.1

ἐπαγρυπνέω.definition: keep awake and think over, keep a watchful; watch for, D.S.14.68: abs., Aristaenet.1.27

ἐπαγρύπνησις.definition: watching for, ibid.; Aristeas167; watchfulness, Phld.Lib.p.7 O

ἐπάγρυπνος.definition: wakeful, sleepless, Mitteis Chr.77.11 , cf. Vett. Val.11.16, Aristaenet.1.27

ἐπάγω.definition: set on, urge on, as hunters do dogs, Od.19.445, cf. X.Cyn.10.19:— in Med., ib.6.25

ἐπαγωγεύς.definition: coat of clay on a wall, IG22.1672.61

ἐπαγωγή.definition: bringing on or to; bringing in to one's aid, introduction, Id.3.100, cf. 82 ; introduction of food through the gullet, Arist.Spir.483a9

ἐπαγωνίζομαι.definition: contend with, Plu.Fab.23; continue; c. dat. rei, contend in, IG12.860.19 ; contend for, Ep.Jud.3: lay stress on, Gal.14.246; Plu.Num.8; Aristid.Rh.1p.500S.: abs., S.E.M.3.93; exert oneself, IG22.1343.16

ἐπαείδω.definition: contr. Att. fut. Ar.Ec.1153; sing as an incantation, X.Mem.2.6.11; Pl.Phd.114d, cf. 77e; Id.R.608a; sing to one so as to charm or soothe him, Id.Phdr.267d, Lg.812c, al.:—Pass., Porph.Chr.35: abs., use charms or incant…

ἐπαέξω.definition: make to grow, prosper, Od.14.65:— Pass., increase, grow, Semon.7.85 , Nic.Th.449

ἐπαθρέω.definition: = look with favour on, B.12.227, prob. l. in Id.5.8; simply, behold, v.l. in Q.S.1.111

ἐπαιάζω.definition: cry over, mourn over; join in the wail, Bion1.2, etc.; Luc.Luct.20

ἐπαιγίζω.definition: rush upon, twice in Hom. of a stormy wind, . . Il.2.148; . . Od.15.293; Alciphr.3.42: metaph., AP5.285 : c. dat., rush over, of a stream that has burst its banks, Opp.C.2.125: c. acc., of the dolphin, Id.H.2.583

ἐπαιδέομαι.definition: fut. E.IA900 : aor; c. acc., reverence, A.Fr.135, Antipho Soph.Oxy.1364.270, Pl. l.c., Herod.2.39

ἐπαιθύσσω.definition: flash at, Nonn.D.2.322; intr., rush violently on, Opp.C.4.176

ἐπαινέτης.definition: praiser, commender, Hp.Acut.6; rhapsodist, Pl.Ion536d; cf. IV

ἐπαινέω.definition: Aeol. Simon.5.19; Lacon; praise, commend in any way , or Alc.37A, Hdt.3.34,6.130; E.Hipp.264; commend one for a thing, but in this case the thing is always a neut. Pron. or Adj., A.Pr.342 ; S.Aj.1381, cf. Pl.Smp.222a;…

ἔπαινος.definition: approval, praise, commendation, Simon.4.3; complimentary address, panegyric ; Pl.Phdr.260c; Id.Smp.177d; Id.Phdr.260b; Aeschin.3.50; Pl.Lg.947c; Plb.1.1.1, D.S.13.22, D.H.10.57

ἐπαιονάω.definition: bathe, foment , Ath.2.41c:—Med., bathe , Nic.Al.463:—also Philostr.Gym.42

ἐπαίρω.definition: Ion. and poet. Hdt.1.204 and always in; lift, raise, 10.80; S.Ph.889; Id.OT1276 codd.; E.Tr.99 ; Ar.V.996; Amphis l.c.; SIG1109.24; IG3.1132; D.18.291; opp. Plu.Luc.3:—Med., didst lift and put me to thy breast, A.R.3.…

ἐπαισθάνομαι.definition: have a perception or feeling of, c. gen; abs., become sensible, recover one's senses, Hp.Morb.3.8

ἐπαίσθησις.definition: perception, Epicur.Ep.1p.13U., cf. Phld.Mus.p.42K., al., Sor.2.19; Epicur.Nat.125 G., Porph.Abst.1.57, 3.15

ἐπαΐσσω.definition: Ep. aor. Od.10.322, Iterat; c. dat. pers., rush upon her, Od.10.295: in Il. only c. dat. instrum., 5.584, 10.369, etc.; so . . Od.14.281

ἐπαισχύνομαι.definition: fut. to be ashamed at or; late in Act., make ugly, mar, Nonn.D.20.61, 42.421

ἐπαιτέω.definition: beg as a mendicant, Id.OC1364, cf. E.Rh.715: abs., Vett.Val.68.30, Luc.Asin.35

ἐπαίτης.definition: beggar, Telesp.14 H., Nech. ap. Vett.Val.290.2, Ath.5.192f, D.C.66.8 codd

ἐπαιτητάριον.definition: little beggar, name of an amulet, PMag.Par.1.2378

ἐπαιτιάομαι.definition: fut. Ion. bring a charge against, accuse, etc.; Hp.Aër.22; accuse one of a thing, Th.6.28, D.21.114; for your mishaps, A.Pr.974; also I accuse her of this burial, that she planned it, S.Ant.490: c. inf., Id.OT645; . .…

ἐπαΐω.definition: contr. E.HF773 : aor. 1; perceive, feel, Pi.Fr.75.15 ; Hdt.3.29; Ael.NA1.5; Hierocl.in CA24p.472M.: c. part., Ar.V.516; Hp.Prorrh.2.16; A.R.1.1023, 2.195: abs., when he perceived it, Hdt.9.93

ἐπαιωρέω.definition: keep hovering over another; Pass., hover over or on the surface, float upon, Dsc.5.92, cf. 75; buoyed up by . ., Luc.Alex.16; hang over it, conduct it remissly, Plu.Pel.29; in Hp.Art.75, of one who throws his whole we…

ἐπακανθίζω.definition: in pres. part., pointed, Thphr.HP3.10.1,al.; thorny, set with thorns, ib.4.8.8, 6.4.1, al

ἐπακμάζω.definition: to be in one's prime, Ph.1.33; also of; of persons, flourish in succession to, D.H.Pomp.4; ib.1; also of animals and crops, Ph.1.28, 2.424

ἐπακολουθέω.definition: follow close upon, follow after, pursue; attend to, follow mentally, understand, Pl.Phd.107b; Id.Lg.861c; Id.Sph.243a; Id.Lg.963a, etc

ἐπακολούθησις.definition: cognizance, concurrence; consequence, consequentially, opp. Stoic.2.333, Stoic. ap.Plu.2.1015c, M.Ant.6.44, S.E.M.1.194; result, Gal.19.382

ἐπακόλουθος.definition: following, Aristid.Rh.2p.522S.: Comp., PMag.Par.1.1536. Adv. agreeably to, Antip. ap.Stob.4.22.103, cf. PMasp.97 ii 68

ἐπακονάω.definition: whet, in Pass., IG7.3073.104,119; whet against, Lib.Decl.40.35

ἐπακοντίζω.definition: dart a thing at a person, Socr.Ep.30.13 codd

ἐπακούω.definition: fut. ib.Ge.30.33, later Psalm.Solom.18.3:-hear, c. acc. rei, of the Sun, Il.3.277, cf. Od.11.109; prov., as thou speakest, so wilt thou be answered, Il.20.250; Hes.Op.448; Ar.Eq.1080: c. acc. rei et gen. pers., Od.19.…

ἐπακριβής.definition: accurate: neut. as Adv., Aps.Rh.p.316 H

ἐπακρίζω.definition: reach the top of a thing, he reached the farthest point in deeds of blood, of Orestes, A.Ch.932

ἐπάκριος.definition: on the heights, epith. of Zeus; a district in Attica, Str.9.1.20

ἐπακροάομαι.definition: = abs., Pl.Com.16, Nic.Dam.Vit.Caes.29: c. gen. pers., Act.Ap.16.25, Luc.Icar.1: c. gen. rei, Hld.2.17: c. acc. rei, Men.Epit.Oxy.1236v16; Ant.Lib.11.6 hearkening, obedience, LXX1 Ki.15.22

ἐπακτήρ.definition: Ep. word, = hunter, huntsman, Od.19.435; Il.17.135; later, fisherman, A.R.1.625

ἐπαλαλάζω.definition: raise the war-cry, A.Th.497,951 , D.S.19.30; X.Cyr.7.1.26; Jul.Or.1.36b

ἐπαλάομαι.definition: wander about or over, Od.4.81; ib.83: subj. aor. 15.401

ἐπαλαστέω.definition: to be full of wrath at a thing, Od.1.252, cf. A.R.3.369,557

ἐπαλγής.definition: painful, Aristeas167, Str.11.13.2, Philum. ap.Aët.5.127, Aët.15.13, Opp.H.4.508: Comp., LXX4 Ma.14.10, Onos.42.19, Aret.SD2.3. Adv. Poll.3.99

ἐπαλγύνω.definition: give pain, Nic.Al.335; afflict, Q.S.4.416:—Med., feel pain at, Tz.H.4.398

ἐπάλειμμα.definition: unguent, Dsc.1.43.4, cf. Inscr.Prien.112.90, al. , Michel544.20

ἐπαλείφω.definition: metaph., from anointing athletes, prepare for contest, stir up, irritate, Plb.2.51.2; set them upon him, D.L.2.38; Ph.1.680; so perh. in physical sense, irritate, Hp.Mul.1.99, Epid.5.20

ἐπάλειψις.definition: painting over of colours; smearing over, anointing, EM69.41

ἐπαλέξω.definition: Ep. Verb, defend, succour, Il.8.365; ward off, keep off, Il.20.315

ἐπαληθεύω.definition: prove true, substantiate, verify; prove one's right to, Ph.2.6, 263

ἐπαλθέω.definition: heal, cure, fut. Nic.Al.395: aor. ib.614:—Med., aor. Id.Th.654

ἐπαλινδέομαι.definition: Pass., lit., roll on: hence had been effaced, A.R.4.1463:—also Nic.Th.266

ἐπαλλαγή.definition: premium on exchange of currency, PCair.Zen.22.2

ἐπάλλαξις.definition: interweaving or dovetailing; overlapping of species, Id.GA732b15; confusion of different things, Str.12.8.2

ἐπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. change over: once in Hom; intr., alternate, interlocking teeth, Arist.PA661b18; of leaves, dub. in Thphr.HP4.6.10

ἐπαλληλία.definition: sequence, unbroken series, Eust.11.32 , cf. EM576.2; taking one drug after another, 'mixing medicines', Gal.19.679

ἐπάλληλος.definition: also D.C.74.10,al.:—one close; Gramm., succession, sequence of two nominatives, A.D.Synt.179.13,al

ἔπαλξις.definition: means of defence: mostly in; in sg., mostly, line of battlements, parapet, Il.12.381,al. ; the defenders of the wall, Th.2.13, cf. 7.28, Ar.Ach.72: pl., of individual crenellations, Th.3.21

ἐπαλφιτόω.definition: add meal to wine, prob. in Ath.10.432b

ἐπαμαξεύω.definition: = traverse with cars, . . marked with the tracks of wheels, S.Ant.251

ἐπαμάομαι.definition: scrape together for oneself, heaped him up a bed , Od.5.482; Thgn.428, cf. Thphr.HP4.13.5, AP7.446 ; having heaped up a grave or barrow, Hdt.8.24; so Polyaen.2.1.23; Plu.2.982b; Porph.Abst.4.9:—later in Act., D.L.6.79…

ἐπαμβατήρ.definition: poet. for one who mounts upon, assailant: metaph., of leprous eruptions, A.Ch.280

ἐπαμείβω.definition: exchange, barter, Il.6.230; Orph.A.422:—Med., come one after another, come in turn to, Il.6.339; Archil.9.9

ἐπαμπέχω.definition: and , put on over, overwrap, E.Tr.1148; enwrap, Ph.2.379; Plu.Oth.5:—Med., Ph.1.358, al., D.Chr.6.26; Plu.2.1102d:— Pass., Id.Sert.10

ἐπαμύντωρ.definition: helper, defender, Od.16.263; as fem., Orph.L.587

ἐπαμύνω.definition: come to aid, succour, Il.6.361; ward off, v.l. for in AP5.6

ἐπαμφιέννυμι.definition: cloak or veil, prob.l. in Men.404.5; in later form Aristid.Or.30.18:—Pass., [S.]Fr.1127.2

ἐπαμφοτερίζω.definition: to be double: hence, play a double game; of statements or arguments, to be ambiguous, susceptible of two interpretations, Isoc.12.240, cf. Pl.R.479b; . . Luc.DDeor.16.1

ἐπαμφοτερισμός.definition: inclination both ways, wavering; uncertainly of parentage, Ph.2.202

ἐπαναβαίνω.definition: poet. Opp.H.3.638:—get up on; of animals, cover, Id.HA540a22, Clearch.36

ἐπαναβάλλω.definition: throw on or over:—Med; lift up, Ath.12.529a

ἐπανάβασις.definition: search for higher principles; rise, diastole of the pulse, Gal.7.430

ἐπαναβιβάζω.definition: causal of make to mount upon, Th.3.23, cf. D.C.50.23

ἐπαναβιβασμός.definition: in pl., ascending steps in argument, Herm.in Phdr.p.64A

ἐπαναβλαστάνω.definition: grow upon, Choerob. in An.Ox.2.198.30, Sch.Dsc.p.362 Matth

ἐπαναγιγνώσκω.definition: read over, read out, f.l. in Lys.10.18, cf. Plb.31.13.10; PPetr.2p.3 ; of a teacher, S.E.M.10.19, Porph.Chr.58:—Pass., D.7.19

ἐπαναγκάζω.definition: compel by force, constrain, c. acc. et inf., A.Pr.671, Ar.Av.1083, PHib.1.34.3 , etc.:—Pass., Ar.Pl.525, etc.: freq. with inf. omitted, Hdt.8.130, cf. Ar.Pl.533, Th.5.31

ἐπαναγορεύω.definition: proclaim publicly:—impers. in Pass., proclamation is made, Ar.Av.1071

ἐπανάγω.definition: bring up: hence; stir up, excite, Hdt.7.160

ἐπαναγωγή.definition: sailing against, naval attack, Th.7.34; leading up, exalting, Pl.R.532c

ἐπαναδίδωμι.definition: intr., increase more and more, Hp.Epid.1.25

ἐπαναδιπλόω.definition: repeat yet again, Arist.Pr.910b25, Gal.15.879:—Pass., to be repeated, Arist.APr.49a11, Metaph.1003b28

ἐπαναδίπλωσις.definition: doubling, folding, of the; repetition, Arist.APr.49a26

ἐπαναζώννυμαι.definition: Med., gird on one's clothes, Ph.2.479

ἐπαναθέω.definition: run up against, Onos.18: abs., Id.6.1

ἐπαναίρεσις.definition: slaughter, destruction, Plb.2.37.8: pl., Nech. in Cat.Cod.Astr.7.140

ἐπαναιρέω.definition: make away with, destroy, D.S.19.51; remove; kill after or together with, App.BC4.15, al.; ib.4.26

ἐπαναίρω.definition: lift up, raise high, X.Cyn.6.23:—Med., raise the spear one against the other, S.OC424; but raised his staff against him, Th.8.84, cf. Hsch. s.v. rise up, Ar.Eq.784

ἐπανακαινίζω.definition: renew, revive, LXXJb.10.17, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.4 M.:—also Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.49.549

ἐπανακαλέω.definition: invoke besides, A.Ag.145; recall, Aret.SD2.13 :—Med., Arr.An.4.27.1, cf. Dam.Pr.245, Procl.in Alc.p.182 C.:—Pass., Hierocl.in CA7p.429M

ἐπανακάμπτω.definition: intr., come back again, Arist.Pr.916a32: abs., bend back, of ducts or veins, Id.HA510a21,514a11; return, Aq., Sm., Thd.Is.35.10

ἐπανάκειμαι.definition: to be imposed upon as punishment; to be superadded, Numen. ap.Eus.PE14.8

ἐπανακλαγγάνω.definition: give tongue again and again, X.Cyn.4.5,6.23

ἐπανάκλησις.definition: recall, reaction; double inspiration, Hp.Epid.2.3.7, Gal.7.899

ἐπανακλίνω.definition: make to lie down, Hp.Acut.37, cf. Sm.Ca.2.5; incline one valve of the heart towards the other, Hp.Cord.10

ἐπανακράζω.definition: call out to, in aor. imper. Poll.5.85

ἐπανακρούω.definition: poet. put a ship back , Hsch.: metaph., Isyll.6:—Med., put back, Ar.Av.648

ἐπανακυκλέω.definition: recur, of intermittent fevers, Gal.7.412; Pass., make a counter revolution, Pl.R.617b; but simply, revolve, Dam.Pr.23

ἐπανακύκλησις.definition: return of a circle into itself, Pl.Ti.40c

ἐπανακύπτω.definition: have an upward slope, X.Eq.12.13; rise up to thwart, J.BJ1.31.1

ἐπαναλαμβάνω.definition: take up again, resume, repeat; revise, correct, Id.Lg.781b; Thphr.CP3.7.8

ἐπανάληψις.definition: in Rhet., resumption, repetition; = III, Gal.7.433

ἐπαναλίσκω.definition: consume still more, D.50.42: aor; spend in addition, IG 12.24 ; but PCorn.1.88

ἐπαναμένω.definition: poet. wait longer, Hdt.8.141; wait for one, Id.Nu.803; Id.Lys.74: impers., what there is in store for me to suffer, A.Pr.605 ; Id.Pers.807; . . S.OC1718

ἐπαναμιμνῄσκω.definition: remind one of, mention again to one, Pl.Lg.688a, cf. Arist.Mem.451a12, Porph.Abst.1.30; . . D.6.35

ἐπανανεόομαι.definition: Med., revive, Pl.R.358b; renew, POxy.237 viii41

ἐπαναπαύω.definition: Med., come to rest, of a machine, HeroAut.24.4: metaph., come to rest in, Iamb.Comm.Math.8; Ev.Luc.10.6; LXXNu.11.26

ἐπαναπέμπω.definition: send back to a point, Hp.Mul.2.133, prob. in PPetr.2p.64

ἐπαναπέτομαι.definition: aor. 2 inf. fly up, Hsch. s.v

ἐπαναπήγνυμι.definition: fix in or on:—Med., fix their spears in the ground, Orph.A.319

ἐπαναπιπράσκω.definition: put up to sale again:—Pass., aor. part. PPetr.3p.120 : fut. PTheb.Bank1.24 , cf. UPZ112iii12

ἐπαναπλέω.definition: put to sea against, Hdt.8.9, cf; sail back again, ib.24, D.56.29, Plb.1.28.10

ἐπαναποδίζω.definition: retrace one's steps in argument, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.813.20

ἐπαναπρίασθαι.definition: acr., buy at a re-sale, IG7.3073.26

ἐπαναρρήγνυμι.definition: tear open again, Plu.Cat.Mi.70:—Pass., burst open afresh, Hp.Loc.Hom.14

ἐπαναρρίπτω.definition: or throw up in the air: seemingly intr. , spring high in the air, X.Cyn.5.4

ἐπανασείω.definition: lift up and shake, Hp.Foet.Exsect.4: metaph., threaten one with it, D.H.11.6; Procop.Arc.23:—Pass., of soldiers, being used to overawe . ., J.AJ19.1.16, cf. 17

ἐπανασκοπέω.definition: consider yet again, Pl.Cra.428d, Hp.Mi.369d; Id.Tht.154e

ἐπανασπείρω.definition: sow again; and second sowing, Tz.ad Hes.Op.444

ἐπανάστασις.definition: rising up to go to stool: hence; rising up again, D.S.18.31

ἐπανάστημα.definition: rising, blister, Sch.Ar.Ra.238; eminence, hill, Phlp.in de An.311.24

ἐπαναστρέφω.definition: intr., turn back upon one, wheel round; Pass., return to the surface, Arist.Fr.335

ἐπαναστροφή.definition: = return, of the chorus; Rhet., repetition of the last word or words of a sentence at the beginning of the next, Hermog.Id.1.12; of the syllables in Eust.1751.40

ἐπανάτασις.definition: stretching upwards, holding up; metaph., threatening, Ph.1.282 , al., POxy.237 viii 10 , Iamb.Myst.6.6; brandishing, PHal.1.186

ἐπανατείνω.definition: poet. Orph.A.61,332:—stretch; freq. in Med., brandish threatingly, PHal.1.186 ; Luc.Cat.13, cf. Jul.Or.6.196b; Plb.2.44.3: c. inf., threaten to do, Id.15.29.14:—Pass., POxy.1408.17

ἐπανατέλλω.definition: intr., rise, Hdt.2.142; Id.3.84; Id.7.54; AP12.178 ; H Arist.Mete.376b29; of a star, Sammelb.2134.7; rise again, Gem.6.10; having risen from bed, A.Ag.27; Plu.Aem.18; show oneself, appear, A.Ch.282; E.HF1053 ; the tim…

ἐπανατέμνω.definition: Ion. cut open further, Hp.VC13; cut open again, Aret.CA1.4

ἐπανατίθημι.definition: lay upon, Ar.V.148; Med., shift one's position, of patients under operation, Gal.18.425

ἐπανατολή.definition: invisible rising of stars just after sunrise or sunset, Ptol.Alm.8.4

ἐπανατρέπω.definition: overturn, upset, Hdn.3.8.5; intr., return, Cratin.181

ἐπανατρέφω.definition: feed up, recruit, nourish, Hp.Aph.2.7, Aret.CD1.5

ἐπανατρέχω.definition: aor. 2 return, recur; of property rights, pass, PLond.3.1044.14 , 5.1727.46

ἐπανατρυγάω.definition: glean after the vintage, c. acc., LXXDe.24.21, Le.19.10

ἐπαναφέρω.definition: intr. in Act., rise or be referred to a cause, Pl.Ly.219c; put into the account, D.41.20, cf. IG22.1607a7

ἐπαναφορά.definition: referring, reference; reference of a question to an assembly, And.3.33; to the people, Harp

ἐπαναφυσάω.definition: play on the flute in accompaniment, Ar.Th.1175

ἐπαναφωνέω.definition: pronounce in addition or after, opp. S.E.M.1.130

ἐπαναχωρέω.definition: retreat, return, CharonFr.2, Ar.Lys.461, Th.6.49; Pherecr.59; Hdt.9.13; Th.1.63, cf. 3.96; Id.4.44; Pl.Lg.781e; return from . ., Plu.2.580a; withdraw from, PLond.5.1727.16

ἔπανδρος.definition: manly, Demad.37, Phld.Ir.p.65 W., Vett. Val.14.24, al.; D.S.4.50; IG4.951 ; masculine spirit, Corn.ND20; Hierocl.p.63 S. . Adv. S.E.M.11.107; CIG4239 , cf. SIG709.6

ἐπάνειμι.definition: used as fut. of go; c. acc. rei, return to, recapitulate, ib.693c; Id.Ti.61d

ἐπανείρομαι.definition: or , question again; ask again, Pl.Prt.329a, cf. Grg.451b; . . J.AJ18.6.6

ἐπανεμέω.definition: vomit thereafter, Hp.Epid.1.12; of ruminants, bring back into the mouth, Gal.2.545

ἐπανέρχομαι.definition: go back, return, Anacr.23; recur, of intermittent fevers, etc., Gal.7.412, 16.711

ἐπανερωτάω.definition: of persons, question again, v.l. in; of things, ask over again, Id.Grg.454c, Lg.645d

ἐπάνεσις.definition: abatement, of fevers; name of a bandage, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.43.1

ἐπανέχω.definition: hold up, support; seemingly intr. , rest upon, v.l. in D.19.51; to be contented with, Alciphr.1.38; rely on, rest contented with, Artem.1.12; cf

ἐπανήκω.definition: pf. PAmh.2.50.5 :— to have come back, return, E.IA1628 , Pl.Com.68 , Ph.2.117; D.47.55; Plb.6.58.3; Paus.3.9.2; LXXPr.7.20

ἐπανθεμίζω.definition: metaph., flit like a bee from flower to flower, S.Ichn.323

ἐπανθέω.definition: bloom, be in flower, Theoc.5.131, LXXJb.14.7; metaph., of any thing that forms on the surface, Hdt.2.12, cf. Str.11.13.2; Ar.Nu.978; . . Id.Ec.903; ib.13; also of hair turning grey, . . Id.V.1065, cf. X.Cyn.4.8

ἐπάνθημα.definition: efflorescence, fine flower, Id.in Nic.p.39 P., al.; special virtues, ib.p.118 P

ἐπανθίζω.definition: deck as with flowers, make bright-coloured; metaph., deck as with flowers, decorate, adorn, A.Ch.150; Id.Th.949:—Pass., Philostr.VS1.15.4.—The aor. Med. is prob. corrupt in A.Ag.1459

ἐπάνθισμα.definition: lit. efflorescence: hence coloured froth, Hp.Prorrh.1.21, cf. Aret.SD1.11

ἐπανθισμός.definition: efflorescence, scum, Dsc.5.92; name for a vein, Dionys. ap. Ruf.Onom.205

ἐπανθρακίζω.definition: broil on the coals, Cratin.143 (cod. A; blacken with charcoal, AP11.66

ἐπανθρακόομαι.definition: Pass., to be broiled on the coals, Poll.6.55

ἐπανιάομαι.definition: to be annoyed at a thing, X.Eph.1.15, Poll.5.129

ἐπανίημι.definition: let go, give up, c. acc., D.2.30; dismiss, Id.18.177; remit, Plu.Lyc.22; release from, X.Cyn.7.1; relax, Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.5

ἐπανισόω.definition: make equal, balance evenly, Th.8.57; IG22.1013.15; Just.Nov.92.1 Intr.; Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.4.2; Polyaen.7.16.2; reduce, Arist.Resp.478a3; the others like wise he made equal to one another, distributing to them their fa…

ἐπανίστημι.definition: set up again, ib.778d; make to rise against, Plu.Sert.13; raise in revolt against, App.Hisp.101

ἐπάνοδος.definition: return, LXXSi.17.24, etc.; Plu.Tim.38; Iamb.inNic.p.76P.; to one's country, E.Ep.2.2, cf. Hdn.8.7.7: metaph., ascent of the soul, Dam.Pr.75; simply, journey, PLips.45.17

ἐπανοίγω.definition: open, CIG4259 : in aor. Med., cause to be opened, Epigr.Gr.340

ἐπανοιδέω.definition: swell up, rise on the surface, Hp.Nat.Mul.2, Arist.HA531b3:—Pass., in same sense, Hp.VC13

ἐπανορθόω.definition: impf. with double augm; correct, amend, revise, Pl.Lg.769e; Is.1.18; Pl.Prt.340d; correct one, teach him better, Ar.Lys.528, cf. Isoc.1.3, Iamb.l.c.; IG12.108.49:—Med. in proper sense, correct oneself, Pl.R.361a: but …

ἐπανόρθωσις.definition: setting right, correcting, Ti.Locr.104b; Jul.Or.2.80c; Diocl.Fr.138; revision, Lex ap.D.24.22; to be capable of improvement, opp. Arist.EN1165b18; of circumstances, amendment, Plb.1.66.12, 1.11.2, etc

ἐπανορθωτής.definition: corrector, restorer, D.H.8.67; of writings, Gal.7.894; = Lat. corrector morum, D.C.54.30; also, = Lat. corrector civitatis, IG4.1417 , 5.541 , 7.91

ἐπαντιάζω.definition: to be present, prob. in h.Ap.152

ἐπαντλέω.definition: pump over or upon, pour over, Pl.Phd.112c ; Id.Phdr.253a; pour a flood of words over, E.Fr.899.4, cf. Ael.NA6.51; Diph.107; irrigate, Plu.2.688e: metaph., Philostr.VS1.25.2; Id.VA6.11: abs., Luc.Tim.18:—Pass., to be i…

ἐπάντλησις.definition: pouring over, as of water over a; pumping, Stud.Pal.10.259.15

ἐπανύω.definition: fut. complete, accomplish, Hes.Sc.311:—Med., procure, . . codd. in S.Tr.995 ; carry into effect, Ph.1.77

ἐπάνω.definition: Adv., above, on the upper side or; as Prep., c. gen., Id.1.179 , Pl.Phd.109d; IG12.872.32 ; having risen superior to . ., Plu.2.1063c; J.BJ1.4.2; D.L.6.28

ἐπάξιος.definition: worthy, deserving of; deserved, Pi.I.4.44; worthy, meet, A.Th.865 ; S.El.971, etc.; meet with one's deserts, A.Pr.70. Adv. S.OT133, Iamb.Myst.3.20

ἐπαξιόω.definition: think right, deem it right, c. inf; expect, believe, c. acc. et inf., . . . . ib.658; but . . deems thee worthy of honour, so as to render thee a due return, Id.OC1497

ἐπαξονέω.definition: place on axles, Orph.Fr.49.39; enroll in tablets, register, LXXNu.1.18

ἐπαοιδία.definition: later form of foreg., Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.9, Hsch

ἐπαοιδός.definition: = LXXEx.7.11,22,al., Ph.1.449 , Arr.Epict.3.24.10, Man.5.183 . Adv. by way of a charm, Steph.in Hp.2.458D

ἐπαπειλέω.definition: hold out as a threat to one; c. dat. only, threaten, Il.13.582

ἐπαπερείδομαι.definition: Pass., lean upon, Posidon.26; support, Ph.Byz.Mir.6.2

ἐπαποδύω.definition: strip one for combat against another, set him up as a rival to, Plu.2.788d:—Med., strip and set to work at a thing, Ar.Lys.615; Ph.1.360; set upon, attack, Plu.Marc.3

ἐπαποθνήσκω.definition: die after another, Pl.Smp.180a, 208d, J.BJ5.12.3; die while yet speaking, Id.AJ13.11.3: abs., Plu.Aem.35

ἐπαπολαύω.definition: revel in, D.S.37.3: c. gen., Tz.H.9.315; profit by, Anon.in Rh.111.28

ἐπαπόλλυμι.definition: or kill in addition, Ael.NA10.48, Luc.Merc.Cond.42:—Med., die after, D.C.60.34: abs., Aristid.Or.25.22

ἐπαπόλογος.definition: in Arc. form requiring defence, SIG306.34

ἐπαποπνίγω.definition: choke besides:—Pass., aor. 2 may you be choked besides, Ar.Eq.940

ἐπαπορέω.definition: raise a new doubt or question; c. dat., criticize, Diog.Oen.18

ἐπαπορητικός.definition: dubitative: a kind of rhetorical question, Stoic.2.61, cf. D.L.7.68; Gal.16.722. Adv. Phlp.inAPo.359.15, Eust.1114.30

ἐπαποστέλλω.definition: send to attack, Id.32.5.11; Id.2.8.12; D.S.12.24, cf. LXXJb.20.23

ἐπαράομαι.definition: Cret. part. Leg.Gort., Cyren; c. dat. only, curse solemnly, Pl.Lg.931b, Jul.Or.2.50b, Leg.Gort.2.40, etc

ἐπαραρίσκω.definition: aor. 1 aor. 2 to or; intr. in Ion. pf. plpf. tight or exactly, a cross-bolt was fitted therein, Il.12.456; part. close-fitting, well fixed, firm on his feet, Arat.83: also Ep. aor. part. Pass., well-fitted, prepared, …

ἐπαράσσω.definition: Att. dash or clap to, Pl.Prt.314d, cf. Plu.Art.29; Hld.10.31; strike rods against the thin parts, Gal.10.998

ἐπαργυρόομαι.definition: to be overlaid with silver, IG22.1485.48: metaph., of costly dinners, . . Mnesim.3.2

ἐπάργυρος.definition: overlaid with silver, Hdt.1.50,9.80, cf. IG12.276, BMus.Inscr.4.481*.472; Onos.1.20

ἐπάρδευσις.definition: watering: hence, shower, of rain; irrigation, POxy. 1631.14 , al

ἐπάρδω.definition: irrigate, Arr.An.4.6.5: metaph., Luc.Am.45, cf. LXX4 Ma.1.29, Plot.6.7.33; Ph.2.345; Him.Ecl.32.6:—Pass., J.BJ4.8.3; of the body by nourishment, Ti.Locr.102b

ἐπαρέσκομαι.definition: to be satisfied, . . Eustr.in EN270.16: aor. Med., Hsch

ἐπαρήγω.definition: come to aid, help, Il.23.783, Od.13.391, E.El.1350 , Ar.V.402: abs., A.Ch.725 ; S.El.1197; also in Prose, X.Cyr.6.4.18, LXX2 Ma.13.17

ἐπαρηγών.definition: helper, A.R.1.1039, Milet.1.205a : c. gen., Orph.A.348, L.677

ἐπαριθμέω.definition: count in addition, Paus.10.5.8; count the cities by the days, i. e. visit a city a day, Aristid.Or.26.93

ἐπαριστερεύομαι.definition: to be awkward, clumsy, Hsch. s.v

ἐπαρίστερος.definition: towards the left, on the left hand; written from right to left, Tab.Defix.67a8

ἐπάρκεια.definition: help, support, Plb.1.48.5, al.: pl., Id.6.52.5; ib.49.7

ἐπαρκέω.definition: fut. : Ep. aor. inf; c. acc. rei, ward off, prevent, A.R.2.1161; S.Aj.360

ἐπαρκής.definition: helpful, Emp.22.4; of remedies; sufficient, Plu.Cic.7, cf. D.P.1101. Adv. IG4.491

ἐπάρουρος.definition: attached to the soil as a serf, Od.11.489

ἐπαρτάω.definition: hang on or over; the elevated part of the beam, Arist.Mech.850a23
