ἐπιδερμίς.definition: outer skin, epidermis; web of water-birds' feet, Arist. ap. Sch.Il.2.460

ἐπιδεσμέω.definition: bind up or on, Pall.in Hp.Fract.12.284C., Paul.Aeg.3.35, Hippiatr.11

ἐπίδεσμος.definition: upper or outer bandage, Hp.Off.9, Ar.V.1440, Arist.HA630a6, Ph.Bel.96.19: metaph., of fortresses as the `fetters' of Greece, Str.9.4.15: heterocl. pl. Ael.NA8.9:—also Gal.13.686

ἐπιδεύομαι.definition: Ep. for II), to be; to be lacking in, fall short of, c. gen. rei, 23.670, cf. 17.142: also c. gen. pers., fallest far short of them, 5.636; or both together, 24.385: later c. acc. rei, A.R.2.1220.—The Act. occurs only…

ἐπιδεύτερος.definition: secondary, of minor rank, of a dramatist, Suid. s.v

ἐπιδέχομαι.definition: receive besides, Men.583; receive, welcome, Plb.21.18.3; POxy.281.9

ἐπιδέω.definition: fut. bind, fasten on; bind up, bandage, Hp.VC13, Fract.21, Art.14:—Pass., with one's wounds bound up, X.Cyr.5.2.32, al.; ib.2.3.19

ἐπίδηλος.definition: seen clearly, manifest, Thgn.442; formed, Hp.Carn.13

ἐπιδημεύω.definition: = sq., live among the people, live in the throng, opp. live in the country, Od.16.28

ἐπιδημέω.definition: to be at home, live at home, opp; of diseases, to be prevalent, epidemic, Hp.Prog.25

ἐπιδημία.definition: stay in a place, Pl.Prm.127a; arrival at . . IG3.1023

ἐπιδημιουργέω.definition: order perfectly, of the stars, Hp.Ep.18

ἐπιδιαβαίνω.definition: cross over after another, Hdt.4.122; spread, of diseases, Gal.8.297; Aët.12.2

ἐπιδιαγράφω.definition: pay in addition, PRev.Laws 34.14 ; f.l. in Vett.Val.348.11

ἐπιδιαθήκη.definition: additional will, codicil, J.AJ17.9.4; pledge, security, Lys.Fr.110 S

ἐπιδιαίρεσις.definition: further incision, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.8.4, Gal.1.386

ἐπιδιαιρέω.definition: fut. PPetr.2p.10 :— divide; make a cross-incision in, Gal.12.522

ἐπιδιάκειμαι.definition: to be staked upon a throw at dice, used; to be laid upon, of vegetables, Sor.1.51

ἐπιδιακρίνω.definition: decide as umpire, Pl.Grg.524a; confirm a sentence, D.C.57.20

ἐπιδιαλύω.definition: come as a relief to, c. acc., Antyll. ap. Orib.6.8.5

ἐπιδιαμένω.definition: remain after, D.L.Prooem.11, Dsc.1.12, Artem.1.45; continue to exist, Diog.Oen.36

ἐπιδιαπλέω.definition: sail across after or besides, Id.47.47

ἐπιδιαρθρόω.definition: articulate further, Procl.Inst.177, Ammon.in Int.195.22, Prisc.Lyd.36.8:—hence Dam.Pr.431

ἐπιδιαρρέω.definition: flow through or melt away besides, Erot. s.v

ἐπιδιαρρήγνυμαι.definition: aor. Pass., burst at or because of a thing, Ar.Eq.701

ἐπιδιασαφέω.definition: declare further, Vett.Val.87.20, al.; make more explicit, Hdn.Fig.p.95 S.:—Pass., become clearly understood, Plb.32.16.5

ἐπιδιασκευάζω.definition: revise again, prepare a new edition of a work, Hp.Acut.3

ἐπιδιατάσσομαι.definition: make additions to a will, Ep.Gal.3.15

ἐπιδιατείνω.definition: stretch by inflation yet further; intr., spread far, of fame or rumour, Plb.31.23.3; extend so as to include, . . Phld.Rh.2.209 S

ἐπιδιατίθημι.definition: arrange besides or afterwards; Med., make a second or later will, Pap.Erzherzog Rainer723

ἐπιδιατρίβω.definition: spend time on, Thphr.Od.11; spend, J.AJ11.5.2, cf.Hdn.2.11.1; dwelling on it, Arist.Mete.371a23

ἐπιδιαφθείρω.definition: destroy, ruin besides, in Pass., Ph. ap. Eus.PE8.14; become corrupt, Gal.8.42

ἐπιδίδωμι.definition: give besides, Il.23.559; of a physician, administer, Ph.1.253; give afterwards, Dsc.4.148

ἐπιδιεξέρχομαι.definition: to be excreted afterwards, opp. Gal.16.699

ἐπιδίζημαι.definition: inquire besides, go on to inquire; seek for or demand besides, Id.5.106: so Mosch.2.28

ἐπιδιήγησις.definition: after- or repeated narration, Arist.Rh.1414b14, Corn.Rh.p.364H

ἐπιδιίστημι.definition: let an interval elapse; Pass., have a second diastole, of the pulse, Ruf.Syn.Puls.8.7

ἐπιδικάζω.definition: adjudge property in dispute to one, of the; Med., of the claimant, go to law to establish one's claim, Pl.Lg.874a, PGnom.28,40 ; . . I have obtained it by a lawsuit, Is.11.19

ἐπιδικασία.definition: process at law to obtain an inheritance, Is.3.41, 61 , Lex ap.D.43.16, Ph.2.443; for her hand as heiress, Is.3.72

ἐπιδικάσιμος.definition: to be claimed as one's right, J.AJ4.2.4; much sought for, Luc.Somn.9

ἐπίδικος.definition: disputed at law, liable to be made the; Subst. an heiress for whose hand her next of kin are claimants at law, Is.3.64; ib.73

ἐπιδινεύω.definition: later form for sq., Opp.H.4.218, Hld.3.3

ἐπιδινέω.definition: whirl for the throw, swing round before throwing, Il.3.378, cf. Od.9.538, etc.:—Med., turn over in one's mind, resolve, 20.218:—Pass., wheel about, as birds in the air, 2.151; . . Nic.Al.33; so of drones, Arist.HA624a24

ἐπιδιορθόω.definition: correct afterwards, GDI5039.9 : —Med., to have deficiencies set right also, complete unfinished reforms, Ep.Tit.1.5; simply, correct, Syrian.in Metaph.167.11

ἐπιδιόρθωσις.definition: correction of a previous; excusing of an unpleasant statement , Alex.Fig.1.4, Longin.Rh.p.194 H

ἐπιδιορίζω.definition: define or determine further, Arist.Cael.303a13, Gal.7.706, al

ἐπιδιουρέω.definition: pass along with the urine, Hp.Prorrh.2.4

ἐπιδιπλασιάζω.definition: make double, v.l. in Hdn.6.8.8:— Pass., J.AJ19.1.5

ἐπιδιπλοΐζω.definition: redouble: prob. f.l. for A.Eu.1014 codd

ἐπιδιπλόω.definition: make double, LXXEx.26.9; multiply by two, Paul.Al.H.4:—Pass., Vett.Val.223.34

ἐπιδισκεύω.definition: throw away: hence, discard, in Pass., prob. in Phld. Herc.1251.17

ἐπιδιστάζω.definition: doubt about a thing, Thphr.Od.45; Porph.Marc.19

ἐπιδίφριος.definition: one who sits at his work, plies a sedentary or humble trade, D.H.Th.50, PLond.5.1708.21 , Just.Nov.90.1Intr.; Iamb.VP34.245; a sedentary trade, D.H.2.28; Artem.2.14

ἐπιδιώκω.definition: pursue after, Hdt.4.1, 160, Lys.3.35; prosecute again, Is.Fr.157

ἐπιδοιάζω.definition: entertain doubts over, turn over and over, A.R.3.21; cf

ἐπιδοξάζω.definition: form an opinion about a thing:—Pass., matter of opinion, Thphr.CP1.5.5

ἐπίδοξος.definition: likely, of persons; of repute, glorious, Pi.N.9.46; and in late Prose, as LXXSi.3.18, D.S.13.83, Plu.2.239d, etc. Adv. LXX1 Es.9.45, IG12.117, 288 , Artem.2.30

ἐπιδορπίζομαι.definition: eat in the second course or for dessert, Diph.79, Sophil.4.5: in Poll.6.102 is f.l. for cf. ib.79

ἐπιδορπίς.definition: old name for Philem. ap. Ath.1.11d

ἐπιδόρπισμα.definition: second course, dessert, Philippid.20 , Com.Adesp.141 , Ath.14.664f

ἐπιδόσιμος.definition: given over and above; contributed freely, IG22.1629.960, cf. 950, Inscr.Prien.112.100

ἐπίδοσις.definition: free gift, esp. voluntary contribution to the state, `benevolence', benefaction, D.18.171; Id.21.161, cf. Thphr.Char.22.3; Histria7.23 ; charitable endowment, POxy.705.59

ἐπιδοτήρ.definition: giver of more, opp. of planets, Ptol.Tetr.189

ἐπιδουπέω.definition: make a noise or clashing, Plu.Eum.14; Id.Crass.23

ἐπιδράσσομαι.definition: Att. lay hold of, Plu.Alex.25, Gal.4.537, etc.; Alciphr.3.60: metaph., Phld.Rh.2.266S.; Jul.Or.6.188c; Plu.2.793c; Id.Oth.2

ἐπιδράω.definition: perform over a person, of purificatory rites, Philostr.VA6.5

ἐπιδρομή.definition: running over, inroad; metaph., brief notice, Phld.Rh.2.268S.; in his summary notice of them, D.L.7.48; summary, Corn.Rh.p.389H.; Dam.Pr.369; Gal.9.431; Iamb.in Nic.p.72P

ἐπίδρομος.definition: that may be overrun, a wall; metaph., intelligible, Them.Or.13.162c

ἐπιδυσφημέω.definition: give an ill name to, Arist.EN1145a33

ἐπιδύω.definition: aor. 2 set upon or so as to interrupt an action, Il.2.413; Ep.Eph.4.26, cf. LXXDe.24.15, Ph.2.324

ἐπιδωμάω.definition: build upon, pf. Pass. Ph.Byz.Mir.4.4: written ib.2.3 ; cf

ἐπιεικής.definition: fitting, meet, suitable; of statements, rights, etc

ἐπιείσομαι.definition: only fut. and aor., rush, hasten to or against, Il.11.367; Od.15.504; Il.21.424

ἐπιέννυμι.definition: put on besides or over, we threw a cloak over him, Od.20.143: elsewh. Hom. has only pf. part. Pass. : in metaph. sense c. acc., clad in shamelessness, strength, Il.1.149, 8.262, etc.; AP7.283 ; covered with hair over …

ἐπιετής.definition: of this year, SIG690 ; v.l. in Plb.3.55.1

ἐπιζαρέω.definition: = E.Rh.441 , Ph.45: said to be Arc. by Eust.909.28

ἐπιζάω.definition: Ion. survive, Hdt.1.120; Pl.Lg.661c , cf. Eus.Mynd.38, etc.: metaph. of envy, Plu.Num.22

ἐπιζεύγνυμι.definition: and join at top, Hdt.7.36; join to, . . A.Eu.405: metaph., Arist.HA531b22, cf. Rh.1407b19; Ph.1.209; nor let thy mouth be joined to evil sayings, A.Ch.1044: Math., let the point A be joined to the point B, Arist.Mete.…

ἐπίζευξις.definition: fastening together, joining; Gramm., repetition of a word, Hdn.Fig.p.99 S., Phoeb.Fig.1.3

ἐπιζέω.definition: Act., cause to boil, heat, c. acc., Id.Cyc.392: me taph., Id.IT987

ἐπιζήμιος.definition: Dor. etc. bringing; penal: punishments, penalties, Pl.Lg.784e,788b; Tab.Heracl.1.127; = Epist.Philipp. ap.D.18.157: sg., fine, IG5.6.36 , 5.1498

ἐπιζητέω.definition: seek after, wish for, miss, Hdt.3.36; request, Anatolian Studies 38, cf. PMasp.156.16

ἐπιζήτησις.definition: seeking after, craving; inquiry, PSI4.386.40 , Phld.Sign.21,28 , J.Ap.1.22, Iamb.Myst.1.18

ἐπιζητητέος.definition: to be looked for, required, Arist.EN1094b13; to be sought for, Chor.in Rh.Mus.49.502

ἐπιζυγέω.definition: in pass. sense, to be joined, Nic.Fr.74.22

ἐπιζυγίς.definition: iron pin upon which the strands of; cross beam, Apollod.Poliorc.172.7

ἐπίζυγος.definition: of tiles, dub. sens. in Inscr.Délos 366 A 21,23

ἐπιζύγωμα.definition: part of the latch of a door, Et.Gud.288.36

ἐπιζώννυμι.definition: gird on:—Pass., with their clothes girt on so as to leave the breast bare, v.l. for in Hdt.2.85; girt with.., Plu.CG15 codd.; Paus.9.39.8

ἐπιθαλαμιογράφος.definition: writer of epithalamia, Tz. ad Lyc.p.1 S

ἐπιθαλάμιος.definition: belonging to a bridal, nuptial; Subst. , or bridal song, sung in chorus before the bridal chamber, Theoc.18tit., Luc.Symp.40, Him.Or.1.1

ἐπιθαλαμίτης.definition: epith. of Hermes in Euboea, Hsch

ἐπιθαλασσίδιος.definition: Att. = sq., Th.4.76, X.HG3.4.28, Pl.Lg.704b, etc.; is prob. f.l. in Str.2.1.16, 3.4.20

ἐπιθάλπω.definition: warm on the surface, Xenoph.31, cf; comfort afterwards, BCH47.284

ἐπιθανάτιος.definition: condemned to death, D.H.7.35; the funeral torches, Lib.Decl.40.15; but deadly, ib.2.28

ἐπιθάνατος.definition: sick to death, hard at death's door; deadly, Hp.Mochl.36; of poisons, Thphr.CP6.4.5

ἐπιθάπτω.definition: bury again, Philostr.Her.1.3; bury another in the same grave, CIG4341d , 4366k , sqq

ἐπιθαρσέω.definition: Att. put trust in or on; take heart to resist, App.BC3.10, cf. Ael.NA4.34,9.1; venture on . . , ib.5.56: abs., take courage, D.C.41.50,al

ἐπιθαρσύνω.definition: Att. cheer on, encour Il.4.183, D.H.10.41, Plu.Mar.36

ἐπιθαυμάζω.definition: pay honour to, by giving him a fee, Ar.Nu.1147; in wonder at . . , Plu.Marc.30: abs., Arr.Epict.1.26.12

ἐπιθεάομαι.definition: survey, examine, Sch.Ar.Nu.499; look at, Agath.5.3; reflect on a thing, Poll.6.115

ἐπιθειάζω.definition: call upon in the name of the gods, adjure; inspire, Id.2.580d,589d, Max.Tyr.37.5

ἐπιθειασμός.definition: appeal to the gods, Th.7.75; inspiration, Poll.1.16, Ph.2.299

ἐπίθεμα.definition: = cover, Arist.HA529b8; capital of a column, LXX3 Ki.7.4 sq

ἐπιθεραπεία.definition: care of a statue, IGRom.4.293ai43, ii62

ἐπιθεράπευσις.definition: Rhet., indignant reiteration of a charge, Ps.-Ascon. in Verr.Act.i §27

ἐπιθεραπεύω.definition: to be diligent about, work zealously; apply after-treatment, Hp.Mochl.41

ἐπιθερμαίνομαι.definition: Pass., become feverish, Hp.Epid.1.1; later in Act., warm up, PHolm.17.40

ἐπιθεσπίζω.definition: of Triton, prophesy or divine upon; of an oracle, give sanction, D.H.2.6; Id.3.35

ἐπιθέτης.definition: plotter, impostor, Luc.Trag.172; official of a religious association, IG3.1280a

ἐπίθετος.definition: additional, D.H.3.71; esp. at; fictitious, Thphr.HP9.8.8; opp. D.H.4.70, cf. 68

ἐπιθέω.definition: run upon, at or after, Hdt.9.107, X.Cyn.6.10; metaph., Plot.2.9.6; to be diffused over, Id.5.3.17, al

ἐπιθεωρέω.definition: examine over again or carefully, ascertain; consider next in order, Epicur.Nat.13G

ἐπιθεώρησις.definition: inspection, CPHerm.7 ii 23; Astrol., aspect, Ptol.Tetr.193

ἐπιθεωρία.definition: Astrol., aspecting from the right, Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.155.15

ἐπιθήγω.definition: whetor sharpen yet more, Ael.NA5.16: metaph., stimulate yet more, Plu.786b

ἐπιθηματουργία.definition: making of lids or covers, Pl.Plt.280d

ἐπιθηραρχία.definition: contingent of four elephants, Ascl.Tact.9, Ael.Tact.23

ἐπιθήραρχος.definition: officer commanding such a contingent, ll.cc

ἐπιθιγγάνω.definition: aor.2 touch, Thphr.Od.11; reach as far as, Id.2.921d

ἐπιθλίβω.definition: press upon the surface, D.S.3.14; tread, Nonn.D.7.91; crowd round, App.BC4.45: metaph., repress, check, Plu.2.782d

ἐπίθλιψις.definition: pressure on the surface, Aret.CA1.9 ; crushing, Orib.Fr.74

ἐπιθοάζω.definition: sit as suppliant at an altar, A.Ch.856 ; E.Med.1409; cf. II; but invoking the gods, and shd. prob. be read

ἐπιθολόω.definition: make turbid, Luc.Ind.7, Max.Tyr.33.5: metaph., Plu.in Hes.66; Philostr.V A6.11; Iamb.VP24.107; Agath.3.11:—Pass., become turbid, Placit.3.5.8, Gal.6.57, Luc.Lex.4: metaph., Artem.4Prooem.; Iamb.in Nic.p.4P., cf. Myst.…

ἐπιθόρνυμαι.definition: cover, of the male, Luc.Am.22, etc.; Philostr.V A5.29, cf. Im.2.3: abs., Ael.N.A.10.2, al

ἐπιθορυβέω.definition: in token of displeasure, X.HG1.7.13, Luc.Asin.54

ἐπιθρηνέω.definition: lament over, Babr.118.8: abs., Plu.2.123c, Diog.Oen.61: c. acc. cogn., Hld.10.37

ἐπιθρυλέω.definition: disturb with noise, EM456.40; proclaim noisily, Agath.2.2

ἐπιθρύπτω.definition: enfeeble, enervate, Philostr.V A1.37:—Pass., practise affectations, Aristaenet.1.28; effeminate, Plu.Dio17

ἐπιθρῴσκω.definition: leap upon, c. gen; leap over a space, so far do [the horses] spring at a bound, 5.772; Hes.Sc.438

ἐπιθυμέω.definition: set one's heart upon a thing, long for, covet, desire, c. gen. rei, Hdt.2.66, A.Ag.216, etc.: also c. gen. pers., Lys.3.5, X.An.4.1.14 ); of political attachments, And.4.28; Lys.20.3: c. inf., desire to do, Hdt.1.24; …

ἐπιθύμημα.definition: object of desire, Id.Lg.687c; yearning, desire, Hp.de Arte1, Antipho Soph.110, Epicur.Fr.141: pl., Philyll.30

ἐπιθυμητής.definition: one who longs for or desires; abs., lover, follower, X.Mem.1.2.60

ἐπιθυμία.definition: Ion. desire, yearning; c. gen., longing after a thing, desire of or for it, Th.2.52, 7.84, etc.; Democr.224; Antipho2.1.7; And.2.10; Pl.Cra.406b; Id.Criti.113d; Id.Prt.318a, Tht.143e; Id.Lg.841c; Id.Ti.19b; X.Cyr.1.1.…

ἐπιθυμιάω.definition: offer incense, Plu.Alex.25, CIG2715.6 : c.acc., prob. in Men.260 , cf. Plu.2.372d; Milet.3.145 , SIG694.43 , Artem.4.2:—Pass., Dsc.1.68

ἐπιθύνω.definition: = S.Ph.1059: Ep. Iterat. A.R.3.1325: c.dat., Man.2.340

ἐπιθύριος.definition: over a door, IG4.1488.22; fixed on a door, ib.22.1408.20

ἐπίθυσις.definition: burning of incense, BMus.Inscr.789 , Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10 codd.; OGI383.142

ἐπιθύτης.definition: one who burns incense, Gloss.; so prob. in CIG3663 A15

ἐπιθύω.definition: sacrifice upon, h.Ap.491; burn incense, LXX3 Ki.12.33, J.BJ7.3.3, D.S.12.11, 18.61, Porph.Abst.2.59; D.S.18.61, v.l. in Ar.Pl.1116: generally, offer on, D.H.1.40 codd

ἐπιθωρακίζομαι.definition: put on one's armour, v.l. for

ἐπιθωΰσσω.definition: shout or call out, give loud commands, A.Pr.73; thou didst urge this upon not unwilling ears, ib.279; . . E.IT1127

ἐπικαγχαλάω.definition: exult in, Q.S.1.161; exult over, ib.643: abs., Id.2.374

ἐπικαθαιρέω.definition: pull down or destroy besides, Th.8.20

ἐπικαθαίρω.definition: purge yet more, Hp.Judic.11, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.169 ; of supplementary menstruation, Sor.1.28

ἐπικαθέζομαι.definition: sit down upon, Ar.Pl.185; to be supported, rest on, HeroBel.83.11, cf. J.AJ8.3.5

ἐπικαθεύδω.definition: sleep upon, Luc.Ind.4; sit on eggs, Arist.HA542b20: metaph., go to sleep over, i.e.neglect, Just.Nov.88.2.1

ἐπικάθημαι.definition: Ion. sit upon, Hdt.6.72; sit at his counter, of a banker's clerk or money-changer, D.49.17, cf. 33: abs., Id.36.7

ἐπικαθίζω.definition: set upon, Hp.Art.78: abs., (sc; Intr., sit upon, Eup.94.5; light upon, Plu.Them.12, cf. Thphr.CP6.10.5

ἐπικαθίημι.definition: let down, set upon; let down, shut, App.Hann.51

ἐπικαθικνέομαι.definition: Dor.3sg. fut. impose a surcharge or penalty, IG5.1421.15

ἐπικαθίστημι.definition: set upon, establish, D.C.41.50; set over, Pl.Ti.72b

ἐπικαθυγραίνομαι.definition: to be kept moist, Sor.1.44, Orib.Fr.144, Paul.Aeg.3.63

ἐπικαίνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be adorned or furnished with, 20.35 ; Q.S.12.145

ἐπικαιρία.definition: opportunity, Hp.Gland.4; title of work by Democr., D.L.9.48

ἐπικαίριος.definition: important, X.Oec.15.11; of persons, the most important persons of the army, Id.Cyr.3.3.12, cf. HG3.3.11: c.inf., those whose cure is all- important, Id.Cyr.8.2.25

ἐπίκαιρος.definition: in fit time or place, seasonable; serious, important, important symptoms, Hp.Epid.1.25; Id.Acut

ἐπικαίω.definition: light up or kindle on a place, h.Ap.491; burn on the surface, scorch, Hp.Aër.17 ; Pl.Ep.340d; Plb.38.8.7, cf. Apollon.Mir.23; Antipho Soph.26; of lightning, Arist.Mete.371b14; of hot iron, Id.HA631b26; of cold, Hp.Aër…

ἐπικαλέω.definition: summon a god to a sacrifice or as witness to; pray for, PLond.5.1676.24

ἐπικαλύπτω.definition: cover over, cover up, shroud; put as a covering over, E.HF642 codd. :—Pass., when the eyelids are drawn down, Arist.Sens.437a25

ἐπικαμπή.definition: bend, return or angle of a building; draw up their army angular-wise, i.e. with the wings thrown forward at an angle with the centre, so as to take the enemy in flank, X.Cyr.7.1.6; Arr.An.2.9.2, cf. 3.12.2

ἐπικαμπής.definition: curved, curling, BGU781 ii4 ; Luc.Gall.28; Plu.Cam.32; convex, Pall.in Hp.Fract.12.284C.; of hammer-toes, Heph.Astr.1.1. Adv. Sch.rec.A.Th.384

ἐπικάμπιος.definition: Subst. = Arr.Tact.26.7; Ael.Tact.31.4; opp. Polyaen.4.3.22, cf. Plb.5.82.9; also of fleets in naval warfare, Id.1.27.4

ἐπικάμπτω.definition: bend into an angle; Act., move to pity, Lib.Decl.46.13:—Pass., abs., Ctes.Fr.29.56, Lib.Or.6.38; Id.Loc.1.31

ἐπικαμπύλος.definition: crooked, curved, in the shoulders, h.Merc.90; Hes.Op.427

ἐπικαρπία.definition: produce, crop, Pl.Lg.955d; harvest-rights, Tab.Heracl.1.108, BGU101.19 ; usufruct, D.H.3.58

ἐπικαρπίζομαι.definition: draw the nutriment from, exhaust, of crops, Thphr.HP8.9.3

ἐπικάρπιος.definition: I) bringer or guardian of; pedicle or fruit-stalk, Phanias ap.Ath.2.68c, cf. 51c

ἐπικαταβαίνω.definition: go down to a place; go down after or against an enemy, Hdt.8.38, Th.4.11, 7.84

ἐπικαταβάλλω.definition: let fall down or droop at a thing, X.Cyn.4.3; impose a fine, Tab.Heracl.1.134, where for Ahrens corrected

ἐπικατάγνυμαι.definition: to be broken upon, of eggs; pf. part. Pass. perh. = weak, Cat.Cod. Astr.8.188

ἐπικατάγω.definition: work out a calculation; usu. in Pass., of ships or persons at sea, come to land along with or afterwards, Th.3.49, 8.28, J.AJ18.7.2, D.Chr.37.4, D.C.42.7, etc

ἐπικαταδαρθάνω.definition: aor. 2 fall asleep afterwards, Th.4.133, Pl.R.534d

ἐπικαταδέω.definition: bind upon or to, Hp.Epid.5.58, Luc.Asin.16,34

ἐπικαταδύνω.definition: dive after, Poll.1.108; of stars, set after, Procl.Hyp.5.52; Gem.9.1:—also Med., Cleom.1.3, Theo Sm.p.138 H

ἐπικατάδυσις.definition: setting of a star just after; Astrol., name of eighth Antioch. Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.117.11

ἐπικατακλίνω.definition: make bend down upon; introduce as a concubine, J.AJ1.10.4

ἐπικατακολουθέω.definition: attend to, Sch.Pi.O.6.108: abs., comply, PLille4.6

ἐπικαταλαμβάνω.definition: follow and catch up, overtake; of fruit which forms before the last year's fruit is ripe, overtakes it, Thphr.HP2.6.10

ἐπικαταλείπω.definition: bequeath in addition, Ramsay Studies in the Eastern Rom.Emp.345

ἐπικαταπίπτω.definition: fall upon, Luc.Anach.1; Q.S.3.399; metaph., fall to the lot of, Id.7.78

ἐπικαταπλάσσω.definition: put on a plaster as well, Hp.Fract.25

ἐπικαταπλέω.definition: bear down upon, of ships, D.S.16.66, Charito8.6

ἐπικαταράομαι.definition: bring curses, LXXNu.5.19,22; call down; curse , ib.Ma.2.2

ἐπικαταράσσομαι.definition: Pass., fall with a crash, D.H.10.16, 11.26

ἐπικαταρρέω.definition: run down, of humours, from the head to; fall down upon, Plu.Pel.4

ἐπικαταρρήγνυμι.definition: tear, rend, J.AJ2.6.7:—Pass; Pass., to be violently purged, Gal.16.691

ἐπικατασκάπτω.definition: destroy, D.H.1.39; throw down upon, Id.4.48; J.AJ13.13.3; destroy as well, App.Ill.8, al

ἐπικατασκευάζω.definition: bring about in addition, J.BJ4.3.3; Med., establish by additional arguments, Arg.D.46

ἐπικατασπάω.definition: draw down after, Arist.Pr.901a2:—Pass., to be drawn in afterwards, Hp.Vict.3.70

ἐπικατασπένδω.definition: pour besides as a libation over, J.BJ1.3.6

ἐπικατάστασις.definition: in Tactics, wheeling through four right angles and return to original point, Ascl.Tact.10.1, 9

ἐπικαταστρέφω.definition: invert and put over, Gp.10.56.6, cf. Dsc.5.79; Sch.S.Ant.134

ἐπικατασφάζω.definition: later Phld.Ir.p.36; slay in succession or after, D.H.3.20, App.Hann.59, al

ἐπικατατέμνω.definition: carry the workings of a mine beyond one's boundaries, D.37.36

ἐπικαταφέρω.definition: fell, knock down on top of; Pass., of stars, follow the sun, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.22, Anon. in Ptol.Tetr.22; name of eighth Thrasyll.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.101

ἐπικαταφορά.definition: Astrol., name of eighth Firm.2.19.9, 7.6.8, al.; cf. II

ἐπικατάφορος.definition: prone to, or Terpsicles ap.Ath.9.391e, Ath.13.608d

ἐπικαταχρίω.definition: in Med., smear oneself with, Orib.Fr.85

ἐπικαταψεύδομαι.definition: tell lies besides, Hdt.3.63, Th.8.74; accuse falsely, J.AJ17.5.5

ἐπικάτειμι.definition: go down into, Th.2.49: abs., of persons, J.AJ1.19.3: metaph., descend in the scale, Dam.Pr.87

ἐπικατεράω.definition: pour off liquid on a thing, Heras ap.Gal.13.39, Orib.Fr.88

ἐπικατέχω.definition: detain, D.H.9.60, Luc.Herm.23, Arg. Cratin. in POxy.663.39; restrain, D.Chr.3.34

ἐπικατηγορέω.definition: predicate of a thing besides, S.E.M.9.334; attribute to . . , Plu.2.1113b; D.H.1.66 :—Pass., to be added to the predicate, Arist.APr.49a25; to be predicated of, c. dat., Iamb.in Nic.p.34P

ἐπικατηγορία.definition: further predication or characterization, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.41 F., al., cf. S.E.M.10.297

ἐπικατορύσσομαι.definition: Pass., to be buried after, Antipho3.2.10

ἐπικαττύω.definition: mend shoes, Poll.7.82; metaph., vamp up old plays, Com.Adesp.46

ἐπίκαυμα.definition: blister caused by a burn, A; ulcer on the eye, esp. the cornea, Gal.12.758, 14.774, 19.434

ἐπίκαυσις.definition: burning, Str.13.4.11; inflammation of the surface, scorching up, joined with Pl.Ax.368c

ἐπίκειμαι.definition: serving as Pass. to to be laid; of doors, to be put to or closed , Od.6.19: metaph., Thgn.421

ἐπικείρω.definition: Ep. aor. 1 cut off, cut down; metaph., cut short, baffle, Il.15.467, cf. 16.120

ἐπικελαδέω.definition: shout at or to, esp.in applause, cheer, Il.8.542

ἐπικελεύω.definition: exhort, encourage, cheer on, c. dat; give consent or authorization, PPetr.3p.133 , PTeb.201

ἐπικέλλω.definition: aor. 1 also Act.Ap.27.41; abs., run ashore, Od.9.138; A.R.3.575: c.acc., Id.2.352; also of the ship itself, Od.13.114; of a fish, rush into the net, Numen. ap. Ath.7.321b

ἐπικέλομαι.definition: call upon, Il.9.454; A.Supp.40 : c. dat., A.R.3.85

ἐπικεντρίζω.definition: apply the spur, AP9.777; graft vines, Gp.5.17.11

ἐπικεντρόομαι.definition: Astron., occupy a cardinal point, cj. for Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.115

ἐπίκεντρος.definition: Astron., occupying a cardinal point, Vett.Val.9.19, Man.1.34, Doroth.ap.Heph.Astr.2.5, S.E.M.5.40: Comp., Ptol.Tetr.79

ἐπικέντρωσις.definition: occupation of a cardinal point, Paul.Al.P.1

ἐπικεράννυμι.definition: mix in addition, mix fresh wine, Od.7.164, cf. Gal.18.169:—Med., Damocr. ap. eund.14.100

ἐπικερδής.definition: profitable, advantageous, TAM2.245 , Aesop.137, Vett.Val.189.30, al., Heph.Astr.2.30, App.BC1.57

ἐπικερτομέω.definition: mock, used by Hom. only in part; c. acc., he reproached him, Hdt.8.92; for a thing, Agath.5.22; tease, banter, Theoc.20.2, cf. Luc.Bis Acc.12

ἐπικεύθω.definition: conceal, hide, always with a neg., Il.5.816; Od.5.143; . . 15.263; 4.744, cf. 17.141: and in A.Ag.800 , c. acc., I will not hide it from thee, cf. A.R.3.332

ἐπικεφάλαιος.definition: of or for the head, Suid; Subst. = Arist.Oec.1346a4, POxy.1157.14 ; SIG1009.4

ἐπικεφαλαιόω.definition: add up, Vett.Val.260.21:— Med., sum up; Pass., to be summed up, D.C.52.28

ἐπικεφάλιον.definition: poll-tax, IGRom.4.181 , IG12.724.11, POxy.1438.14 , : more freq. in pl., Cic.Att.5.16.2, BGU833, Wilcken Chr.28 , POxy.2131.10 , etc

ἐπικέφαλον.definition: head of battering-ram, Ath.Mech.23.8; money distributed at so much a head, head-money, IG12.946.22 ; = Hsch

ἐπικηδεύω.definition: form connexions by; bury, Hsch. s.v

ἐπικήδομαι.definition: take thought for, Nonn.D.7.60: c. inf., Steph.in Hp.1.157 D

ἐπικηραίνω.definition: to be hostile to one, Hsch

ἐπικηρόω.definition: wax over, rub with wax, Polyaen.2.20

ἐπικηρυκεία.definition: sending an embassy to treat for peace, entering into negotiation, D.5.18, cf. Plb.14.2.13, Theopomp.Hist.209

ἐπικηρυκεύομαι.definition: send ambassadors to treat for peace, make proposals for a treaty of peace, to one, Ar.Th.336, Th.4.27; Hdt.4.80,6.97; Ar.Th.1163

ἐπικήρυξις.definition: proclamation of a reward, Ulp.ad; generally, proclamation, Ph.Bel.98.36

ἐπικηρύσσω.definition: esp. of penalties, . . proclaim death as the penalty, X.HG1.1.15; set a price on his head, Hdt.7.214 ; D.I.c.; issue letters of marque, Plb.4.26.7:—Pass., . . Hdt.7.213; the price set upon one's head, Nymphod.12, cf. …

ἐπικίδνημι.definition: spread over, spread a brave spirit over your ills, Orac. ap. Hdt.7.140:-in Hom. always Pass. , is spread over the earth, Il.2.850, cf. A.R.2.978; far as the morning light is spread, Il.7.451,458; Q.S.5.347

ἐπικίνδυνος.definition: in danger, insecure; dangerous, Gorg.Pal.4 ; Pl.R.467d; Phld.Ir.p.29 W.; Pl.Lg.736c, cf. X.Mem.4.6.10; Id.An.1.3.19; to one, Hp.Aph.4.16, Th.3.54; there is danger, Arist.HA588a10

ἐπικινέω.definition: Act.only as f.l. for or , Iamb.VP 3.17:—Pass., to be moved, Luc.Asin.6; gesticulate at a thing. v.l. Epict.Ench.33.10: metaph., to be moved, zealous, LXX1 Es.8.69; also, to be moved to passion, Phld.Piet.21

ἐπικίρνημι.definition: Ion. for Heraclit.All.35, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.8:—Pass., Hdt.1.51, Plu.2.270a, cf. Heraclit.All.40

ἐπικλάζω.definition: sound to, Opp.H.5.295; made thunder sound in answer to him, Pi.P.4.23

ἐπικλαίω.definition: weep in answer, Ar.Th.1063; at a thing, Nonn.D.30.114

ἐπικλείω.definition: Ep. Att. shut to, close, Ar.Pax101 ; Tryph.200:-Med., Luc.Tox.50:-Pass., to be shut to, opp. X.Eq.12.6: c. dat., to be covered by . . , Gal.18.429

ἐπικλῄζω.definition: = 3, Orph.A.1359, cf. Poet.deherb.154:—Pass., Poet. ap. D.L.6.100, App.Syr.17

ἐπικληρόω.definition: Dor. assign by lot; have assigned one by lot, D.C.37.50

ἐπικλήρωσις.definition: assignment by lot, SIG333.29 , Milet.3 No. 143.31

ἐπίκλησις.definition: surname, additional name; used by; after Hom., in other cases, surname, name, Th.1.3, etc

ἐπίκλητος.definition: called upon, called in as ally; specially summoned, held a privy council, Hdt.7.8 ; privy councillors, among the Persians, Hdt.8.101, 9.42; committee of a council, SIG353.2 , Str.14.1.21

ἐπικλίνεια.definition: inclination, bend, Heliod. ap; tendency, Gal.17 .726

ἐπικλινής.definition: prone, inclined, Them.Or.15.187b; Ph.1.252. Adv. ib.37,al

ἐπικλίντης.definition: moving sideways, earthquakes that move at acute angles, Arist.Mu.396a1 Lyd.Ost.53 codd.)

ἐπίκλιντρον.definition: couch, arm-chair, Ar.Ec.907; back of a couch or chair, IG11 .144 A 66, B 8 , Gp.13.14.9

ἐπικλίνω.definition: put to, shut a door: hence, in Pass., once; bend towards, prick the ears, X.Cyn.6.15; lean against . . , Paus.9.30.10; Philostr.Her.19.11; pull it open, Arist.PA660b22:—Pass., spars leaning on the wall and inclined at…

ἐπίκλισις.definition: slope, Str.1.3.7; inclination towards, Antip. ap.Stob.4.22.25, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.175

ἐπικλονέω.definition: urge violently on, A.R.3.687; Q.S.8.426:— Pass., rush like a tide upon, of persons, A.R.1.783; of storms, Q.S.14.501

ἐπίκλοπος.definition: thievish, tricky, wily; c.gen., cunning in speech, Il.22.281; cunning in archery, Od.21.397

ἐπικλύζω.definition: Aeschin.3.173:—overflow, flood; metaph., deluge, swamp, E.Tr.1327 , cf. Theoc.25.201; A.R.3.695; Ph.1.91; Luc.Pseudol.25; Lib.Decl.50.44; Jul.Or.1.8b:—Pass., Id.ad Them.257c

ἐπίκλυσις.definition: overflow, flood, Th.3.89; Thphr.Fr.171.11: pl., Them.Or.13.167b

ἐπικλύω.definition: listen to, hear, c. acc., Il.23.652, cf. A.R.3.598; S.Ichn.39: c.gen., Od.5.150, cf. A.R.1.1240, Eratosth.19

ἐπικλώθω.definition: spin upon, Hermipp.48; elsewh; spin to one, assign, prop. of the Fates who spun the thread of destiny; also of all powers which influence men's fortunes, Od.3.208, cf.4.208, etc.; Callin.1.9, cf. Them.Or.32.356d:—Med.…

ἐπικνάω.definition: scrape or grate over; scratch, Hld.2.8

ἐπικνίζω.definition: scratch the surface, Thphr.HP4.2.1, CP5.2.4 ; of the plough, AP6.238

ἐπίκοιλος.definition: porous, spongy, Hp.VC1 ; cj. for in Sor.1.122

ἐπικοιμάομαι.definition: fall asleep after a thing, Hp.Aph.5.27; overlay, LXX3 Ki.3.19; J.AJ8.2.2

ἐπίκοινος.definition: common to many, promiscuous; Gramm., common, of gender, D.T.634.19, Gell.13.7.3. Adv. A.D.Conj.253.20

ἐπικοινόω.definition: Med., share, ib.1.4:— Pass., to be shared with, Pl.Lg.631d

ἐπικοινωνέω.definition: communicate with, Hp.Prog.7; share in a thing with one, what letters has it in common? Pl.Cra.394c; having nothing in common with . . , Aeschin.3.44: generally, share in, c.gen., Ph.1.561

ἐπικοίτιος.definition: at bedtime, of self- examination, Hierocl.in CA19p.460M

ἐπικόλλημα.definition: that which is glued on, tessellated work, Id.HP4.3.4

ἐπικομίζω.definition: bring or carry to, Str.11.2.17, cf. Arist. ap. D.L.5.14 :—Med., bring with one, J.AJ2.15.2; D.C.50.11, cf. PLips.41.10

ἐπικομπάζω.definition: add boastingly, E.HF981; Plu.Cam.22: abs., boast, Ph.1.550

ἐπικόπανον.definition: chopping-block, billet, Men.33, IG11.199 B89 , Poll.10.101

ἐπικοπή.definition: cutting close, pollarding, of trees; cutting down, felling, fall by a single blow, D.C.38.50, 49.29

ἐπίκοπος.definition: of coins, re-stamped, EM360.41, Hsch; Act., for cutting: as Subst., = Luc.DMort.10.9, Eust.1476.33; support for cutting upon, in surgery, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.23.66, Antyll.ib.18, Gal.2.685

ἐπικόπτω.definition: pf. Phld.D.1.15:—strike upon (i.e; later, of trees, lop, pollard, Thphr.CP5.17.3; cut down brushwood, PLond.3.1170B26 : metaph., cut short, bring down from high estate, Arist.Pol.1284b2; Plu.2.529b; check, impede, ib.…

ἐπικορρίζω.definition: strike or peck on the head, Arist.HA614a10

ἐπικορύφωσις.definition: culmination, terminal number of an arithmetical series, Nicom.Ar.2.3

ἐπικοσμέω.definition: add ornaments to, decorate after or besides, Hdt.1.184; adorn, Hyp.Eux.24,25; IG22.1277; Arist.PA658a32; honour them with . . , Hdt.7.228; honour, celebrate, Ar.Ra.385; of funeral honours, X.Cyr.7.3.11: abs., Demetr.E…

ἐπικόσμησις.definition: adornment, decoration; perfecting of matter by form, Syrian.in Metaph.38.21

ἐπίκοτος.definition: wrathful, vengeful, Pi.Fr.109.4; Pass., hateful, S.Fr.428

ἐπικοτταβίζω.definition: throw the cottabus on or at, Poll.6.110, prob.f.l. for

ἐπικουρέω.definition: to be an act as an ally, once in; serve as allies or mercenaries, Isoc.4.168; Pl.R.575b

ἐπικούρημα.definition: protection, X.An.4.5.13; remedy, Gal.6.171: pl., aids, succours, Iamb.Protr.20

ἐπικούρησις.definition: succour, protection, Antipho Soph.Oxy.1364.158; Euryph. ap. Stob.4.39.27; against evils, E.Andr.28; Pl.Lg.919b

ἐπικουρία.definition: Ion. aid, succour; position of the , Pl.R.415c

ἐπίκουρος.definition: helper, ally, Hom. only in Il., mostly; mercenary troops, opp. citizen-soldiers, Th.2.33, cf. Hdt.1.154, 2.163, 3.145, Lys.12.94, X.HG7.1.12, etc.; Hermipp.63.18; used as body-guard by tyrants, Hdt.1.64, 6.39, Th.6.55,58

ἐπικουφίζω.definition: lighten a ship by throwing out part of its; lift up, support, S.Aj.1411 ; lift up the soil, X.Oec.17.13

ἐπικραδαίνω.definition: wave on high, Hld.3.1; quiver, Poll.5.61

ἐπικράζω.definition: shout to or at, Luc.Anach.16 : aor. 1 inf. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.1

ἐπικραίνω.definition: Ep. 3sg. fut. dub. in A.Ag.1340 codd.: aor. 1 Ep. :—Med., 3pl. aor. 1 Q.S.14.297:—bring to pass, accomplish, may he fulfil it, Il.15.599; he fulfilled it not for them,3.302, cf. 2.419 ; grant me this prayer, fulfil it…

ἐπικρανίς.definition: membrane of the brain, Erasistr. ap. Placit.4.5.3, dub. in Gal.2.728

ἐπικρανῖτις.definition: pl. top course of a wall, IG12.372.16, al

ἐπίκρανον.definition: that which is put on the head, head-

ἐπικράτεια.definition: predominance, in heredity, Placit.5.7.6; S.E.P.1.80; named from its dominant element, opp. Gal.15.74, cf. 5.672, 17.216; Placit.4.9.9: Gramm., prevalence, authority, A.D.Synt.256.26, al.; numerical superiority, ib.326.14

ἐπικρατέω.definition: prevail in battle, be victorious, [to them] though they are victorious as it is, Il.14.98, cf. Ar.Lys.767; conquer or die, Hdt.7.104; Id.1.173; gain the advantage in most points in the war, Th.4.19

ἐπικρατής.definition: master of a thing: only Comp. superior in . . , Th.6.88; having the upper hand of . . , D.C.55.30; Memn.34.3; with success, D.S.37.2.—Hom. only in Adv. with overwhelming might, impetuously, Il.16.67,81,23.863 ; so Hes…

ἐπικράτησις.definition: mastering, conquest of; supreme power, D.C.47.21

ἐπικρατήτωρ.definition: ruling star, Ps.-Ptol.Centil.25, cf. Vett.Val.132.15, etc

ἐπικραυγάζω.definition: cry out to or at, Arr.Epict.1.21.3,4.1.19

ἐπικρεμάννυμι.definition: Pass., aor. overhang, of a rock, h.Ap.284; Plu.Publ.10: metaph., hang over, threaten, Simon.39.3; Pi.I.8.14 ; Th.2.53; impending danger, Id.7.75, cf.3.40: c.dat.pers., A.R.3.483; Ep.3pl. impf. Nonn.D.20.173

ἐπίκριμα.definition: = Lat. decretum, OGI453.23 , 669.28 ; Epist. ap. J.AJ19.6.3

ἐπικρίνω.definition: c.acc.pers., judge, Ph.2.380:—Pass., ib.309; select, pick out, D.S.1.75; distinguish, esteem, Hp.Jusj

ἐπίκρισις.definition: verification, Gal.17.354, cf. 1.117; in Egypt, revision of lists and selection of privileged persons, POxy.288.35 , PFay.27.24 , BGU324.2,19 , etc

ἐπικριτής.definition: adjudicator, arbiter; in Egypt, examining magistrate , PFay.27.3 , PTeb.320.2

ἐπίκριτος.definition: approved, J.BJ3.5.5; oxyt., capable of determination or resolution, S.E.P.1.170

ἐπικροτέω.definition: rattle on or over; c. acc., strike with a rattling sound, clash, Alciphr.1.12; Luc.Syr.D.44; Opp.C.2.244

ἐπίκροτος.definition: beaten or trodden hard, esp. of ground, X.Eq.Mag.3.14; Arist.HA558a6: metaph., their sonorousness, Philostr.VS1.25.7

ἐπίκρουσις.definition: treatment with rods as counter-; medical percussion, Paul.Aeg.3.69,6.51

ἐπικρούστιον.definition: a surgical instrument, perh. slasher, Hermes 38.282

ἐπικρύπτω.definition: poet. aor. 2 Q.S.7.235 :—throw a cloak over, conceal, A.Eu.317 ; Pl.Cra.421b; f.l.for E.Supp.296:—freq. in Med., disguise, S.Fr.88.12 ; . . E.Fr.553; Pl.La.196b, cf. Prt.346b; D.17.17: abs., with concealment or secrec…

ἐπίκρυφος.definition: unknown, inglorious, Pi.O.8.69, Max.21; concealed, Plu.Arat.10

ἐπίκρυψις.definition: concealment, Str.2.3.8, Plu.Nic.23; latencies, quiescences, Aret.CD1.5

ἐπικρώζω.definition: caw or croak at, Orac. ap. Ar.Eq.1051; . . Them.Or.4.61d

ἐπικτάομαι.definition: gain or win besides, A.Eu.901; Hdt.2.79; extend one's empire, Th.1.144; Id.4.61; add to those you have, X.HG7.1.3; as an ally, A.Eu.671; S.Ant.846 ; acquire additional property, PGiss.108.3 , etc.:—late in Pass., Agat…

ἐπικτείνω.definition: kill besides or again, slay the slain anew, S.Ant.1030; f.l. for Plu.Caes.46

ἐπίκτησις.definition: further acquisition, fresh gain, S.Ph.1344; Arist.HA522a18: pl., D.H.9.53

ἐπίκτητος.definition: gained besides or in addition, acquired land, which was formerly under water, as the Delta of Egypt, Hdt.2.5, cf. 10; property added to one's hereditary property, Pl.Lg.924a, cf. Lycurg.48; a foreign wife , or newly a…

ἐπικτίζω.definition: found in addition or anew, Str.14.1.12; found in or among, Plu.2.328b codd

ἐπικτυπέω.definition: aor. 1 : aor. 2 A.R.1.1136:—make a noise upon, stamp on the ground with the feet, Ar.Ec.483; clashed on their shields with . ., A.R. l.c.; Id.2.1081; strike, Nonn.D.38.397: abs., re-echo, respond, Ar.Av.780; of a chor…

ἐπικυδής.definition: only in Comp. , glorious, distinguished, X.HG5.1.36; brilliant, successful, Isoc.4.139; Plb.16.4.3; and of persons, more sanguine, Id.5.69.11, cf. Ph.1.252, al., Onos.23.2. Adv. Comp. Plb.5.23.2

ἐπικυέω.definition: simply, become pregnant again, BGU1058.30 , al

ἐπικύησις.definition: superfetation, Id.Fr.259,260 Bonitz; title of treatise by Hp

ἐπικυΐσκομαι.definition: become doubly pregnant, i.e. pregnant again before the first foetus is born, Hdt.3.108, Hp.Superf.1, Arist.GA773b28

ἐπικυκλέω.definition: intr., come round in turn upon, S.Tr.130:—Pass., D.H.Rh.10.17

ἐπικύκλησις.definition: return in a cycle, Alex.Aphr.de An.30.26

ἐπικύκλιος.definition: circular: , a round Sicilian cake, Epich.26 codd. Ath.; of a bandage, in a circle, Gal.18.820

ἐπίκυκλος.definition: Astron., epicycle, Plu.2.1028b, Theo Sm.p.162H., Ptol.Alm.3.3, Iamb.VP6.31 , etc

ἐπικυλινδέω.definition: Pass., to be applied by rolling, Gal.11.757; Pass., degenerate, Id.19.560: metaph., Dam.Pr.88

ἐπικυλινδρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be flattened by rollers, Thphr.CP5.6.7

ἐπικυλλόω.definition: mould a cake of dough, prob. for Hsch

ἐπικυμαίνω.definition: flow in waves over; trans., cause to rise in waves, J.AJ4.3.2

ἐπικυματίζω.definition: float upon the waves, Ph.1.455, Ael.Ep.18: metaph., , Ph.1.553; also of persons, Id.2.300; of a runner, Philostr.Her.2.3:— Pass., Phld.Mort.33; opp. Id.Rh.2.55S

ἐπικύπτω.definition: pf. :—bend oneself over, stoop over, bow down, Hp.Art.52, Ar.Th.239; Arist.HA522b18; of the horn of the moon, Thphr.Sign.27; stoop down to get something, X.Cyr.2.3.18; pore over a book, Luc.Herm.2; lean upon, Id.DMort…

ἐπικυρόω.definition: confirm, sanction, ratify, Th.3.71, cf.S.El.793, X.An.3.2.32, D.15.34, SIG167.20, etc.: c.inf., . . E.Or.862:—Pass., Th.5.45; Arist.Ath.37.1, cf. Sammelb. 1161.17

ἐπικυρτόω.definition: bend forward, Hes.Sc.234:—Pass., to be arched, Luc.Am.14

ἐπικύρω.definition: Ep. impf. Ep. aor. 1 and :—light upon, fall in with, c. dat., Il.3.23; Hes.Op.755; kept always touching his neck with . . , Il.23.821; let his sword touch her neck, Q.S.13.394; Pi.P.10.21: c. gen., meet with, obtain, …

ἐπικύρωσις.definition: ratification, confirmation, Arist.Ath.41.3, cf. D.H.9.51, Just.Nov.42.1.1

ἐπικωκύω.definition: lament over, S.El.283; ib.805: abs., Hld.1.13

ἐπικωλύω.definition: hinder, check, X.Oec.8.4; . . S.Ph.1242; IG7.3073.35 ; ib.45: abs., to be a hindrance, Th.6.17:—Pass., PPetr.3p.109 , etc

ἐπικωμάζω.definition: rush on or in with a party of revellers, Plb.26.1.4, Call.Epigr.43: generally, make a riotous assault, Ar.Ach.982; Men.881; go careering about, Pl.Lg.950a; Plu.2.772f: metaph., Chor.in Jahrb.9.177:—Pass., to be visite…

ἐπικώμιος.definition: of, at, or for a or festal procession, Pi.P.10.6, N.8.50; epith. of Apollo, IGRom.4.1539 ; = praises, Pi.N.6.32: sg., revel, Gloss

ἐπικωμῳδέω.definition: make a jest of, caricature, Pl.Ap.31d

ἐπίκωπος.definition: at the oar, rower, Men.Eph. ap; of a boat, furnished with oars, Moschio ap.Ath.5.208f, cf. D.H.3.44, D.S.3.40; phaselus epicopus, dispatch-boat, Cic. Att.14.16.1, cf. 5.11.4

ἐπιλαγχάνω.definition: pf. :—succeed another in an; obtain, have allotted to one, Ph.1.629, al

ἐπιλάζυμαι.definition: hold tight, stop, i.e. to be silent, E.Andr.250.—Poet. word for

ἐπιλαλέω.definition: interrupt in speaking, Sm.Ps.122.4; charm , LXXJe.8.17

ἐπιλαμβάνω.definition: take or get besides; simply, take, receive, PEleph.10.1 , OGI179.18 , etc

ἐπιλαμπρύνω.definition: make splendid, adorn; of sound, make loud and clear, raise high, Id.Comp.14; of frogs, Plu.2.912c

ἐπιλάμπω.definition: shine after or thereupon; shine upon , abs., Hp.Aër.6, X.Cyn.8.1: c.dat., Plu.Fab.6; Id.Arat.22, cf. Theo Sm.p.121H.: metaph., . . AP5.16 ; bring them new light; OGI194.20 , cf. ib.669.7

ἐπίλαμψις.definition: shining, of heavenly bodies, Ph.1.24, al.; Id.2.7 ; illumination, Iamb.Myst.5.26, also cj. for in Hp.Epid.6.1.4

ἐπιλαρχία.definition: double i.e. two or 128 horse, Ascl.Tact.7.11, Arr.Tact.18.2

ἐπιλεαίνω.definition: smooth over, Plu.2.74d; chew, Ph.1.63, al.: metaph., ib.180

ἐπιλέανσις.definition: chewing small, rumination, ib.254: metaph., ib.115

ἐπιλέγω.definition: say in connexion with an action, etc; call by name, Hdt.5.70; Pl.Lg.700b:—Med., A.Supp.49 :— Pass., to be surnamed, J.AJ13.10.4

ἐπιλείβω.definition: also pour wine over a thing, Il.1.462; A.R.1.1133: abs., Od.3.341

ἐπιλείπω.definition: leave untouched, Pl.Prt.310e: c.part., Id.Phlb.26b, cf. 52d; of things, fail one, c.acc. pers., . ., Thgn.1131; Hdt.7.21, cf. 2.174; so Id.2.25; Ar.Av.1106; Th.5.103: c.inf., Antipho5.17; time would fail me, Isoc.1.11…

ἐπιλεκτάρχης.definition: commander of a picked band, Plu.Arat.32:— hence SIG421.18

ἐπίλεκτος.definition: chosen, Ph.1.242; esp. of soldiers, X.An.3.4.43, HG5.3.23, IG22.680.12, IPE12.352.39 ; in Egypt, OGI731 , UPZ110.21

ἐπιλεπτύνω.definition: smear over with a thin coat; sift finely, Hsch. s.v

ἐπιλευκαίνω.definition: to be whitish. Arist.PA676a32; of a plant, Thphr.HP3.12.9, etc

ἐπίλευκος.definition: white on the surface, whitish, Thphr.HP3.7.5

ἐπιλεύσσω.definition: look towards or at, one can only see so far before one, Il.3.12

ἐπιλήγω.definition: end in or at, J.BJ3.9.3, cf. 3.10.7; prob.l., ib.3.3.4

ἐπίληθος.definition: causing to forget, c.gen., . ., Od.4.221 ; Ael.NA15.19, cf.4.41

ἐπιλήθω.definition: cause to forget; Med., or more commonly Aeol. and Dor. Alc.Supp.25.6, S.El.146 , fut. aor. 2 Pl.Ap.17a: late aor. 1 Nonn.D.48.969: with pf. Act. Hdt.3.46, Pi.O. , but more freq. E.Ba.188, Ar.Nu.631, Lys.26.1, Pl.Phd.7…

ἐπιληκέω.definition: clap the hands in applause, or beat time to the dancers, Od.8.379

ἐπιληπτίζω.definition: have an epileptic fit, Plu.2.290b:—Pass., Alex.Trall.1.15

ἐπίληπτος.definition: Ion. caught or detected in; culpable, censurable, Ph.2.348; Id.2.4, al., cf. Porph.Chr.23; of errors in metre, Heph.4.6

ἐπιλησμονή.definition: forgetfulness, Cratin.410 ap.Sch.Ar.Nu.788, LXXSi.11.27; Ep.Jac.1.25:—also , Hsch., and Alex.315

ἐπιλησμοσύνη.definition: = foreg., Cratin.410 ap.Suid. , IG12.561 , Archig. ap. Gal.8.149, D.C.56.41

ἐπιλήσμων.definition: gen. apt to forget, forgetful; Act., causing forgetfulness, ChioEp.3.6

ἐπιλήψιμος.definition: reprehensible, Luc.Rh.Pr.22; liable to seizure, Polem.Call.34

ἐπίληψις.definition: taking hold of, clasping; in Law, claiming property by seizing, Pl.Lg.954e

ἐπιλιμπάνω.definition: = Gramm., to be wanting, of a tense, An. Ox.4.393, etc

ἐπιλινευτής.definition: one who catches with nets, prob. in AP6.93

ἐπιλιχμάω.definition: lick up, Babr.48.6:—Med., lick up, devour, Ph.1.550: metaph., ib.305, cf. 527

ἐπιλλίζω.definition: make signs to one by winking; blink, when drowsy, Nic.Th.163

ἐπιλόγευσις.definition: levying of arrears of taxation, PRev.Laws 19.12 . etc

ἐπιλογεύω.definition: levy arrears of taxation, ib.6.1 , PPetr. 3p.69 , etc

ἐπιλογή.definition: picking out, choice, Lysim. ap. J.Ap.1.34, cf. Cod.Just.1.5.16.2; selection, Plb.7.16.7, etc.; SimonEq.tit.; Ps.-Ptol.Centil.6

ἐπιλογίζομαι.definition: Att. fut. Pl.Ax.365b: aor; address the peroration, Theodect. ap.Rh.7.33 W

ἐπιλογισμός.definition: reckoning, calculation; description, account, Apollod.Poliorc.138.13 , Erasistr. ap. Gal.8.317

ἐπίλογος.definition: reasoning, inference, only Ion; peroration of a speech, Arist.Rh.1414b12, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.96, Phld.Rh.1.202 S., Longin.12.5, etc

ἐπιλοιδορέω.definition: cast reproaches on, cj. in Plb.15.33.4:—Med., Suid. s.v

ἐπιλύζω.definition: Ep. have the hiccough besides, Nic.Al.81

ἐπιλυπέω.definition: trouble, annoy, offend besides, v.l. in Hdt.9.50, LXX2 Ma.8.32:—Pass., to be troubled at, . . S.E.M.11.127

ἐπίλυπος.definition: sad, Ph.2.29; in low; painful, Arist.EN1117a34; a thing that causes pain, ib.1110b19; Plu.2.13a. Adv. D.S.17.118

ἐπίλυσις.definition: solution, S.E.P.2.246; explanation, 2 Ep.Pet.1.20, Vett. Val.172.3 , Hld.1.18, 4.9, Iamb.Protr.21

ἐπιλύω.definition: loose, untie, Theoc.Adon.42; let; solve, explain, Ev.Marc.4.34:—Pass.,S.E.P.2.246, Sch.Od.9.106:—Med., J.AJ8.6.5, Vett.Val.259.4, Ath.10.45of, al.: pf. part. Pass. lucid, of writings, Vett.Val.329.25

ἐπιλωβεύω.definition: make mockery of a thing, Od.2.323

ἐπιμαίνω.definition: make madly in love with, Anon. ap; Pass., with aor. 2. but also aor.1 Med. Il.6.160, AP6.309 , Luc.Syr.D.21: pf. be mad after, c.dat., Il. l.c., cf. Anacr.3, Mosch.Fr.2.2,Plu.Brut.5; Call.Cer.30; Ar.V.744 , cf. 1469 ,…

ἐπιμαίομαι.definition: c. acc., lay hold of, grasp, he clutched his sword-hilt, Od.11.531; . . ib.591; having clutched [the sword] with my hand, 9.302, cf. 19.480; took her by the hand, A.R.3.106

ἐπιμανθάνω.definition: learn besides or after, opp. Th.1.138: c.inf., Hdt.1.131; . . Id.2.160

ἐπιμαντεύομαι.definition: prophesy, c. acc. et inf., App.BC4.127; ib.138, Philostr.VA5.19

ἐπιμαρτυρέω.definition: bear witness to a thing, depose to; bear witness in favour of, Phld.Oec.p.57J

ἐπιμαρτύρησις.definition: confirmation, corroboration; Astrol., supporting by aspect, Paul.Al.O.4, Ptol.Tetr.200

ἐπιμαρτυρητής.definition: one who calls to witness, Gloss

ἐπιμαρτυρία.definition: a calling to witness; supporting by aspect, Man.2.400 , cf. 3.314 , al

ἐπιμαρτύρομαι.definition: call to witness, appeal to, in case; call on earnestly, conjure, Th.6.29

ἐπιμασάομαι.definition: chew, Alciphr.3.51; chew after other food, Gp.12.30.9:—Pass., Dsc.3.45

ἐπιμαστίω.definition: whip or beat besides, Nonn.D.1.80, al

ἐπιμαχέω.definition: stand by, help one in battle, for the mutual defence of their countries, Th.5.27

ἐπιμαχία.definition: defensive alliance, opp. , Id.1.44, 5.48, D.12.7: metaph. of the state, Arist.Pol.1280b27

ἐπιμάχομαι.definition: fight after, act as a reserve, Ael.Tact.17, Arr.Tact.15.5

ἐπίμαχος.definition: that may easily be attacked; contended for, contested, Hld.8.1

ἐπιμείγνυμι.definition: and add by mixing; intr., mingle with others, have intercourse or dealings, Th.1.2; X.An.3.5.16; Hld.6.13; come to it, Id.5.33; Philostr.VA5.24:—Pass., Hp.Morb.1.11; X.Cyr.7.4.5; Th.2.1: abs., Id.1.146; also join them…

ἐπιμειδάω.definition: smile at or upon, in Hom. always in phrase, he addressed him with a smile, Il.4.356, al.; in 10.400, of a scornful smile; but Hes.Th.547: c.dat., AP6.345

ἐπιμειλίσσομαι.definition: placate, J.BJ1.20.3:—Act., aor. 1 inf. prob. for Hsch

ἐπιμείρομαι.definition: to be assigned by fate, Vett.Val.346.6

ἐπιμελαίνομαι.definition: to become black on the surface, a; of fruit, blacken in ripening, Thphr.HP3.15.6

ἐπιμέλεια.definition: written IG22.483.24; a commission or charge, Aeschin.3.13, Arist.Pol.1299a20 ; ib.1322b18, cf. ib.30 ; a special office at Athens, Din.3.15; so = POxy.281.2

ἐπιμελέομαι.definition: also Hdt.1.98, 2.2,174,al; of public commissions, have charge of, be inspector or curator of, Lys.7.29; X.Cyr.8.1.14; Id.An.4.8.25; CIG4011 : c.acc. cogn., Pl.Lg.812e:—in Att. Inscrr., is usual of a definite commissio…

ἐπιμελής.definition: careful or anxious about; abs., careful, attentive, Ar.Nu.501, X.Mem.2.6.38, etc.: Comp. S.Fr.472, cf. X.An.3.2.30: Sup., Isoc.4.142; Men.223.9. Adv. carefully, X.Mem.2.4.2, Pl.Ti.88c, Men.Pk.32, etc.; Ion. Hp.Art.55;…

ἐπιμελητεία.definition: office of IG22.1338.30 ; term of such office, SIG825 A5

ἐπιμελητεύω.definition: to be an PTeb.61.71 , IG3.393, SIG829 A 7 , 855.6 , etc

ἐπιμελητής.definition: one who has charge of a thing; military commander, Plb.3.79.4

ἐπιμελῳδέω.definition: sing over or at a person, Aristid.Or.29.30

ἐπίμεμπτος.definition: = sq., of persons or actions; blaming, Sch.S.Tr.446. Adv. Arg.Aeschin.3

ἐπιμέμφομαι.definition: cast blame upon, c.dat. pers; c. acc. rei, impute as matter of blame, Hdt.1.75, cf. 2.161, etc

ἐπιμένω.definition: stay on, tarry, abs., Il.19.142, Od.17.277; 11.351; do you wait, and I will put on my armour, Il.6.340; also . . . . Od.4.587; . . h.Cer.160, Ar.Nu.196; so . . X.An.5.5.2: after Hom., remain in a place, And.1.75, etc.…

ἐπιμερής.definition: superpartient, of numbers of the form 1+2/x, 1+3/x, etc., Theo Sm.p.76H., Nicom.Ar.1.17, al.; cf

ἐπιμερίζω.definition: impart, give a portion, v.l. in LXXJb.31.2; Astrol., assign a number of years to life, Vett. Val.164.9

ἐπιμερισμός.definition: distribution, Hsch.s.v; Astrol., assignment, Vett. Val. 97.9, Critodem.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.102.4

ἐπιμερότης.definition: the quality of being Iamb.in Nic.pp.44.70P

ἐπιμεσόω.definition: to be at the middle, dub.l. in LXXJe.15.9

ἐπιμετρέω.definition: add to the measure, give over and above, Plu.Lys.4, cf. Alex.42; Luc.DMort.5.1; prolong one's magistracy, Plu.Comp.Ages.Pomp.3, etc.; add, in speaking, Plb.28.17.2, etc.: c. gen. partit., add some jests, Luc.Nav.19; a…

ἐπίμετρον.definition: something added to make good measure excess, Theoc.12.26, PTeb.91.11 ; make an increase, Thphr.CP4.13.7, Plu.2.676b; ib.503d; into the bargain, Plb.6.46.6; S.E.P.2.47, cf. Gal.8.493

ἐπιμήδομαι.definition: imagine or contrive a thing against one, Od.4.437, cf. Q.S.14.479

ἐπιμηθεύομαι.definition: think of afterwards or too late, Eust.67.27:— also Corn.ND18

ἐπιμηνάω.definition: 3pl. pf. = they have been content to wait, Schwyzer91.11

ἐπιμηνιεύω.definition: hold the office of ib.241.90 , 495.180 , BCH17.555 , Test.Epict. 4.15,35, etc.; hold monthly chairmanship, SIG708.2

ἐπιμήνιος.definition: monthly, HondiusNovae; priests who offered the Hsch.; . . SIG1106.63 , cf. 1044.24 , Test.Epict.2.33

ἐπιμηνίω.definition: to be angry with, Il.13.460, cf. App.BC3.55; Id.Mith.55

ἐπιμηρύομαι.definition: wind a layer of gut on top of others, Ph.Bel.65.43

ἐπιμητιάω.definition: Ep. part. consider how to do, c. inf., A.R.3.668

ἐπιμηχανάομαι.definition: devise plans against, take; devise besides, X.Cyr.8.8.16; D.Chr.6.11, cf. App.BC4.120

ἐπιμηχάνημα.definition: Dor. a means towards a thing, Hippod. ap. Stob.4.1.94

ἐπιμηχάνησις.definition: device, contrivance, on purpose, artificially, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.153

ἐπιμήχανος.definition: craftily devising, contriver of ill deeds, Orac. ap. Hdt.6.19

ἐπιμιμνήσκομαι.definition: fut. Hdt.1.5, etc., rarely; make mention of, ib.191, cf. Hdt.1.5,85, A.Ch.l.c., S.Ph.1400, etc.; `but, by the way', Herod.5.53, cf. 6.42; also Hdt.2.101, X.Cyr.1.6.12, Pl.Mx.239c, etc.: with neut. pron. in acc., Hdt.1…

ἐπιμίμνω.definition: poet. for abide or continue in, Od.14.66, 15.372

ἐπιμίσγω.definition: older poet. and Ion. form (found also in; mostly Pass., in Il. always in hostile sense, I have always to be dealing with the Trojans, am always clashing with them, Il.10.548; as the fight was joined again, 5.505; in O…

ἐπιμίσθιος.definition: engaged for hire, Dam. ap. Suid. s.v. cf. Hsch.s.v. :—pecul. fem. AP7.403

ἐπιμισθόω.definition: contract for, in Pass. of bricks, Michel1512 , cf. IG12.189.30 , 11.165.36, 199A106 , PPetr.3p.109 ; v.l. in Ael.VH3.14

ἐπιμοιράομαι.definition: receive by lot, receive as one's share, c. acc., get earth enough for a grave, Moschio Trag.6.31, cf. Ps.-Phoc.99 : c. gen., have a share of, Ph.2.178

ἐπίμοιρος.definition: partaking in, c. gen., B.1.48, cf. Euryph. ap. Stob.4.39.27

ἐπιμοιχεύω.definition: commit adultery besides, with one, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.6

ἐπίμομφος.definition: inclined to blame, E.Rh.327; blameable, unlucky, A.Ag.553; dub.l., Id.Ch.830

ἐπιμονή.definition: tarrying, delay, Th.2.18; residence; steadfastness, Pl.Cra.395b, Plu.Sert.16; persistence, Sor.2.16,40; of fruit, Thphr.CP2.9.8

ἐπίμονος.definition: staying on, lasting long, Plb.6.43.2; continue him in his command, ib.15.6; delay their payment, Id.38.11.10; Hermes 17.5 ; Sor.1.43; or persevering in it, Plb.29.26.2, Plu.Flam.1; Stoic.3.32. Adv. constantly, permane…

ἐπιμοριασμός.definition: formation of a number of the form 1+1/x, Iamb.in Nic.p.108P

ἐπιμόριος.definition: containing a whole + a fraction with 1 for its numerator , superparticular, Arist.Pr.921b5; Ph.2.183 , Plu.in Hes.59; of the rhythm of the pulse, Gal.8.516; also Arist.Metaph.1021a2. Adv. Nicom.Ar.2.20; opp. , ib.1.20…

ἐπιμοριότης.definition: the property of being Iamb.in Nic.p.44P

ἐπιμορφάζω.definition: pretend, c. inf., Ph.1.387; c.acc., simulate, ib.340,698:—Med., Hsch

ἐπιμοτόω.definition: apply a , in imper. Pass. Heliod. ap. Orib.44.10.9

ἐπίμοχθος.definition: toilsome, B.1.71, cf. Man.4.248: gloss on Sch.Ar.Pax383; Hp.Ep.17. Adv. with toil, App.Pun.72; so neut., LXXWi.15.7

ἐπιμύζω.definition: murmur or mutter at another's words, Il.4.20 :—Med., Hsch

ἐπιμυθεύομαι.definition: to be added fabulously, Arist.HA605a5, Ant.Diog.5

ἐπιμύθιος.definition: coming after the fable: the moral, Luc.Bacch.8, Aphth.Prog.1, Herm.in Phdr.p.92A

ἐπιμυκτηρίζω.definition: turn up the nose, mock at, Men.562.4

ἐπιμύλιος.definition: at or in the mill, epith. of Artemis; of a millstone, LXXJd.9.53

ἐπιμύρομαι.definition: to be washed by the sea, A.R.1.938; but dribbles, An.Ox. 3.220

ἐπιμύσσω.definition: laugh at, cj. in Luc.DMort.6.3: aor. 1 Hsch

ἐπιμύω.definition: pf. Sor.2.27:—close the eyes; wink at, in token of assent, Ar.V.934

ἐπιμωκάομαι.definition: mock at, Sch.S.OT970, Sch.A.R.1.486:—also v.l. in Luc.JTr.16

ἐπίμωμος.definition: blameworthy, Hld.7.2; blemished, Artem.5.67: opp. Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.1

ἐπινάσσω.definition: fut. stuff up, close up, Hsch.; cf; pour, heap over, Gp.6.6.2

ἐπιναυπηγέω.definition: build upon the ship, Poll.1.92; build in addition, Anon.Argent.p.75 Keil

ἐπινάω.definition: send forth emanations or influences, Ascl.in Metaph.23.5:—Pass., ib.120.2, cf. 186.1

ἐπινεανιεύομαι.definition: behave like a youth, in good sense; commit further outrages, Lib.Decl.13.9,56

ἐπινείφω.definition: snow upon, Thphr.HP4.14.6 , CP5.9.13; impers., fresh snow falls, or it keeps snowing, X.Cyn.8.1

ἐπινέμησις.definition: appropriate apportioning of; spreading, Plu.Lys.12, Epicur.Ep.2p.40U.; of disease, Antyll. ap. Orib.50.8.3

ἐπινέμω.definition: allot, distribute; turn one's cattle to graze on another's land, Id.Lg.843d; Arist.Pol.1305a26, cf.D.55.11; enjoy right of pasturage, Berl.Sitzb.1927.7

ἐπίνευσις.definition: inclination of the head, Gal.2.461; movement down, opp. Ath.Mech.26.2; of patients in bed, Philum.ap.Aët.9.23

ἐπινευστάζω.definition: incline forwards, opp. of the crescent moon, Arat.789

ἐπινεύω.definition: make a sign to another to do a thing, order him to do, c. inf., . . Il.9.620:abs., Od.16.164 , h.Cer.169,466, X.Cyr.5.5.37

ἐπινέφελος.definition: clouded, overcast, Hp.Epid.3.2; bringing clouds, Arist.Pr.947b5

ἐπινέφω.definition: bring clouds over the sky, Arist.Pr.944b26; Alex.29; Thphr.Vent.61: or impers., it is cloudy, Id.CP3.24.4

ἐπινέω.definition: spin to, esp. like of the Fates, span for him with her thread at his birth, Il.20.128,24.210: —Pass., Ael.NA7.1, cf. Fr.260; Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.14

ἐπινηνέω.definition: Ep.for , only in impf., heap or pile upon, c. gen. loci, Il.7.428; perh. to be read in Iamb.VP3.17

ἐπινήφω.definition: to be sober at or in, Plu.2.87e; for it, Luc.Am.45

ἐπινήχομαι.definition: swim to or over to, c. acc., Call.Del.21; swim against, attack, Opp.H.2.46

ἐπινίκιος.definition: as Subst., , song of victory, triumphal ode, such as Pindar's, cf. Ath.1.3e; . . A.Ag.174

ἐπίνικος.definition: = foreg., Pi.O.8.75, cf. Stratt.40 : Subst. , Aristid.Or.28.34, 61

ἐπινίσσομαι.definition: go over, c. gen., S.OC689; c. acc., come upon, visit, A.R.4.817, Nic.Th.470, Pae.Delph.6: abs., Theoc.8.43, A.R.4.281

ἐπινοέω.definition: think on or of, contrive, Hdt.1.48; have in one's mind, intend, purpose, Th.2.8, cf. X.An.2.5.4, etc.: c. pres. inf., Hdt.1.27, Ar.Th.338, X.An.6.4.9, etc.: fut., Hdt.3.134: aor., Id.2.152, 5.24,65, E.Rh.195 , Pl.Ti.3…

ἐπινόημα.definition: thought, purpose, contrivance; conception, Epicur.Nat.130,137 G

ἐπινομή.definition: a grazing over the; right of pasturage, Schwyzer 197.33

ἐπινομία.definition: a grazing over the boundaries: right of pasture, X.Cyr.3.2.23 , Berl.Sitzb.1927.7 , IG9.61.7 , 5.511 ; SIG534.15

ἐπινόμιον.definition: payment for pasturage, IG5.456; = sq.1, title of work ascribed to Plato, Theo Sm.pp.7,84,178H

ἐπινομίς.definition: addition to a law, appendix, name; new-year's gift, Ath.3.97d

ἐπινοσέω.definition: to be ill after, Hp.Epid.1.16, cf. Phryn.PSp.120B

ἐπινοσσοποιέομαι.definition: Med., build their nests upon, Ps.-Democr.Symp. Ant.p.6G

ἐπινοτίζω.definition: sprinkle on the surface, Dsc.2.83.2; Pass., perspire slightly, Philum. ap. Aët.5.78

ἐπινυκτερεύω.definition: pass the night at or in, Heraclit.All.9; of water, stand for a night, Plu.2.690c

ἐπινυκτίς.definition: pustule which is most painful by

ἐπινύμφειος.definition: bridal, prob. in S.Ant.814 : fem. Supp.Epigr.2.874

ἐπινυμφεύομαι.definition: contract a second marriage, of a woman, GDI3721.5

ἐπινύσσω.definition: prick on the surface, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.5; stabbing pains, Arching. ap. Gal.8.110:—Pass., Sor.Fract.24, f.l. in Luc.Lex.11

ἐπινυστάζω.definition: drop asleep over, Plu.Brut.36: abs., Luc.Bis Acc.2, Agath.4.18

ἐπινωτίζω.definition: attack from behind, E.HF362 ; = Archipp.5:—Med., take on one's back, Paus.Gr.Fr.143

ἐπινώτιος.definition: on the back, Batr.80, Luc.Am.26; shoulder-blades, Poll.2.133

ἐπίξανθος.definition: inclining to yellow, tawny, of hares, X.Cyn.5.22; of deer, Poll.5.76; of the open lime- flower, Thphr.HP3.10.4, cf.4.2.7

ἐπιξεναγός.definition: officer attached to an Ascl.Tact.6.3, Ael.Tact.16.4, Arr.Tact.14.6

ἐπιξενόομαι.definition: have hospitable relations with, be intimate with, D.50.56, cf. D.S.1.23; lent to or communicated with, Heraclit. ap. S.E.M.7.130

ἐπιξέστης.definition: workman who dresses blocks of masonry, IG22.1672.31

ἐπιξέω.definition: scrape or graze on the surface, Hp.VC14 , Aret.CD1.2; Hld.5.14: metaph., polish a poem, Vit.Apollon.Rhod

ἐπιξηραίνω.definition: dry on the surface, Hp.Fract.33, Arist.Pr.928a9:— Pass., to be so dried, Hp.Prorrh.2.6; have an interval of dryness, Id.Acut.28: generally, to be dried up, Ruf.Ren.Ves.6.5; to be constipated, Aret.CA1.1

ἐπίξηρος.definition: very dry, cf.Aret.SD1.15: Comp., more arid, Id.CA1.1

ἐπίξυνος.definition: poet. for a common field, in which several persons have rights, Il.12.422

ἐπιξύω.definition: grate over, Pl.R.406a, cf; skim over, Arat.650

ἐπίοπτος.definition: poet. for observed, Opp.H.1.10; visible, Arat.25

ἐπιορκέω.definition: also IG22.1126.9; simply, = swear, Sol. ap. Lys.10.17

ἐπιορκία.definition: false swearing, perjury, X.An.3.2.4, etc.; D.19.220: pl., Pl.Grg.525a; X.An.2.5.21

ἐπίορκος.definition: sworn falsely, of oaths; of persons, forsworn, perjured, Hes.Op.804, Schwyzer179a , E.El.1355 , Ar.Nu.399,al.: Antipho6.48. Adv. Hdn.6.9.2

ἐπιόσσομαι.definition: have before one's eyes, Il.17.381; gaze on, A.R.2.28 ; i.e.live, Nic.Th.276

ἐπιόψομαι.definition: fut. , I will choose, Il.9.167, Od.2.294: aor. I ind. chose, IG2.948.1 , cf. Pl.Lg.947c , Hsch., Suid.: aor. 1 Pass., IG2.949.2

ἐπιπαιανίζω.definition: sing a paean over, D.S.5.29: c.acc.cogn., Plu.Marc.22

ἐπιπαίζω.definition: mock at, Hld.10.13: abs., Alex.172.16; sport upon, Philostr.Im.2.17

ἐπιπαραγίγνομαι.definition: arrive on the scene, Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39xxi 25, Mitteis Chr.8.3 , etc.; of generals, succeed in a command, Plb.1.31.4; of troops, come up, Id.4.12.7; of events, come also upon, Junc. ap. Stob.4.50.27

ἐπιπαράκειμαι.definition: to be adjacent, Steph.in Hp.1.209 D

ἐπιπαραμένω.definition: continue to stay with some one, Phld.Herc.1041.1

ἐπιπαρανέω.definition: heap up still more besides, Th.2.77

ἐπιπάρειμι.definition: to be present besides or in; Astrol., occupy a position as well, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.16

ἐπιπαρεμβάλλω.definition: re-form, Plb.12.19.6; intr., fall into line with others, Id.3.115.10, 11.23.5

ἐπιπαρέξειμι.definition: pass farther along, of the sun , Arist.Pr.912a11

ἐπιπαρέρχομαι.definition: go past on the way to a place; Astrol., intervene as well, Vett. Val.291.9

ἐπιπαροινέω.definition: in Pass., to be further intoxicated , prob. in Phld.Ir.p.33 W

ἐπιπαροξύνω.definition: incite still more, D.C.44.35, Ach.Tat.1.8:—Pass., of persons in fever, suffer from successive accesses, v.l. in Hp.Epid.1.2, cf. Gal.7.306; of a sore, become more inflamed, Hp.Prorrh.1.162

ἐπίπασμα.definition: powder for sprinkling, Aret.CA2.2; Sch.Theoc.15.114, cf. Alex.Trall.Febr.3

ἐπιπάσσω.definition: Att. Dor. inf. IG4.951.119 , cf. upon or over, Il.4.218, cf. 5.401, IGl.c., Euphro11.10; Hdt.4.172; Orph.L.455, Luc.DMar.15.3: c. partit. gen., Id.Pisc.22: abs., Theoc.2.18:—Pass., Pl.R.405e, cf. PTeb.1.19

ἐπίπαστος.definition: a kind of cake with comfits upon it, Ar.Eq.103, 1089, Pherecr.130.3; but , = Hp.Hum.5, Theoc.11.2, Aret.CA2.2

ἐπιπαταγέω.definition: make a noise with, Men.Prot.p.50 D

ἐπιπαφλάζω.definition: boil, upon or over, Q.S.11.229, cf. Nonn.D.7.34; boil, foam in, c. dat., ib.1.237

ἐπιπεδόομαι.definition: to be made plane, Iamb.inNic.p.27 P.,al

ἐπίπεδος.definition: on the ground, on the ground-floor; level, flat, Pl.Criti.112a; X.HG7.1.29, etc.; not on a level, but . . , ib.6.4.14; PThead.20i3 ; = Lat. de plano, J.AJ19.5.3: irreg. Comp. X.HG7.4.13

ἐπιπέδωσις.definition: formation of a plane surface, Iamb.in Nic.p.59 P

ἐπιπείθομαι.definition: to be persuaded; trust to, put faith in, A.Ag.1095 , cf. IG14.1389ii 32

ἐπιπειράομαι.definition: do violence to a woman, c. acc., Leg.Gort.2.17, cf. Hsch

ἐπιπέλομαι.definition: come to or upon, . . Od.15.408, cf. 13.60: elsewh. only in Ep. aor.2 part. rolling on, approaching, when the eighth revolving year had come, 7.261; Hes.Sc.87, Th.493 ; A.R.2.1231, 4.670, etc.; of persons, Id.3.25,127;…

ἐπιπέμπω.definition: pf. POxy.743.30 :—send after; send to, IG12.94; of the gods, send upon or to, Hdt.7.15; Pi.Fr.75.2 ; Pl.Phdr.245b ; esp. by way of punishment, send upon or against, let loose upon, generally of the gods, . . E.Ph.811 …

ἐπιπεριελίσσω.definition: wrap round a second time, Hp.Art.38

ἐπιπερκάζω.definition: turn dark, of grapes ripening: begin to get a dark beard, AP11.36

ἐπίπερκνος.definition: somewhat dark, of grapes ripening: hence, of the colour of certain hares, X.Cyn.5.22, Poll.5.67

ἐπιπέσσω.definition: Att. bake, SIG57.36; Pass., to be concocted, Gal.UP14.11

ἐπιπετάννυμι.definition: spread over, X.Cyn.5.10, cf.Aret.CA1.10:—Pass., Q.S.14.25; Aret.SD2.9

ἐπιπέτομαι.definition: fut. Hdt.7.15: aor. or; c.acc., fly over, E.Hel.1486 ; Ar.Av.118; Ael.NA17.16: metaph., fly over to, run eagerly after, Ar.Av.1471 ; flitting from one to another, Pl.R.365a

ἐπιπήγνυμι.definition: or make to freeze on the top; Pass., to be fastened on, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.4.39

ἐπιπηδάω.definition: fut. Pl.Ly.216a:—leap upon, rush at, assault, Ar.V.705, cf. Pl.l.c., PTeb.44.18 ; Plu.2.512d: c.gen., J.BJ2.21.6; ib.10; of male animals, Arist.HA539b32, cf. Pl.Phdr.254a: metaph., rush in, plunge in, Gal.18.635

ἐπιπήδησις.definition: springing upon, assault, Plu.2.916d : metaph., ib.76c, etc.; of the male animal, ib.768e, 1095a

ἐπιπιέζω.definition: press upon, Od.4.287; A.R.3.1335, cf. Dsc.2.4

ἐπιπιεσμός.definition: pressing upon, Gal.8.509, Archig. ap. eund.8.931

ἐπιπίλναμαι.definition: only pres., Ep. for come near, Od.6.44 ; Il.19.92

ἐπιπίνω.definition: drink afterwards or besides, Hp.Acut.56, Ar.Pax712; opp. Ctes.Fr.57.25; drink some wine with their food, Pl.R.372b; Arist.EN1146a35: esp. drink after eating, Od.9.297; . . . . Ar.Eq.354, cf. Pl.1133, Philem.85.3; X.Cy…

ἐπιπιπράσκω.definition: sell the right of succession to a priesthood, SIG1014.8 ; to an inheritance, dub. in PLond.1.113 .88

ἐπιπίπτω.definition: fall upon or over; of money, accrue, SIG953.66

ἐπιπλαδάω.definition: to be loose, flabby on the surface, Ph.2.418 codd

ἐπιπλάζομαι.definition: fut. aor. I about over, Od.8.14; A.R.3.1066:—later in Act., Nic.Al.127

ἐπίπλασις.definition: application of a Aret.CA2.3; of plasters, ib.1.9

ἐπίπλασμα.definition: plaster, Hp.Art.40, Aret.CA1.1, Lyc. ap. Orib.9.25.1, etc

ἐπιπλάσσω.definition: Att. spread or plaster on; plaster up, Arist.Pr.875a36; Thphr.Sens.8

ἐπίπλαστος.definition: plastered over, Alciphr.3.11; metaph.,feigned, false, J.BJ4.4.3; ib.1.32.2, Luc.DMort.27.7; Id.Am.3; Hdn.3.15.7. Adv. M.Ant.2.16

ἐπιπλατής.definition: flat, broad, only in Adv. Aët.7.31

ἐπιπλέκω.definition: wreathe into a chaplet, AP12.256.5; bind, ib.18.189; bind upon, ib.36.365:—Pass., Luc.Cont.16

ἐπιπλέω.definition: sail against, attack by sea, Hdt.5.86; Th.3.76; X.HG1.5.11, etc.; D.S.20.50: abs., Hdt.1.70, 6.33; also of the ships, Th.3.80: generally, sail on, Plb.1.25.4, etc

ἐπιπληρόω.definition: fill up, Ephipp.4 ; no resources whence we shall man our ships afresh, Th.7.14:—Pass., Gal.15.781

ἐπιπλήσσω.definition: punish, chastise, esp. with words, rebuke. reprove, c.acc.pers., Il.23.580, cf. Pl.Prt.327a: c. dat., Il.12.211, cf. Isoc.1.31; Pl.Lg.805b, cf. 1 Ep.Ti.5.1, etc.; for a thing, Pl.Plt.286b:—Pass., to be rebuked, Id.Grg…

ἐπιπλινθοβολέω.definition: lay courses of bricks above, IG22.463.58

ἐπιπλοκήλη.definition: hernia of the omentum, Gal.7.36:—hence one who suffers from it, Id.14.789

ἐπιπνέω.definition: Ep. (as always in Hom., cf; blow furiously upon, Hdt.3.26: metaph., . . A.Th.343 , cf. S.Ant.136

ἐπιποθέω.definition: desire besides or yearn after, c.acc., Hdt.5.93, Ph.2.598; feel the want of, Pl.Lg.855e; LXXPs.118.20; ib.61 .11

ἐπιπόθητος.definition: longed for, desired, Ep.Phil.4.1; missed, found wanting, App.Hisp.43

ἐπιπολάζω.definition: fut. Isoc.5.64: pf; metaph., have the upper hand, prevail, [Epich.] 282; D.9.25, cf. Isoc.5.64, 8.107; Plb.30.13.2

ἐπιπολαιόρριζος.definition: with roots which run along the surface, Thphr.HP1.6.4, 2.5.1

ἐπιπόλαιος.definition: on the surface, superficial; shallow , Hp.VC21; i.e. not deep-set, X.Smp.5.5

ἐπιπόλασις.definition: being on the surface, coming to the surface, Hp.Hum.3, Arist.Sens.440b16

ἐπιπολή.definition: elsewh. only in gen., as Adv., on the top, Hdt.2.62, Arist.GA747a5, etc.; . . . , . . X.Mem.3.1.7; Id.Oec.19.4; uppermost, Hp.Art.77; Pl.Phlb.47c, cf. 46e; of arguments, to be superficial, Arist.Rh.1400b31; but quite …

ἐπιπομπή.definition: visitation, punishment, Aristeas131; enchantment, Poet.deherb.22 , 165 , 175, PMag.Par.1.2159

ἐπιπονέω.definition: c. dat., labour on or at, J.AJ18.8.5, cf. 19.2.5

ἐπίπονος.definition: painful, f.l. for in; of persons, laborious, patient of toil, Ar.Ra.1370 , Pl.Phdr.229d; also, sensitive to fatigue, easily exhausted, Thphr.Sens.11

ἐπιπορεία.definition: coming on the scene, of marionettes, opp. HeroAut.19.1

ἐπιπορεύομαι.definition: = 4, of a general, Plb.11.12.1, cf. 15.10.1, Plu.Tim.12; also come before the assembly, Plb.4.9.2; Ev.Luc.8.4: metaph., go or run through, Plu.2.470a

ἐπιπόρευσις.definition: course, of planets; name for the fifth Cat.Cod.Astr.8.152

ἐπιπορθμεύομαι.definition: spread, of a morbid condition, Sch.Nic.Al.544

ἐπιπορπάομαι.definition: buckle on oneself, buckle on, Plb.38.7.2

ἐπιπόρπημα.definition: Dor. garment buckled over the shoulders, cloak, mantle, part of the dress of a musician, Pl.Com.10, App.Pun.109

ἐπιπορσαίνω.definition: prepare for one, offer, supply, Nic.Fr.74.54 codd. Ath

ἐπιπορφυρίζω.definition: have a tinge of purple, Arist.Col.796b14, Thphr.HP3.18.2, 6.2.1, al

ἐπιποτάομαι.definition: lengthd. for fly or hover; float upon, Dsc.5.75; Porph.Antr.10

ἐπιπράττομαι.definition: exact over and above from, Anon. ap. Suid

ἐπιπρέπεια.definition: congruity, suitableness; appearance, Archyt. ap. Stob.3.1.114, cf. Simp.in Cael.661.10

ἐπιπρεπής.definition: becoming, Diotog. ap. Stob.4.7.62; = foreg. I, Luc.Im.7

ἐπιπρέπω.definition: to be conspicuous; beseem, suit, c. dat., Plu.2.794a: impers., it is fitting, c.inf., Xenoph.26

ἐπιπρεσβεύομαι.definition: send an embassy, Id.6.56; Plu.Sert.27,Ant.68; send a second embassy, App.Gall.18

ἐπιπρίω.definition: grind with rage at, AP7.531 , cf. Hsch

ἐπιπροβαίνω.definition: pf. stretch forward, project, D.P.128, Ruf.Oss.37

ἐπιπροθέω.definition: run on farther, Id.1.582, Nic.Th.382: rush into, Opp.H.3.379

ἐπιπροϊάλλω.definition: poet. Verb, set out or place before; send on one after another, h.Cer.326; Q.S.6.231

ἐπιπροΐημι.definition: poet. Verb, send forth, . . on board ship to Ilium, Il.18.58; but . . . . to the ships, to go . . , 17.708; sent them forth to supplicate, 9.520; shoot an arrow at him, 4.94; A.R.4.1185; Nic.Th.778; Orac. ap. Luc.Alex…

ἐπίπροικος.definition: woman who inherits a charge upon a property as her dowry, AB 256; but simply, dowered, opp. Poll.3.35, cf. Hsch

ἐπιπροπίπτω.definition: fall forwards, A.R.4.1449, Nic.Al.496; project, Sor.1.69

ἐπιπροσγίγνομαι.definition: to be added besides, A.D.Synt.260.28, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69, POxy.1725.18

ἐπιπρόσειμι.definition: Astrol., to be present as well, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.18

ἐπιπροσθετέω.definition: occult, Phld.Sign.10; metaph. of nutriment, Hp.Alim.4

ἐπιπροσθέτησις.definition: occultation, Epicur.Ep.2p.40U; name of a bandage, Nicet. ap. Gal. 18.792

ἐπιπροσθέω.definition: to be before or in the way, Thphr.Vent.32; of occultations or eclipses, Zeno Stoic.1.34, Chrysipp.ib.2.199, Procl.Hyp.5.14, al.; but Ascl.Tact.12.10; protection from the wind, Ath.Med. ap.Orib.9.12.1: c. dat., Hp.Medi…

ἐπιπρόσθησις.definition: being before, covering, Thphr.Vent.30; esp. of eclipses or occultations, Arist.Cael.293b22, Procl.Hyp.5.15, etc.; superposition of colour, Arist.Mete.342b9 ; of objects that serve as cover, Plb.3.71.3

ἐπιπροστίθημι.definition: add besides, Longin.44.1:—Med., corrupt in Artem.4.82

ἐπιπροφαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to appear before one, of A.R.3.917

ἐπιπροχέω.definition: pour forth, h.Pan.18:—Pass., gush forth, burst loose, Nonn.D.21.69

ἐπιπταίρω.definition: sneeze at, he sneezed as I spoke the words , Od.17.545, cf. h.Merc.297, Nonn.D.7.107: metaph., to be gracious to, favour, Theoc.7.96; Id.18.16

ἐπιπτήσσω.definition: crouch for fear, Aristid. ap. Philostr.VS2.9.3

ἐπιπτίσσομαι.definition: to be shelled, freed from the husk, Gp.3.7.1

ἐπίπτυγμα.definition: over-fold, flap, such as covers the orifices in animals, operculum, Arist.PA679b18,HA526b29,528b7: pl., opercula, of crustaceans, Id.Resp.477a4

ἐπίπτυξις.definition: application to one another of vocal cords, Gal.UP7.13

ἐπιπτύσσω.definition: fold up, fold, Luc.Dem.Enc.25; Dam.Isid.131: abs., produce folds, Gal.11.508:—Pass., to be folded over, Hp.Epid.6.8.28; of the epiglottis, Arist.HA495a28, cf. PA664b28; of the vocal cords, Gal.UP7.13

ἐπιπτυχή.definition: = flap, J.AJ17.5.7, Plu.2.979c; Id.Pomp.35; rags and tatters, Luc.DMort.1.2

ἐπίπτωσις.definition: falling upon, Nicom.Harm.12; falling over the forehead, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.8.1

ἐπιπυκνόομαι.definition: Pass., to become dense, Arist.Col.794a14, Sor.2.29

ἐπιπυνθάνομαι.definition: learn after, D.H.Th.29; inquire again, Diogenian.3.34

ἐπιπυρέσσω.definition: aor.1. have fever afterwards, Hp.Prorrh.1.15, Gal.18.568; after drinking wine, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.23

ἐπιπυριάω.definition: foment as well, Paul.Aeg.3.77; gloss on Hsch

ἐπιπωλέομαι.definition: go about, go through, c.acc., of the general inspecting his troops, Il.3.196, etc.; but in 11.264, of reconnoitring an enemy.—Them. has visit, Or.6.75c: c. dat., ib.11.152b

ἐπιπωλέω.definition: sell the right of succession to a priesthood, in Pass., SIG 1014.85,107

ἐπιπωμάζω.definition: cover with or as with a lid, HeroSpir.1 Praef. p.150, Simp. in Cael.520.15, al., Sm.Ps.68.16:—Pass., to be so covered, Hp.Loc.Hom.47, Anthem.p.151 W.—So HeroSpir.1.28

ἐπιπωμασμός.definition: covering with a lid or cover, of an arrow, Eust.1630.63

ἐπιπωματίζω.definition: cover as with a lid, close up, Arist.Cael.294b15, Thphr.Ign.59:—Pass., ib.49; Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.16; Arist.Fr.311; of the epiglottis, Gal.14.716
