εὐρυπυλής.definition: with broad gates, Il.23.74, cf. Od.11.571

εὐρυρέεθρος.definition: with broad channel, broad-flowing, Il.21.141; cf. sq

εὐρυρέων.definition: broad-flowing, shd. be written divisim, Il.2.849, etc

εὐρυσθενής.definition: of far-extended might, mighty, in Hom. always of Poseidon, Il.7.455, 8.201, Od.13.140; of Zeus, B.18.17; Apollo, Pi.I.2.18; Telamon, Id.N.3.36; Himera, Id.O.12.2; ib.4.12, P.5.1

εὐρύσορος.definition: with wide bier or tomb, AP7.528

εὐρύστερνος.definition: broad-breasted, Hes.Th.117; APl.4.303, Orph.L.645; Theoc.18.36: later in Prose, Gal.4.629; of Poseidon, Corn.ND22

εὐρύτρυπος.definition: = foreg., f.l. for in Democr. ap. Thphr.Sens.73

εὐρυφαρέτρης.definition: Dor. with wide quiver, of Apollo, Pi.P.9.26: acc. sg. Id.Pae.6.111; Id.Fr.148

εὐρυφυής.definition: broad-growing, broad-eared, in reference to the manner in which the grains of barley are set on the stalk, Od.4.604

εὐρυχαδής.definition: wide-gaping, wide-mouthed, of cups, AP6.305 , Luc.Lex.7

εὐρυχαίτης.definition: Dor. with wide- streaming hair, of Dionysus, Pi.I.7.4

εὐρυχανής.definition: = foreg., Opp.H.3.344; of a wounded man, Nonn.D.22.242

εὐρύχορος.definition: with broad places, spacious, Il.2.498, Od.15.1, etc.; Il.9.478; of Troy, Sapph.Supp.20a.12; Pi.O.7.18, P.4.43; B.9.31; Pi.P.8.55, E.Ba.87 , Orac. ap. D.21.52; AP6.319

εὐρυχωρής.definition: = Hp.VM22 , Paus.3.19.1: Comp. Arist.HA508a28: Sup. Id.PA668b16

εὐρυχωρία.definition: Ion. open space, free; an open field for battle, X.Cyr.4.1.18, HG7.4.24; to fight with plenty of sea- room, cf. Th.2.83,al

εὐρύχωρος.definition: roomy, wide, Arist.PA675b27; D.S.19.84; Max. Tyr.1.3; wide spaces, Aen. Tact.2.2, Ph.Bel.92.47

εὐρωστέω.definition: to be robust, Poll.3.121, POxy.1493.8; display moral strength, Phld.Piet.33b

εὐρωστία.definition: stoutness, strength, Arist.Mir.830a9, D.S.17.88, PRyl.235.8 ; Plu.Cat.Mi.44; personified, Ath.Mitt.32.308

εὔρωστος.definition: stout, strong, X.HG4.3.6, cf.Aen. Tact.1.7, PCair.Zen.56.1 , etc.; Arist.HA617b3; X.HG6.1.6; Isoc.15.116 ; Arist.Phgn.810a25. Adv. X.Ages.2.24; Antiph.1 D

εὐρωτιάω.definition: to be or become mouldy, decay, Thphr.CP1.6.8, Luc.Nec.15, etc.; the life of 'the great unwashed', Ar.Nu.44

εὐσαρκία.definition: fullness of flesh, good condition, Hp.Art.53, Arist.HA493b22, Ph.1.666; coupled with Phld.Mort.29: pl., Antyll. ap. Stob.4.37.16; of fruit, Thphr.CP1.9.2

εὔσαρκος.definition: fleshy, in good condition, Hp.Aph.4.7, X.Lac.5.8, Arist.HA583a9, Phld.Mort.30, etc.; of meat, Amphis16; opp. on the one hand, and on the other, Gal.6.30

εὐσεβέω.definition: live or act piously or reverently, abs., Thgn.145, Berl.Sitzb.1927.8 , S.Aj.1350, etc.; towards one, Id.Ant.731; E.Alc.1148; Pl.Smp.193a; Men.Mon.567; AP10.107 ; S.Ph.1441; Isoc.3.2; of outward acts of service, PRyl.1…

εὐσεβία.definition: Ion. poet. for Thgn.1142 codd., Pi.O.8.8, S.Ant.943 , OC189 ; personified, Emp.4.5, Critias6.22, Epigr.Gr.1055 , etc

εὐσήμαντος.definition: easily remarked or observed; easily designated, PMeyer 20.46

εὐσημία.definition: good prognostic, Hp.Epid.6.2.17; favourable omen, Arist.Ath.44.4

εὔσημος.definition: Dor. of good signs or omens; easily known by signs, conspicuous, A.Supp.714; . . Id.Ag.818; Hp.Mochl.16; Annuario 4/5.225 ; Thphr.CP6.19.5 ; . . not easy to distinguish, ib.3.8.2; legible, clear, SIG1023.96 ; OGI665.1…

εὐσθένεια.definition: strength, firmness, Democr.57 codd. , Thphr.CP3.1.6, 2.1 , Ph.2.548 ; of scents, Thphr.Od.19

εὐσθενέω.definition: to be strong, healthy, Hp.Morb.Sacr.10 , E.Cyc.2, Arist.Pr.862a11, 925a3 ; f.l. for A.Eu.895; so prob. in D.C.53.8

εὐσθενής.definition: Ep. stout, Il.Pers.6, cf. Ph.Bel.56.31, Q.S.14.633; strong, firm, APl.4.323 : irreg. Sup. Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.28. Adv. Gal.17.185, f.l. in Ph.1.264

εὐσιτέω.definition: to have a good appetite, Hp.Aph.2.31; f.l. for Pyrgio1; to be well fed, f.l. in Thphr.HP4.8.13

εὔσιτος.definition: with good appetite, Hp.Coac.124; easy to feed, Philostr.VA1.41

εὐσπλαγχνία.definition: good heart, firmness, E.Rh.192, PMasp.97 D 69

εὔσπλαγχνος.definition: with healthy bowels, Hp.Prorrh.2.6; compassionate, LXXPrec.Man.7, Ep.Eph.4.32, 1 Ep.Pet.3.8, PMag. Leid.V.9.3, PMasp.20.11

εὐσταθέω.definition: to be steady, stable; enjoy sound, stable health, Epicur.Fr.68, cf. 413, Sor.1.87, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.7.8.1

εὐσταθής.definition: Ep. as always in Hom; metaph., steadfast, tranquil, Democr.191; Plu.2.44a; Hdn.2.6.5; Aret.SA1.10; ib.2.3; dub. in Phld.D.3tit

εὔσταθμος.definition: accurately measured, dub. in PTeb.5.85 , v.l. in LXXSi.26.18 ; of full weight, Cod.Just.10.27.2.6. Adv. precisely equal in weight, Hp.Mul.1.1: Comp. BKT3p.15

εὐσταλής.definition: convenient, neat, Hp.Fract.37 , prob. in Id.Mochl.1; convenient to handle, manageable, Id.Superf.7 ; a fair and easy voyage, S.Ph.780

εὐστομαχία.definition: wholesomeness of food, Hices. ap. Ath.7.298b, Aët.9.30, Paul Aeg.2.49; f.l. for Dsc.2.16

εὐστόμαχος.definition: equable, tranquil. Adv; good for the stomach, wholesome, Diocl.Fr.125, Dsc.1.117, Sor.1.94, Hices. ap. Ath.15.689c, Gal.6.593: Sup., lemma ad Ath.7.310a

εὐστομέω.definition: to be sing sweetly, of the

εὐστομία.definition: poet. goodness of sound; pleasantness to the mouth, goodness of taste, Thphr.CP6.16.2, Dsc.2.16: pl., Plu.2.687d; f.l. for Hices. ap. Ath.7.310f

εὔστομος.definition: with mouth of good size, of; with large mouth, of cups, Luc.Lex.7; of a harbour, Poll.1.100

εὐστοχέω.definition: pf. inf. D.S.2.31:—hit the mark, succeed, opp. Plb.1.14.7, etc.: c. gen., to hit them exactly, Id.2.45.5, 28.3.6, 32.3.10; Str.17.1.6; Id.5.3.8: c. acc., Apollod.1.7.4: abs., Plb.9.12.1; J.BJ1.15.1; guess aright, Plu.…

εὐστοχία.definition: Ep. skill in shooting at a; metaph., sagacity, shrewdness, Arist.EN1142b2, Plb.18.33.7; of artists, D.H.Comp.25, cf. APl.4.310 , etc.; Ph.Fr.11 H

εὔστοχος.definition: aiming well, E.HF195; . . Id.Ph.140, cf. Fr.321 ; Luc.Nav.33. Adv. X.Cyr.1.4.8; Parth.15.1, Luc.Nigr.36: Sup. D.C.67.14

εὐσύγκριτος.definition: either well-compounded, well- constituted, or discriminating, Diog.Oen.1,2

εὐσύμβλητος.definition: old Att. = sq. I, Hdt.7.57; A.Pr.775

εὐσύμβολος.definition: old Att. easy to divine; easy to deal with, honest, upright, X.Mem.2.6.5; suits which afford easy arbitration, A.Supp.701 . Poll.5.139

εὐσυμπερίφορος.definition: easy to live with, accommodating, D.L.7.13

εὐσυνάγωγος.definition: easily collected together, a place convenient for collecting imports, Arist.Pol.1331b2

εὐσυνάλλακτος.definition: easy to deal with, Plu.2.42f, cf. Ptol.Tetr.165, Vett.Val.116.32. Adv. LXXPr.25.10

εὐσυνείδητος.definition: with a good conscience, M.Ant.6.30; honest, Sammelb.4426.12

εὐσυνθεσία.definition: good arrangement of words, Eust.85.34; observance of treaties, Ph.2.267

εὐσύνθετος.definition: easy to compound into a word; easy to put together or construct, Ph.Bel.56.34, Apollod.Poliorc.155.16

εὐσύνοπτος.definition: easily taken in at a glance, seen at; metaph., easily taken in by the mind, of a poem, Arist.Po.1459a33; . . Id.Rh.1409b1; of the facts of a case, ib.1414a12, cf. Pol.1323b7; of a falsity or error, easily seen or dete…

εὐσύντακτος.definition: well-arranged, Arr.Tact.16.10; with good syntax, easy, Eust.66.36. Adv. Id.336.4

εὐσυντέλεστος.definition: easily brought to a conclusion, Vett.Val.212.17

εὐσχημονέω.definition: to behave with decorum, Pl.Lg.732c, Men.Mon.646, Phld.Rh.2.281 S., PSI5.541.5

εὔσχημος.definition: = EM398.19; v.l. in D.H.Comp.17. Adv. v.l. in E.Hec.569

εὐσχημοσύνη.definition: gracefulness, elegance, Pl.Smp.196a; of the body, 1 Ep.Cor.12.23; IGRom.4.1029.35

εὐσχήμων.definition: gen. elegant in figure; in bad sense, with an outside show of goodness, specious in behaviour, E.Med.584

εὐσχολέω.definition: to have abundant leisure, Phld.Rh.1.377 S., D.S.10.7, M.Ant.11.18: c. inf., J.AJ5.2.5; Id.BJ3.7.29; for a thing, Luc.Am.33: Muson.Fr.48p.130H

εὔσχολος.definition: unoccupied, esp. by war, Plb.4.32.6; leisured, leisurely, Phld.Oec.p.64J.; Hierocl. ap. Stob.4.22.24 : Comp. Telesp.47 H., M.Ant.4.24

εὐσωματέω.definition: to be well-grown, to be strong and lusty, E.Andr.765, Ar.Nu.799; Orib.1.3.5; of trees, Plu.2.641a

εὐσωματία.definition: strength or good habit of body, Poll.2.235

εὐτακτέω.definition: to be orderly, behave well, Th.8.1; Act., pay regularly, PHib. 1.35.6 , cf. POxy.1471.16 ; PSI4.350.2 , etc.:—Pass., SIG 672.10 , cf. BGU1107.11

εὔτακτος.definition: well-ordered, orderly; esp. of soldiers, etc., orderly, well-disciplined, Ar.V.424, Th.2.89, IG7.1.7 , etc.; Th.7.77: Comp., X.An.3.2.30; well-behaved, Epicur.Fr.217; name of a category of IGRom.4.482 ; at regular int…

εὐτειχής.definition: Pi.O.6.1, N.7.46, E.Andr.1009 ; prop. oxytone, cf. Hdn. Gr.2.37,687; but acc. Il.16.57

εὐτεκνέω.definition: to be happy in children, E.Fr.520, Stoic.3.156, Plu.2.278b

εὐτεκνία.definition: poet. blessing of children; personified, Syria 6.295 . in ll. cc. poet., and Theoc.18.51.]

εὔτεκνος.definition: blest with children, Sup; of animals, kind to their young, Arist.HA563b6, 614b33

εὐτεκνόω.definition: make people happy in their children, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.217

εὐτέλεια.definition: meanness, shabbiness, Lys.30.21; Luc.Dom.14; thrift, economy, economically, Ar.Ra.406 ; without extravagance, Th.2.40; to be cut down to an economical standard, Id.8.86; ib.1: in pl., economies, Antiph.164.1

εὐτελής.definition: easily paid for, cheap, Hdt.2.86; mean, paltry, worthless, of persons, A.Th.491; of character, Arist.Pol.1272b41; opp. Id.Po.1448b26 ; Eup.189; Men.338; Id.615; so of things, shabby, Pl.Lg.806a; of land, depreciated i…

εὐτελίζω.definition: disparage, ib.1073c, Luc.Pr.Im.13, Anacreont.27 A 10; make disreputable, Cat. Cod.Astr.8.205

εὐτεχνία.definition: skill in art, Str.1.2.33, D.H.Dem.35, Luc.Herm.20, APl.4.142.6

εὔτεχνος.definition: skilfully wrought, Hp.Ep.14; skilful, of persons, AP6.206 , cf. Epigr.Gr.979

εὐτοκέω.definition: bring forth easily, Hp.Superf.2; to be prolific, of trees or animals, Thphr.CP1.14.1, Ph.1.249, al.: metaph., ib.520:—Pass., to be brought forth easily, Corn.ND34

εὐτοκία.definition: easy delivery, Call.Epigr.54, AP9.268; fertility, Ph.1.183; of crops, ib.301

εὔτοκος.definition: bringing forth easily, Arist.HA576a22; = I , Ph.1.274; fertile, Hp.Nat.Mul.16

εὐτολμία.definition: courage, boldness, E.Med.469, Arist.Rh.Al.1423b3, VV1250b5: pl., D.S.17.10, Ph.2.382

εὔτολμος.definition: brave-spirited, courageous; in bad sense, daring, audacious, Anatolian Studies 204

εὐτονέω.definition: have power or faculties, Hp.Ep.16,17; have power or means to do, Plu.2.531b, cf. 533e; IG14.830.10 , cf. Wilcken Chr.176.18 ; SIG1109.30, cf. 49

εὐτονία.definition: tension, vigour, D.S.5.39; ib.34; Medic., tension, Ruf.Sat.Gon.46 ; also gentle force, Hp.Ep.15

εὔτονος.definition: well-strung, vigorous, of men's; distended, Neophr. Medea in PLit.Lond.77 Fr. 2.7

εὔτορνος.definition: well-turned, rounded, circular; easy to turn, of wood, Thphr.HP5.6.4 , 5.6.2

εὐτραπελεύομαι.definition: to be witty, ready, Plb.12.16.14, D.S.38/9.7; cj. Dind. for Eust.1053.18

εὐτραπελία.definition: ready wit, liveliness, Hp.Decent.7; rarely in bad sense, = Ep.Eph.5.4

εὐτράπελος.definition: easily turning or changing; of persons, ready with an answer or repartee, witty, Arist.EN1108a24, 1128a10; Plb.23.5.7; Jul.Or.7.227a: Sup., Plb.9.23.3

εὐτραφής.definition: well-fed, thriving, fat; Act., nourishing, A.Th.308 ; Id.Ch.898, Philostr.VA3.9; v.l. in Thphr.CP1.18.1

εὐτρεπής.definition: readily turning: hence generally, prepared, ready, E.Ba.440; ib.844; . . Epicr.10.4; Antiph.80.12; Men.Pk.117; Plb.6.26.10; also of persons, D.4.18; . . Id.21.112, cf. Com.Adesp.15.19 D.; D.H.2.3, Ph.1.174. Adv. to be…

εὐτρεπίζω.definition: Att. fut. pf. AP9.316.8; Medic., treat, Hp.Loc.Hom.1, al.; dub. in Thphr.Char.13.9

εὐτροπέομαι.definition: Pass., to be easily dealt with, Apollod.Poliorc.138.5

εὐτροπία.definition: good disposition, Democr.57; Ph.2.399; in reading aloud, expression, Aët.16.67

εὐτροφέω.definition: thrive, flourish, Arist.GA765b26, Thphr.HP8.8.4, etc.: —also Med. or Pass., Id.CP4.1.4

εὐτροφία.definition: good nurture, thriving condition, Pl.Prt.351a, 351b,cf. Arist.HA542a28, Thphr.HP5.2.2, Orph.Fr.49 vi 89: pl., Ph.2.1, Antyll. ap. Stob.4.37.16

εὔτροφος.definition: nourishing, healthy; Pass., well-nourished, thriving, of trees, D.S.17.89; of children, Hp.Dent.1, Orph.Fr.49 vi 88: Comp., Hp.Dent.13, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.9.5.6: metaph., of diseases, Luc.Abd.27

εὐτυκάζομαι.definition: make ready: . Hsch.: hence restored by Dind. for . . in A.Th.149

εὔτυκος.definition: rare form for sq., well-built; ready, ib.994: c. inf., . . ib.974 ; B.8.4; Pratin.Lyr.2; Theoc.24.88; Call.Lav.Pall.3; v.l. in Hdt.1.119

εὐτύχεια.definition: poet. for S.Fr.1050; festival in honour of Eutyches, SIG2588.55 : sg., fund devoted to its maintenance, Inscr.Délos 370.44

εὐτυχέω.definition: impf. or S.Fr.107.10, etc; of things, turn out well, prosper, A.Ag.1327; S.El.945; Id.Fr.681; . . if they succeed, Th.3.39, cf. 4.79:—also in Pass., Id.7.77; Plu.Num.12: Gal.Protr.12; Alciphr.2.3; of a person, Iamb.VP2.9

εὐτύχημα.definition: piece of good luck, success, E.Ph.1356, Pl.Smp.217a, Men.5.3 D., etc.; X.An.6.3.6

εὐτυχής.definition: successful, fortunate, of persons and; Adv. Pi.N.7.90, A.Pers.325, etc.; Ion. Hdt.3.39: Comp. E.Heracl.247 ; Pl.Euthd.280a: Sup. at close of letter, D.H.Amm.2 fin

εὐτύχησις.definition: in pl., lucky strokes of fortune, Phld.Rh.2.217 S

εὐτυχία.definition: Ion. good luck, success, Pi.O.6.81, Hdt.1.32, Th.7.77, etc.; Antipho2.4.4; defined, Arist.Rh.1361b39; E.IT1490 , Ar.Ec.573 ; Pl.Men.72a; Id.Lg.798b; Th.1.120: pl., pieces of good luck, successes, Id.2.44

εὔυδρος.definition: well-watered, abounding in water; of a river or spring, with beautiful water, B.10.119; E.IT399 ; Pae.Delph.5; so prob. Polyzel.2

εὔυμνος.definition: celebrated in many hymns, h.Ap.19; used in beautiful hymns, Id.Epigr. in Berl.Sitzb. 1912.548. [The penult. short in Epich.91.]

εὐυπέρβατος.definition: easily stepped over: of a socket; easy of access, PFay. 110.9 , POxy.1272.16

εὐυπόδητος.definition: of a sandal, easy to bind under the foot, Tz.ad Lyc.853

εὐυπόκριτος.definition: playing one's part well, Vett.Val.48.1; also of marriage, Id.119.33

εὐυπόληπτος.definition: easy to take up, light; in Comp., more easily enclosed, v.l. in Arist.Sens.438a15, cf.Alex.Aphr.in Sens.26.20,36.1

εὐυφής.definition: well-woven, Tim.Pers.180; AP10.2 ; Herm.in Phdr.p.192 A., BGU1564.10; v.l. in S.Tr.602

εὐφαντασίωτος.definition: gifted with a vivid imagination, Vett.Val.47.1, Quint.6.2.30; Cat.Cod.Astr.8.209; also in bad sense, fantastic, fanciful, Vett.Val.150.12

εὐφάνταστος.definition: imaginative, Phlp.in de An.155.30; easily imagined, Procl.in Prm.p.518S

εὐφημέω.definition: Dor. use words of good; avoid all unlucky words, during sacred rites: hence, as the surest mode of avoiding them, keep a religious silence, Il.9.171, cf. Call.Ap.17, 18, etc.; mostly imper., hush! be still! Ar.Nu.297,…

εὐφημία.definition: use of words of good omen, opp; abstinence from inauspicious language, religious silence, = S.Tr.178; Pl.Lg.717c; as a proclamation of silence before a prayer, Ar.Th.295, cf.Av.959; so . . S.Fr.893; . . E.IA1564; Pl.L…

εὐφημίζομαι.definition: use words of good omen, A.D.Pron.10.22, Hsch. s.v. EM388.43

εὐφημισμός.definition: use of an auspicious word for an inauspicious one, e.g. for for etc., Eust.1398.52, Demetr.Eloc.281; Corn.ND21, Hermog.Prog.7, Palaeph.51, Olymp.in Mete.105.19; Phld.Piet.111

εὔφημος.definition: Dor. uttering sounds of; abstaining from inauspicious words, i.e. religiously silent, . . A.Ag.1247; Id.Ch.581; so perh. Id.Fr.40; moving the lips of reverent thought, i.e. keeping a holy silence, S.OC132 ; so i.e. in…

εὔφθογγος.definition: well-sounding, cheerful, Thgn.534; A.Ch.341 ; E.Tr.127 ; sweet-voiced, of birds, Str.15.1.69: Sup., Id.6.1.9

εὐφιλής.definition: well-loved, A.Ag.34; Act., loving well, Id.Eu.197

εὐφιλόπαις.definition: the children's darling, of a lion's whelp, A.Ag.721

εὐφιλοτίμητος.definition: properly made an object of ambition, Arist.EN1122b22

εὐφόρβιον.definition: spurge, Euphorbia resinifera, Dsc.3.82, Gal.13.270; freq. also, its resinous juice, S.E.P.1.93, Edict.Diocl.32.70

εὐφορέω.definition: bear well, be productive, Hp.Ep.10; of ships, have a prosperous voyage, Luc.Lex.15

εὐφορία.definition: power of enduring easily, Hp.Fract.35; sense of well-being in disease, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.106, cf. Gal.11.10, 14.615, Orib.Syn.6.6

εὐφράδεια.definition: correctness of language, Phld.Rh.1.165 S., S.E.M.1.98

εὐφραδής.definition: expressing oneself correctly or; Pass., well-expressed, Lyd.Mens.4.64, cf. Sch.Il.14.382 , etc

εὐφραίνω.definition: Ep. fut. Att. A.Ch.742; Pass., make merry, enjoy oneself, Od.2.311, cf. Hdt.4.9, Ev.Luc.16.19, etc.; at or in a thing, Pi.P.9.16, Ar.Nu.561, Pl.Lg.796b; Ar.Ach.5, X.Smp.7.5, Aeschin.1.191; X.Hier.1.16; ib.8; ib.4.6: c…

εὐφυής.definition: well-grown, shapely; of good natural disposition, X.Mem.1.6.13, al., Arist.EN1114b8, Thphr.Char.29.4; of horses and dogs, X.Mem.4.1.3 , Jul.Or.2.87a

εὐφυΐα.definition: natural goodness of growth or shape; good natural parts, and morally, goodness of disposition, freq. in both senses at once, Arist.EN1114b12, Rh.1362b24, etc.; defined as Pl.Def.413d

εὐφωνέω.definition: have a good voice, Phld. Rh.1.367S

εὐφωνία.definition: goodness of voice, X.Mem.3.3.13; excellence of tone, of horns, Arist.Aud.802b2

εὔφωνος.definition: sweet-voiced, musical; euphonious, Democr.18b, D.H.Comp.12, Demetr.Eloc.70; D.H.Comp.14

εὐχάρεια.definition: grace, charm, Simp.in Epict.p.119 D.; cf. II

εὐχαρής.definition: = Men. Rh.p.406 S.; v.l. for LXXWi.14.20

εὐχαριστέω.definition: bestow a favour on, oblige; to be thankful, return thanks, Decr. ap. D.18.92, IPE12.352.14 ; Posidon.36 J., cf. Phld.Ir.p.92 W., al.; or for a thing, Plb.4.72.7, D.S.16.11, etc.; esp. to the gods, UPZ59.10 , cf. LXXJu…

εὐχαριστήριος.definition: expressive of gratitude, Ph.2.157; PMasp.6.6 : as Subst., , thank-offering, Plb.5.14.8, cf. Sch.Pi.P.7.9; mission of thanks to the Senate, D.S.29.11: sg., . . IG12.1086 , cf. 3.132l, IPE 12.162.2, OGI699 , LXX2 Ma.12.45

εὐχαριστία.definition: thankfulness, gratitude, Decr. ap; giving of thanks, SIG798.5 , cf. Ph.1.60, LXXWi.16.28, Corp.Herm.1.29, etc.: pl., 1 Ep.Ti.2.1

εὐχάριστος.definition: agreeable, X.Oec.5.10; grateful, thankful, X.Cyr.8.3.49 , Inscr.Prien.103.8 , Ep.Col.3.15, etc. Adv. D.S.1.90; Ph.1.520; Plu.2.477f

εὐχέρεια.definition: tolerance of or indifference to evil; indifference to danger or hardship: hence, coolness, fortitude, Pl.R.426d; Id.Lg.942d, cf. Alc.1.122c; Plb.22.3.8; cf

εὐχερής.definition: tolerant of or indifferent to evil; unscrupulous, reckless, D.21.103, Arist.Metaph.1025a2. Adv. heedlessly, recklessly, D.18.70, cf. 264

εὐχετάομαι.definition: Ep. for only in pres. and impf; boast, profess, c. inf., Od.1.172, etc.; with inf. omitted, A.R.1.189, Orph.A.289; brag, . . Il.12.391; 17.19; 20.348; to glory over them, Od.22.412

εὔχομαι.definition: impf. Il.3.275, etc.: fut; c. acc. et inf., pray that, Od.15.353, 21.211, Hdt.1.31; of an unrealizable wish , Arist.EN1118a32, cf. Macho ap.Ath.8.341d: c. inf. alone, Il.2.401; . . Hdt.1.27; Pi.P.4.293, etc.; c. acc. …

εὐχρημάτιστος.definition: good man of business; richly endowed, Heph.Astr.1.1

εὐχρηστέω.definition: to be serviceable, for a thing; lend, advance, UPZ 123.26, Inscr.Prien.108.109

εὐχρηστία.definition: ready use, Arist.Oec.1345b1; service rendered, Inscr.Prien.105.25

εὔχρηστος.definition: also Orph.Fr.272; easy to execute, ib.18.4

εὐχροέω.definition: to be of a good, healthy look, Hp.Morb.2.1, Ar.Lys.80, Gal.17.215

εὔχροια.definition: Ion. goodness of complexion, fresh and healthy look, Hp.Coac.67, Arist.HA584a14, Thphr.Sud.39, Dsc.Eup.1.105, Aret.SA2.4

εὐχρωτέω.definition: imper. in an epitaph, = etc., IG14.2305

εὐχυλία.definition: goodness of flavour, Hices. ap. Ath.3.87c, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.57; wholesomeness of juice, Sor.1.53

εὔχυλος.definition: juicy, succulent, Thphr.CP6.11.15 , Archig. ap.Gal.12.460, etc.; of meat, Alex.189, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.62c, Hices. ib.7.282d: metaph., Phld.Po.1676 Fr. 11. Adv. Hp.Mul.1.17

εὐχυμία.definition: = Hp.Loc.Hom.10; Medic., healthy state of the humours, Gal.11.491, al

εὔχυμος.definition: well-flavoured, Posidon.3J; productive of healthy humours, wholesome, Hp.Aff.55, Gal.17.876

εὐχωλή.definition: Ep. form of prayer, vow; votive offering, Sammelb.1719, al

εὐχωλιμαῖος.definition: bound by a vow, under a vow; = Lat. ludi votivi, D.C.79.9

εὐψυχέω.definition: to be of good courage, Ep.Phil.2.19; farewell! a common inscr. on tombs, IG12.393 , etc

εὐψυχής.definition: agreeably cool, Hdn.6.6.4: Comp., Id.1.12.2, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.13.1: written Aët.5.74

εὐψυχία.definition: good courage, high spirit, A.Pers.326, E.Med.403, Th.1.121, etc.; goodness of soul, opp. Pl.Lg.791c

εὔψυχος.definition: of good courage, stout of heart; cooling, Thphr.CP5.14.1

εὕω.definition: aor. 1 , singe, esp. of singeing off the bristles of swine before they are cooked, Od.14.75, cf. 426, 2.300; Il.9.468; so of the Cyclops, Od.9.389: metaph., of a shrewish wife, . . Hes.Op.705 . , Od.2.300 , Hes.l.c.: …

εὐωδία.definition: Ion. sweet smell, Hdt.4.75, X.Smp.2.3, etc.; esp. of sacrifices, LXXGe.8.21: metaph. in Ep.Eph.5.2: in pl., Pl.Ti.65a: in pl., also, fragrant substances, D.S.1.84

εὐωδιάζω.definition: have a sweet savour, 'bouquet', LXXZa.9.17: c. acc. cogn., emit a sweet savour, ib.Si.39.14:—Pass., to be fragrant, Str.15.2.3, Dsc.2.76.8

εὐωδίζομαι.definition: perceive a sweet smell, S.E.M.7.293; ib.11.227

εὐώνυμος.definition: of good name, honoured; expressed in well-chosen terms, Luc.Lex.1

εὐωχέω.definition: fut. Thphr.Char.8.3: aor. 1; metaph., of other luxuries, Pl.Grg.518e; . . ib.522a ; so to entertain him with them, Thphr.Char.8.3:—Med., relish, enjoy, c. gen., Pl.R.352b

εὐωχία.definition: good cheer, feasting, Ar.Ach.1009; generally, supply of provisions for an army, Plb.3.92.9; plenty, Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.10

ἐφαιμάσσω.definition: make bloody, Orib.46.24.3, Cleopatra ap. Gal.12.404:—Pass., Cass.Pr.57

ἐφαιμορραγέω.definition: have secondary haemorrhage, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.52.1:—also Id.ib.50.51.1

ἐφαιρέω.definition: take hold on, overspread; Med. aor. 2 choose as successor, D.C.49.43:—Pass., to be chosen or appointed to succeed another, Th.4.38, cf. IG9.694.93

ἐφάλλομαι.definition: fut. LXX1 Ki.10.6: Ep. aor. 2 part. : regul. aor. 2 inf. IG4.951.27 :—spring upon, so as to attack, c. dat., Il.21.140, cf. 13.643; 11.489, etc.; ib.421, cf. Od.14.220: without hostile sense, c. gen., having leaped up…

ἐφαμαρτάνω.definition: causal, seduce to sin, LXXJe.39.35; abs., miss one's aim, Tryph.Trop.p.194 S

ἐφαμαρτέω.definition: = Herod.5.43; read by Aristarch. in Il.12.412, al

ἐφαμματίζω.definition: bind upon or together, Orib.49.22.23, cj. in Sor.Fasc.48

ἐφαμμίζω.definition: in Pass., become covered with sand, PTeb.60.42

ἐφανδάνω.definition: Ep. please, be grateful to, c. dat., Il.7.407; ib.45; Od.16.406: aor. Musae.180: c. inf., A.R.3.950, Orph.A.773

ἐφαπλόω.definition: spread or unfold over, Orph.A.1336: c. gen., . . Babr.95.2; . . Nonn.D.15.9: c. dat., ib.20.385; Orph.A.457: metaph., Hierocl.in CA21p.467M.:—Pass., to have the skin of the front feet spread over the hands, Longus1.20…

ἐφάπλωμα.definition: anything spread over, rug, cloak, Eust.1347.40

ἐφάπτω.definition: Ion. bind on or to; Med., aor. 1 3sg. Pi.P.8.63; lay hold of, once in Hom., Od.5.348, cf. Thgn.6, A.Supp.412, etc.; S.Aj.1172, etc.; E.El.1225 ; partake of food, Iamb.VP3.17; treat, Philostr.VA8.7; reach it, E.Hel.556…

ἐφάπτωρ.definition: also laying hold of, seizing; one who strokes or caresses, ib.312, 535

ἐφαρμογή.definition: adjustment, Plu.2.780b: Geom., of; agreement, Arr.Epict.1.22.2

ἐφαρμόζω.definition: Att. Dor. Theoc.1.53; intr., fit on or to, . . Il.19.385

ἐφέδρα.definition: Ion, sitting by or before a place; sitting upon, Pl.Plt.288a

ἐφεδράζω.definition: pf. part. set or rest upon; support, Id.7.8:—Pass., Sor.1.70

ἐφέδρανον.definition: that on which one sits; seat, Phryn.Trag.7

ἐφεδρεία.definition: sitting by, waiting for one's turn, of pugilists, etc., drawing 'byes', Pl.Lg.819b

ἐφεδρεύω.definition: sit upon, rest upon; occupy land, PStrassb.114.3

ἐφέδρευσις.definition: lying in wait, v.l. in Aq.Jb.37.3

ἐφεδρήσσω.definition: poet. for sit upon; sit by, AP7.161 : abs., Coluth.69:—also Id.15

ἐφεδρίζω.definition: sit or ride upon, in a game wherein the loser carried the winner on his back, title of play by Philemon

ἐφεδρισμός.definition: or the game itself, Poll.9.118, Hsch

ἐφεδριστήρ.definition: one who plays the game, Id.:—also Phot. s.v

ἔφεδρος.definition: sitting or seated upon, c. gen; firm seat, bench, Hp.Fract.8

ἐφέζομαι.definition: chiefly used in part. and 3sg. impf.; inf; sit by or near, c. acc., . . prob. for Id.Eu.446. cf

ἐφελίσσω.definition: aor. 1 part. dub. in D.23.161 , but found in Gal.18.7):—roll up, i.e. skip.., Gal. l. c.:—Med., wriggle behind one, Nic.Th.220:—Pass., to be rolled up, Paus.4.26.8

ἐφελκίς.definition: scab of a sore or wound, Aret.SD2.3, Gal.8.6, al., Archig. ap. eund.12.679

ἐφελκόομαι.definition: Pass., break out into sores, Hp.Epid.6.8.21

ἐφελκυσμός.definition: = foreg., Eust.52.24; suction, Sor.1.118; opp. Paul.Aeg.6.88

ἐφέλκω.definition: Ion. fut. E.HF632: aor. 1 inf; bring on, bring in its train , E.Med.552, cf. Ion1149, HF776 ; Pl.Phd.65e:—Med., AP10.37

ἐφέπω.definition: Ep. impf. iterat. Il.16.732; c. dat. pers., apply, direct towards or against, Il.16.732, cf. 724

ἐφερμηνεύω.definition: interpret, Philostr.VA3.25: abs., Philostr. Jun.Im.8, cf. Phlp.in APo.435.30

ἐφερπύζω.definition: later pres. for sq., Nic.Fr.74.41, AP9.231 , Orph.L.707, etc

ἐφέρπω.definition: fut. A.Eu.500 : aor. 1; poet., come on or over, come gradually or stealthily upon, A.Eu.314 ; E.Alc.269 : abs., A.Eu.943

ἐφεσπερεία.definition: keeping awake in the evening, Suid

ἐφεσπερεύω.definition: keep awake in the evening, Poll.1.71

ἐφεστιάζομαι.definition: feast, make merry. Hsch., Phot., Suid

ἐφέστιος.definition: generally, of or in the house or family, . . A.Th.853 ; Id.Ag.1310; Id.Eu.169 ; S.Tr.206 ; Id.Fr.866; E.El.216; the chambers of the house, A.Th.73: Ion. household, family, Hdt.5.72, 73; later D.H.1.24, POxy.2106.18

ἐφέτης.definition: commander, in pl., A.Pers.79; at Athens, the Ephetae, a court which tried cases of homicide under the IG12.115, Decr. ap. And.1.78, prob. in Arist.Ath.57.4, Lex ap.D.23.37, Harp

ἐφετμή.definition: poet. word, command, behest, Il.14.249; 21.299: freq. in pl., behests, esp. of the gods or one's parents, 5.508, Pi.O.3.11, etc.; Il.1.495, cf. Pi.P.2.21, A.Ch.300, E.IA634; demands, prayers, Pi.I.6.18

ἐφεύρεμα.definition: discovery, invention, in pl., Sch.E.Hec.627; artifices, tricks, IG22.1119.4

ἐφεύρεσις.definition: discovering, discovery, Sch.D.T.p.31 H., Just.Nov.84.1.1 , DavidProll.44.8

ἐφευρίσκω.definition: Ion. fut. aor. 2; discover besides, v.l. for in Od.19.158; Paus.3.12.10

ἐφεψιάομαι.definition: mock or scoff at, Od.19.331, cf. 370

ἐφέψω.definition: boil over again, Philoch.171:—Pass., boiling over, Pall.Febr.12

ἐφήβαρχος.definition: overseer of the youth, a magistrate in several Greek cities, OGI339.42 , IG12.134 , 12.524 , SIG798.23 , etc., cf. Arr.Epict.3.1.34, 7.19

ἐφηβαρχέω.definition: hold this office, CIG1957g , OGI583.10 , Not.Arch.4.189

ἐφηβάω.definition: Ion. come to man's estate, grow up to manhood, Hdt.6.83, A.Th.665, E.Fr.559, X.Cyr.6.1.12

ἐφηβεία.definition: youth, adolescence; ephebic training, IG22.1028.42, SIG 1109.130, etc

ἐφηβεύω.definition: to be an arrive at man's estate, Str.14.1.18, Paus.7.27.5, Artem.1.54; those who have undergone the ephebic training, IG22.665, etc., cf. Hp.Ep.25; = Hld.7.8

ἐφήβιος.definition: celebration on reaching adolescence, EM532.2; pubic, ossa Cael. Aur.CP3.140

ἔφηβος.definition: hyperdor. one arrived at; young girl, Hsch

ἐφηγέομαι.definition: lead to a place: c. dat. pers., esp. as Att. law-term, lead the magistrate to a place where a criminal lay concealed, whom the informer durst not seize himself, D.22.26, cf. 26.9, Poll.8.50

ἐφήγησις.definition: action against one who harboured a criminal, or concealed public property, AB187, Phot.,EM403.23, Suid., Zonar

ἐφήδομαι.definition: exult over, X.HG5.3.20, D.Chr.11.64, etc.; . . D.18.18; D.C.Fr.109.16: abs., X.Ages.7.5; D.15.21: rarely in good sense, Aristaenet.1.12

ἐφηδύνω.definition: sweeten, give a relish to, season; soothe, win over, Ph.1.566, cf. 2.268

ἐφήκω.definition: fut. S.El.304:—to have arrived, Id.Aj.34; so far as it reaches, so much space as it occupies, X.Lac.12.5

ἐφηλόω.definition: nail on, in Pass., Apollod.Poliorc.158.8, Ath.Mech.25.3: metaph., the bolt is driven home, i. e. it is irrevocably fixed, A.Supp.944; cf

ἔφημαι.definition: pf. Pass. used as a pres., to be; act as assessor (cf. A.Eu.629

ἐφημερευτής.definition: in pl., title of those who took their turn of serving their equals at a Jewish festival. Ph.2.481

ἐφημερεύω.definition: keep guard by day, Plb.21.27.6, IGRom.1.817; those cleaners who are now taking their turn of service in the temple, UPZ7.6 ; cf

ἐφημερέω.definition: to be president for the day, prob. in IG14.830.20

ἐφημερία.definition: division of the priests for the daily; the service itself, LXX1 Es.1.16

ἐφημέριος.definition: Dor. also Pi.N.6.6; for a day only, taking no thought for the morrow, Od.21.85; short- lived, Thgn.656; of men, creatures of a day, A.Pr.547 , Ar.Av.687; Ti.Locr.99d

ἐφημερίς.definition: diary, journal, esp. a military; day-book, account-book, PCornell1.2 , PCair.Zen.176.357 , Plu.2.829c. D.L.6.86; to profess philosophy for the ledger, Plu.2.999a

ἐφημερόβιος.definition: living for the day, from hand to mouth, Ph.2.389, cf. Ptol.Tetr.160

ἐφήμερον.definition: short-lived insect, the may-fly; a poisonous plant, Colchicum autumnale, Thphr.HP9.16.6, Nic.Al.250; = Dsc.4.83

ἐφήμερος.definition: for the day, daily, Hp.Aph.4.55; D.H.8.41, Ep.Jac.2.15, Vett.Val.62.17. cf. D.S.3.32 ; Ascl.Tact.1.4; Luc.Pseudol.17; Plu.Per.16, etc.: neut. pl. as Adv., once a day, Orib.Eup.1.9

ἐφησυχάζω.definition: remain quiet, Plb.2.64.5; acquiesce in, PLond.5.1708.261 ; Just.Nov.123.21 Intr

ἐφιαλτεία.definition: a herb used as a preventive of nightmare, Poet.de herb.162

ἐφιάλτης.definition: Aeol. Alc.129, also ibid.:—nightmare, conceived as a throttling demon, Phryn.Com.1, Dsc.3.140 , Artem.2.37, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.177, Str.1.2.8; pr. n. of one of the Aloidae, Il.5.385, Od.11.308, Pi.P.4.89 , and Att. pr…

ἐφιδρόω.definition: Ion. perspire in addition to or after, Hp.Epid.1.3 ; perspire slightly over the whole body or on the upper part only, Id.Prorrh.1.4, al., Gal.16.513:—Pass., perspire consecutively, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.23.6

ἐφίδρυσις.definition: planting firmly, in pl., of the feet, Ph.1.125

ἐφιδρύω.definition: place or set upon. ib.116:—Med. with pf. Pass., place oneself upon, mount, ib.21, al.: metaph., ib.114

ἐφιζάνω.definition: Acol. impf. Alc.Supp.28.7:—Hom. only in Il., always in impf., sit at or in, 10.578, v.l. in 20.11; sit upon, 10.26; Mosch.2.108: c. acc., A.R.1.667: later also in prcs., Aret.SA2.12; Philostr.Im.2.1, cf. Porph.Antr.19…

ἐφίζω.definition: Dor. Theoc.5.97; causal, in Ep. aor. upon, once in Hom. in Act., set me ashore, Od.13.274:—more freq. in Med., having set [me] on his knees, 16.443: fut. Il.9.455: imper., Od.15.277; 14.295 :— Med. also, reduce a disl…

ἐφίημι.definition: Ion. Dor. 3sg. Pi.I.2.9, Ion; in Hom., c. inf., set on, incite to do, Od.14.464; so Il.1.518, 18.108,124

ἐφικνέομαι.definition: Ion. fut. Xenoph.6.3; reach at, aim at, c. gen., of two combatants, Il.13.613; simply, reach or hit with a stick, Pl.Hp.Ma.292a; Isoc.12.227; D.25.101, cf. Plu.2.267c, etc.; Antiph.55.20; Luc.Nigr.36

ἐφιμείρω.definition: strengthd. for c. acc., Nic.Fr.74.42: c. gen., AP5.268 , Nonn.D.14.355: c. inf., Musae.80:— Med., in tmesi, Arat.975

ἐφιππάζομαι.definition: ride a tilt at, Cratin.358; ride upon, Luc.DMar.6.2; sens. obsc., Artem.1.79

ἐφιππαρχία.definition: double consisting of 1024 horse, Ascl.Tact.7.11, Arr.Tact.18.4, Suid. s.v

ἐφιππεύω.definition: ride against, attack with cavalry; ride upon, Babr.76.15

ἐφίππιος.definition: for putting on a horse; horse-course, a course of a certain length so called, Pl.Lg.833b

ἔφιππος.definition: on horseback, riding, Eup.27; a rushing wave of horses, S.El.733

ἐφίπταμαι.definition: late pres. of Mosch.1.16, Arist.Mir.841b31, J.AJ1.10.3, 3.1.5, Plu.Cleom.39, Porph.Abst.1.25

ἐφιστάνω.definition: late form for set over; stop, check, v.l. in Dsc.4.16

ἐφίστημι.definition: set over, A.Ag.1202; Id.Supp.303; Hdt.5.27; Pl.Alc.1.122b, cf. X.Lac.2.1; Id.An.5.1.15; Isoc.2.27; Arist.Pol.1292b28; Plb.2.65.9; Id.10.20.5; D.26.22; Id.18.112: c. inf., Isoc.7.37:—Pass., to be appointed, instituted,…

ἐφοδεία.definition: going the rounds, visiting; making a round of visits, SIG656.26

ἐφοδευτής.definition: one who goes the rounds: spy, Aq.Ge.42.9

ἐφοδεύω.definition: go the rounds, X.HG2.4.24, 5.3.22; rarely c. dat., superintend, watch over, A.Ch.728

ἐφοδιάζω.definition: Ion. furnish with supplies for a; generally, supply or furnish with a thing, D.S.5.34; also Apollod.Poliorc.138.1

ἐφόδιον.definition: mostly in pl. Ion. (v; less freq. in sg., Epich.[261]; Th.2.70; . . X.An.7.3.20; D.19.158, cf. SIG390.58 : metaph., Hyp.Epit.27; . . Men.472, cf. 360, 792; Phld.Lib.p.180.; Plu.Alex.8; Id.2.8c; Artem.4.67

ἐφόδιος.definition: for a journey, EM348.43; on the road, accessible, BGU1116.8

ἔφοδος.definition: accessible, f.l. for Th.6.66 , Polyaen.1.49; one who goes the rounds, X.Cyr.8.6.16

ἐφόλκιον.definition: small boat towed after a ship, Moschio; generally, appendage, AP7.67 , Plu.Pomp.40; of a verse or phrase, Aristid.2.23 J., 330 J.; = sq. 2, Men.Pk.380

ἐφολκίς.definition: = foreg. I, Ach. Tat.3.3; = foreg. 2, burdensome appendage, E.Andr.200, cf. HF631, 1424 , Ael.Fr.110

ἐφομαρτέω.definition: accompany, come on , abs., Il.8.191, 12.412, 23.414 , Nic.Al.479: c. dat., A.R.1.201: rare in Prose, as Arr.An.1.19.2

ἐφομιλέω.definition: live with or among, c. acc., dub. in Hermesian.7.51: c. dat., Nonn.D.5.410

ἐφοπλίζω.definition: get ready, of meals; arm against, Opp.C.3.244:—Med., AP9.39 , cf. APl.4.151.9

ἐφοράω.definition: Ion.3sg. inf. Hdt.1.10, 3.53; Astrol., = III, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.126

ἐφορεία.definition: office of ephor, X.Lac.8.3; frontier, Hecat.217 J

ἐφορεῖον.definition: office or court of the ephors, X.Ages.1.36, Plu.2.232f

ἐφορεύω.definition: = c. acc., A.Supp.627 , 677; to be ephor, Th.8.6, X.HG1.3.1, Abh.Berl.Akad. 1925.8 , Tab.Heracl.1.122

ἐφορμαίνω.definition: rush on, A.Pers.208, cf. Orph.H.33.5, 74.7; upon or against one, Opp.C.3.367

ἐφορμάω.definition: Ion. stir up, rouse against one; intr., rush upon, attack, E.Hipp.1275 , Plu.Pomp.19, etc.; D.C.36.24: abs., Plb.8.6.1: c. inf., desire, Opp.H.2.94, Orph.L.34; f.l. for in X.HG1.6.21.—This use is more freq. in Pass

ἐφορμέω.definition: Ion. lie moored at or over against a place, blockade it, having escaped the blockading fleet, Hdt.8.81, cf. Th.8.75, X.An.7.6.25; Th.4.24: c. dat., Id.7.3, cf. 3.31; Id.8.30; X.HG6.2.7; Plb.1.46.5: c. acc., App.BC5.72…

ἐφορμή.definition: way of attack, only room for one to attack, Od.22.130, cf. A.R.4.148, Opp.H.4.623; assault, attack, Th.6.90; enterprise, A.R.4.204

ἐφόρμησις.definition: lying at anchor so as to watch an enemy, blockading, Th.2.89, 8.15; means of so doing, Id.6.48; Id.3.33

ἐφορμίζω.definition: bring a ship to her moorings, bring; intr. in Act., seek refuge in, AP9.244 , cf. 254

ἐφυβρίζω.definition: insult over one, Il.9.368; exult maliciously, S.Aj.955

ἐφύβριστος.definition: wanton, insolent, Vett. Val.71.18; Pass., contemptible, LXXWi.17.7. Adv. Posidon.7 J

ἐφυγραίνομαι.definition: Pass., become moist: of the bowels, to be relaxed, Hp.Epid.1.10

ἔφυγρος.definition: moist on the surface, Arist.Pr.935a28; ib.896a17: Comp., Thphr.CP2.4.7

ἔφυδρος.definition: Ion. moist, rainy, of; abounding in water, Hdt.4.198, cf. Hp.Aër.1, Arist.Mete.347a31, Dsc.1.15

ἐφυμνέω.definition: sing or chant at or after; of music, sound in accord, S.Fr.412

ἐφυμνιάζω.definition: sing as the refrain, Eratosth. ap. Sch.Pi.O.9.1

ἐφύμνιον.definition: burden, refrain, of a hymn, A.R.2.713, Call.Ap.98, Sos.8.4, Ph.1.535, Ath.15.701c, Sch.Pi.O.9.1

ἐφυστερέω.definition: to be late, in arrear, J.AJ19.1.5, cf. 18.9.3; to be deferred, Sor.1.21, Gal.7.471: c. gen., to be left behind by, Alex.Aphr.in Mete.31.28

ἐφυστερίζω.definition: come later, come after, = Th.3.82, cf. D.H.Th.29; to be deferred, overdue, Gal.7.471

ἐφύω.definition: rain upon: impers. c. dat., Thphr.HP4.14.8, etc.: abs., it rains after, Id.CP6.17.7:—pf. part. Pass. exposed to rain, X.Cyn.9.5

ἐχεδερμία.definition: being hide-bound, of horses, Hippiatr.26: = Lat. coriago, Veget.Mulom.2.118

ἐχεδημία.definition: = Academia , coined by Dicaearch. ap. Plu.Thes.32

ἐχέθυμος.definition: a master of one's passions, under self- control, Od.8.320:— Subst. is v.l. for in Ph.2.267

ἐχέκολλος.definition: glutinous, sticky, Hp.Art.33 ; Plu.2.966d; ib.735f; takes glue best, Thphr.HP5.6.2. Adv. Dsc.5.153

ἐχεμυθέω.definition: to hold one's peace, Ph.1.309, al., J.BJ1.24.1, Luc.DDeor.21.2; things unspoken, Iambl.Protr.21; a Pythagorean word, Id.VP20.94

ἐχεμυθία.definition: silence, reserve, Plu.Num.8, cf. 2.728d, Ph.2.267 , Alciphr.3.55, Ath.7.308d, Iamb.VP6.32, etc

ἐχενηΐς.definition: a small fish, supposed to have the power of holding ships back, Arist.HA505b19, Opp.H.1.212, Plin.HN9.79; in form = Lat. remora, Donat.ad Ter.Andr. 739, Eun.302

ἐχενίκειον.definition: endowment created by Echenice, Inscr. Délos 370.42:—hence festival maintained thereby, ib.366A 133

ἐχεπάμων.definition: gen. holding property: hence, heir or representative, IG9.334.16

ἐχεπευκής.definition: sharp, piercing, Il.1.51,4.129: expld. by Eust., etc., as bitter, and so later Nic.Th.600; ib.866, cf. Orph.L.475

ἐχέτλη.definition: plough-handle, Hes.Op.467, A.R.3.1325, AP7.650 , D.S.9.7, Alciphr.3.19, Luc.JTr.31:—hence plough, Hsch

ἐχέφρων.definition: gen. sensible, prudent, Il.9.341, cf. Od.13.332; freq. as epith. of Penelope, 4.111, etc.; later of animals, Nonn.D.16.226: late in Prose, Syn.Alch.p.65 B. Adv. D.S.15.33

ἐχθαίρω.definition: Dor. 3pl. Theoc.24.29: impf. E.Supp.879: aor. 1 Il.20.306, A.Pers.772, etc.; Dor. Timocr.1.4:—Med., Ep. aor. 1 in act. sense, Nic.Al.618, cf. —Pass., S.Aj.458: fut. Med. in pass. sense, Id.Ant.93: :—hate, detest, Il.9…

ἔχθιστος.definition: Sup. of most hateful; most hostile, Th.2.71; Id.7.68: c. gen., his bitterest enemies, X.An.3.2.5: Luc. has also Trag.246

ἐχθίων.definition: gen. Comp. of more hateful, A.Pers.438, S.OT272, E.El.222, Ar.Av.370, Th.4.86, Pl.Ly.214c. Adv. X.Smp.4.3

ἐχθοδοπέω.definition: show enmity towards, engage in hostility with, Il.1.518

ἔχθρα.definition: Ion. hatred, enmity, Hdt.5.81, Pi.P.4.145, etc.: in philos. sense, = I.5, Plot.3.2.2; hatred for, enmity to one, Antipho2.4.1, Th.3.10; Ar.Pax133; Hdt.1.5, Th.2.68; Ep.Rom.8.7; A.Pr.491 , Th.2.68; to be at feud with o…

ἐχθραίνω.definition: impf. X.Ages.11.5: aor. 1; make hateful or hostile, Max.l.c

ἐχθρεύω.definition: to be at enmity with, LXXEx.23.22, al., Phld.Rh.2.134 S., Tz.H.1.671

ἐχθροδαίμων.definition: gen. hated of the gods, S.OT816

ἐχθρόξενος.definition: hostile to strangers, inhospitable, A.Pr.727, cf. Th.606,621; E.Alc.558

ἐχθροποιέω.definition: make hostile, App.BC5.60, cf. Hsch.:—Pass., Ptol.Tetr.191

ἔχθω.definition: hate, A.Fr.353; S.Ph.510 , E.Med.117 ; S.Aj.459: c. dupl.acc., E.Andr.212:—Hom. only in Pass., Od.4.502; . . ib.756; 19.338; 14.366; A.Ag.417 ; E.Hipp.1402.—Only pres. and impf., exc. pf. part. Pass. Lyc.827: the form…

ἔχιδνα.definition: viper, Hdt.3.108, S.Tr.771; pr. n. of a monster, Hes.Th.297, S.Tr.1099

ἐχιδναῖος.definition: of or like a viper, AP7.71; snaky, Nonn.D.14.216

ἐχιδνότοκος.definition: born of a viper, Anon.Prog.9inRh.1.626 W

ἐχινομήτρα.definition: the largest kind of sea-urchin, Echinus melo, Arist.HA530b6

ἐχινόπους.definition: kind of prickly-plant, Genista acanthoclada, perh. the same as Eleg. ap. Plu.2.44e , cf. Hsch.s.v. EM405.12

ἐχμάζω.definition: hold fast, hinder, Eust.904.4, Sch.E.Or.265, Hsch.; cf

ἐχυρότης.definition: strength, Ph.2.116, cf. 120, 1.478 , 688, J.AJ15.11.4. in Ph.1.644 shd. be restored.)

ἐχυρόω.definition: make secure, fortify, Phot., Suid.; is v.l. for Isoc.5.122

ἔχω.definition: possess, of property, the most common usage, Od.2.336, 16.386, etc.; the propertied class, Hdt.6.22; a wealthy man, S.Aj.157 ; E.Alc.57, Ar.Eq.1295, Pl.596; the poor, E.Supp.240; Id.Ph.405; to have debts due to one, D…

ἑψάνδρα.definition: cooking up men, epith. of Medea, from her renewing old Aeson, AP15.26.5

ἕψημα.definition: anything boiled: in pl., vegetables; mash, Thphr.HP4.4.10

ἕψησις.definition: boiling, Hp.VM5; Hdt.4.61, cf. SIG57.34 ; PTeb.406.22 ; smelting of ore, Thphr.HP5.9.1; concoction, softening, Gal.13.415, Aret.SA2.6: pl., Pl.Plt.303e

ἑψητήρ.definition: dish or pan for boiling, AP6.305

ἑψία.definition: Ion. amusement, S.Fr.3; plaything, Nic.Th.880: pl., EM406.8; Hsch

ἑψιάομαι.definition: Ep. Verb, amuse oneself, Od.17.530; 21.429; . . A.R.3.118, cf. 1.459, Call.Dian.3, Cer.39, Nonn.D.10.326 ap. Sch.A.R.3.118; but cf

ἕψω.definition: impf. Ar.Ra.505, al.: fut. Nicoch.15; digest, Hp.Acut.28

ἕω.definition: Ion. subj. aor. 2 of; gen. and acc. of , the dawn

ἑωλίζω.definition: keep till next day; Pass., to be or become stale, of grain, Gal.6.518

ἑωλισμός.definition: keeping till next day, of food, Ruf. ap. Orib.4.2.7

ἑωλοκρασία.definition: mixture of dregs, heel-taps, etc., with which the drunken were dosed at the end of a revel by their stronger headed companions: metaph., having discharged the stale dregs of his rascality over me, D.18.50, cf. Harp., …

ἐωρέω.definition: = prob. in S.OC1084 , cf. Hsch., Dosith.p.431 K

ἐγγύθεν.definition: Adv., from nigh at hand; with Verbs of rest, hard by, Il.10.508; Od.6.279

ἐγγύθι.definition: Adv. hard by, near, in Ep. mostly c. gen; of Time, nigh at hand, Il.10.251

ἐγγύς.definition: of Place, near, nigh, at hand: freq. in Hom., Od.10.86: c. gen., hard by, near to; so nearer to grief, S.OC1217: c. dat., Il.11.340, E.Heracl.37; dub. in IG12.974: mostly with Verbs of rest, A.Pers.686, Eu.65; but Id.…

ἐγερτί.definition: Adv. eagerly, busily, S.Ant.413; wakefully, Heraclit.63, E.Rh.524

ἐγκάς.definition: Adv. deep in, prob. in Hp.VC5, cf. Gal.19.94

ἐγκαταμεμιγμένως.definition: Adv. in a mixed manner, Sch.rec.S.OT95

ἐγκεκλιμένως.definition: Adv. with the accent thrown back, Sch.Il.1.277, 6.289

ἐγκλιδόν.definition: Adv. leaning, bent down, h.Hom.23.3; aslant or askance, A.R.3.1008; AP5.249

ἐγκονητί.definition: Adv. actively, vigorously, by perseverance, Pi.N.3.36

ἐγκυτί.definition: Adv., to the skin, close shaven, Archil.37, cf. Call.Fr.311. Archil., Call.]

ἐγρηγορότως.definition: Adv. part. of waking, Plu.2.32a, Luc.Herm.1 , Porph.Plot.9

ἐθελοντηδόν.definition: Adv. voluntarily, spontaneously, Th.8.98, D.C.53.8; f.l. for sq., Plb.6.31.2

ἐθελοντήν.definition: Adv. voluntarily, Hdt.1.5, X.Mem.2.1.3, Plb.1.49.5, al

ἐθνηδόν.definition: Adv. by nations, as a whole nation, LXX4 Ma.2.19

εἶα.definition: an exclamation used to cheer or urge on, on! up! away! used with the imper. sg. or pl., cf. E.Med.820, etc.; come then! A.Ag.1650, Ar.Th.659; well now! Id.Pax467; Id.Ra.396; E.HF622, Ar.Pl.760; Id.Pax459; ib.468; . . …

εἰδότως.definition: Adv. of knowingly, Aeschin.1.111; as one who knows, scientifically, Arist.Ph.188a5

εἶθαρ.definition: Adv. at once, forthwith, Il.5.337, Theoc.25.213, Antim.16.5, A.R.2.408, Nic.Th.547

εἰθισμένως.definition: Adv., in the accustomed manner, Arcesil. ap. D.L.4.35

εἰκότως.definition: Adv. of Att. pf. part. of suitably, c. dat., A.Ag.915; fairly, reasonably, Id.Supp.403 , S.OC432, 977, Isoc.12.101, etc.; 'tis reasonable, E.IT911, cf. Or.737 ; And.1.140, cf. 142; unreasonably, Th.1.37: folld. by ib.…

εἰληδόν.definition: by twisting or coiling round, AP9.14.6

εἰνάνυχες.definition: as Adv., nine nights long, Il.9.470; cf

εἰρομένως.definition: Adv. running on: in order, PSI4.439 ; in continuation, Apollon.Cit.2

εἰσάντα.definition: Adv. right opposite: looking in the face, Il.17.334; Od.11.143; 5.217:—also B.5.110

εἰσόπιν.definition: Adv. back: c. gen., hereafter, A.Supp.617

εἶτα.definition: Ion. , Adv., used to; of Sequence in time, without any notion of Cause, then, next, .., .. S.El.262, cf. Pl.Phdr.251a, etc.; soon, presently, S.OT452; well, what then? Ar.Nu.347, Pl.Prt.309a; .. then.. after that, Ar.…

εἰωθότως.definition: Adv. of , in customary wise, S.El.1456, Aristid.Or.51.48, etc.; in his usual manner, Pl.Smp.218d

ἕκαθεν.definition: Adv., from afar, Il.2.456; = far off, far away, Od.17.25

ἑκάς.definition: Adv. afar, far off, Il.20.422, etc; Comp. farther, Od.7.321, h.Bacch.29, Alc.Supp.5.8 , Hdt.6.108, E.HF1047 , etc.: c. gen., Hdt.2.169, al.; also dub. in Theoc.15.7: Sup. farthest, Il.10.113, Hdt.4.33: c. gen., farthe…

ἑκαστάκις.definition: Adv., each or every time, IG9.694.8 ; = ib.22: GDI 3051

ἑκαστάχη.definition: Adv. everywhere, Suid.; f.l. for in X.Cyr.6.2.5

ἑκασταχόθεν.definition: Adv. from every side, Th.7.20,21, X.HG3.4.3

ἑκασταχόθι.definition: Adv. = on each side, Plu.Lys.19, PLips.119r

ἑκασταχοῖ.definition: Adv. to each side, every way, Plu.Mar.20, Hdn.Gr.1.502

ἑκασταχόσε.definition: Adv. to each side, Th.4.55, 8.5, Pl.Criti.116a

ἑκάστοθι.definition: Adv. for each or every one, Od.3.8 , Aen.Tact.11.11

ἑκάστοτε.definition: Adv. each time, on each occasion, Parm.16.1, Hdt.1.90, Antipho6.13, X.An.2.4.10, Pl.R.393b; .. Ar.Nu.1280; Pl.Phlb.58a; wherever on each occasion, Hdt.8.115

ἑκατεράκις.definition: Adv., at each time, X.Cyr.4.6.4; in both directions, Gal.UP8.7

ἑκατέρη.definition: Cret. Adv. on either side, Schwyzer197.4 ; ib.186.18

ἑκατέρωθεν.definition: Adv. on each side, on either hand; on both sides, by father and mother, Poll.8.85

ἑκατέρωθι.definition: Adv. on either side, Pi.O.2.69, Hdt.2.19,106, Arist.Ath.54.8, etc

ἑκατέρως.definition: Adv. in either way, Pl.Lg.895e, Ph.1.316; in both languages, i.e. Greek and Latin, Inscr.Prien.105.30

ἑκατέρωσε.definition: Adv. to either side, either way; both ways, Id.Phd.112e; Id.R.619a

ἐκεῖ.definition: Aeol. Sapph.51; Dor; Philos., in the intelligible world, Plot.1.2.7, 2.4.5, etc

ἐκεῖθεν.definition: poet. (the only form used by Hom., also; by attraction for S.OC1227 codd

ἐκεῖσε.definition: poet. (the only form in Hom., used by; to the other world, E.Alc.363; from this world to the other, Pl.Phd.117c

ἐκκειμένως.definition: Adv. openly, to be open, frank, Philostr.VS2.17

ἐκκεχυμένως.definition: Adv.pf.part.Pass. of profusely, extravagantly, Isoc.15.207; without reserve, Pl.Euthphr.3d; Aristaenet.2.16; Just.Nov.74.4

ἐκκριδόν.definition: Adv. apart, alone, prob.l. in Tryph.224

ἐκλελυμένως.definition: Adv.pf.part.Pass. of loosely, carelessly, Isoc.Ep.6.6; Plu.Lyc.18; freely, licentiously, Ath.12.519f

ἑκοντήν.definition: Adv. = foreg., Theognost.Can.161.24, Arr. ap. Suid.,SIG880.48 . —The remark of Phryn. I refers not to this Adv., but to a Noun used by Epict.Gnom.67; IPE12.40.21

ἑκοντί.definition: Adv. willingly, Ps.-Phoc.16, Them.Or.16.209a; but may generally be read, Arist.Rh.Al.1431b20, Plu.Comp.Eum.Sert.2

ἔκπαλαι.definition: Adv. for for a long time, Ph.1.323, 2 Ep.Pet.3.5, J.AJ16.8.4, Plu.2.548d, Plot.6.4.14, POxy.938.3 , etc

ἐκπεπληγμένως.definition: Adv., to be in a state of panic, D.Prooem.39.1

ἐκπέρυσι.definition: Adv. more than a year ago, Luc.Sol.7

ἐκποδών.definition: Adv., opp. away from the feet, i.e. out of the way, away, depart and get away, Hdt.8.76; stand aside, A.Ch.20; E.Hel.1023, etc.; Hdt.6.35; X.HG6.5.38; A.Pr.346, S.Ant.1321 ; Ar.Ach.305; Id.Ra.853: abs., out of the way…

ἔκποθεν.definition: Adv. from some place or other, A.R.2.224, 824; Q.S.3.437: Id.9.420, 14.74

ἐκπορθητικῶς.definition: Adv. with a view to plundering completely, Eust.1490.65

ἐκτάδην.definition: Adv., outstretched, lie outstretched, i.e. dead, E.Ph.1698, Luc.DMort.7.2

ἔκτοθεν.definition: Adv., Ep. for = from; abs., outside, without, A.Ch.473 ; S.El.802; marry from an alien house, E.Andr.975; things abroad, is dub. in Od.9.239

ἔκτοθι.definition: Ep. Adv., out of, outside, far from; simply, from, ib.1291

ἔκτοσε.definition: Adv. outwards: c. gen., out of, Od.14.277

ἔκτοτε.definition: Adv. for thereafter, Socr.Rhod.1, Arr.An.1.26.4, Plu.Caes.48, POxy.486.9 , Vett.Val.168.28, Sm.Is.16.13, Sch.D.T.p.427 H.: condemned by Luc.Sol.7

ἐλασσόνως.definition: Adv. of in a lesser degree, Hp.Vict.1.35, etc.; Antipho4.4.6

ἐλαττονάκις.definition: Adv. fewer times, multiplied by a less; less frequently, Arist.Mete.368b25

ἑλικηδόν.definition: Adv. = spirally, ib.1; revolving in a circle, Nonn.D.1.195

Ἑλληνιστί.definition: Adv. in the Greek language, Pl.Ti.21e, PTaur.1v4 , Ph.2.546, J.AJ14.10.2, etc.; to understand Greek, X.An.7.6.8; Act.Ap.21.37; in Greek fashion, Luc.Scyth.3

ἔμβραχυ.definition: Adv. in brief, in fine, in Att. with relat; slightly, somewhat, Gal.18.410

ἐμμαπέως.definition: Adv., quickly, hastily, Il.5.836; Od.14.485, h.Ven.180; Hes.Sc.442

ἔμπαλιν.definition: Adv., in Trag. and Prose freq. with Art; as before and vice versa, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.154.28

ἐμπεφυκότως.definition: Adv. clinging firmly, gloss on Sch.Theoc.15.68, cf. Hsch. s.v

ἐμπλέγδην.definition: Adv. by interlocking: hence in Math. of proportion, alternando, Nicom.Ar.2.29

ἐμπλήδην.definition: Adv. fully, as a whole, Nic.Al.129

ἔμπλην.definition: Adv. near, next, close by, c. gen., Il.2.526; before its case, Lyc.1029: abs., Hes.Sc.372

ἐμποδιζομένως.definition: Adv. pres. part. Pass., as if fettered, Pl.Cra.415c

ἐμποδών.definition: Adv. perh. formed by anal. to; in one's way, i.e. presenting an hindrance, . . Hdt.6.82; when all impediments had been cleared away, Id.7.183; Ar.Lys.1161; A.Pr.13; Id.Th.1021; S.OT445; E.Ion1047; Ar.Pax473; E.Hec.372…

ἔμπροσθα.definition: Adv., Aeol. and Dor. for sq., Tab.Heracl.1.57, 101, A.D.Adv.153.17

ἔμπροσθεν.definition: sts. also Hdt.5.62, 7.144, al; of Place, before, in front, Hdt.7.126, X.Cyr.4.2.23; and the front, the foreside, Id.HG2.3.55, Hdt.5.62, etc.; forwards, Id.4.61; in front, opposite, X.Cyr.2.2.6: metaph., Isoc.l.c

ἐνάκις.definition: Ep. Adv. nine times, Od.14.230:—usu.written in codd.: is v.l. in Nicom.Harm.8: also AP14.120.8; Iamb.in Nic.p.17P

ἐναλλάγδην.definition: Adv. = AP5.301.16 , Man.4.181, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.30, Agath.1.12,al

ἐναλλάξ.definition: Math., alternando, Arist.EN1131b6, APo.74a18,99a8; permutando, Euc.5 Def.12

ἐναμοιβαδίς.definition: Adv. = alternately or one after another, A.R.1.380, 4.1030

ἔναντα.definition: Adv. opposite, over against, c.gen., Il.20.67; Pi.N.10.66; S.Ant.1299 ; E.Or.1478

ἔναντι.definition: Adv. in the presence of, c. gen., LXXGe.12.19, al., IG7.2225.52 , Ev.Luc.1.8, GDI2072.26 ; cf

ἐναντιοζύγως.definition: Adv. in an opposite series, Theol.Ar.11

ἐναντιπέρα.definition: Adv. on the opposite side, Epigr. Gr.981.6

ἐναπομεμαγμένως.definition: Adv. by a distinct impression, Stoic.2.31

ἐνδεινῶς.definition: Adv. terribly: Comp. dub. in Them.Or.4.56a

ἑνδεκάκις.definition: parox.], Adv. eleven times, Arist.HA562b25, Theo Sm.p.126H

ἐνδεχομένως.definition: Adv. of foreg., = Decr. ap. D.18.165, Plb.1.20.4, al., D.S.20.26, LXX2 Ma.13.26, etc.; PPetr.2p.53; to the best of his ability, Aristeas41

ἐνδιεσπαρμένως.definition: Adv., in scattered passages, Eun.VSp.454 B

ἔνδοθεν.definition: gen., from inside the tent, S.Aj.741; of oneself, by one's own doing, A.Th.194; neither of oneself nor by help of others, S.Tr.1021

ἔνδον.definition: Adv. within, Il.11.98, etc; master of oneself, self-possessed, Antipho5.45; so E.Heracl.709: abs., A.Ch.233

ἐνδυκέως.definition: Adv. sedulously, kindly, freq. in Hom. (esp; steadfastly, B.5.125, cf. 112

ἐνενίαυτα.definition: Adv., in the course of the year, BGU920.18

ἔνερθε.definition: and Dor. A.D.Adv.153.17; also; Adv. from beneath, up from below, Il.20.57; A.Pers.630; E.Alc.1139, cf. 985 ; Id.Hel.966

ἐνηλλαγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of; crosswise, = Procop.Gaz.p.163B

ἔνθα.definition: of Place, there, Il.14.216, etc.: also with Verbs of motion, thither, 13.23, 14.340, Od.3.297, 6.47, 12.5; hither and thither, 2.213, etc.; LXX4 Ki.2.8; also Od.10.574: rare in Trag. and Com., A.Supp.33 ; Ar.Av.1556: …

ἐνθάδε.definition: after Hom. more freq., = here or there, Ar.V.765; in this world, opp. the nether-world, Pi.O.2.57, Pl.Grg.525b; Ar.Ra.82; opp. A.Supp.923, S.Ant.75; also, the people of this country, Id.OC42; ib.78; Eup.357; opp. Th.6.17

ἔνθαπερ.definition: Adv. there where, where, stronger form of Il.13.524, Hdt.1.14, Th.6.32, X.Lac.5.7,al.; to the place where, S.El.1495, Ph.515

ἔνθεν.definition: Demonstr., thence; of Place, Il.10.179, etc.: also in tracing pedigrees, 4.58; . . . . on the one side and on the other, Od.12.235, cf. 59; E.Hec.1152; on this side and on that, Hdt.4.175, Th.7.81, Pl.Prt.315b, etc.; …

ἐνθένδε.definition: Adv. hence, Il.8.527, Od.11.69, etc.; from; of Time or Consequence, from that time, Th.2.1; or thereafter, S.Ph.895, E.IT91; or what followed, the event, Id.Med.1167, cf. S.OT1267, El.1307

ἐνιαχῆ.definition: Adv., in some places, c. gen; sometimes, Plu.2.427f, Ath.11.478b

ἐνιαχοῦ.definition: Adv., in some places, Arist.HA545a32, D.H.Rh.5.7, etc.; in some cases, Pl.Phd.71b, Jul.Gal.152d; sometimes, BGU747ii9

ἐνίοτε.definition: Adv. at times, sometimes, E.Hel.1213, Ar.Pl.1125, Hp.Praec.14, etc.; . ., . . Pl.Grg.467e; . . . . Id.Tht.150a; . . . . Id.Phlb.46e; . . . . Arist.Mete.360b2

ἐννῆμαρ.definition: Ep. Adv. for nine days, Il.1.53, al

ἐνοικί.definition: Adv. in the house, at home, Hdn.Epim.255

ἐνταυθοῖ.definition: Adv. hither, come and lie down here, Il.21.122; Od.18.105, 20.262; here, Arist.Ph.229b28, cf. D.27.54: freq. with or without v.l. in Com. and Prose, Cratin.37, Ar.Ra.273, Lys.568, al., Pl.Ap.18d, 33d, al., Antipho5.2,…

ἐντετριμμένως.definition: Adv., adroitly, 'like an old hand', Poll.5.144

ἐντεῦθεν.definition: Ion. Adv., (related to as; of Place, hence or thence, Od.19.568, Hdt.1.2, al., A.Pr.836, Pers.488, Th.8.42, etc.; Pl.Euthd.271c; matters there, i.e. in the house, S.El.1339; LXXNu.22.24, Ev.Jo.19.18; Sch.D.T.p.29H.; '…

ἐντυπάς.definition: Adv., once in Hom., Il.24.163 lying wrapt up in his mantle so closely as to show the contour of his limbs , cf. Sch.ad loc., Hsch.; A.R.1.264, cf. 2.861, Q.S.5.530, Epic.in Arch.Pap.7p.3

ἐνωπαδίως.definition: Adv., in one's face, to one's face, Od.23.94

ἑξάκις.definition: Adv., six times, Pi.O.7.86, Pl.R.337b, etc.:—also cj. in Simon.156, Call.Fr.120, AP14.129 , 141 , CIG2834.4

ἐξαρκούντως.definition: Adv. pres. part. of enough, sufficiently, Ar.Ra.377 Isoc.12.8; is content with . ., Pl.Grg.493c

ἐξαῦτις.definition: Ep. Adv. once more, anew, Il.1.223, etc; of place, back again, backwards, Il.16.654, A.R.3.482

ἑξαχῇ.definition: Adv. in six parts, Pl.Ti.36d; in six ways, Ph.1.44:—also Hdn.Gr.1.496

ἑξαχῶς.definition: Adv. in six ways, Arist.Top.112b27, Gal.9.702

ἐξεζητημένως.definition: Adv., exquisitely, in a recherché manner, Gloss

ἐξειργασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of carefully, accurately, Plu.Alex.1

ἐξέναντι.definition: Adv. right opposite, BMus.Inscr.918 , cf. TAM2.210

ἐξεπίτηδες.definition: Adv. = on purpose, Hp.Art.47; with malice prepense, D.21.56, 187, Phld.Lib.p.62 O

ἐξέτι.definition: Prep. with gen., . . ever since the time when . ., Il.9.106; from our fathers' time, Od.8.245; A.R.4.791; Call.Ap.104; IG14.1549: also in late Prose, App.BC2.86, Ael.NA5.39; Ph.2.94

ἐξηλλαγμένως.definition: Adv., strangely, unusually, D.S.2.42, Plu.2.745f, S.E.M.8.187, Iamb.Protr.5, etc

ἑξῆμαρ.definition: Adv. for six days, six days long, Od.10.80, 14.249

ἐξημαρτημένως.definition: Adv., wrongly, to no purpose, Pl.Lg.891d

ἐξητασμένως.definition: Adv., after full investigation, deliberately, M.Ant.1.16, Them.Or.16.203c; with deliberate precision , Ph.1.605, al., Aristid.Or.45.4

ἐξονομακλήδην.definition: Adv. by name, Il.22.415; Od.4.278; 12.250; Critias6.8 D

ἐξόπιθεν.definition: and Adv., Ep. for; Prep. with gen., behind, Il.17.521

ἐξόπισθεν.definition: poet. Adv., Att. for; Prep. with gen., Ar.Ach.868, LXX3 Ki.19.21; S.Fr.598

ἔξωθεν.definition: rarely Diog.Oen.18, Adv., from; = Hdt.1.70, Pl.Ti.33c, etc.; those outside, Hdt.9.5, etc. ; Aeschin.2.5; matters outside the house, opp. A.Th.201, cf. E.El.74, etc.; foreign states, Pl.Plt.307e; foreign to the subject…

ἐοικότως.definition: Att. Ion. Adv. of part; reasonably, fairly, naturally, as was to be expected, Hdt.2.25, A.Supp.403 ; unfairly, Th.1.37; freq. emphat. at the close of a sentence or clause, ib.77,2.93, Isoc.1.48, etc

ἐπαινουμένως.definition: Adv. pres. part. Pass., praiseworthily, D.S.16.88

ἐπαλλάξ.definition: Adv., = crosswise, Hp.Nat. Mul.5, X.Eq.1.7; alternately, D.S.19.30

ἐπαμοιβαδίς.definition: Adv., interchangeably: hence so thick they grew with interwoven boughs, Od.5.481, cf. A.R.4.1030 :—in Hsch. also

ἐπάν.definition: Conj., later form of , Arist.Ath.42.2, Thphr.Char.24.10, IG22.1298.18 , Plb.2.2.9, Agatharch.32, Str.10.4.20, etc.: c. ind. in late Greek, Sch.Luc.Peregr.9 Men.223.2, Alex.269.]

ἐπάνωθεν.definition: or Adv. above, on top; up country, inland, Th.2.99

ἐπεί.definition: Conj., both temporal and causal; also; of a definite occurrence in past time, mostly c. aor., after they had prayed, Il.1.458; after D. had died and A. had succeeded, X.An.1.1.3: rarely c. impf., Ar.Nu.1354; E.IT260; …

ἔπειτα.definition: Ion. and Dor. , Adv; of mere Sequence, without any notion of cause, thereupon, thereafter, then, freq. from Hom. downwds., as Il.1.48, 2.169, etc.: when in strong opposition to the former act or state, with past tense…

ἐπέκεινα.definition: with Art., Att. or Att. the part beyond, the far side, Hdt.3.115, cf. Th.6.63, etc.; beyond it, E.Hipp.1199; A.Supp.257, cf. X.HG5.1.10; abs., Id.An.5.4.3; Th.7.58; Pl.R.587c; Porph.Sent.25, Jul.Or.4.132c

ἐπές.definition: Prep. , c. dat., as far as relates to, SIG306.9 , cf. IG5.6.54

ἐπεσσυμένως.definition: Adv., violently, v.l. in; hastily, promptly, Aret.CA2.3

ἐπηλλαγμένως.definition: Adv., crosswise, Hp.Oss.16; changeably, Hierocl.Prov.p.462 B

ἐπιβλήδην.definition: Adv. laying on, of hammers, A.R.2.80

ἐπιγράβδην.definition: Adv., scraping the surface; like lines, Orph.L.365

ἐπιδρομάδην.definition: Adv., = Orph.A.561, H.21.5; rapidly, Nic.Th.481; cursorily, Str.2.1.6

ἐπίκαρ.definition: Adv. head-foremost, better divisim v. II

ἐπικέφαλα.definition: Adv. mouth downwards, of jars, Aët.1.138

ἐπίκλην.definition: Adv. by surname, by name, Pl.Sph.221c; Id.Ti.58d; called after . . , Id.Phlb.48c; PLips.6.7 , cf. Luc.Symp.6, IG12.529 ; D.C.75.16. 2. nominally, Apollod.3.13.4.-Prop. acc. from an obsolete nom. = ; occurs in Pl.Ti.38…

ἐπιλίγδην.definition: Adv. grazing, Il.17.599, Luc.Nigr.36. v.l. Il.l.c.]

ἐπιμίξ.definition: Ep. Adv. mixedly, confusedly, pell-mell, Il.11.525, cf. 21.16; Ares rages without respect of persons, Od.11.537; Il.14.60: in later Prose, LXXWi.14.25

ἐπιπρό.definition: Adv. right through, onwards, A.R.2.133, D.P.276

ἐπίπροσθεν.definition: rarely Antiph.250, SIG493.12; of Place, before, put before one as a screen, E.Or.468, X.Cyr.1.4.24; to be in the way, intercept the view, Pl.Grg.523d, cf. Ti.40c; take cover behind, X.Cyr.3.3.28

ἐπιρρεμβῶς.definition: Adv. aimlessly, desultorily, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69

ἐπιρρήδην.definition: Adv., by name or surname; explicitly, openly, A.R.2.640; directly, ib.847; clearly, Arat.191

ἐπισταδόν.definition: Adv., standing over each in turn , i.e. one after another, successively, Od.12.392; 13.54; standing by, A.R.1.293; standing up to each other, Id.2.84.—The words of Od.16.453, seem to have given rise to the other expl.…

ἐπιστολάδην.definition: Adv. girt up, of dress, like Hes.Sc.287

ἐπιστροφάδην.definition: Adv. turning this way and that way, Il.10.483; 21.20, cf. Od.22.308, 24.184 ; wander back- and forwards, h.Merc.210; on all sides, Opp.C.1.79: Poet. and late Prose, Ph.2.33,320

ἐπισχεδόν.definition: Adv. near at hand, hard by, h.Ap.3, cf. A.R.2.490 : as Prep. c. dat. vel gen., ib.604, 4.948

ἐπιτάξ.definition: Adv., in a row, Arat.380; = Com.Adesp.1296; forthwith, straightway, cj. in E.Fr.292.2

ἐπιτεταμένως.definition: Adv., intensely, Dsc.5.152; Id.1.77; vehemently, Phld.Ir.p.74 W.; Ath.2.45d, etc

ἐπιτετμημένως.definition: Adv., briefly, 'for short', Str.4.6.2; succinctly, Corn.ND35, Ptol.Tetr.107, Hld.2.32

ἐπιτηδές.definition: Adv. of set purpose, advisedly, twice in Hom., Il.1.142; Od.15.28:—later proparox., Hdt.3.130, al., Hp.VC11, Ar.Eq.893,al., Th.3.112, Pl.Cri.43b, etc.: Dor. Theoc.7.42 : hence, cunningly, deceitfully, E.IA476; fitting…

ἐπιτόπως.definition: Adv. suitably, of stars, Vett.Val.5.3,7, al

ἐπιτροχάδην.definition: Adv. trippingly, fluently, glibly; cursorily, D.H.Amm.2.2, Man.1.11

ἐπιφραδέως.definition: Adv., circumspectly, wisely, Parm.1.16, A.R.1.1336; carefully, Id.2.1134, 3.83: Comp. Hsch

ἐπιψαύδην.definition: Adv. grazing, gloss on Sch.Il.17.599, cf.Suid

ἑπομένως.definition: Adv. pres. part. of in a secondary; next in order, Arist.GA736b13, Plb.4.1.7, Ph.1.560

ἑπτάκις.definition: Adv. seven times, Pi.O.13.40, Ar.Lys.698, etc.:— poet. Simon.156, A.R.3.861, etc.: also in later Prose, SIG 1068.8 , Iamb.in Nic.p.17 P.:—Lacon. IG5.213.16

ἕπταχα.definition: Adv. in seven parts, Od.14.434:—so D.C.55.26: Gal.19.280

ἐπωμαδόν.definition: Adv. on the shoulder, A.R.1.738, Q.S.13.541, APl.4.279

Ἐρεβόσδε.definition: Adv. to or into Erebos, Od.20.356

ἐρι.definition: insepar. Particle, like used as a prefix to strengthen the sense of a word, very, much ; mostly Ep. and Lyr

ἐριοπωλικῶς.definition: Adv. like a wool-dealer, roguishly, Ar.Ra.1386

ἐρρεντί.definition: Adv. , = of unknown meaning, Alc.130; perh. cf

ἐρρυθμισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., gracefully, D.C.79.16

ἐσάχρι.definition: Adv., as far as, c. gen., A.R.1.604, APl.4.307 ; Ezek.Exag.5

ἐσκεμμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., deliberately, D.24.157, Lib.Ep.61.7

ἐσπευσμένως.definition: Adv., with eager haste, D.H.Dem.54, J.AJ5.6.3, Arr.Epict.1.20.12

ἐσπουδασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., seriously, in earnest, Pl.Sis.390c; zealously, Str.10.3.5, J.AJ16.7.1; hastily, Hld.1.27

ἑσταότως.definition: Adv. standing still, quietly, v.l. for Il.19.79

ἐστενωμένως.definition: Adv., in brief compass, Eustr.in APo.199.2

ἐστοχασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., hitting the mark: c. gen., Hld.7.5: abs., Ptol.Tetr.9

ἐστραμμένως.definition: Adv., in a varied manner, Thom.Mag.p.294 R

ἐστρίς.definition: Adv. until three times, thrice, Pi.O.2.68, Pae.Erythr.tit. p.140 P.: better written divisim

ἐσχηματισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., by the possession; figuratively, Aps.p.331 H., Sch. Ar.Pl.23; artificially, disingenuously, of argument, Herm.in Phdr.p.84 A.; fraudulently, Just.Nov.6.5

ἔσωθεν.definition: rarely; within, inside, Hdt.1.181, 2.36, A.Ag.991 , S.Tr.601: c. gen., E.Cyc.516 ; Id.Heracl.l.c

ἑτέρωθεν.definition: in pregnant sense with Verbs of rest, on the other side, opposite, Il.3.230, cf. 6.247

ἑτέρωθι.definition: Adv. on the other side; = elsewhere, Il.5.351, 15.348, Od.4.531, Pl.Prm.146c, etc.; nowhere else, Hdt.3.113; anywhere else, Antipho6.39; in another passage, Ph.1.372, cf. Hdt.9.58: c. gen., in another part of my story…

ἑτέρωσε.definition: Adv. to the other side, Il.4.492, Od.16.179; in pregnant sense with certain Verbs, on the other side, Il.20.151; D.4.40

ἔτι.definition: of the Past, mostly with impf., Il.10.493, cf. Hdt.9.102, Th.5.111, etc.: with aor., Pl.Prt.310c, etc.; Th.8.45, Pl.Sph.242d: with the sense, already, Id.Men.93a

εὖ.definition: of knowledge or action, well, thoroughly, competently, Il.2.382; Od.20.161; Hdt.1.59; Pl.Euthd.307b, etc.; cunning with the bow, Il.2.718, etc.; A.Pers.173 ; ib.784; parenthetic in colloquial speech, Ar.Pax1296, cf. D…

εὐαποσείστως.definition: Adv. so as to be easily shaken off: hence, insecurely, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.90

εὖγε.definition: or Adv. well, rightly, in replies; without a Verb, good! well said! well done! Pl.Grg.494c, al.; doubled Ar.Eq.470; Id.Ec.213; Id.Nu.866: c. gen., Luc.Vit.Auct.8

εὐδοκουμένως.definition: Adv. pres. part. Med. of satisfactorily, c. dat., Plb.18.51.10, D.S.28.11

εὐθύ.definition: neut. of used as Adv.; v. B

εὐνῆθεν.definition: Adv. from, out of bed, Od.20.124, A.R.2.197

εὐράξ.definition: Adv. on one side, sideways; an exclamation in Ar.Av.1258, to frighten away birds

εὐσυμμέτρως.definition: Adv. in suitable proportions, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.32

εὖτε.definition: Ep., Ion., and poet. Adv. (rare in Trag., never; with ind., of a definite occurrence in past time, when he sent him, Il.8.367, cf. 11.735, 23.85, E.Ion888 : with impf., . . Hdt.7.209, prob. in B.3.25: freq. with a cor…

ἐφάπαξ.definition: Adv. once for all, Eup.175, Ep.Rom.6.10; at once, Ep.Cor.15.6

ἐφοδευτικῶς.definition: Adv. by tracing an argument, advancing to a conclusion, S.E.M.8.308, P.2.142

ἐφύπερθε.definition: before a vowel Adv. above, atop, Il.24.645, cf. 9.213; Od.4.150, cf. Il.14.184; from above, Od.9.383, Theoc.23.59: c. gen., Simon.183.7: Geog., above, c. gen., A.R.2.393

ἐχθές.definition: Adv. = yesterday, Ar.Nu.175, Th.616, etc.; AP11.35 ; Theoc.2.144; today or yesterday, S.Ant.456; AntiphoFr.58; LXXRu.2.11, cf. M.Ant.10.7. , etc.; cf

ἐχομένως.definition: Adv. pres. part. of = prob. in Epicur.Ep.2p.40U., cf. Apollod.3.1.1, Ph.1.84, A.D.Pron.101.6, Bito57.1, Petos. ap. Vett.Val.332.32, etc.; next after him, D.L.4.23

ἐχόντως.definition: Adv. pres. part. of in phrase = , Pl.Lg.686e; Id.Phlb.64a

ἐψευσμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., falsely, wrongly, Pl.Lg.897a, Str.1.2.30, etc

ἐψιλωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., in an expressionless tone, of reciters or rhapsodes, Phld.Rh.1.200 S

ἐψιμυθισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., with paint or cosmetics, Sch.Ar.Pl.1064
